WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: 2015 in film

{{Year nav topic5|2015|film|radio|television|music}}
{{Yearsinfilm}}

'''2015 in film''' is an overview of events, including the highest-grossing films, award ceremonies, festivals, and a list of films released and notable deaths.

Fox Film (now [[20th Century Studios|20th Century Fox]]), [[Universal City, California]] and [[Universal Studios Lot]] celebrated their [[Centennial|100th anniversaries]]; ''[[The Sound of Music (film)|The Sound of Music]]'' and [[Dolby]] celebrated their 50th anniversaries.

==Evaluation of the year==
[[Richard Brody]] of ''[[The New Yorker]]'' described 2015 as, "one of Hollywood's worst years" but also stated that it was also "a terrific year for movies over all". He emphasized that,

{{blockquote|The anticipated Oscarizables have mainly ranged from the blandly enjoyable to the droningly disastrous. Partly, the problem is merely one of scheduling: most of Hollywood's inspired directors, the ones whose images have a natural musical sublimity and complexity, weren't on call this year. My list reflects the unfortunate accident of a calendar year with no release by many of the best American directors working in or out of the Hollywood system, such as [[Martin Scorsese]], [[Sofia Coppola]], [[Wes Anderson]], [[Miranda July]], [[Terrence Malick]], [[James Gray (director)|James Gray]], [[David Fincher]], [[Steven Soderbergh]], and [[Paul Thomas Anderson]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Brody |first1=Richard |author-link1=Richard Brody |title=The Best Movies of 2015 |url=https://www.newyorker.com/culture/cultural-comment/the-best-movies-of-2015 |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |publisher=[[Condé Nast]] |access-date=29 March 2020 |date=11 December 2015 }}{{Dead link|date=September 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>}}

''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]'' grossed over $2 billion, becoming the third film to surpass that milestone, and the [[List of highest-grossing films|<!--This is the PEAK POSITION the film achieved NOT the CURRENT. Please do NOT adjust!-->third<!--This is the PEAK POSITION the film achieved NOT the CURRENT. Please do NOT adjust!--> highest-grossing film of all time]]. ''[[Jurassic World]]'', ''[[Furious 7]]'', ''[[Avengers: Age of Ultron]]'', and ''[[Minions (film)|Minions]]'' have each grossed over $1 billion, making them among the highest-grossing films of all time. ''[[Spectre (2015 film)|Spectre]]'' and ''[[Inside Out]]'' grossed more than $850 million.

''Minions'' became the first non-Disney animated film and the third animated film overall after ''[[Toy Story 3]]'' (2010) and ''[[Frozen (2013 film)|Frozen]]'' (2013) to gross over $1 billion, and is currently the [[List of highest-grossing animated films|sixth highest-grossing animated film of all time]].

=== 2015 notable box office records ===

==== Studio records ====
2015 is the first year that a single studio ([[Universal Pictures]]) released three films that each grossed over $1 billion,<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://variety.com/2015/film/news/minions-billion-worldwide-box-office-1201580727 |title='Minions' Hits $1 Billion at Worldwide Box Office |first=Dave |last=McNary |author-link=Dave McNary |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=August 28, 2015 |access-date=August 30, 2015}}</ref> the first year that a single studio released two films that both grossed over $1.5 billion, and the first year that a single studio released two films that both grossed over $1 billion outside of [[North America]].
* Universal also generated $2 billion and $3 billion in a single year at the international box office faster than any studio before, doing so on June 10, June 14, and July 17, 2015, respectively. The previous records was held by [[20th Century Fox]] when it reached $2 and $3 billion on June 15 and July 30, 2010, respectively. Universal previously grossed $2 billion in [[2013 in film|2013]], reaching the milestone on September 17 of that year.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2015/06/universal-pictures-international-fastest-to-2-billion-box-office-1201441589/ |title=Universal Pictures International Has Fastest Climb To $2B At Box Office |first=Anita |last=Busch |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |publisher=([[Penske Media Corporation]]) |date=June 11, 2015 |access-date=July 11, 2015}}</ref><ref name="3billion">{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2015/06/universal-record-fastest-to1-billion-domestic-3-billion-worldwide-box-office-jurassic-world-1201442647/ |title=Universal Reaches $1B Domestic, $3B Global Box Office In Industry-Record Time |first=Nancy |last=Tartaglione |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |publisher=([[Penske Media Corporation]]) |date=June 14, 2015 |access-date=July 11, 2015}}</ref> Furthermore, the studio also broke the record for fastest studio to generate $1 billion in the United States and Canada (on June 14, 2015), beating the previous record ascendance achieved by [[Paramount Pictures]] on June 22, 2008,<ref name="3billion" /> and $2 billion (on August 16, 2015), beating the previous speed record of December 25, 2009, held by [[Warner Bros.]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/universal-hits-new-north-american-815617 |title=Universal Hits New North American Box Office Record |first=Grigg |last=Kilday |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |publisher=([[Prometheus Global Media]]) |date=August 15, 2015 |access-date=August 16, 2015}}</ref> and the fastest to $3, $4, and $5 billion worldwide (It achieved the $5 billion milestone on July 17, 2015, breaking the record previously held by Fox near the end of November 2014).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2015/07/universal-jurassic-world-minions-5-billion-record-1201479265/ |title=Universal Sets Record As Fastest To $5 Billion, 'Jurassic World' Hits $600M At Domestic B.O. |first=Anthony |last=D'Alessandro |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |publisher=([[Penske Media Corporation]]) |date=July 17, 2015 |access-date=July 18, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/box-office-universal-zooms-past-809496 |title=Box-Office Milestone: Universal Zooms Past $5 Billion Worldwide |first=Rebecca |last=Ford |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |publisher=([[Prometheus Global Media]]) |date=July 17, 2015 |access-date=July 18, 2015}}</ref><ref name="FRecords">{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2015/08/universal-pictures-highest-grossing-box-office-year-in-industry-history-1201492365/ |title=Universal Pictures Has Highest-Grossing Box Office Year In Industry History |first=Anita |last=Busch |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |publisher=([[Penske Media Corporation]]) |date=August 5, 2015 |access-date=August 9, 2015}}</ref> Universal is also the first studio to achieve $6 billion at the global box office in one year.
* [[Walt Disney Studios (division)|Walt Disney Studios]] became the first studio to release three films within a single franchise – the [[Marvel Cinematic Universe]] (MCU) – that each grossed over $1 billion, with ''[[Avengers: Age of Ultron]]'' joining [[2012 in film|2012]]'s ''[[The Avengers (2012 film)|The Avengers]]'' and [[2013 in film|2013]]'s ''[[Iron Man 3]]''. The MCU also became the highest-grossing film franchise with the release of ''Avengers: Age of Ultron'', surpassing the [[Harry Potter (film series)|''Harry Potter'' film franchise]] ($7.723 billion, [[2001 in film|2001]]–[[2011 in film|2011]]), and becoming the first franchise to gross over $8 billion. With the subsequent release of ''[[Ant-Man (film)|Ant-Man]]'', the MCU also became the first franchise to gross over $9 billion.
* ''Furious 7'' became the highest-grossing film ever distributed by Universal, surpassing the 22-year-old record set by [[Jurassic Park (film)|''Jurassic Park'']] in 1993. However it shortly lost the record to ''[[Jurassic World]]'' in June, just two months later. It was also the first film distributed by Universal to gross $1 billion in its initial release, since ''Jurassic Park'' did so after it was re-released in 2013.

==== Film records ====
* ''[[Furious 7]]'' became the fastest film to reach $1 billion in ticket sales worldwide, doing so in 17 days; this record was later surpassed by Universal's own ''Jurassic World'' two months later, accruing the same amount in 13 days; this record was in turn surpassed six months later by ''Star Wars: The Force Awakens'', which accrued $1 billion in 12 days. ''Furious 7'' also became the first American film ever to gross over [[Renminbi|¥]]2 billion (amassing ¥2.426 billion) at the Chinese box office.
* ''[[Jurassic World]]'' grossed $524.4 million worldwide in its opening weekend, making it the highest-grossing worldwide opening of all time, surpassing ''[[Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2]]'' ($483.2 million in [[2011 in film|2011]]). ''Jurassic World'' also grossed $208.8 million in North America in its opening weekend, beating the previous record held by ''[[The Avengers (2012 film)|The Avengers]]'' ($207.4 million in [[2012 in film|2012]]). Both records were later surpassed by ''Star Wars: The Force Awakens'' in the same year. It also became the highest-grossing film that was not the highest-grossing film of its year, surpassing ''[[Iron Man 3]]''.
* ''[[Terminator Genisys]]'' became the first American film to earn $400 million worldwide without also grossing $100 million in North America. The only other production to hit that threshold before was the French film ''[[The Intouchables]]'' (2012).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/scottmendelson/2015/08/30/box-office-terminator-genisys-crosses-400-million-worldwide/ |title=Box Office: 'Terminator Genisys' Crosses $400 Million Worldwide |author=Scott Mendelson |work=Forbes |date=August 30, 2015 |access-date=August 31, 2015}}</ref>
* ''[[Minions (film)|Minions]]'' became the fastest animated film to $1 billion in 49 days, surpassing ''[[Toy Story 3]]'' (75 days). It also becomes the first Non-Disney animated film to gross over $1 billion, and is the highest-grossing spinoff film, as well as the highest-grossing prequel.
* ''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]'' broke all pre-sale ticket records and grossed $529 million in its opening weekend, making it the highest-grossing worldwide opening of all time, surpassing ''Jurassic World'' ($524.4 million on 12–14 June 2015). ''The Force Awakens'' also grossed $248 million in North America in its opening weekend, beating the previous record held by ''Jurassic World'' ($208.8 million).<ref>{{Cite web |title='Star Wars: The Force Awakens' tickets break records |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2015/10/21/star-wars-the-force-awakens-breaks-presale-records.html |website=CNBC |date=21 October 2015 |access-date=2015-12-03}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title='Star Wars: The Force Awakens' breaks presale records |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-film-starwars-sales-idUSKCN0SE2RC20151020 |newspaper=Reuters |date=2015-10-20 |access-date=2015-12-03}}</ref> The film subsequently became the first to exceed $800 million in the domestic box office on January 9 and $900 million on February 5. It also became Disney's first film to gross over $1 billion at the foreign box office, as well as the third film to ever gross over $2 billion worldwide. This makes it the third highest-grossing film of all time.
* 2015 is tied with [[2018 in film|2018]] and [[2026 in film|2026]] for the greatest number of films to gross more than $1 billion with five,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Child |first=Ben |date=January 4, 2016 |title=Global box office hit all-time high of $38bn in 2015 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2016/jan/04/global-box-office-hits-all-time-high-in-2015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160104130339/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2016/jan/04/global-box-office-hits-all-time-high-in-2015 |archive-date=January 4, 2016 |access-date=January 21, 2024 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 Worldwide Box Office |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/world/2018/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200801135142/https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/world/2018/ |archive-date=August 1, 2020 |access-date=January 21, 2024 |website=[[Box Office Mojo]]}}</ref> surpassing [[2012 in film|2012]]'s record of four,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Levine |first=Nick |date=March 4, 2013 |title=''The Hobbit'' becomes 15th movie to make $1 billion worldwide |url=https://www.nme.com/news/film/the-hobbit-becomes-15th-movie-to-make-1-billion-w-869697 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240114105219/https://www.nme.com/news/film/the-hobbit-becomes-15th-movie-to-make-1-billion-w-869697 |archive-date=January 14, 2024 |access-date=January 21, 2024 |website=[[NME]]}}</ref> but later was surpassed in [[2019 in film|2019]] to have nine films with that milestone.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McClintock |first=Pamela |date=January 10, 2020 |title=2019 Global Box Office Revenue Hit Record $42.5B Despite 4 Percent Dip in U.S. |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/2019-global-box-office-hit-record-425b-4-percent-plunge-us-1268600/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210522233552/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/2019-global-box-office-hit-record-425b-4-percent-plunge-us-1268600/ |archive-date=May 22, 2021 |access-date=January 21, 2024 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref> It has also set the record for the greatest number of films crossing the $1.5 billion mark with three.

== Events ==
* January 22, 2015 – [[Pacific Data Images]] shuts down as part of [[DreamWorks Animation]]'s restructuring plans following the box-office underperformance of ''[[Mr. Peabody & Sherman]]'' and ''[[Penguins of Madagascar]]'' the year prior, cutting off 500 jobs.<ref name="VarietyCutting500">{{cite news|last1=Graser|first1=Marc|title=DreamWorks Animation Cutting 500 Jobs; Dawn Taubin and Mark Zoradi Exiting|url=https://variety.com/2015/film/news/dreamworks-animation-cutting-500-jobs-takes-290-million-charge-1201412212/|access-date=February 25, 2017|work=Variety|date=January 22, 2015}}</ref>
* December 16, 2015 – [[Steven Spielberg]], [[Reliance Entertainment]], [[Entertainment One]] and [[Participant (company)|Participant Media]] launch new production company [[Amblin Partners]], which would produce films using the [[DreamWorks Pictures]], [[Amblin Entertainment]] and Participant Media banners. On the same day, they also announced a five-year distribution deal with [[Universal Pictures]], where the films will be distributed and marketed under either the main Universal label, or its specialty label, [[Focus Features]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lang |first1=Brent |title=Steven Spielberg, Jeff Skoll Bring Amblin Partners to Universal |url=https://variety.com/2015/film/news/steven-spiellberg-universal-1201662956/ |access-date=December 23, 2015 |work=Variety |date=December 16, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Cieply |first1=Michael |title=Steven Spielberg and DreamWorks Studios in Deal to Form New Company |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/12/17/business/media/steven-spielberg-and-dreamworks-studios-in-deal-to-form-new-company.html |access-date=December 23, 2015 |work=The New York Times |date=December 16, 2015}}</ref>

The '''51st annual [[Toronto International Film Festival]]''' was held from September 10 to September 20, 2026.<ref>{{cite news |title=TIFF Unveils New Details for 2026 Market Launch |url=https://playbackonline.ca/2025/12/05/tiff-unveils-new-details-for-2026-market-launch/ |work=Playback |access-date=March 3, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205190356/https://playbackonline.ca/2025/12/05/tiff-unveils-new-details-for-2026-market-launch/ |archive-date=December 5, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The festival's opening film was ''[[Being Heumann]]'' by [[Sian Heder]], and its closing film was ''[[Villeneuve: The Rise of a Legend]] (Villeneuve : l'ascension d'une légende)'' by [[Yan Lanouette Turgeon]].

The festival also hosted the 2026 edition of the [[Student Academy Awards]],<ref>Scott Feinberg, [https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/2026-student-academy-awards-toronto-film-festival-1236594917/ "Student Academy Awards Will Be Held at Toronto International Film Festival"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260903081455/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/2026-student-academy-awards-toronto-film-festival-1236594917/ |date=September 3, 2026 }}. ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'', May 13, 2026.</ref> and non-English language winners of the festival's [[Platform Prize]] are now automatically eligible for the [[Academy Award for Best International Feature Film]].<ref name=oscar>{{Cite web|last=Hoepfner|first=Fran|date=May 1, 2026|title=The Oscars Fixed Best International Feature! Or … Did They?|url=https://www.vulture.com/article/oscars-new-rules-best-international-feature-category.html|access-date=May 1, 2026|website=[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260502202124/https://www.vulture.com/article/oscars-new-rules-best-international-feature-category.html|archive-date=May 2, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

The festival's first programming announcement of three Gala titles was revealed on July 7, 2026,<ref>Anthony D'Alessandro, [https://deadline.com/2026/07/tiff-2026-being-heumann-prima-facie-cynthia-erivo-1236975564/ "TIFF 51st Edition Sets Siân Heder’s ‘Being Heumann’ As Opening Night Film"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260910043743/https://deadline.com/2026/07/tiff-2026-being-heumann-prima-facie-cynthia-erivo-1236975564/ |date=September 10, 2026 }}. ''[[Deadline Hollywood]]'', July 7, 2026.</ref> and a second announcement of five Special Presentations films was released on July 16.<ref>Amber Dowling, [https://playbackonline.ca/2026/07/16/ben-shirinians-the-housewife-joins-tiff-special-presentations/ "Ben Shirinian’s The Housewife joins TIFF Special Presentations"]. ''[[Playback (magazine)|Playback]]'', July 16, 2026.</ref> Several full sections were announced in the week of July 20, with additional announcements in the week of August 3, before the complete schedule was announced August 11.

==Market==
The festival included the formal launch of a film market, separately from the public event, building on the introduction of the Industry Selects program at the [[2020 Toronto International Film Festival]].<ref>Scott Roxborough, [https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/toronto-film-festival-launches-official-market-1236586467/ "The Toronto Film Fest’s Big Market Play: Can It Fill the Cannes-Berlin Gap?"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260903071525/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/toronto-film-festival-launches-official-market-1236586467/ |date=September 3, 2026 }}. ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'', May 7, 2026.</ref> The market took place at the [[Metro Toronto Convention Centre]], while the main public festival remained at the [[Princess of Wales Theatre]], [[Roy Thomson Hall]], the [[Royal Alexandra Theatre]], the [[TIFF Lightbox]] and [[Scotiabank Theatre Toronto]], with the Convention Centre's [[John Bassett Theatre]] added as a festival screening venue.

In February 2025, the festival announced the first members of the inaugural advisory committee for the market project, including former [[Marché du Film|Cannes Film Market]] head Jerome Paillard, film producers [[Niv Fichman]], Vincent Maraval and Noah Segal, former [[Société de développement des entreprises culturelles|SODEC]] president Monique Simard, [[Creative Artists Agency]] financier Roeg Sutherland, and Kerry Swanson of Canada's Indigenous Screen Office.<ref name=market>Jeremy Kay, [https://www.screendaily.com/news/tiff-unveils-market-advisory-committee-as-talks-continue-on-location-timing-of-2026-event/5202006.article "TIFF unveils market advisory committee as talks continue on location, timing of 2026 event"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261003171004/https://www.screendaily.com/news/tiff-unveils-market-advisory-committee-as-talks-continue-on-location-timing-of-2026-event/5202006.article |date=October 3, 2026 }}. ''[[Screen Daily]]'', February 14, 2025.</ref> Additional advisory committee members were announced in May, including Moses Babatope, [[Michael Barker (film distributor)|Michael Barker]], Arianna Bocco, Janet Brown, Diana Bustamante Escobar, Vicki Dobbs, Jeongin Hong and Laura Michalchyshyn.<ref name=market2>Jeremy Kay, [https://www.screendaily.com/news/tiff-the-market-sets-2026-dates-adds-advisory-board-members/5205104.article "TIFF: The Market sets 2026 dates, adds advisory board members"]. ''[[Screen Daily]]'', May 16, 2025.</ref>

Charles Tremblay, formerly of film distributors Métropole Films and MK2, was the leader of the film market.<ref>Andrew Tracy, [https://playbackonline.ca/2025/08/29/tiff-taps-distribution-vet-charles-tremblay-as-head-of-market/ "TIFF taps distribution vet Charles Tremblay as head of market"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250909223716/https://playbackonline.ca/2025/08/29/tiff-taps-distribution-vet-charles-tremblay-as-head-of-market/ |date=September 9, 2025 }}. ''[[Playback (magazine)|Playback]]'', August 29, 2025.</ref>

The market included a dedicated program for genre films, produced in collaboration with the [[Fantasia International Film Festival]]'s Frontières market.<ref>Jamie Casemore, [https://playbackonline.ca/2026/05/29/frontieres-to-launch-canadian-genre-showcase-at-tiff-market/ "Frontières to launch Canadian genre showcase at TIFF market"]. ''[[Playback (magazine)|Playback]]'', May 29, 2026.</ref> It also included the presentation of the established [[TIFF-CBC Films Screenwriter Award]] for as yet unproduced screenplays by emerging Canadian filmmakers.<ref>Jeremy Kay, [https://www.screendaily.com/news/tiff-the-market-unveils-programming-labs-financier-meetings-ip-exchange/5215229.article "TIFF: The Market unveils programming: labs, financier meetings, IP exchange"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260903061818/https://www.screendaily.com/news/tiff-the-market-unveils-programming-labs-financier-meetings-ip-exchange/5215229.article |date=September 3, 2026 }}. ''[[Screen Daily]]'', March 26, 2026.</ref>

==Awards==
===Tribute Awards===
The first recipients of the [[TIFF Tribute Awards]] were announced on July 29, 2026.<ref name=penelope>Clayton Davis, [https://variety.com/2026/film/awards/tiff-tribute-honorees-2026-penelope-cruz-1236823023/ "Penélope Cruz, Isabelle Huppert, Lee Chang-dong Among First TIFF Tribute Awards Honorees"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260831095107/https://variety.com/2026/film/awards/tiff-tribute-honorees-2026-penelope-cruz-1236823023/ |date=August 31, 2026 }}. ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'', July 29, 2026.</ref> They include [[Rosalind Eleazar]] and [[Isabelle Huppert]] as the winners of the Performer Award, [[Lee Chang-dong]] as the winner of the Director Award, [[Sian Heder]] as the winner of the Jeff Skoll Award in Impact Media, and [[Penélope Cruz]] as recipient of the Special Tribute Award.<ref name=penelope/>

A second round of Tribute Award recipients was announced in August, including [[Seth Rogen]] for the Norman Jewison Award, cinematographer [[Adam Pietkiewicz]] as recipient of the Artisan Award, filmmaker [[Bassam Tariq]] as the winner of the Rising Talent Award, [[Helen Mirren]] as recipient of the Share Her Journey Groundbreaker award, and [[Fan Bingbing]] as a second Special Tribute Award recipient.<ref>Jeremy Kay, [https://www.screendaily.com/news/helen-mirren-seth-rogen-fan-bingbing-join-tiff-tribute-award-roster/5219665.article "Helen Mirren, Seth Rogen, Fan Bingbing join TIFF Tribute Award roster"]. ''[[Screen Daily]]'', August 25, 2026.</ref>

===Regular awards===
The festival's juried and audience-voted awards were announced on September 20 at the festival's conclusion.<ref>Pete Hammond, [https://deadline.com/2026/09/la-bola-negra-wins-oscar-predictive-toronto-film-festival-peoples-choice-award-1237108736/ "‘La Bola Negra’ Wins Oscar Predictive Toronto Film Festival People’s Choice Award"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260920172412/https://deadline.com/2026/09/la-bola-negra-wins-oscar-predictive-toronto-film-festival-peoples-choice-award-1237108736/ |date=September 20, 2026 }}. ''[[Deadline Hollywood]]'', September 20, 2026.</ref>

=== Platform ===
The [[Platform Prize]] program was announced on July 21. The jury consisted of [[Pablo Trapero]], [[Amma Asante]], [[Sylvia Chang]], [[Luc Déry]] and Albert Lee.<ref>Zac Ntim, [https://deadline.com/2026/07/tiff-platform-12-films-amma-asante-jury-2026-1236999177/ "TIFF Platform: International Oscar Qualifying Competition Expands To 12 Films; Amma Asante Among Jury Members"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260922224000/https://deadline.com/2026/07/tiff-platform-12-films-amma-asante-jury-2026-1236999177/ |date=September 22, 2026 }}. ''[[Deadline Hollywood]]'', July 21, 2026.</ref> As noted above, the Platform Prize competition is one of six international film festival awards which now qualify non-English winners for the [[Academy Award for Best International Feature Film]] independently of the national submission process.<ref name=oscar/>

'''''Bright Star''''' is a 2009 [[biographical fiction|biographical]] [[romantic drama film]], written and directed by [[Jane Campion]]. It is based on the last three years of the life of poet [[John Keats]] (played by [[Ben Whishaw]]) and his romantic relationship with [[Fanny Brawne]] ([[Abbie Cornish]]). Campion's screenplay was inspired by a 1997 biography of Keats by [[Andrew Motion]], who served as a script consultant.

''Bright Star'' was in the main competition at the [[2009 Cannes Film Festival]], and was first shown to the public on 15 May 2009. The film's title is a reference to a sonnet by Keats titled "[[Bright star, would I were stedfast as thou art]]", which he wrote while he was with Brawne.

==Plot==
In 1818 [[Hampstead]], the fashionable Fanny Brawne is introduced to poet John Keats through the [[Charles Wentworth Dilke|Dilke]] family.  The Dilkes occupy one half of a double house, with [[Charles Armitage Brown|Charles Brown]] occupying the other half. Brown is Keats' friend, housemate, and associate in writing.

Fanny's flirtatious personality contrasts with Keats' more aloof nature. She begins to pursue him after her siblings Samuel and Toots obtain his book of poetry, "[[Endymion (poem)|Endymion]]". Her efforts to interact with the poet are fruitless until he witnesses her grief for the loss of his brother, Tom. Keats begins to open up to her advances while spending Christmas with the Brawne family. He begins giving her poetry lessons, and it becomes apparent that their attraction is mutual. Fanny is nevertheless troubled by his reluctance to pursue her, as to which her mother surmises, "Mr. Keats knows he cannot like you, he has no living and no income."

After Fanny receives a valentine card from Brown, Keats passionately confronts them and asks if they are lovers. Brown sent the valentine in jest, but warns Keats that Fanny is a mere flirt playing a game. Fanny is hurt by Brown's accusations and Keats' lack of faith in her; she ends their lessons and leaves. The Dilkes move to [[Westminster]] in the spring, leaving the Brawne family their half of the house and six months rent. Fanny and Keats then resume their interaction and fall deeply in love. The relationship comes to an abrupt end when Brown departs with Keats for his summer holiday, where Keats may earn some money. Fanny is heartbroken, though she is comforted by Keats' love letters. When the men return in the autumn, Fanny's mother voices her concern that Fanny's attachment to the poet will hinder her from being courted by a more obviously eligible suitor. Fanny and Keats secretly become engaged.

Keats contracts [[tuberculosis]] the following winter. He spends several weeks recovering until spring. His friends collect funds so that he may spend the following winter in Italy, where the climate is warmer. After Brown impregnates a maid and is unable to accompany him, Keats finds accommodation in London for the summer, and is later taken in by the Brawne family following an attack of his illness. When his book sells with moderate success, Fanny's mother gives him her blessing to marry Fanny once he returns from Italy. The night before he leaves, he and Fanny say their tearful goodbyes in privacy. Keats dies in Italy the following February of complications from his illness, as his brother Tom had done.

In the last moments of the film, Fanny cuts her hair in an act of mourning, dons black attire, and walks the snowy paths that Keats had walked many times. There she recites the love sonnet that he had written for her, called "Bright Star", as she grieves the death of her love.

==Cast==
* [[Ben Whishaw]] as [[John Keats]].<br />Keats was one of the key figures in the second generation of the [[Romantic poetry|Romantic movement]] despite the fact that his work had been in publication for only four years before his death. During his lifetime his poems were not generally well received by critics, and at the age of 25 he died believing that he was a failure. However, his reputation grew and he had a significant posthumous influence on many later poets.
* [[Abbie Cornish]] as [[Fanny Brawne]].<br />Like the real life Fanny Brawne, Fanny in the film is a fiery and fashionable eighteen-year-old who spends her time creating dresses, hats, and various other garments. She is also something of a flirt and enjoys attending [[Ball (dance party)|balls]], inciting Keats' jealousy. Though the real life Fanny Brawne went on to marry and have children, she never sold Keats' love letters. They were sold after her death by her children.
* [[Paul Schneider (actor)|Paul Schneider]] as [[Charles Armitage Brown]], Keats' best friend.
* [[Kerry Fox]] as Fanny's mother, a widow.
* [[Thomas Sangster]] as Samuel Brawne, Fanny's younger brother.
* Edie Martin as Toots, Fanny's younger sister.
* [[Antonia Campbell-Hughes]] as Abigail O'Donaghue Brown, housemaid and mother of Charles Brown's child.
* [[Claudie Blakley]] as Mrs Dilke
* [[Gerard Monaco]] as [[Charles Wentworth Dilke|Charles Dilke]]
* [[Olly Alexander]] as Tom Keats, Keats' brother
* [[Samuel Roukin]] as [[John Hamilton Reynolds]]
* [[Amanda Hale]] as Reynolds' sister
* [[Jonathan Aris]] as [[James Henry Leigh Hunt|Leigh Hunt]]
* [[Samuel Barnett (actor)|Samuel Barnett]] as [[Joseph Severn]]

==Production==
In addition to "Bright Star" several other poems are recited in the film, including "[[La Belle Dame sans Merci]]" and "[[Ode to a Nightingale]]". Both Campion and Whishaw completed extensive research in preparation for the film. Many of the lines in the script are taken directly from Keats' letters.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thepoetryplace.wordpress.com/2009/10/24/bright-star/|title=Bright Star|last=Beal|first=Jane|date=2009-10-24|website=The Poetry Place|language=en|access-date=2019-06-01}}</ref> Whishaw, as well, learned how to write with a [[quill]] and ink during filming. The letters that Fanny Brawne receives from Keats in the film were actually written by Whishaw in his own hand.

[[Janet Patterson]], who has worked with Campion for over 20 years, served as both costume designer and production designer for the film.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=McElheny |first=Meghan |url=http://www.wmagazine.com/w/blogs/editorsblog/2010/01/19/five-minutes-with-bright-star.html |title=Five minutes with Bright Star costume designer Janet Patterson: Editors' Blog |magazine=[[W (magazine)|W]] |access-date=8 September 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110912130456/http://www.wmagazine.com/w/blogs/editorsblog/2010/01/19/five-minutes-with-bright-star.html |archive-date=12 September 2011 }}</ref>

The Hyde House and Estate in [[Hyde, Bedfordshire]], substituted for the [[Keats House]] in [[Hampstead]]. Campion decided that the Keats House (also known as Wentworth Place) was too small and "a little bit fusty".<ref name=Telegraph>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/film/cannes-film-festival/5330240/Cannes-2009-film-charts-John-Keats-romance-with-Fanny-Brawne---in-Luton.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090518193439/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/film/cannes-film-festival/5330240/Cannes-2009-film-charts-John-Keats-romance-with-Fanny-Brawne---in-Luton.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 May 2009|first=Anita |last=Singh|title=Cannes 2009: film charts John Keats' romance with Fanny Brawne – in Luton|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=15 May 2009|access-date=15 May 2009}}</ref> Some filming also took place at [[Elstree Studios (Shenley Road)|Elstree Studios]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.elstreefilmstudios.co.uk/film_tv_search.aspx?searchsectorm=f_title&id=b&fid=571&searchtextm=Bright%20Star |title=Film and TV Search Bright Star |website=Elstree Film Studios |access-date=8 September 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111007112114/http://www.elstreefilmstudios.co.uk/film_tv_search.aspx?searchsectorm=f_title&id=b&fid=571&searchtextm=Bright%20Star |archive-date=7 October 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Composer [[Mark Bradshaw (composer)|Mark Bradshaw]] can be seen in the film as the conductor while the male choir performs the track ''Human Orchestra'', which Bradshaw arranged from the third movement of the [[Serenade No. 10 (Mozart)|serenade for twelve winds and string bass]] by [[Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Interview : Mark Bradshaw, composer of the "Bright Star" soundtrack. |url=https://www.filmsdelover.com/2010/04/24/interview-mark-bradshaw-composer-of-the-bright-star-soundtrack/ |website=filmsdelover.com |access-date=26 August 2023 |date=24 April 2010}}</ref>

==Reception==
===Critical response===
The film garnered positive reviews from critics. Review aggregator [[Rotten Tomatoes]] reports that 83% out of 175 critics gave the film a positive review, with an average score of 7.26/10. The website's critical consensus states, "Jane Campion's direction is as refined as her screenplay, and she gets the most out of her cast – especially Abbie Cornish – in this understated period drama."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/bright_star |title=Bright Star (2009) |work=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media]] |access-date=16 March 2018}}</ref> On [[Metacritic]], the film has a weighted average score of 81 out of 100, based on 34 critics, indicating "universal acclaim".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.metacritic.com/movie/bright-star |title=Bright Star Reviews |work=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |access-date=16 March 2018}}</ref>

Mary Colbert of [[Special Broadcasting Service|SBS]] awarded the film five stars out of five. "If Campion intended to inspire an appreciation and rediscovery of Keats' poetry," she writes, "she has not only succeeded but herself created an artistic monument to his life, love, poetry and soul." Craig Mathieson stated in the same review that ''Bright Star'' is Jane Campion's "best work since ''The Piano'', her epochal 1993 masterpiece."<ref>{{cite news | title=Bright Star (review) | work=[[Special Broadcasting Service|SBS]] | url= http://www.sbs.com.au/films/movie/3377/Bright-Star |first1=Mary |last1=Colbert |first2=Craig |last2=Mathieson |access-date=14 February 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110208214157/http://www.sbs.com.au/films/movie/3377/Bright-Star |archive-date=2011-02-08}}</ref> [[Roger Ebert]] gave the film three and a half stars out of four.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thou still unravish'd bride of quietness: Keats and Fanny Brawne|last=Ebert|first=Roger|url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/bright-star-2009|website=RogerEbert.com|date=23 September 2009}}</ref>

Poet and scholar [[Stanley Plumly]], the author of ''Posthumous Keats: A Personal Biography'', wrote of the film's writing and direction: "Jane Campion has understood the richly figurative in Keats' life without sacrificing the literal wealth of its texture. She has evoked the mystery of his genius without giving up the reality of its dailiness."<ref>{{cite web|last=Plumly|first=Stanley|author-link=Stanley Plumly|title=Bright Stars: Campion's Film of and from Keats|url=http://poemsoutloud.net/columns/archive/bright_stars/|work=Poems Out Loud|publisher=[[W.W. Norton & Company]]|date=22 October 2009|access-date=16 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141029144018/http://poemsoutloud.net/columns/archive/bright_stars/|archive-date=29 October 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2019, ''[[The Guardian]]'' added the film in its 100 best films of the 21st century list.<ref>{{cite web |title=The 100 best films of the 21st century |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2019/sep/13/100-best-films-movies-of-the-21st-century |website=The Guardian |date=13 September 2019 |access-date=17 September 2019 |archive-date=22 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200622105737/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2019/sep/13/100-best-films-movies-of-the-21st-century |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2019, the BBC polled 368 film experts from 84 countries to name the 100 greatest films directed by women; ''Bright Star'' was voted at No. 54.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=The 100 greatest films directed by women|url=https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20191125-the-100-greatest-films-directed-by-women-poll|access-date=January 15, 2021|website=BBC Culture}}</ref>

===Box office===
''Bright Star'' grossed $3,110,560 at the box office in Australia<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://film.vic.gov.au/resources/documents/AA4_Aust_Box_office_report.pdf |title=''Film Victoria – Australian Films at the Australian Box Office'' |access-date=24 October 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110218045303/http://film.vic.gov.au/resources/documents/AA4_Aust_Box_office_report.pdf |archive-date=18 February 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> for a worldwide total of $14.4m.<ref name=BoxOffice/>

== Soundtrack ==
{{Main|Bright Star (soundtrack)}}
[[Lakeshore Records]] released the soundtrack for ''Bright Star'' digitally ([[iTunes]] and [[Amazon.com|Amazon Digital]]) on 15 September 2009 and in stores on 13 October 2009. The film's soundtrack features original music by [[Mark Bradshaw (composer)|Mark Bradshaw]] with dialogue from the film voiced by Cornish and Whishaw.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fanbolt.com/featured-album.php?id=16 |title=Bright Star Soundtrack |publisher=Fanbolt.Com |access-date=8 September 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110710224453/http://www.fanbolt.com/featured-album.php?id=16 |archive-date=10 July 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cduniverse.com/productinfo.asp?pid=7992624 |title=Bright Star Soundtrack CD |publisher=Cduniverse.com |access-date=8 September 2010}}</ref>

==''Book of Love Letters and Poems''==
A collection of Keats's love letters and selected poems was published in 2009 as a companion to the motion picture, entitled ''Bright Star: Love Letters and Poems of John Keats to Fanny Brawne''. The 144-page book was published by [[Penguin Books|Penguin]] and includes an introduction written by Campion.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.penguin.co.uk/books/404950/bright-star-by-john-keats/9780099529651|title=Bright Star – John Keats – Penguin Group (USA)|publisher=Us.penguingroup.com|date=16 September 2009|access-date=15 November 2022}}</ref>

'''''Bug''''' is a 2006 [[psychological horror]] film directed by [[William Friedkin]] and written by [[Tracy Letts]], and starring [[Ashley Judd]], [[Michael Shannon]], [[Lynn Collins]], [[Brían F. O'Byrne]], and [[Harry Connick Jr.]] Letts adapted the screenplay from his [[Bug (play)|1996 play of the same name]]. It follows an isolated woman living in a rural Oklahoma motel who spirals into [[psychosis]] after taking in a mysterious [[Gulf War]] veteran.

''Bug'' debuted at the 2006 [[Cannes Film Festival]] before being purchased by [[Lions Gate Entertainment|Lionsgate]], which released the film the following year in May 2007. The film received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised its intensity, directing, acting, and take on [[paranoia]], but were polarized about its writing, in particular the film's ending. Friedkin and Letts collaborated again as director and writer on the 2011 film ''[[Killer Joe (film)|Killer Joe]]''.

==Plot==
Waitress Agnes White works at a [[lesbian bar]] while living in a run-down motel in rural [[Oklahoma]]. Unable to move on after the disappearance of her young son Lloyd nearly ten years before, Agnes binges on drugs and alcohol with her lesbian friend R.C.

Agnes is plagued by silent telephone calls that she believes are being made by her abusive ex-husband Jerry Goss, who has recently been paroled. Jerry had attempted to murder her, and stalked her prior to his arrest. One night, R.C. introduces Agnes to drifter Peter Evans. Agnes strikes up a bond with Peter and allows him to stay the night. The pair's sleep is interrupted by a malfunctioning smoke alarm, which Peter destroys with a [[Magic 8 Ball]] handed to him by Agnes.

The next morning, Jerry barges into Agnes's room while Peter is out getting food. After menacing her, Jerry attempts to reconcile. Agnes then insults him, and Jerry punches her. Jerry leaves, promising to return. Peter later comforts Agnes, and the two have sex that night.

Peter wakes Agnes up in the middle of the night, having apparently found an aphid in the bed. A paranoid Peter kills many aphids, and reveals that he is being pursued. However, he refuses to reveal who is hunting him on the grounds that it will put Agnes in danger and flees. Agnes, feeling abandoned, bursts into tears and a remorseful Peter returns. Peter reveals himself to be a veteran of [[the Gulf War]]. He claims that he was subjected to biological testing by the U.S. government, that the anonymous calls were made by government agents in anticipation of his arrival, and that the room has become infested by bugs planted by the government as part of the experiments. Peter's movements and behavior become more erratic as he fights the "invisible" bugs he claims are infesting his body.

Over time, Agnes begins to share in his behavior. R.C., who has taken Agnes to visit a dermatologist, is convinced that there are no bugs in the motel. Agnes has also reported to the motel owner that their room has bugs but says that he told her that none of the other rooms have a bug problem. R.C. tries to convince Agnes to leave Peter, mentioning that someone named Dr. Sweet is looking for him. But, after Peter has an episode, Agnes slaps R.C. and tells her to leave. Peter and Agnes isolate themselves, closing the room, covering it with [[flypaper]] and [[aluminum foil]] to fend off communications, and lighting it with the glow from [[bug zapper]]s. Peter, believing that microscopic bug egg-sacs were implanted in one of his teeth, tears the tooth out with pliers. After examining the tooth using a child's microscope, he believes that he sees the bugs, as does Agnes. Peter is progressively more obsessed with using the microscope, believing that the bugs are living in and eating his blood.

Jerry eventually bursts in with Dr. Sweet. Sweet sends Jerry outside and tells Agnes that Peter escaped from a [[mental institution]] where he was undergoing treatment and that [[delusional parasitosis|delusions about insects]] are a known symptom of Peter's mental illness. Agnes distrusts Sweet, who later claims to know where Lloyd is and that the bugs are in fact real. Sweet attempts to convince her that he can help Agnes and Peter escape from the conspiracy.

Peter appears from the bedroom wielding a knife. He argues with Sweet, who readies a syringe, preparing to sedate Peter, but Peter stabs Sweet to death. Distraught, Agnes believes that Peter has destroyed her chance of learning more about her son, but Peter insists that Sweet was not even human, merely a 'robot' sent by the government. Together, Peter and Agnes elaborate upon Peter's beliefs in an escalating conspiracy, becoming convinced that Agnes's son was kidnapped by the government to lead her and Peter to meet. They believe that each was separately infected with bugs meant to mate with each another and take over the world. To prevent this, Agnes and Peter decide to douse each other in [[gasoline]]. Jerry, furious over Agnes's unstable behavior, tries to break into the room but she injures him with a [[staple gun]]. Agnes and Peter declare their love for each other before setting themselves ablaze.

Toys in Agnes's room are later shown completely intact, with no sign of the aluminum foil. The body of Sweet is then shown lying prone in the foil-covered room which is undamaged by fire. It is left unclear which shot, if any, is "real".

==Cast==
* [[Ashley Judd]] as Agnes White
* [[Michael Shannon]] as Peter Evans
* [[Lynn Collins]] as R.C.
* [[Brían F. O'Byrne]] as Dr. Sweet
* [[Harry Connick Jr.]] as Jerry Goss

==Themes==
===Substance abuse and mental illness===
''Bug'' primarily deals with interconnected themes of [[paranoia]], substance abuse, [[psychosis]],{{sfn|Lennard|2019|p=112}} and [[conspiracy theory|conspiracy theories]],<ref name=movieweb>{{cite web|url=https://movieweb.com/bug-underrated-masterpiece/#:~:text=Bug%20offered%20a%20disturbing%20and,highly%20addictive%20drug%2C%20crystal%20meth.|work=[[MovieWeb]]|title=Bug: The Exorcist Director's Underrated Masterpiece About Meth and Motels|last=Naidoo|first=Neville|date=August 12, 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20250131052140/https://movieweb.com/bug-underrated-masterpiece/|archive-date=January 31, 2025}}</ref> with a particular focus on [[delusional parasitosis]].<ref name=Radford>{{cite web|url=https://centerforinquiry.org/blog/skeptical_cinema_bug_and_folie_a_deux/#:~:text=In%20the%20film%2C%20a%20man,on%20cases%20of%20delusional%20parasitosis.|work=[[Center for Inquiry]]|title=Skeptical Cinema: 'Bug' and folie a deux|date=December 3, 2013|last=Radford|first=Benjamin|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20250131053356/https://centerforinquiry.org/blog/skeptical_cinema_bug_and_folie_a_deux/|archive-date=January 31, 2025}}</ref> Some critics and writers have noted that the film depicts the psychological effects of chronic [[methamphetamine]] use, though the characters in the film are not seen explicitly using the substance.<ref name=movieweb/> Writing for ''[[MovieWeb]]'', Neville Naidoo notes: "By using narcotics to skew the main character's perspectives, the film cleverly masks elements of reality with gut-wrenching paranoia that make for an uncomfortable thrill ride. It uniquely captures what hardcore meth addicts likely suffer through as a consequence of years of frequent usage of the drug. In this way, the film also doubles as a frightening allegory for addiction and the hell that addicts put themselves and others through."<ref name=movieweb/>

Benjamin Radford, a psychologist at the [[Center for Inquiry]], wrote of the film's depiction of delusional parasitosis in 2013, noting that it "masterfully evokes paranoia, delusions, and claustrophobia. Not only is ''Bug'' a very good horror film, but it also provides a fairly realistic (though of course fictionalized) layperson’s look at these disorders."<ref name=Radford/>

===Genre===
Friedkin has said that the film would have been flagged, in the 1960s or 1970s, as a horror film,<ref name="citypaper.com">{{cite news|last1=Grey|first1=Ian|title=The Eternal Struggle|url=http://www2.citypaper.com/film/story.asp?id=13637|work=Baltimore City Paper|access-date=December 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120406194134/http://www2.citypaper.com/film/story.asp?id=13637|archive-date=April 6, 2012|date=May 23, 2007}}</ref> but insisted it is no such thing.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/ent/stories/DN-friedkin_0525gl.State.Edition1.27e4961.html |title=William Friedkin is bugged |date=May 24, 2007 |work=[[Dallas Morning News]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930042008/http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/ent/stories/DN-friedkin_0525gl.State.Edition1.27e4961.html |archive-date=September 30, 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He told [[Mandatory (company)|ComingSoon.net]] that "There were all sorts of people who looked at ''Bug'', (including magazine people like ''[[Fangoria (magazine)|Fangoria]]'') and they called it a horror film," he said. The horror connection "came from a lot of sources."<ref name="ComingSoon.net"/> Friedkin claims that ''Bug'' is "in many ways, a [[black comedy]] love story.<ref name="citypaper.com"/> He stated in an interview, that "It's not a genre film, but marketing works in mysterious ways. They have to find a genre for it. 'This is a comedy. This is a melodrama. This is a love story. This is a horror film. This is an adventure film.' ''Bug'' doesn't fit easily into any of those categories."<ref name="ComingSoon.net"/>

==Production==
===Casting===
Michael Shannon had previously played the role of Peter Evans in a 2004 [[Off-Broadway]] production of Letts's stage play.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.broadwayworld.com/people/Michael-Shannon/|work=[[BroadwayWorld]]|title=Michael Shannon|archive-url=https://archive.today/20250131055109/https://www.broadwayworld.com/people/Michael-Shannon/|archive-date=January 31, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Filming===
Exteriors of the motel were filmed near [[Olancha, California|Olancha]], California, and at [[Grace King High School]] in [[Metairie, Louisiana|Metairie]], Louisiana,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://blog.nola.com/annmaloney/2007/06/pirates_and_paintings.html |title=Pirates and Paintings |date=2007-06-07 |work=[[The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate|NOLA.com]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110725150218/http://blog.nola.com/annmaloney/2007/06/pirates_and_paintings.html |archive-date=July 25, 2011}}</ref> while studio interiors of the motel room were filmed on a soundstage (a high school gymnasium) in Metairie.<ref name="ComingSoon.net">{{cite web|url=http://www.comingsoon.net/movies/features/20415-excl-bug-director-william-friedkin|title=EXCL: Bug Director William Friedkin |website=ComingSoon.net |first=Edward |last=Douglas|date=May 18, 2007|access-date=December 6, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://archive.altweeklies.com/aan/william-friedkin-talks-about-bug/Story?oid=185225|title=William Friedkin Talks About "Bug"|first=Cole |last=Smithey |newspaper=[[Maui Time Weekly]]|date=May 14, 2007|access-date=August 21, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sfgate.com/movies/industrybuzz/article/INDUSTRY-BUZZ-2593097.php|title=Industry Buzz |first=Hugh |last=Hart |date=May 20, 2007 |access-date=December 6, 2014 |work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]}}</ref> A grocery store scene was shot at Migliore's Grocery, and the lesbian bar scene was shot at Boomerang's Bar, both located in [[New Sarpy, Louisiana|New Sarpy]], Louisiana.<ref>{{cite web|first=Allen |last=Lottinger Jr. |url=http://www.heraldguide.com/lifestyles/aug05/hollywood.htm |title=Hollywood South |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070428191611/http://www.heraldguide.com/lifestyles/aug05/hollywood.htm |archive-date=April 28, 2007 |website=St. Charles Herald-Guide |date=August 6, 2005}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4HFYKKVMvxcC&pg=PT86|title=Bayou Underground: Tracing the Mythical Roots of American Popular Music|publisher=ECW Press|first=Dave |last=Thompson|date=September 1, 2010|isbn=978-1554906826}}</ref> Filming took place over 21 days.<ref name="ComingSoon.net"/>

The set design was done by [[Franco-Giacomo Carbone]], the production designer of films such as ''[[Hostel (2005 film)|Hostel]]'' (2005) and ''[[Rocky Balboa (film)|Rocky Balboa]]'' (2006).<ref name="FilmGrab">{{cite web |title=Bug |url=https://film-grab.com/2014/04/18/bug/ |date=2014-04-18 |website=film-grab.com |access-date= January 1, 2024}}</ref>

Most of the film's action occurs in a seedy motel room. The scenario has three interconnected rooms — a bathroom, a [[kitchenette]] and a living room. At one point in the film, the room has several dozen [[Flypaper|fly strips]] hanging from the ceiling. At another point the entire room is covered from floor to ceiling in tinfoil.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lectrosonics.com/US/Press-Releases/it-s-all-lectrosonics-wireless-for-william-friedkin-s-new-thriller-bug.html|title=It's All Lectrosonics Wireless for William Friedkin's New Thriller " Bug "|date=March 1, 2006|website=Lectrosonics|access-date=December 8, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160114034417/http://www.lectrosonics.com/US/Press-Releases/it-s-all-lectrosonics-wireless-for-william-friedkin-s-new-thriller-bug.html|archive-date=January 14, 2016|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref> Friedkin has said the tinfoil was a nightmare to work with, because it had to be repaired constantly, and because it reflected everybody who was there, including the crew.<ref name=AudioComm>{{cite AV media|last=Friedkin |first=William (director) |title=Audio commentary |work=Bug |medium=DVD |publisher=Lionsgate |date=2007}}</ref>

==Music==
The [[film score]] was composed by [[Brian Tyler (composer)|Brian Tyler]],<ref name=soundtrack>{{cite web |last=Brennan |first=Mike |url=https://www.soundtrack.net/album/bug-original-score/ |website=SoundtrackNet |title=Bug (score) |date=May 21, 2007 |access-date=August 21, 2021}}</ref> with additional music by [[Serj Tankian]]. The end title song "Disappearing Act" was written and performed by [[Chris Cornell]]. [[Jay Faires]] was the film's music supervisor.

===Soundtrack===
{{Main|Bug (2006 soundtrack)}}
The film's theme song is performed by Serj Tankian, the lead singer of the [[rock band]] [[System of a Down]]. "[[Beautiful Day (Scott Weiland song)|Beautiful Day]]" is performed by [[Scott Weiland]], the lead singer of the rock band [[Stone Temple Pilots]].<ref name="AllMusic">{{cite web |title=Bug Original Soundtrack |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/bug-mw0000566954 |website=[[AllMusic]] |access-date=1 January 2024}}</ref>

Additional artists are [[Sean Watkins|Sean]] and [[Sara Watkins]] (of [[Nickel Creek]]), [[Chainsaw Kittens]], [[The Backsliders]], [[Susan Tedeschi]], [[Jerry Leiber]], [[The Coasters]], Alvin Robinson, [[Los Tigres del Norte]], [[Leon Russell]], and [[Brian Tyler (composer)|Brian Tyler]].<ref name="AllMusic" />

The soundtrack was released in stores on May 22, 2007.<ref name=soundtrack/>

==Release==
Distributed by [[Lionsgate Films|Lionsgate]], the film premiered in May 2006 in [[France]] in the [[Directors' Fortnight]] section at the [[2006 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref name=Cannes>{{cite web|url=https://fipresci.org/festival/59th-cannes-film-festival/|title=Festival Reports – Cannes 2006|website=Fipresci.org|archive-url=https://archive.today/20250131052420/https://fipresci.org/festival/59th-cannes-film-festival/|archive-date=January 31, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref>

The film received its U.S. premiere at [[Fantastic Fest]] on September 25, 2006, in [[Austin, Texas]]. It opened in the U.S. at 1,661 theaters on May 25, 2007.

It was released to theaters in France on February 21, 2007. It drew praise from most critics in France, but did not reach the top in the box office.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.allocine.fr/film/fichefilm-57476/critiques/spectateurs/|title=Bug critiques presse et spectateurs|access-date=August 21, 2021 |website=Allociné|language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cinemovies.fr/film/bug_e54614|title=Bug - Film de William Friedkin (2007) |website=cinemovies.fr |access-date=December 8, 2014|language=fr|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140722232400/http://www.cinemovies.fr/film/bug_e54614|archive-date=July 22, 2014|df=mdy-all}}</ref> In its opening week in France, it ranked as number twenty of the most-visited films of the week, and earned $216,244 from sixty-six screens.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.allocine.fr/boxoffice/france/sem-2007-02-21/|title=Box Office Cinéma France|date=February 28, 2007|website=[[Allociné]]|archive-url=https://archive.today/20141208113330/http://www.allocine.fr/boxoffice/france/sem-2007-02-21/|archive-date=December 8, 2014|url-status=live |language=fr}}</ref>

===Home media===
''Bug'' was released on [[DVD]] on September 20, 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dreadcentral.com/reviews/4916/bug-dvd/|last=Barton|first=Steve|title=Bug (DVD)|website=[[Dread Central]]|date=September 20, 2007|access-date=August 21, 2021}}</ref> The DVD release included an audio commentary track by William Friedkin and making-of featurettes.<ref name="DVD">{{cite web |last1=Jane |first1=Ian |title=Bug |url=https://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/30809/bug/ |website=[[DVD Talk]] |date=October 3, 2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20250131054638/https://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/30809/bug/|archive-date=January 31, 2025}}</ref>

''Bug'' was also made available on [[HD DVD]] as a German exclusive, and was subsequently released on [[Blu-ray]] in Germany as well.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bug Blu-ray (Special Edition)|url=https://www.blu-ray.com/movies/Bug-Blu-ray/2236/ |date=April 8, 2010 |website=Blu-ray.com |access-date=1 January 2024}}</ref>

On November 6, 2022, [[Kino Lorber]], under license from Lionsgate, announced plans for an [[Ultra HD Blu-ray]] release of ''Bug'', based on a new 4K remaster,<ref>{{cite web |title=Kino: William Friedkin's Bug Heading to 4K Blu-ray |url=https://www.blu-ray.com/news/?id=31614 |website=Blu-ray.com |access-date=1 January 2024 |date=2022-11-06}}</ref> but the planned release was ultimately shelved until after Friedkin's death in 2023. The film was finally released by Kino on November 26, 2024 in both 4K and standard Blu-ray editions, making its North American debut on both formats.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bug (4KUHD) |url=https://kinolorber.com/product/bug-4kuhd |website=Kino Lorber |access-date=3 January 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

==Reception==
===Box office===
During its opening weekend in the United States, it earned $3.24 million, and ranked as number four at the U.S. [[box office]]; it was one of the most-seen films of the weekend, placed behind the popular franchise films ''[[Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End|Pirates of the Caribbean 3]]'', ''[[Shrek the Third|Shrek 3]]'' and ''[[Spider-Man 3]]''.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://nypost.com/2007/05/28/pirates-grabs-box-office-booty-to-wreck-shrek/|title="Pirates" Grabs Box-Office Booty to Wreck "Shrek"|first=Dan |last=Kadison |date=May 28, 2007|archive-url=https://archive.today/20141208113353/http://nypost.com/2007/05/28/pirates-grabs-box-office-booty-to-wreck-shrek/|archive-date=December 8, 2014|url-status=live|work=[[The New York Post]]}}</ref>

===Critical response===
{{Rotten Tomatoes prose|62|6.6|131|consensus=Disappointing resolution aside, ''Bug'' uses its claustrophobic setting and cinéma vérité camerawork to tense, impressive effect.|access-date=January 31, 2025|ref=y}} [[Metacritic]], which uses a [[Weighted arithmetic mean|weighted average]], assigned the {{#switch:  | episode = episode | series = series | season = season | film }} a score of 62 out of 100, based on 29 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref name="Metacritic">{{cite web |title=''Bug'' |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/bug |website=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[Fandom (website)#Fandom, Inc.|Fandom, Inc.]] |access-date=January 31, 2025 |archive-url= |archive-date= |url-status=}}</ref> Audiences surveyed by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film a rare average grade of "F" on an A+ to F scale.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/why-cinemascore-matters-box-office-225563/|last=McClintock|first=Pamela|title=Why CinemaScore Matters for Box Office|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=August 19, 2011|access-date=August 21, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.avclub.com/is-an-f-from-cinemascore-actually-a-good-thing-our-c-1842666687 |title=Is an "F" from CinemaScore Actually a Good Thing? Our Critics Weigh In|last1=Dowd|first1=A. A.|last2=Rife|first2=Katie|website=[[The A.V. Club]] |date=April 3, 2020|access-date=August 21, 2021}}</ref>

At Cannes, ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'' critic [[Roger Ebert]] remarked, "The film has caused a stir at Cannes, not least because its stars, Ashley Judd and Michael Shannon, achieve a kind of manic intensity that's frightening not just in itself but because you fear for the actors."<ref>{{cite news|last=Ebert|first=Roger|author-link=Roger Ebert|date=22 May 2006|title=Cannes #4: 'Bug' by Friedkin|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|location=Cannes, France|url=https://www.rogerebert.com/festivals/cannes-4-bug-by-friedkin|access-date=August 21, 2021}}</ref> A year later, he awarded the film 3{{frac|1|2}} stars out of 4, describing it in his review as "lean, direct, unrelenting" and calling it "a return to form after some disappointments like [[Jade (1995 film)|''Jade'']]." He also acknowledged others' criticism of its single-location setting, which he defended by writing, "There is nothing here to 'open up' and every reason to create a claustrophobic feel. Paranoia shuts down into a desperate focus. It doesn't spread its wings and fly."<ref>{{Cite web|last=Ebert|first=Roger|author-link=Roger Ebert|date=May 24, 2007|title=Without a net|url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/bug-2007|access-date=August 21, 2021|website=[[RogerEbert.com]]}}</ref>

Judd was praised for her performance by critic Dennis Dermody from ''[[Paper (magazine)|Paper]]'', who wrote: "Ashley Judd gives a raw, shattering Oscar-worthy performance."<ref name="Poster">{{cite web |title=Bug film poster |url=https://collections.new.oscars.org/Details/Archive/70261609 |website=Academy Collections |access-date=1 January 2024 |date=2007}}</ref> Stephen Schaeffer from the ''[[Boston Herald]]'' called it "one of the most disturbing horror movies imaginable".<ref name="Poster" /> The film received generally positive reviews from the UK media, with [[Peter Bradshaw]] awarding it three out of five stars in ''[[The Guardian]]'',<ref>{{cite news|url= https://www.theguardian.com/film/2007/nov/09/horror |title=Bug|first=Peter |last=Bradshaw |date=November 9, 2007 |author-link= Peter Bradshaw |work=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=August 21, 2021}}</ref> and [[Jason Solomons]] calling the film "a minor masterpiece of tension and insanity", with Judd's "finest performance in years".<ref name="Solomons">{{cite news |last1=Solomons |first1=Jason |title=Bug |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2007/nov/11/horror.thriller |access-date=1 January 2024 |work=The Guardian |date=2007-11-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131214191451/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2007/nov/11/horror.thriller |archive-date=2013-12-14 |url-status=live}}</ref> It was also critic [[Mark Kermode]]'s film of the week on [[BBC Radio 5 Live]].<ref name="BBC">{{cite AV media |title=''Into The Wild''; ''Planet Terror''; ''Good Luck Chuck''; ''Bug'' |url=https://archive.org/download/kermodeandmayocollection/071109%20-%20Into%20The%20Wild;%20Planet%20Terror;%20Good%20Luck%20Chuck;%20Bug.mp3 |website=[[Kermode and Mayo's Film Review]] |publisher=[[BBC Radio 5 Live]] |access-date=1 January 2024 |date=July 11, 2009 |time=11:24}}</ref><ref name="Film4">{{cite AV media |title=Mark Kermode introduces psychological horror Bug |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6iScFneGPNE |website=[[Film4]] |url-status=live|archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/6iScFneGPNE|archive-date=January 30, 2025 |date=2012 |via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref>

===Awards===
The film received an award at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival from the [[International Federation of Film Critics]] in the Director's Fortnight section.<ref name=Cannes/>

Judd was nominated for a [[Saturn Award for Best Actress]].<ref>{{cite news |title='300' leads Saturn nominations |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/300-leads-saturn-n |access-date=1 January 2024 |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=February 21, 2008}}</ref>

<!--This article underwent review and has been designated WP:GOOD article status. WP:CAREFUL: "it is important that you take care of the common good and not edit disruptively or recklessly." Please do not make any major changes without consensus.-->

'''''Carol''''' is a 2015 [[romantic drama]] film directed by [[Todd Haynes]]. The screenplay by [[Phyllis Nagy]] is based on the 1952 romance novel ''[[The Price of Salt]]'' by [[Patricia Highsmith]] (republished as ''Carol'' in 1990). The [[Historical drama|historical]] film<!--Film set in early 1950s, with Eisenhower seen on TV and referenced on radio.--> stars [[Cate Blanchett]], [[Rooney Mara]], [[Sarah Paulson]], [[Jake Lacy]], and [[Kyle Chandler]]. Set in 1950s [[New York City]], the story is about a forbidden affair between an aspiring female photographer and an older woman going through a difficult divorce.

''Carol'' was in development since 1997, when Nagy wrote the first draft of the screenplay. British company [[Film4 Productions]] and its then-chief executive [[Tessa Ross]] financed development. The film was in [[development hell]], facing problems with financing, rights, scheduling conflicts, and accessibility. [[Number 9 Films]] came on board as a producer in 2011, when [[Elizabeth Karlsen]] secured the rights to the novel. The film is co-produced by New York–based [[Killer Films]], which joined the project in 2013 after Haynes's collaborator [[Christine Vachon]] approached him to direct. [[Principal photography]] on the British-American production began in March 2014, in [[Cincinnati]], [[Ohio]], and lasted 34 days. Cinematographer [[Edward Lachman]] shot ''Carol'' on [[Super 16 mm]] film.<ref name=Fauer2016>{{cite magazine|last1=Fauer |first1=Jon |author-link=Jon Fauer|title=Ed Lachman ASC on Super 16mm "Carol" |url=https://www.fdtimes.com/2016/01/29/ed-lachmans-super-16-carol/ |magazine=Film and Digital Times |date=January 29, 2016 |access-date=March 18, 2022 }}</ref><ref name=Mulcahey2016>{{cite magazine|last1=Mulcahey |first1=Matt |title="The Grain of Super 16 Gives the Film Another Layer": Edward Lachman on ''Carol'' |url=https://filmmakermagazine.com/96921-the-grain-of-super-16-gives-the-film-another-layer-dp-edward-lachman-on-carol/ |magazine=[[Filmmaker (magazine)|Filmmaker]] |date=January 14, 2016 |access-date=March 18, 2022 }}</ref>

''Carol'' premiered at the [[2015 Cannes Film Festival|Cannes Film Festival]] on May 17, 2015, and was [[theatrical release|released]] in the United States on November 20 and in the United Kingdom on November 27. Grossing over $42 million on an $11 million budget, the film received widespread acclaim for Haynes's direction and the performances of Blanchett and Mara, and was the best-reviewed film of 2015. It competed for the [[Palme d'Or]] at Cannes, where Mara tied with [[Emmanuelle Bercot]] for the [[Cannes Film Festival Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]] award. The film received [[List of accolades received by Carol (film)|many accolades]], including nominations for six [[88th Academy Awards|Academy Awards]], nine [[69th British Academy Film Awards|BAFTA Awards]], and five [[73rd Golden Globe Awards|Golden Globe Awards]]. It also won five [[Dorian Awards]] and awards from the [[New York Film Critics Circle]], [[Los Angeles Film Critics Association]], and [[National Society of Film Critics]]. ''Carol'' was ranked by the [[British Film Institute]] as the [[List of LGBT films voted the best|best LGBTQ film of all time]],<ref name=BFI30 /> and named one of the [[BBC's 100 Greatest Films of the 21st Century|greatest films of the 21st Century]] by the [[BBC]].<ref name=BBC100 />

==Plot==
<!--683 words (as of June 2022). WP:FILMPLOT – "Plot summaries for feature films should be between 400 and 700 words."-->
<!--Before making significant changes to Plot: please review discussions on talk page regarding this section. See: WP:CAREFUL-->
 
During the [[Christmas season]] of 1952, aspiring photographer Therese Belivet is working in Frankenberg's department store in Manhattan. She meets a glamorous woman, Carol Aird, who is searching for a doll for her daughter, Rindy. At Therese's recommendation, Carol purchases a model train set instead. When Carol departs, she leaves her gloves on the counter. Therese mails them to her using Frankenberg's sales slip with Carol's name and address.

Therese's boyfriend, Richard, wants her to go to France with him, hoping they will marry, but she is ambivalent about their relationship. A mutual friend, Dannie, invites Therese to his workplace, ''[[The New York Times]]'', and offers to introduce her to a photo editor friend. Meanwhile, Carol is going through a difficult divorce from her husband, Harge. Carol calls Frankenberg's to thank the clerk who returned the gloves and invites Therese to lunch. Therese visits Dannie and he kisses her, but she becomes uncomfortable and leaves.

Carol invites Therese to her home in New Jersey. She stops to purchase a Christmas tree, and Therese takes candid photographs of her. Harge arrives unexpectedly to take Rindy to Florida for Christmas; he becomes suspicious of Therese, as Carol had an affair years before with her friend Abby. Therese witnesses their argument. After Rindy leaves, a distressed Carol takes Therese to the train station so she can return home.

Carol calls to apologize to Therese and they meet at her apartment, where Carol surprises her with a suitcase containing a gift of a [[Canon Inc.|Canon]] camera and film. Carol has learned that Harge is petitioning the judge to consider a "[[morality clause]]" against her, threatening to expose her [[homosexuality]] and give him full custody of Rindy. She decides to take a road trip to escape the stress of the divorce proceedings and invites Therese to join her. Richard accuses Therese of being infatuated with Carol and predicts Carol will soon tire of her. The two argue and their relationship comes to an end. On the second night of the trip, Therese meets a traveling salesman, Tommy Tucker.

On New Year's Eve, Carol and Therese kiss for the first time and have sex. The next morning, they discover that Tucker is actually a private investigator Harge hired to obtain evidence against Carol. Carol confronts Tucker, threatening him at gunpoint, but he claims to have already sent tape recordings to Harge. Carol and Therese turn back. The next day, in Chicago, Therese learns that Carol has flown home to fight for custody of her daughter, having asked Abby to drive Therese home. Abby gives her a letter from Carol. Back at home, Therese telephones Carol, but knowing that she risks losing custody of Rindy if she continues her relationship with Therese, Carol hangs up.

Therese creates a portfolio of her photographs and gets a job at ''The New York Times''. In the meantime, Carol has been seeing a psychotherapist as a condition of the divorce settlement. During a confrontational meeting in mid-April with divorce lawyers, Carol suddenly admits to the truth of what the tapes contain and refuses to deny her sexuality. To avoid going to court and the likelihood of a public scandal, she tells Harge that he can have custody of Rindy if he allows her regular visits.

Carol writes to Therese, and they meet in the lounge of the [[Ritz Tower]] Hotel. Carol reveals she is going to work for a furniture house and has taken an apartment on [[Madison Avenue]]. Therese declines Carol's invitation to live with her. Carol tells Therese that she is meeting associates in the [[Oak Room (Plaza Hotel)|Oak Room]], and that if she changes her mind, they can have dinner. Therese remains still and Carol says, "I love you." They are interrupted by Jack, a colleague who has not seen Therese in months, and Carol departs.

Therese accepts Jack's ride to a party, but finds she cannot connect with anyone. She leaves for the Oak Room. She scans the diners and sees Carol at a table. Therese hesitates, then walks toward Carol. Their eyes meet. Carol gazes at Therese with a smile that slowly grows.
