==Reception==
=== Box office ===
{{As of|2025|12|13|df=DMY}}, ''Conclave'' has grossed worldwide total of $128{{nbsp}}million with just over a quarter of this coming from the Canada and United States having a gross take of $32.5{{nbsp}}million.<ref name="BOM"/><ref name="NUM"/> Deadline Hollywood calculated the film made a net profit of $15 million after all ancillaries.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2025/10/box-office-bombs-springsteen-smashing-machine-1236598171/|title=What's Up With The Fallout For Adult Upscale Movies At The Fall Box Office|date=October 28, 2025|first=Anthony|last=D'Alessandro|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=October 29, 2025|archive-date=22 December 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251222054613/https://deadline.com/2025/10/box-office-bombs-springsteen-smashing-machine-1236598171/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In the United States and Canada, ''Conclave'' was released alongside ''[[Venom: The Last Dance]]'', and was projected to gross $4–6 million from 1,753 theatres in its opening weekend.<ref name="Budget">{{Cite web |last1=D'Alessandro |first1=Anthony |last2=Tartaglione |first2=Nancy |date=22 October 2024 |title=''Venom: The Last Dance'' Hopes To Boogie To $150 Million Global Opening – Box Office Preview |url=https://deadline.com/2024/10/venom-the-last-dance-box-office-1236144422/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/fdKJ |archive-date=23 October 2024 |access-date=23 October 2024 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref> The film made $2.5 million on its first day, including $500,000 from Thursday night previews. It went on to debut to $6.6 million, finishing in third.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/weekend/2024W43/|title=Domestic 2024 Weekend 43|website=[[Box Office Mojo]]|access-date=2 November 2024}}</ref> The film drew significantly older audiences. 77% of viewers were over 35 years old, with the largest demographic group being those over 55 at 44%, and 67% identifying as Caucasian.<ref name="opening">{{Cite web|last1=D'Alessandro|first1=Anthony|ref=none|date=28 October 2024|title=''Venom: The Last Dance'' Trips Stateside with $51M Opening, but Makes Up for Shortfall Abroad – Sunday AM Update|url=https://deadline.com/2024/10/box-office-venom-the-last-dance-1236158112/|access-date=28 October 2024|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|archive-date=8 November 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241108220848/https://deadline.com/2024/10/box-office-venom-the-last-dance-1236158112/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine| last=Rubin | first=Rebecca | title=How ''Conclave'' Became One of Awards Season's Biggest Indie Box Office Hits |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]| date=2024-11-18 | url=https://variety.com/2024/film/box-office/conclave-box-office-success-adult-oscar-films-1236210375/| access-date=2024-11-24 | archive-date=25 November 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241125151704/https://variety.com/2024/film/box-office/conclave-box-office-success-adult-oscar-films-1236210375/ | url-status=live}}</ref> The film then made $5&nbsp;million in its second weekend (dropping 23.7%)<ref>{{Cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony|ref=none|date=3 November 2024 |title=''Venom: The Last Dance'' Has Great Second Weekend Hold with $26M; ''Forrest Gump'' Reteam ''Here'' Isn't Anywhere with $5M Opening – Box Office Update |url=https://deadline.com/2024/11/box-office-venom-the-last-dance-here-tom-hanks-1236164404/ |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |access-date=4 November 2024 |archive-date=9 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241109223443/https://deadline.com/2024/11/box-office-venom-the-last-dance-here-tom-hanks-1236164404/ |url-status=live}}</ref> and $4.1&nbsp;million in its third weekend (dropping just 18.1%), finishing in fourth and sixth place, respectively.<ref>{{Cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony|ref=none|date=10 November 2024 |title=''Venom: The Last Dance'' $16M, ''Christmas Pageant'' & ''Heretic'' in Fierce Battle for No. 2 with $11M+ Apiece – Veterans Day Box Office |url=https://deadline.com/2024/11/box-office-heretic-best-christmas-pageant-ever-1236170937/ |access-date=10 November 2024 |website=Deadline |archive-date=1 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241201143130/https://deadline.com/2024/11/box-office-heretic-best-christmas-pageant-ever-1236170937/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Critical response===

{{Rotten Tomatoes prose|93|8.1|338|Carrying off papal pulp with immaculate execution and career-highlight work from Ralph Fiennes, ''Conclave'' is a godsend for audiences who crave intelligent entertainment.|ref=yes|access-date=26 October 2026}} [[Metacritic]], which uses a [[Weighted arithmetic mean|weighted average]], assigned the film a score of 79 out of 100, based on 54 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref name="Metacritic">{{cite web |title=''Conclave'' |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/conclave |website=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[Fandom (website)#Fandom, Inc.|Fandom, Inc.]] |access-date=14 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211201415/https://www.metacritic.com/movie/conclave/ |archive-date=11 December 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "B+" on an A+ to F scale, while those surveyed by [[PostTrak]] gave it an 84% overall positive score, with 62% saying they would "definitely recommend" it.<ref name="opening" />

The film's cinematography and ensemble cast were widely praised;<ref name="Macdonald">{{Cite news|last=Macdonald |first=Moira |date=2024-10-24 |title=Review: ''Conclave'' is a thrilling peek into one of the Vatican's biggest mysteries |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/entertainment/movies/conclave-review-ralph-fiennes-pope-thriller-is-actually-pretty-thrilling/ |access-date=2024-10-25 plot,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weaver |first=Jackson |date=25 October 2024 |title=''Conclave'' is slick, unserious – and verging on great calling it "a pretty thin and silly mystery ... that seems like it's deeper than it actually is".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walsh |first=Katie |date=2024-10-24 |title=Review: In ''Conclave'', a quest to import".<ref name="Ehrlich">{{Cite web |last=Ehrlich |first=David |date=2024-08-31 |title=''Conclave'' Review: Ralph Fiennes Tries to Keep the Faith in a Very Silly but Wonderfully Staged Papal |access-date=2024-10-25 |website=[[IndieWire]]}}</ref> The ''[[Chicago Tribune]]''{{'}}s [[Michael Phillips (critic)|Michael Phillips]] praised the film's "delicious portraits in pursuit, deceit and evasion".<ref>{{Cite news|last=Phillips |first=Michael |date=2024-10-24 |title=''Conclave'' review: A deluxe Vatican mystery, with Ralph Fiennes monitoring a shifty-eyed flock of cardinals |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2024/10/24/conclave-review-a-deluxe-vatican-mystery-with-ralph-fiennes-monitoring-a-shifty-eyed-flock-of-cardinals/ |access-date=2024-10-25|newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]]}}</ref>

[[Mark Kermode]] praised the film for what he saw as a thoughtful and respectful portrayal of the papal election process. He highlighted the strong performances, particularly by Fiennes, and said that the film created suspense and intrigue without resorting to sensationalism. He also noted the nuanced exploration of the [[Catholic Church]]'s future and its internal politics, which he found compelling and well-executed.<ref>{{cite AV media |date=29 November 2024 |author=Mark Kermode |author-link=Mark Kermode |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tZaEYUMiiC4 |title=Mark Kermode reviews ''Conclave'' – Kermode and Mayo's Take |website=[[YouTube]] |url-status=live |access-date=11 December 2024 |archive-date=12 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241212215240/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tZaEYUMiiC4}}</ref> [[Richard Lawson (writer)|Richard Lawson]] of ''[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]'' said that the film rightly portrayed "both the seriousness of [the conclave] process and the [[Camp (style)|campy]] ridiculousness of it", and thought that the film "touch[es] fingers with prestige greatness while keeping its feet firmly planted in the realm of rollicking entertainment".<ref name="Lawson">{{Cite magazine |last=Lawson |first=Richard |author-link=Richard Lawson (writer) |date=2024-09-09 |title=''Conclave'' Is a Compelling Papal Thriller That Makes One Major Misstep |url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/story/conclave-ralph-fiennes-movie-review |access-date=2024-10-25 |magazine=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]] |archive-date=8 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241008162657/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/story/conclave-ralph-fiennes-movie-review |url-status=live}}</ref> 
Lawson called the final twist "reckless" and insufficiently thought through,<ref name="Lawson" /> while ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]''{{'}}s Peter Debruge called it "one of the most satisfying twists in years, a [[Hail Mary pass|Hail Mary]] that both surprises and restores one's faith (maybe not everyone's, but certainly that of the disillusioned)".<ref name="Debruge">{{Cite web |last=Debruge |first=Peter |date=2024-08-31 |title=''Conclave'' Review: Ralph Fiennes, Looking Tortured, Leads a Tense Search for a New Pope |url=https://variety.com/2024/film/reviews/conclave-review-ralph-fiennes-1236125537/ |access-date=2024-10-25 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |archive-date=10 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241110132346/https://variety.com/2024/film/reviews/conclave-review-ralph-fiennes-1236125537/ |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Manohla Dargis]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' noted that the film's stance towards the Catholic Church mirrors [[Cinema of the United States|Hollywood]]'s own stance towards its film industry: "lightly cynical, self-flattering and finally myth-stoking".<ref name="Dargis">{{Cite news |last=Dargis |first=Manohla |author-link=Manohla Dargis |date=2024-10-24 |title=''Conclave'' Review: Serpents and Doves Amok in the Vatican |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/10/24/movies/conclave-review.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241125103943/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/10/24/movies/conclave-review.html |archive-date=25 November 2024 |access-date=2024-10-25|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> Writing in ''[[The Guardian]]'', Benjamin Lee opined that the film was "a glossily transferred [[airport novel]] first and a deeper drama about the world of religion second", awarding it four stars out of five. ''[[The Observer]]'''s Wendy Ide praised Fiennes' performance as "one of the performances of the year", concluding "''Conclave'' is a blast" and giving it five stars out of five.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lee |first1=Benjamin |title=Conclave review – Ralph Fiennes takes charge of tense papal election thriller |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/article/2024/sep/10/conclave-movie-review-ralph-fiennes |website=The Guardian |access-date=1 July 2025 |date=10 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Ide |first1=Wendy |title=Conclave review – Ralph Fiennes is almighty in thrilling papal tussle |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2024/dec/01/conclave-review-ralph-fiennes-is-almighty-in-thrilling-papal-tussle-edward-berger-robert-harris-isabella-rossellini-5-stars |website=The Observer |access-date=1 July 2025 |date=1 December 2024}}</ref> Neil Young, reviewing the film for the [[BFI]], praised the "outstanding" ensemble cast but was less positive on the score, feeling it was unrestrained, "doing much of the creative heavy-lifting" and turning the film into a "rather clangorous affair."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Young |first1=Neil |title=Conclave: the hunt for a new pope begins in Edward Berger's ecclesiastical hoot |url=https://www.bfi.org.uk/sight-and-sound/reviews/conclave-hunt-new-pope-begins-edward-bergers-ecclesiastical-hoot |website=BFI |access-date=1 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250224100856/https://www.bfi.org.uk/sight-and-sound/reviews/conclave-hunt-new-pope-begins-edward-bergers-ecclesiastical-hoot |archive-date=24 February 2025 |date=26 September 2024}}</ref>

Filmmaker [[Alexander Payne]] named it one of his favorite films of 2024, saying: "You just can't believe how riveting it is – funny and suspenseful and so well-cast and well-acted. Berger has the miraculous quality of making something you never forget is a movie, but at the same time, it's as though you're actually there."<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 December 2024 |first=Carole |last=Horst |title=Directors Pick Favorite Films of 2024: Christopher Nolan Praises 'Gladiator II', Barry Jenkins on 'Nickel Boys', Jeff Nichols on 'Sing Sing' and More |url=https://variety.com/lists/christopher-nolan-gladiator-2-michael-mann-barry-jenkins/blitz/}}</ref> Other filmmakers, including [[Oliver Stone]], [[Kelly Fremon Craig]], [[Adam Elliot]], [[Coralie Fargeat]], [[Tim Fehlbaum]], [[Hannah Fidell]], [[William Goldenberg]], [[Reinaldo Marcus Green]], [[Savanah Leaf]], [[Laurel Parmet]], [[Paul Schrader]] and [[Denis Villeneuve]], also lauded the film, particularly the performances of the cast.<ref>{{cite news |last1=O'Flat |first1=Chris |title=65 Directors Pick Their Favorite Films of 2024 |url=https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/directors-pick-best-films-2024/ |access-date=30 December 2024 |work=IndieWire |date=30 December 2024 |archive-date=30 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241230231638/https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/directors-pick-best-films-2024/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.joblo.com/oliver-stone-weighs-in-on-some-2024s-top-movies-wicked-a-complete-unknown-the-brutalist-and-more/ | title=Oliver Stone weighs in on some 2024's top movies: ''Wicked'', ''A Complete Unknown'', ''The Brutalist'', and more| date=2 January 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Mahler |first1=Matt |title=''Dune'' Director Names His Favorite Movies of 2024 |url=https://movieweb.com/favorite-movies-of-2024-dune-director-denis-villeneuve/ |access-date=17 March 2015|work=MovieWeb |date=15 January 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Murray |first1=Emily |title=''Dune: Part Two'' director Denis Villeneuve on GamesRadar+ naming the sci-fi epic as the best movie of 2024, reframing the narrative, and what he's most proud of |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/entertainment/sci-fi-movies/dune-part-two-director-denis-villeneuve-on-gamesradar-naming-the-sci-fi-epic-as-the-best-movie-of-2024-reframing-the-narrative-and-what-hes-most-proud-of/ |access-date=17 March 2015 |work=Total Film |date=9 December 2024 |archive-date=9 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241209215805/https://www.gamesradar.com/entertainment/sci-fi-movies/dune-part-two-director-denis-villeneuve-on-gamesradar-naming-the-sci-fi-epic-as-the-best-movie-of-2024-reframing-the-narrative-and-what-hes-most-proud-of/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In July 2025, it was one of the films voted for the "Readers' Choice" edition of ''[[The New York Times]]''{{'}} list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century", finishing at number 194.<ref>{{cite web |title=Readers Choose Their Top Movies of the 21st Century |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/movies/readers-movies-21st-century.html |website=The New York Times |access-date=2 July 2025 |archive-date=2 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250702200131/https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/movies/readers-movies-21st-century.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

====Nigeria====
[[Otosirieze Obi-Young]], writing for Nigerian magazine ''[[Open Country Mag]]'', argued that the portrayal of Adeyemi is problematic for playing into [[Ethnic stereotype|racist stereotypes]] [[Stereotypes of African Americans|of black men being sexually aggressive]], and that "Sexual abuse ... has become, in the last few decades, the defining moral damage of [[Latin Church|Western Catholicism]], yet the ahistorical vision of ''Conclave'' pins that responsibility not on a cardinal from any of those [[Western world|Western countries]] but on its sole black African papabile."<ref>{{Cite magazine|author=Otosirieze Obi-Young|date=2025-02-17 |title=The Ahistorical Racial Polemic of ''Conclave'' |url=https://opencountrymag.com/in-conclave-a-dangerous-ahistorical-racial-polemic-of-africanness/ |access-date=2025-02-27 |magazine=[[Open Country Mag]]|location=Lagos, Nigeria}}</ref>

===Religious response===
The progressive ''[[National Catholic Reporter]]'' praised ''Conclave'', calling it "a compelling and ecclesial call for a renewed spiritual stewardship characterized by humility, meekness, and, curiously, doubt".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Zachary |date=2024-10-19 |title=''Conclave'' bridges pulpy thrills with spiritual commentary |url=https://www.ncronline.org/culture/conclave-bridges-pulpy-thrills-spiritual-commentary |access-date=2024-10-25 |website=www.ncronline.org |archive-date=30 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241130011536/https://www.ncronline.org/culture/conclave-bridges-pulpy-thrills-spiritual-commentary |url-status=live}}</ref> Kate Lucky of ''[[Christianity Today]]'', an [[Evangelicalism|evangelical]] publication, called the film "gorgeous" and "riveting", and said that "though the film subtly advances progressive convictions, it gives cardinals of all ideological persuasions equal opportunity to fall short".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lucky |first=Kate |date=2024-10-24 |title=''Conclave'' Takes Power—and the Papacy—Seriously |url=https://www.christianitytoday.com/2024/10/conclave-review-power-papacy-ralph-fiennes-stanley-tucci/ |access-date=2024-10-25 |website=Christianity Today |archive-date=11 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211192523/https://www.christianitytoday.com/2024/10/conclave-review-power-papacy-ralph-fiennes-stanley-tucci/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Writing for the ''[[Catholic Herald]]'', Miles Pattenden considered that the film "lacks the subtlety to explore [Church politics] inventively" despite some "exquisite moments", notably the performances of [[Sergio Castellitto]] and Rossellini. He also criticised its "lack of historical awareness", noting that questions concerning voting eligibility at conclaves and intersex clergy (see [[Pope Joan]] and [[Eunuchs in the Byzantine Empire#Eunuchs and the church|castrated men who became Patriarchs of Constantinople]]) were "nothing new to the Church".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pattenden |first=Miles |date=8 February 2025 |title=''Conclave'' revisited: what might actually make a man unfit to be pope? |url=https://thecatholicherald.com/conclave-revisited-what-might-actually-make-a-man-unfit-to-be-pope/ |access-date=10 February 2025 |website=[[Catholic Herald]]|archive-date=13 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250513235524/https://thecatholicherald.com/conclave-revisited-what-might-actually-make-a-man-unfit-to-be-pope/ |url-status=dead}}</ref>

John Mulderig of the Catholic ''[[Our Sunday Visitor|OSV News]]'' said about ''Conclave'' that "rival viewpoints within the church are caricatured with a broad brush ... and the deck is predictably stacked in favor of those who advocate change". He warned that "all moviegoers committed to the church's creeds will want to approach this earnest, visually engaging but manipulative—and sometimes sensationalist—production with caution".<ref name="Mulderig">{{Cite news |last=Mulderig |first=John |date=2024-10-11 |title=Movie Review: ''Conclave'' |url=https://catholicreview.org/movie-review-conclave/ |access-date=2024-10-25 |newspaper=[[The Catholic Review]]}}</ref> The [[Archdiocese of Los Angeles]]' ''[[Angelus (magazine)|Angelus]]'' magazine praised several of the actors' performances but ultimately dismissed the film, writing: "The problem here is not that it is full of [[Anti-Catholicism in literature and media|bias against the Catholic Church]]. The problem is that it is just plain bad. ... At the crucial moment, [Benítez] gives a speech so full of platitudes it could have been written by [[ChatGPT]]."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rebeggiani |first=Stefano |date=October 22, 2024 |title=''Conclave'' review: Cardboard characters and silly plot twists |url=https://angelusnews.com/arts-culture/conclave-movie-review/ |access-date=March 5, 2025 |website=Angelus |archive-date=14 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241114030915/https://angelusnews.com/arts-culture/conclave-movie-review/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The [[Diocese of Winona–Rochester|Bishop of Winona–Rochester]], [[Robert Barron]], dismissed it as [[Oscar bait]] and termed it "a film about the Catholic Church that could have been written by the editorial board of ''[[The New York Times]]''".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barron |first=Robert |date=2024-11-05 |title=Bishop Robert Barron pans ''Conclave'' movie: 'Run away from it as fast as you can' |url=https://www.ewtnnews.com/world/us/bishop-robert-barron-on-conclave-movie-run-away-from-it-as-fast-as-you-can |access-date=2024-11-05 |website=www.catholicnewsagency.com |archive-date=13 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241113031936/https://www.catholicnewsagency.com/news/260263/bishop-robert-barron-on-conclave-movie-run-away-from-it-as-fast-as-you-can |url-status=live}}</ref> Sean Fitzpatrick of ''[[The Catholic World Report]]'', a conservative publication, agreed with Barron's criticisms, while also criticizing the writing of Benítez's intersex status, opining that the statement "I am what God made me" is a "popular" yet "ridiculous" argument.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Fitzpatrick |first1=Sean |date=December 4, 2024 |title=''Conclave'' is both anti-Catholic propaganda and secular confession |url=https://www.catholicworldreport.com/2024/12/04/conclave-is-both-anti-catholic-propaganda-and-secular-confession/ |access-date=March 4, 2025 |work=Catholic World Report}}</ref> Father Hugh Mackenzie, of the [[Archdiocese of Westminster|Roman Catholic Diocese of Westminster]], acknowledged ''Conclave'' was "a slick drama" and Fiennes "a great actor", but criticised the depiction of [[Religious skepticism|doubt]] as a necessary component of [[Faith in Christianity|faith]], and Cardinal Lawrence's breaking of the seal of confession, as "directly undermining the Catholic faith."<ref>{{cite web |last1=MacKenzie |first1=Hugh |title=Film Review: Conclave |url=https://rcdow.org.uk/news/film-review-conclave/ |website=RCDOW |access-date=1 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250325093030/https://rcdow.org.uk/news/film-review-conclave/ |archive-date=25 March 2025 |date=24 February 2025}}</ref>

Cardinal [[Mykola Bychok]] – [[Catholic Church in Australia|Australia]]'s only representative – called the film controversial, especially about [[Prayer in the Catholic Church|prayer]]: "Have you seen in this movie any of the cardinals pray? Not one time, which is Hollywood style."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/may/10/no-phones-lots-of-prayer-australian-cardinals-insight-into-secretive-vatican-conclave|title=No phones, lots of prayer: Australian cardinal's insight into secretive Vatican conclave|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|agency=[[Australian Associated Press]]|date=May 10, 2025}}</ref>

== Impact and real-life parallels ==

=== Social media influence ===
Following the film's release, several outlets noted the film's presence on social media and within [[Internet meme|meme culture]].<ref name="NYT-Zuckerman">{{cite news |last=Zuckerman |first=Esther |title=Why the Messy Cardinals of ''Conclave'' Make for Great Memes |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/11/13/movies/conclave-memes.html |access-date=24 January 2025 |date=13 November 2024 |newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|archive-date=8 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250108183559/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/11/13/movies/conclave-memes.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Vulture-Hoepfner">{{cite news |last=Hoepfner |first=Fran |title=That's So Conclave|url=https://www.vulture.com/article/conclave-memes.html |access-date=24 January 2025 |date=15 November 2024|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|archive-date=8 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250108183559/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/11/13/movies/conclave-memes.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Mashable-Cavender">{{cite news |last1=Cavender |first1=Elena|title=Papal drama ''Conclave'' draws an unlikely online fandom|url=https://mashable.com/article/conclave-memes-explained |access-date=24 January 2025 |date=17 November 2024 |work=[[Mashable]]|archive-date=16 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241216142004/https://mashable.com/article/conclave-memes-explained |url-status=live}}</ref> Memes comparing the film to ''[[RuPaul's Drag Race]]'' and ''[[The Real Housewives]]'' appeared on [[Twitter]], while other users created [[Stan Twitter|fan cams]], including ones set to pop musicians such as [[Charli XCX]].<ref name="NYT-Zuckerman" /> Online comparisons were also made to media such as ''[[Mean Girls]]'', while the "elimination" of the various papal candidates was compared to [[reality television]] shows like [[Survivor (franchise)|''Survivor'']] or [[The Bachelor (franchise)|''The Bachelor'']]. Also noted were memes comparing the characters in the film to real life figures such as [[Donald Trump]] and [[Kamala Harris]], the two major candidates in the [[2024 United States presidential election]], which took place days after the film's U.S. release.<ref name="NYT-Zuckerman" /> Many of these outlets took note of the apparent contradiction that a film that "might be [for] retired folks catching a weekday matinee" was popular in meme culture.<ref name="Mashable-Cavender" />

The Twitter fan account, [[Pope Crave]], a parody of [[Pop Crave]], was created in December of 2024. The account posts memes about the film and gained significant attention following the [[2025 conclave]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kircher |first=Madison Malone |date=2025-05-08 |title=Meet the Meme Maker Behind the Conclave’s Most Viral Moments |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/05/08/style/pope-conclave-memes-crave-club.html |access-date=2026-02-24 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331 |archive-date=7 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250807020058/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/05/08/style/pope-conclave-memes-crave-club.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Real-life parallels===
On 14 February 2025, [[Pope Francis]], who was 88 years old at the time, became very ill and was hospitalized, suffering from multiple chronic respiratory conditions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ewtnnews.com/vatican/pope-francis-stable-after-respiratory-crisis-prognosis-remains-reserved|archive-date=7 April 2025|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250407000000/https://www.catholicnewsagency.com/news/262509/pope-francis-stable-after-respiratory-crisis-prognosis-remains-reserved|access-date=March 1, 2025|title=Pope's health remains stable following respiratory crisis|first=AC |last=Wimmer|agency=[[Catholic News Agency]]|date=March 1, 2025}} [https://twitter.com/intent/follow?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Ebuttonembed%7Ctwterm%5Efollow%7Ctwgr%5EAC_Wimmer&region=follow_link&screen_name=AC_Wimmer Alt URL]</ref> Philiana Ng of ''[[TheWrap]]'' observed that the cast of ''Conclave'' celebrated their ensemble win at the [[Screen Actors Guild Awards]], but acknowledged the real-life parallels of the film – chronicling the aftermath of the death of a fictitious pope – amid Pope Francis's then-current health crisis. Ng quoted Isabella Rossellini: "We are very, very worried for our pope, ... [W]e love this pope – Papa Francesco, Pope Francis. We wish him well. We wish him to recover."<ref>{{Cite web|first=Philiana |last=Ng|date=2025-02-23 |title=''Conclave'' Cast Addresses Film's Timeliness During Pope Francis's Health Crisis: 'We Are Very Worried'|url=https://www.thewrap.com/conclave-pope-francis-health-crisis/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250412055945/https://www.thewrap.com/conclave-pope-francis-health-crisis/ |archive-date=12 April 2025 |url-status=live |access-date=2025-03-01 |work=[[TheWrap]]}}</ref>

The [[Death and funeral of Pope Francis|death of Pope Francis]] on 21 April 2025, resulted in an actual [[2025 conclave|two-day conclave]] being called from 7 May 2025.<ref>{{cite news|newspaper=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |url=https://www.smh.com.au/world/europe/the-pope-has-died-here-s-what-happens-next-20250224-p5lemh.html |access-date=21 April 2025 |archive-date=21 April 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250421090622/https://www.smh.com.au/world/europe/the-pope-has-died-here-s-what-happens-next-20250224-p5lemh.html |date=21 April 2025 |title=The Pope has died. Here's what happens next |name-list-style=and |first1=Jackson |last1=Graham |first2=Angus |url-status=live |last2=Holland}}</ref> According to [[Luminate (company)|Luminate]], Francis's death resulted in a near three-fold increase in home viewership of the film via streaming platforms on 21 April.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2025/film/news/conclave-streaming-views-pope-francis-death-1236375240/|title=''Conclave'' Viewership Soars After Pope Francis' Death, up 283% to Nearly 7 Million Minutes Watched|website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|first=Zack|last=Sharf|date=April 22, 2025|access-date=April 22, 2025|archive-date=8 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250508024446/https://variety.com/2025/film/news/conclave-streaming-views-pope-francis-death-1236375240/|url-status=live}}</ref> According to ''[[Politico Europe]]'', several cardinals watched the film to understand the process for the papal election.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Munster |first=Ben |date=6 May 2025 |title=Cardinals are watching 'Conclave' the movie for guidance on the actual conclave |url=https://www.politico.eu/article/cardinals-watch-conclave-movie-for-real-life-guidance/ |access-date=8 May 2025 |website=[[Politico Europe]] |language=en-GB |archive-date=7 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250507044024/https://www.politico.eu/article/cardinals-watch-conclave-movie-for-real-life-guidance/ |url-status=live }}</ref> According to his brother John, among the cardinals who watched the film to educate themselves about the process was Robert [[Cardinal (Catholic Church)|Cardinal]] Prevost ('Bob' Prevost) from [[Chicago]], who would be subsequently elected as [[Pope Leo XIV]].<ref>{{cite AV media|last=Farr|first=Christian|date=|title=Brother of new pope shares reaction in one-on-one interview|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tbnZ8zz9_og|via=[[YouTube]]|work=[[NBC Chicago]]|type=Television production|access-date=8 May 2025|archive-date=9 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250509024408/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tbnZ8zz9_og|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2025-05-08 |title=Brother reveals last conversation he had with Pope Leo XIV night before he went into conclave |url=https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/pope-leos-brother-reveals-their-last-conversation-night-before-conclave/3741619/ |access-date=2025-05-09 |website=[[NBC Chicago]] |archive-date=9 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250509025834/https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/pope-leos-brother-reveals-their-last-conversation-night-before-conclave/3741619/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

'''''Corsage''''' is a 2022 [[historical drama]] film written and directed by [[Marie Kreutzer]]. It stars [[Vicky Krieps]], Florian Teichtmeister, Katharina Lorenz, Jeanne Werner, Alma Hasun, Manuel Rubey, [[Finnegan Oldfield]], Aaron Friesz, Rosa Hajjaj, Lilly Marie Tschörtner, and [[Colin Morgan]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Safronova|first=Valeriya|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/10/07/movies/the-empress-corsage-sisi.html|title=An Empress Ahead of Her Time Is Having a Pop Culture Moment|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=7 October 2022|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221008062737/https://www.nytimes.com/2022/10/07/movies/the-empress-corsage-sisi.html|archive-date=8 October 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> The film is an [[international co-production]] between Austria, Germany, Luxembourg, and France.

The film debuted in the [[Un Certain Regard]] section of the [[2022 Cannes Film Festival|Cannes Film Festival]] on 20 May 2022. It was released in Austria and Germany on 7 July 2022, and in France on 14 December 2022.

==Plot==
[[Empress Elisabeth of Austria]] is semi-estranged from her philandering husband [[Franz Joseph I of Austria|Emperor Franz Joseph]], with whom she unhappily celebrates her 40th birthday. Frustrated with her loneliness and fading beauty, Elisabeth tries to reassert agency by obsessively maintaining her weight. Elisabeth's youngest daughter [[Marie Valerie]] falls ill after Elisabeth takes her for a nighttime ride, causing discord between Franz and Elisabeth.

[[Rudolf, Crown Prince of Austria|Rudolf]] joins Elisabeth and Marie Valerie on a trip, where Elisabeth amuses herself with a flirtation with her riding instructor [[George "Bay" Middleton|Bay]] and a jaunt with aspiring filmmaker [[Louis Le Prince]]. After Bay rejects her, realizing her vanity, Elisabeth returns to Vienna and attempts to physically reconnect with Franz but fails; she later hears rumors of his affair with a much younger woman. After Rudolf leaves for Prague to begin his military education, Elisabeth expresses a desire to depart with Valerie, angering Franz. The argument causes Elisabeth to jump out the window, surviving with minor injuries.

She spends time with her cousin and kindred spirit [[Ludwig II]] in their native [[Bavaria]], but the visit fails to significantly lift her spirits, and she is further frustrated by her inability to affect the war effort in [[Sarajevo]]. At her behest, Franz finances an extension of the mental ward she frequently visits.

Elisabeth is prescribed [[heroin]] in an attempt to ease her health. She impulsively cuts her hair and feels freer. She has her lady-in-waiting, [[Marie Festetics]], stand-in for her in public, and commands Marie to restrict her diet. She invites Franz's rumored mistress to entertain the emperor regularly. Elisabeth takes a trip to [[Ancona]] with her ladies, including a veiled Marie, during which Elisabeth jumps into the sea.

==Production==
In February 2021, it was announced [[Vicky Krieps]], Florian Teichtmeister, Manuel Rubey, and Katharina Lorenz had joined the cast of the film, with Marie Kreutzer directing from a screenplay she wrote.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.screendaily.com/news/mk2-films-boards-empress-drama-corsage-starring-vicky-krieps-releases-first-image-exclusive/5157416.article|title=mk2 films boards empress drama 'Corsage' starring Vicky Krieps, releases first image (exclusive)|website=Screen Daily|first=Melanie|last=Goodfellow|date=25 February 2021|access-date=20 May 2022|archive-date=29 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221129065245/https://www.screendaily.com/news/mk2-films-boards-empress-drama-corsage-starring-vicky-krieps-releases-first-image-exclusive/5157416.article|url-status=live}}</ref> Krieps is also the film's executive producer.<ref name="crew">{{Cite web|title=Corsage, Feature Film, 2021–2022|url=https://www.crew-united.com/en/Corsage__276939.html|website=Crew United|access-date=30 July 2022|archive-date=30 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220730160610/https://www.crew-united.com/en/Corsage__276939.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

The film is a co-production between Austria's Film AG Produktion, Germany's Komplizen Film, Luxembourg's Samsa Film, and France's Kazak Productions.<ref name="crew"/> With a [[Euro sign|€]]7,5 million budget ([[United States dollar|$]]8.1 million),<ref name="budget"/> the production is 58.62% Austrian,<ref name="unifrance"/> 21.34% Luxembourgish,<ref name="unifrance"/> 10.03% German,<ref name="unifrance"/> and 10.01% French.<ref name="unifrance"/> The film was financially backed by Eurimages, the Austrian Film Fund, Luxembourg Film Fund, FISA – Film Industry Support Austria, the Vienna Film Fund and FilmFernsehFonds Bavaria.<ref name="budget"/>

Principal photography began on 2 March 2021,<ref name="crew"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.screenglobalproduction.com/news/2022/05/17/cannes-case-study-corsage-producer-on-filming-across-europe-during-a-pandemic|title=Cannes Case Study: Corsage producer on filming across Europe during a pandemic|website=[[Kemps Film and TV Production Services Handbook]]|first=Geoffrey|last=Macnab|date=17 May 2022|access-date=20 May 2022|archive-date=31 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220531004114/https://www.kftv.com/amp/news/2022/05/17/cannes-case-study-corsage-producer-on-filming-across-europe-during-a-pandemic#!|url-status=live}}</ref> and wrapped on 7 July 2021.<ref name="crew"/> Filming took place in Austria, Luxembourg, France, Belgium and Italy; locations included the [[Hofburg]] and [[Schönbrunn Palace]] in Vienna, and [[Eckartsau|Eckartsau Castle]] in [[Lower Austria]].<ref name="budget"/>

When asked how much of the film was real and how much was fiction, ''Corsage'''s director and screenwriter Marie Kreutzer said she could not tell in percent because she could not even remember exactly, but that some parts were made up, such as the ending,<ref name="theupcoming">{{Cite web |date=7 June 2022 |last=Sondermann |first=Selina |title="It's never as I planned it to be, but that's the point. I like that": An interview with Marie Kreutzer, director of Corsage |url=https://www.theupcoming.co.uk/2022/06/07/cannes-film-festival-2022-corsage-an-interview-with-marie-kreutzer/ |website=The Upcoming |access-date=30 July 2022 |archive-date=30 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220730160611/https://www.theupcoming.co.uk/2022/06/07/cannes-film-festival-2022-corsage-an-interview-with-marie-kreutzer/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and also the meeting between Elisabeth and [[Louis Le Prince]], which did not happen in real life.<ref>{{Cite web |first=Kaleem |last=Aftab |title=Marie Kreutzer • Director of Corsage |url=https://www.cineuropa.org/en/interview/426176/ |website=Cineuropa |date=30 May 2022 |access-date=22 December 2022 |archive-date=22 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221222040815/https://www.cineuropa.org/en/interview/426176/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Although ''Corsage'' has been compared to [[Sofia Coppola]]'s ''[[Marie Antoinette (2006 film)|Marie Antoinette]]'' (2006) due to the use of modern music and anachronisms,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Corsage: Beyond biography |url=https://www.filmsinframe.com/en/film-review/corsage/ |website=Films in Frame |date=2 December 2022 |access-date=22 December 2022 |archive-date=21 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221221115404/https://www.filmsinframe.com/en/film-review/corsage/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Corsage Review |url=https://www.empireonline.com/movies/reviews/corsage/ |website=Empire |date=20 December 2022 |access-date=22 December 2022 |archive-date=20 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221220110312/https://www.empireonline.com/movies/reviews/corsage/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |first=Kaleem |last=Aftab |title=Review : Corsage |url=https://www.cineuropa.org/en/newsdetail/425650/ |website=Cineuropa |date=20 May 2022 |access-date=22 December 2022 |archive-date=22 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221222040814/https://www.cineuropa.org/en/newsdetail/425650/ |url-status=live }}</ref> director Marie Kreutzer said she does not like Coppola's film and does not want people to think of it.<ref name="theupcoming"/>

==Abuse allegations and #MeToo Movement in Austria==
On 18 June 2022, Austrian director [[Katharina Mückstein]] shared an [[Instagram Stories|Instagram Story]] that read: "Tonight a perpetrator will be on stage and will be applauded. And there is nothing we can do to counter that. It's devastating. I wish all those affected good nerves. [[MeToo movement|#MeToo]] didn't even start in Austria".<ref>{{Cite web |language=de |title=Missbrauchsvorwürfe in der österreichischen Filmbranche #MeToo |trans-title=Allegations of abuse in the Austrian film industry #MeToo |url=https://www.kosmo.at/missbrauchsvorwurfe-osterreichische-filmbranche-metoo/ |website=Kosmo.at |date=5 July 2022 |access-date=22 December 2022 |archive-date=21 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221221113159/https://www.kosmo.at/missbrauchsvorwurfe-osterreichische-filmbranche-metoo/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="profil">{{Cite web |language=de |first=Stefan |last=Grissemann |title=#MeToo in der heimischen Filmbranche: "Diese Schweine stellen" |trans-title=#MeToo in the domestic film industry: "These pigs are asking" |archive-date=21 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221221114700/https://www.profil.at/kultur/metoo-in-der-heimischen-filmbranche-diese-schweine-stellen/402060748 |url-status=live }}</ref> No name was given, but the only event of that kind taking place in Austria that night was the premiere of ''Corsage'' in Vienna, which led to speculation that Mückstein was referring to someone who worked in this film.<ref name="profil"/><ref name="akweb">{{Cite web |last=Jasmina Rauch |first=Bianca |language=de |title=Gatekeeper der Glitzerwelt |trans-title=Gatekeeper of the Glitter World |url=https://www.akweb.de/gesellschaft/metoo-oesterreich-filmszene-gatekeeper-der-glitzerwelt/ |website=[[Analyse & kritik]] |date=16 August 2022 |access-date=22 December 2022 }}</ref> Mückstein later said that she could not name the man for legal reasons.<ref name="profil"/>

Mückstein's Instagram story inspired several women to share their own experiences with sexual harassment, sexism, racism, homophobia and abuses of power in the Austrian film and theatre community, which generated a lot of media attention and sparked a new wave of the [[MeToo movement in Austria]].<ref>{{Cite web |language=de |author1=Helene Dallinger |author2=Beate Hausbichler |author3=Anna Wielander |title=Zahllose Berichte zu Sexismus: #MeToo, die deutschsprachige Fortsetzung |trans-title=Countless reports on sexism: #MeToo, the German-language sequel |language=de |first=Matthias |last=Greuling |title="Schweigekultur muss gebrochen werden" |trans-title=The Culture of Silence Must be Broken |url=https://www.wienerzeitung.at/nachrichten/kultur/film/2153232-Schweigekultur-muss-gebrochen-werden.html |website=[[Wiener Zeitung]] |date=1 July 2022 |access-date=22 December 2022 |archive-date=21 (broadcaster)|ORF.at]] |date=24 June 2022 |access-date=22 December 2022 |archive-date=21 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221221113155/https://orf.at/stories/3272794/ about one of the actors from ''Corsage'' "a long time ago" when the project was already underway, but as long as there are only rumors and no court-confirmed evidence, she will never remove or dismiss a staff member from the stage based on rumors, and if there are neither concrete allegations nor a procedure against someone, she would act as a judge if she reacted with consequences.<ref name="profil"/> "There are neither concrete allegations nor those affected who have contacted authorities to articulate something concrete there. That's what makes the case so problematic. Even though I've worked very well with him and I like him, I can't put my hand on the fire for him. I do not check the reputation of my performers or my team. What lies in their past I cannot and do not want to research completely. I can only urge that official contact points be included and that all of this is not just carried out among colleagues and like-minded people. You have to take steps, not just talk about it behind closed doors. There were certainly reports about this man, but again they only came from people who were neither affected themselves nor had anything to testify directly. One should stick to the facts, because passing on rumors can seriously damage people; I appreciate Katharina Mückstein extremely for her attitude and her commitment to film politics, we are definitely on the same side. But I would definitely have chosen a different path", she said.<ref name="profil"/>

On 9 January 2023, lead actress and executive producer [[Vicky Krieps]] was asked about the alleged abuser in the cast of ''Corsage'' on Instagram, to which she replied: "So, a feminist film made by two women should be discarded because of the misconduct of a male colleague? (Second question) Who exactly is being harmed by this? But thanks for the [[mansplaining]] – always a pleasure."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Vicky Krieps' statement about the abuser in the cast of her film Corsage. owned show children under the age of 14.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 September 2023 |title=Austrian actor gets 2-year suspended sentence over possessing, producing child porn |url=https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/austrian-actor-gets-2-year-suspended-prison-sentence-102927792 |website=ABC News |access-date=23 September 2023 |archive-date=23 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230923230348/https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/austrian-actor-gets-2-year-suspended-prison-sentence-102927792 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Following the charges, Austrian public broadcaster [[ORF (broadcaster)|ORF]]—which co-produced ''Corsage''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Corsage |url=https://www.samsa.lu/portfolio/corsage/ |website=samsa.lu |access-date=15 January 2023 |archive-date=15 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230115143138/https://www.samsa.lu/portfolio/corsage/ |url-status=live }}</ref>—stated that it will refrain from producing and broadcasting works with Teichtmeister with immediate effect.<ref name="orf"/> The cinema chain [[Cineplexx Cinemas|Cineplexx]] also reacted by removing ''Corsage'' from its theaters in Austria.<ref name="orf"/><ref>{{Cite web |last=Alexandra |first=Seibel |date=13 January 2023 |title="Corsage" ab sofort aus dem Kinoprogramm gestrichen |trans-title="Corsage" has been removed from the cinema program with immediate effect |url=https://kurier.at/kultur/corsage-ab-sofort-aus-dem-kinoprogramm-gestrichen/402290765 |website=[[Kurier]] |language=de |access-date=13 January 2023 |archive-date=13 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230113211948/https://kurier.at/kultur/corsage-ab-sofort-aus-dem-kinoprogramm-gestrichen/402290765 |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Corsage''{{'s}} producers, Johanna Scherz and Alexander Glehr stated; "Today we learned of the charges against Florian Teichtmeister for the first time and as film producers and parents we are deeply shocked. Over the weekend we will decide together with the director of the film, Marie Kreutzer, what this means for the film and we will inform you in good time."<ref name="orf"/> On 15 January 2023, Kreutzer released a statement saying that she was "sad and angry that a feminist film that more than 300 people from all over Europe worked on for years may be tarnished and damaged by the horrific actions of one person".<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 January 2023 |title=Corsage – Statement of the Producers and the Director |url=https://www.film-ag.at/en/news |website=Film AG |access-date=17 January 2023 |archive-date=26 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230126130458/https://www.film-ag.at/en/news |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Barraclough">{{Cite web |last=Barraclough |first=Leo |date=16 January 2023 |title='Corsage' to Remain as Austria's Official Oscar Entry Despite Charges Against Actor Florian Teichtmeister for Possession of Child Pornography |url=https://variety.com/2023/film/news/corsage-florian-teichtmeister-1235490763/ |website=Variety |access-date=17 January 2023 |archive-date=17 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230117113556/https://variety.com/2023/film/news/corsage-florian-teichtmeister-1235490763/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Kreutzer said she was informed of the rumors about Teichtmeister in Autumn 2021, after the filming for ''Corsage'' had wrapped,<ref name="Barraclough"/> and when she inquired the actor about these rumors via email,<ref name="KZ220123">{{Cite web |date=22 January 2023 |title=Regisseurin Marie Kreutzer zieht "Corsage" nicht zurück |trans-title=Director Marie Kreutzer does not withdraw "Corsage" |url=https://www.kleinezeitung.at/kultur/6241530/Fall-Teichtmeister_Regisseurin-Marie-Kreutzer-zieht-Corsage-nicht |website=[[Kleine Zeitung]] |language=de |access-date=28 June 2023 |archive-date=7 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230207181145/https://www.kleinezeitung.at/kultur/6241530/Fall-Teichtmeister_Regisseurin-Marie-Kreutzer-zieht-Corsage-nicht |url-status=live }}</ref> he "convincingly assured us (and others) of their falsity".<ref name="Barraclough"/> Kreutzer later said that it was not possible to reshoot Teichtmeister's scenes with another actor due to budget and organization issues and that it would have breached the contract, "we can't just interrupt a project just because there are suspicions or rumors about an actor", she said.<ref name="Kurier">{{Cite web |date=22 January 2023 |title="Corsage"-Regisseurin: "Kann nicht in Festplatten hineinschauen" |trans-title="Corsage" director: "Can't look into hard drives" |url=https://kurier.at/kultur/medien/corsage-regisseurin-kreutzer-ueber-teichtmeister-ich-kann-nicht-in-festplatten-hineinschauen/402300983 |website=[[Kurier]] |language=de |access-date=28 June 2023 |archive-date=8 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230208181229/https://kurier.at/kultur/medien/corsage-regisseurin-kreutzer-ueber-teichtmeister-ich-kann-nicht-in-festplatten-hineinschauen/402300983 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Rumors about Teichtmeister had been circulating in the Austrian press since September 2021, when daily newspaper ''[[Der Standard]]'' published an article reporting that there was talk of a "successful local theater and film actor who is said to be hoarding child pornographic material". The actor's ex-partner reported him, and he was said to have physically attacked and verbally threatened her during their relationship.<ref name="cerny">{{Cite web |last=Cerny |first=Karim |date=13 January 2023 |title=Florian Teichtmeister – Tatbestand: 58.000 Dateien |trans-title=Florian Teichtmeister – Facts: 58,000 files |url=https://www.profil.at/kultur/florian-teichtmeister-tatbestand-58000-dateien/402291038 |website=[[Profil (magazine)|Profil.at]] |language=de |access-date=15 January 2023 |archive-date=15 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230115221556/https://www.profil.at/kultur/florian-teichtmeister-tatbestand-58000-dateien/402291038 |url-status=live }}</ref> Nobody was named at the time, but insiders quickly found out that it was Teichtmeister, according to Austrian magazine ''[[Profil (magazine)|Profil]]'', which also stated that Katharina Mückstein's Instagram post on 18 June 2022 was meant for a different actor,<ref name="cerny"/> and Mückstein herself later stated that she was not talking about Teichtmeister.<ref name="wielander-kronsteiner">{{Cite web |last1=Wielander |first1=Anna |last2=Kronsteiner |first2=Olga |date=16 January 2023 |title=MeToo: Vorwürfe gegen weiteren "Corsage"-Darsteller |trans-title=MeToo: Allegations against another "Corsage" actor |url=https://www.derstandard.at/story/2000142632468/metoo-geruechte-gegen-weiteren-corsage-darsteller |website=[[Der Standard]] |language=de |access-date=17 January 2023 |archive-date=17 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230117142402/https://www.derstandard.at/story/2000142632468/metoo-geruechte-gegen-weiteren-corsage-darsteller |url-status=live }}</ref> Teichtmeister initially denied the allegations by claiming it was an act of revenge by his former partner.<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 January 2023 |title=Kušej über Fall Teichtmeister: "Hat Vorwürfe vehement bestritten" |trans-title=Kušej on the Teichtmeister case: "Vehemently denied the allegations" |url=https://kurier.at/kultur/martin-kusej-ueber-teichtmeister-er-hat-die-vorwuerfe-vehement-bestritten/402291857 |website=[[Kurier]] |language=de |access-date=17 January 2023 |archive-date=17 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230117115059/https://kurier.at/kultur/martin-kusej-ueber-teichtmeister-er-hat-die-vorwuerfe-vehement-bestritten/402291857 |url-status=live }}</ref>

The Film & Music Austria (FAMA) decided that ''Corsage'' would continue to be Austria's official submission for the Oscars in the International Feature Film category despite the charges against Teichtmeister.<ref name="Barraclough"/> The film's international distributors such as [[IFC Films]] (United States), [[Picturehouse Cinemas|Picturehouse Distribution]] (UK and Ireland), Bim Distribuzione (Italy), [[Ad Vitam (company)|Ad Vitam]] (France) and Alamode (Germany) agreed with the statements from Kreutzer and the film's production company that the film should not be overshadowed by the actions of one person, and there was no indication that ''Corsage'' would be removed from theaters in any of these countries.<ref name="Macnab">{{Cite web |last=Macnab |first=Geoffrey |date=16 January 2023 |title='Corsage' filmmakers and int'l distributors react to child porn charges against Florian Teichtmeister |url=https://www.screendaily.com/news/corsage-filmmakers-and-intl-distributors-react-to-child-porn-charges-against-florian-teichtmeister/5178143.article |website=[[Screen Daily]] |access-date=17 January 2023 |archive-date=17 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230117080503/https://www.screendaily.com/news/corsage-filmmakers-and-intl-distributors-react-to-child-porn-charges-against-florian-teichtmeister/5178143.article |url-status=live }}</ref> The film's international sales handler mK2 declined to comment on the situation.<ref name="Macnab"/>

''Kronen Zeitung'' reported that the fact that ''Corsage'' remained as Austria's candidate for the Oscars following the charges against Teichtmeister has divided opinions in the country.<ref name="Richter">{{Cite web |last=Richter |first=Anja |date=16 January 2023 |title=HITZIGE DEBATTE – "Corsage" als Oscarfilm: Schaden für Österreich? |trans-title=Heated Debate – "Corsage" as an Oscar film: damage to Austria? |url=https://www.krone.at/2905377 |website=[[Kronen Zeitung]] |language=de |access-date=17 January 2023 |archive-date=17 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230117113556/https://www.krone.at/2905377 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 17 January 2023, ''Corsage''{{'s}} production company, Film AG, issued a statement saying that the underage actors who worked on the film were never left unsupervised and that there was little or no contact with Teichtmeister behind the camera.<ref name="Schafferhofer"/> The company also said that there was a strict ban on cell phones and photography on the set.<ref name="Schafferhofer">{{Cite web |last=Schafferhofer |first=Julia |date=17 January 2023 |title=Nach Causa Teichtmeister: Neue Details zu Übergriffsvorwürfen gegen zweiten "Corsage"-Darsteller |trans-title=After Teichtmeister's Case: New Details on Allegations of Assault Against the Second "Corsage" Actor |url=https://www.kleinezeitung.at/kultur/kulturkaufmacher/6239298/Nach-Causa-Teichtmeister_Neue-Details-zu-Uebergriffsvorwuerfen |website=[[Kleine Zeitung]] |language=de |access-date=19 January 2023 |archive-date=18 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230118182509/https://www.kleinezeitung.at/kultur/kulturkaufmacher/6239298/Nach-Causa-Teichtmeister_Neue-Details-zu-Uebergriffsvorwuerfen |url-status=live }}</ref> In February 2023, Kreutzer said that she did not know Teichtmeister well, that they shot together for two weeks and she did not see him much before either and that "the shock must be much bigger for the people who knew him well". Kreutzer also added, "He has done other films, he is a famous theatre actor in Austria, but we are in a crossfire now, because ''Corsage'' has been so successful and everybody was putting this story together with the film. I had to talk about it, even though I am neither responsible nor could I have ever known that. I don't wish for anyone to ever experience this."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Balaga |first=Marta |date=3 February 2023 |title='Corsage' Helmer Marie Kreutzer Breaks Down at Goteborg, Talks Scandal |url=https://variety.com/2023/film/global/marie-kreutzer-corsage-vicky-krieps-1235512307/ |website=Variety |access-date=14 May 2025 |archive-date=29 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230329202703/https://variety.com/2023/film/global/marie-kreutzer-corsage-vicky-krieps-1235512307/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

Since 2020, Kreutzer has been working on a new film under the working title ''Johnny Maccaroni'', which deals with a topic similar to Teichtmeister's case.<ref name="KZ220123"/> The project, for which Kreutzer received funding in 2021,<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 2022 |title=Tätigkeits – Bericht 2021 – Österreichisches Filminstitut |trans-title=Activity Report 2021 – Austrian Film Institute |url=https://filminstitut.at/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/O%CC%88FI_Ta%CC%88tigkeitsbericht2021_220x297mm_WEB.pdf |access-date=27 June 2023 |website=Österreichisches Filminstitut |page=42 |language=de |archive-date=10 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221110121207/https://filminstitut.at/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/O%CC%88FI_Ta%CC%88tigkeitsbericht2021_220x297mm_WEB.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> is about a woman who is visited by the police one day because her husband published a photo of their child in a dark web chat group in which men share content about how to abuse a child.<ref name="KZ220123"/> Kreutzer told German newspaper ''[[Süddeutsche Zeitung]]'' in January 2023 that she was unsure whether the film would even come about.<ref name="KZ220123"/>

Krieps, who played the wife of Teichtmeister's character in ''Corsage'', talked about the case for the first time in an interview with ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' on 19 February 2023, saying, "It's the problem of a man who needs probably treatment and help and also, it needs to be judged by the law. To me, I don't even see in what way this could be controversial to the movie. It was a shock to know that someone I was so close to was apparently someone I didn't know. This was more shocking, and shaking me in a way thinking about humans and society and how we think we know each other, but we don't. In that way I thought about it a lot but I never understood what it has to do with the movie. He's not playing [[Empress Elisabeth of Austria|Sisi]] and the movie is not about [[manliness]]. In my eyes it is not really connected."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ramachandran |first=Naman |date=19 February 2023 |title=Vicky Krieps on Berlin Competition Film 'Ingeborg Bachmann': 'I Went So Far, I Felt Like I Almost Lost Myself' (EXCLUSIVE) |url=https://variety.com/2023/film/festivals/vicky-krieps-berlin-ingeborg-bachmann-1235527788/ |website=Variety}}</ref>

===Further allegations===
Austrian newspaper ''Exxpress'' reported on 15 January 2023 that another actor from ''Corsage'' has been accused of sexual assault by an anonymous insider of the film industry.<ref name="exxpress">{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Richard |date=15 January 2023 |title=Was für ein Sumpf: Nach Auffliegen Teichtmeisters weiterer Darsteller unter Verdacht |trans-title=What a swamp: After Teichtmeister was exposed, other actors were suspected |url=https://exxpress.at/was-fuer-ein-sumpf-nach-auffliegen-teichtmeisters-weiterer-darsteller-unter-verdacht/ |website=Exxpress |language=de |access-date=15 January 2023 |archive-date=15 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230115131336/https://exxpress.at/was-fuer-ein-sumpf-nach-auffliegen-teichtmeisters-weiterer-darsteller-unter-verdacht/ |url-status=live }}</ref> "As with Teichtmeister, everything should be covered up with this actor so that the film project is not damaged. Again, many people know about the allegations, and again nobody is bringing it to the public", reported the [[whistleblower]] who tipped off ''Exxpress'' in June 2022<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 June 2022 |title=Ermittlungen in Kinderporno-Fall: Mediengesetz schützt prominenten TV-Kommissar |trans-title=Investigations into child porn case: Media law protects prominent TV commissioner |url=https://exxpress.at/ermittlungen-in-kinderporno-fall-mediengesetz-schuetzt-prominenten-tv-kommissar/ |website=Exxpress |language=de |access-date=1 March 2023 |archive-date=13 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220813094809/https://exxpress.at/ermittlungen-in-kinderporno-fall-mediengesetz-schuetzt-prominenten-tv-kommissar/ |url-status=live }}</ref> about the allegations against Teichtmeister.<ref name="exxpress"/> "In the industry it is known that there are also serious allegations against another Austrian actor. During the shooting of ''Corsage'' there were several serious sexual assaults on the film set. And the scene is also silent about that again", the insider said.<ref name="exxpress"/> ''Exxpress'' also reported that the film's director Marie Kreutzer had been informed about these cases, and that the name of the actor is known to the newspaper, but Austria's media law does not allow him to be named.<ref name="exxpress"/>

''Der Standard'' also reported that there are allegations against another actor from the film.<ref name="wielander-kronsteiner"/> Kreutzer confirmed to ''Der Standard'' on 16 January 2023 that her response to Mückstein's post in July 2022 was not about Teichtmeister.<ref name="wielander-kronsteiner"/> ''Der Standard'' wrote that Kreutzer had several conversations with the second actor after the #MeToo rumors circulating about him were repeatedly brought to her around the start of the shooting for ''Corsage'',<ref name="wielander-kronsteiner"/> and the actor always claimed that the rumors were unfounded.<ref name="wielander-kronsteiner"/> Kreutzer then recommended that he turn to "We_do", the contact and advice center for the film and television industry of Austria.<ref name="wielander-kronsteiner"/> According to reports, the actor followed her advice and is said to have deposited his willingness to talk at "We_do" if he was reported by those affected.<ref name="wielander-kronsteiner"/> The following day, the "We_do" issued a statement saying the article made it look like they are a relief for the people who caused the abuse, which they are not, and that it can even be part of an overall strategy of manipulation. They clarified that they work for the people who were affected. If they want support in a conversation with the person who caused the problem, they will be happy to do it.<ref>{{Cite web |author=We-do Anlaufstelle |date=17 January 2023 |title=KLARSTELLUNG |trans-title=CLARIFICATION |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CngetL6shl8/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/instagram/we_do_anlaufstelle/3017546796905929084 |archive-date=27 June 2023 |access-date=27 June 2023 |website=[[Instagram]] |language=de}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

On 17 January 2023, one of ''Corsage''{{'s}} production companies, Film AG, issued a statement on the second actor accused of sexual assault: "Of course we take such allegations seriously, even if they have nothing to do with the production of the film ''Corsage'' directly. Director Marie Kreutzer commented in detail on this last summer. Back then, she tried to get to the bottom of the rumors with both the actor and many whistleblowers. We had another detailed conversation with the actor yesterday. This conversation didn't bring us any new information either", the statement said.<ref name="Schafferhofer"/> The actor's lawyer told Austrian newspaper ''[[Kleine Zeitung]]'' that there is no investigation against him.<ref name="Schafferhofer"/> On 20 January 2023, the actor issued a statement denying the allegations through his lawyer and asked not to be named further.<ref>{{cite news|last=Leyrer|first=Georg|date=20 January 2023|url=https://kurier.at/kultur/corsage-schauspieler-weist-metoo-vorwuerfe-mit-aller-entschiedenheit-zurueck/402298232|title="Corsage"-Schauspieler weist #MeToo-Vorwürfe "mit aller Entschiedenheit zurück"|work=[[Kurier]]|language=de|access-date=21 January 2023|archive-date=21 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230121063528/https://kurier.at/kultur/corsage-schauspieler-weist-metoo-vorwuerfe-mit-aller-entschiedenheit-zurueck/402298232|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 20 January 2023, German magazine ''[[Der Spiegel]]'' reported that at least three women have accused the unnamed actor of psychological, physical and sexual violence.<ref name="spiegel">{{Cite web |last=Laffert |first=Bartholomäus |date=20 January 2023 |title=Vorwürfe gegen »Corsage«-Darsteller {{!}} Wer wusste was? |trans-title=Allegations against »Corsage« actors {{!}} Who knew what? |url=https://www.spiegel.de/kultur/vorwuerfe-gegen-corsage-darsteller-wer-wusste-was-a-315b391d-0a1d-44a4-a396-1b40bd121b7d |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230122201632/https://www.spiegel.de/kultur/vorwuerfe-gegen-corsage-darsteller-wer-wusste-was-a-315b391d-0a1d-44a4-a396-1b40bd121b7d |archive-date=22 January 2023 |access-date=27 June 2023 |website=[[Der Spiegel]] |language=de}}{{cbignore}}</ref> The producers of ''Corsage'' sent a statement to ''Der Spiegel'' saying, "We trusted him, we shouldn't have done that from today's perspective. It is the right of those affected to decide whether an action is an assault and how they want to deal with it."<ref name="spiegel"/> Shortly before the Vienna premiere of ''Corsage'' in June 2022, the women tried to talk to Kreutzer, who canceled three suggested dates for the meeting claiming she did not have time for it.<ref name="spiegel"/> She later offered to get in touch with one of the women, but it was not accepted.<ref name="spiegel"/> On 22 January 2023, Kreutzer said in a live interview for Austrian TV channel [[ORF III]] that the unnamed actor informed her of the allegations against him two days before shooting began, "That was shortly before shooting started, that's not the moment when you quickly pull someone else out of a hat. Especially when it's about something so vague," she said.<ref name="Kurier"/> In the same interview, Kreutzer made sure to say that this actor is not Manuel Rubey, and that without a name it not only harms ''Corsage'' but also his male colleagues in the film if he does not identify himself.<ref name="Kurier"/>

Festival]] in the following month.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.romacinemafest.it/en/official-selection-2022/ |title=The Official Selection of the Rome Film Festival |website=Cinema Foundation for Rome |date=22 September 2022 |access-date=3 October 2024 |language=en |archive-date=7 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007090948/https://www.romacinemafest.it/en/official-selection-2022/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

It was released in Austria and Germany on 7 July 2022, by Panda Lichtspiele Filmverleih and Alamode Film, respectively.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.alamodefilm.de/kino/detail/corsage.html|title=Corsage|publisher=Alamode Film|access-date=20 May 2022|archive-date=21 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220521153455/https://www.alamodefilm.de/kino/detail/corsage.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> and it was released in the United States on 23 December 2022,<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://variety.com/2022/film/global/ifc-films-cannes-corsage-1235335729/|title=IFC Films Sets U.S. Release Date for Cannes Breakout 'Corsage' (EXCLUSIVE)|magazine=Variety|first=Leo|last=Barraclough|date=9 August 2022|access-date=20 August 2022|archive-date=17 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221017174508/https://variety.com/2022/film/global/ifc-films-cannes-corsage-1235335729/|url-status=live}}</ref> in the United Kingdom on 26 December 2022,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://filmdistributorsassociation.com/release-schedule/past-present-and-future-releases/?filmSearch=Corsage|title=Corsage|publisher=Film Distributors Association|access-date=20 August 2022|archive-date=17 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221017174510/https://filmdistributorsassociation.com/release-schedule/past-present-and-future-releases/?filmSearch=Corsage|url-status=live}}</ref> and in France on 14 December 2022 by [[Ad Vitam (company)|Ad Vitam Distribution]].<ref name="advitam">{{cite web|url=https://www.advitamdistribution.com/films/corsage/|title=Corsage|publisher=[[Ad Vitam (company)|Ad Vitam Distribution]]|access-date=3 August 2022|archive-date=17 October Acclaimed section, where it was screened on 10 August 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://festivaldelima.com/2023/pelicula/corsage-la-emperatriz-rebelde/|title=Corsage: La emperatriz ==Reception==
===Critical reception===
On the [[review aggregator]] website [[Rotten Tomatoes]], 85% of 137 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 7.3/10. The website's consensus reads, "Corsage puts a refreshingly irreverent spin on period biopic formulas, further elevated by Vicky Krieps' terrific turn in the central role".<ref>{{Cite Rotten Tomatoes|id=corsage|type=m|title=Corsage|access-date=22 February 2023}}{{cbignore}}</ref> [[Metacritic]] assigned the film a [[Weighted arithmetic mean|weighted average score]] of 76 out of 100 based on 35 critics' reviews, indicating "generally favorable reviews".<ref>{{cite Metacritic|id=corsage|type=movie|title=Corsage|access-date=13 January 2023}}</ref>

===Box office===
The film grossed [[United States dollar|US$]]3.1 million worldwide.<ref name="bom"/> It was the third most-watched Austrian film of 2022 and sold a total of 57,394 tickets in Austria,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Österreichisches Kino 2000 – 2023 |trans-title=Austrian Cinema 2000 – 2023 |url=https://www.filmaustria.com/kino-charts |access-date=27 June 2023 |website=Film Austria |language=de |archive-date=26 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230626203109/https://www.filmaustria.com/kino-charts |url-status=live }}</ref> 47,501 tickets in Germany, 60,249 in France, 8,607 in Luxembourg, and a total of 348,948 tickets sold in Europe.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Corsage |url=https://lumiere.obs.coe.int/movie/330255 |access-date=27 June 2023 |website=Lumiere |publisher=[[European Audiovisual Observatory]] |archive-date=26 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230526105430/https://lumiere.obs.coe.int/movie/330255 |url-status=live }}</ref>
