==Themes and analysis==
{{quote box|width=40%|align=right|bgcolor=#c6dbf7|quote=[T]he structure of ''Inland Empire'' differs from prior Lynch films, ''[[Lost Highway (film)|Lost Highway]]'' or ''[[Mulholland Drive (film)|Mulholland Drive]]''. It is neither a [[Möbius strip]] that endlessly circles around itself, nor is it divisible into sections of fantasy and reality. Its structure is more akin to a web where individual moments hyperlink to each other and other [[David Lynch filmography|Lynch films]]—hence the musical number that closes the film which contains obvious allusions to everything from ''[[Blue Velvet (film)|Blue Velvet]]'' to ''[[Twin Peaks]]''.|source=Zoran Samardžija, 2010<ref>{{cite journal|last=Samardžija |first=Zoran |date=February 2010 |url=https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/scope/documents/2010/february-2010/samardzija.pdf |title=DavidLynch.com: Auteurship in the Age of the Internet and Digital Cinema |journal=Scope: An Online Journal of Film and Television Studies |number=16 |access-date=2023-01-12}}</ref>}}

When asked about ''Inland Empire'', Lynch refrained from explaining the film, responding that it is "about a woman in trouble, and it's a mystery, and that's all I want to say about it."<ref name="wfaa">{{cite news |work=[[Riverside Press-Enterprise]] |title=David Lynch turns his eye to 'Inland Empire' |first=Helene |last=Blatter |url=http://www.wfaa.com/sharedcontent/dws/ent/stories/090406dnGLempire.64579170.html |date=3 September 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070928045413/http://www.wfaa.com/sharedcontent/dws/ent/stories/090406dnGLempire.64579170.html |archive-date=28 September 2007}}</ref> When presenting screenings of the digital work, Lynch sometimes opened with a loosely-translated version of the ''[[Mundaka Upanishad]]'':

<blockquote>We are like the spider. We weave our life and then move along in it. We are like the dreamer who dreams and then lives in the dream. This is true for the entire universe.<ref>{{cite news |last=Guillen |first=Michael |date=24 January 2007 |title=Inland Empire—The San Rafael Film Center Q&A With David Lynch |work=[[Twitch Film]] |url=http://twitchfilm.net/archives/008819.html |access-date=21 April 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080907005745/http://www.twitchfilm.net/archives/008819.html |archive-date=7 September 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last1=Egenes |first1=Thomas |last2=Reddy |first2=Kumuda |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BcDlPTSbEoEC&pg=PA71 |title=Eternal Stories from the Upanishads |via=[[Google Books]] |location=[[New Delhi]] |publisher=Smrti Books |year=2002 |page=71 |isbn=978-8-18-796707-1}}</ref></blockquote>

Lynch's ''[[Darkened Room]]'' has been analyzed by Kristina Šekrst as a precursor to ''Inland Empire'', creating the Lost Girl motif, along with sharing the same symbolism of the cigarette-burn hole in a silk slip and the watch.<ref name=sekrst>{{cite book|last=Šekrst|first=Kristina|chapter=Narrativism and Performativity in Absurda and Darkened Room|editor=Andrew M. Winters|publisher=Lexington Books|year=2024|title=A Critical Companion to David Lynch|url=https://philarchive.org/rec/SEKNAP}}</ref> [[New York Film Festival]] official Richard Peña summarized the film as "a plotless collection of snippets that explore themes Lynch has been working on for years", including "a [[Hollywood (industry)|Hollywood]] story about a young actress who gets a part in a film that might be cursed; a story about the smuggling of women from [[Eastern Europe]]; and an abstract story about a family of people with rabbit heads sitting around in a [[living room]]."<ref name="wfaa"/> ''[[The Guardian]]'' critic [[Peter Bradshaw]] called the film "a meditation on the unacknowledged and unnoticed strangeness of Hollywood and [[movie making|movie-making]] in general", adding that Lynch "establishes a bizarre series of worm-holes between the worlds of myth, movies and reality."<ref>{{cite news|last=Bradshaw|first=Peter|author-link=Peter Bradshaw|title=Inland Empire – Film Review|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2007/mar/09/thriller|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=25 February 2018|date=2007-03-09}}</ref> Critic [[Mark Fisher (theorist)|Mark Fisher]] wrote that the film "often seems like a series of [[dream sequence]]s floating free of any grounding reality, a dream without a dreamer [in which] no frame is secure", but argued that "it is the ''film'' that is mad, not the characters in it&nbsp;... it is Hollywood itself that is dreaming".<ref name="fisher">{{cite book|last=Fisher|first=Mark|author-link=Mark Fisher (theorist)|title=The Weird and the Eerie|date=2017|publisher=Repeater Books|url=http://k-punk.abstractdynamics.org/archives/009285.html|access-date=27 February 2018|isbn=978-1-91-092438-9}}</ref> He also commented that "to see Lynch's worlds captured on digital video makes for a bizarre short-circuiting: as if we are witnessing a direct feed from the unconscious".<ref name="fisher"/>

[[Dennis Lim (film curator)|Dennis Lim]] of ''[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]]'' described the film as "a three-hour waking nightmare that derives both its form and its content from the splintering psyche of a troubled Hollywood actress", and commented on Lynch's use of digital video, describing it as "the medium of [[home movie]]s, [[viral video]], and [[pornography]]—the everyday media detritus we associate more with&nbsp;... intimate or private viewing experiences than communal ones", adding that the film "progresses with the darting, associative logic of [[hyperlink]]s".<ref name=Slate>{{cite journal|last=Lim|first=Dennis|author-link=Dennis Lim (film curator)|title=David Lynch Goes Digital: Inland Empire on DVD|url=http://www.slate.com/articles/arts/dvdextras/2007/08/david_lynch_goes_digital.html|journal=[[Slate Magazine]]|access-date=25 February 2018|date=2007-08-23}}</ref> Scholar Anne Jerslev has argued that the film "constitutes multiple and fractured modes of perception in a world of digital screens".<ref name=jerslev/> Jerslev further contends that the film features "formal similarities with a [[website]]'s hyperlinked layering of screens/windows, constantly disclosing new worlds from new points of view", but according to theorist [[Steven Shaviro]] "it also builds on cinematic codes, even as it [[deconstruction|deconstructs]] them".<ref name=jerslev>{{cite journal|last=Jerslev|first=Anne|title=The post-perspectival: screens and time in David Lynch's Inland Empire|journal=Journal of Aesthetics & Culture|date=21 March 2012|volume=4|issue=1|article-number=17298|doi=10.3402/jac.v4i0.17298|doi-access=free}}</ref>

David Sweeney interprets ''Inland Empire'' as a film that is, at least thematically, about [[reincarnation]]. He connects this theme to Lynch's interest in [[Theosophy]] and draws parallels with [[James Joyce]]'s ''[[Ulysses (novel)|Ulysses]]'' and the [[Netflix]] series ''[[The OA]]'', highlighting shared motifs of reincarnation and alternate lives.<ref name=sweeney>{{cite book|last=Sweeney|first=David|chapter=Past and Possible Lives in Inland Empire|editor=Andrew M. Winters|publisher=[[Lexington Books]]|year=2024|title=A Critical Companion to David Lynch|isbn=978-1-66692-8105}}</ref>

The ''[[Austin Chronicle]]''<nowiki/>'s Marc Savlov wrote that ''Inland Empire'' "revels in a kind of [[post-9/11]] [[dissociative disorder]] as perpetual panic attack".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Savlov |first=Marc |date=2009-12-25 |title=A Decade Under the Influence |url=https://www.austinchronicle.com/screens/2009-12-25/931434/ |access-date=2025-02-05 |website=[[Austin Chronicle]] |language=en-US}}</ref> During an interview about ''[[Lost Highway (film)|Lost Highway]]'' (1997), Lynch was asked about whether he "ever had that feeling of [[Dissociation (psychology)|dissociation]] from yourself". He responded, "Oh, yeah. There's really many characters inside of us".<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Powell |first=Jeremy |date=2014 |title=David Lynch, Francis Bacon, Gilles Deleuze: The Cinematic Diagram and the Hall of Time |journal=Discourse |publisher=[[Project Muse]] |volume=36 |issue=3 |page=325 |doi=10.13110/discourse.36.3.0309 |jstor=10.13110/discourse.36.3.0309 |issn=1522-5321}}</ref>

==Production==
===Background===
''Inland Empire'' was the first Lynch feature to be completely shot in [[digital video]]; it was shot in [[Standard-definition television|standard definition]] with a hand-held [[Sony DSR-PD150]] by Lynch himself.<ref name=Perez/><ref>{{Cite web |last=Seibold |first=Witney |date=2022-11-13 |title=Why David Lynch Chose To Shoot Inland Empire Digitally |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1093854/why-david-lynch-chose-to-shoot-inland-empire-digitally/ |access-date=2023-01-12 |website=[[/Film]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Lynch stated that he would no longer use film to make motion pictures.<ref name=variety>{{cite news |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |first=Adam |last=Dawtrey |date=11 May 2005 |url=https://variety.com/2005/film/markets-festivals/lynch-invades-an-empire-1117922566/ |title=Lynch invades an 'Empire'; Digital pic details a mystery |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110015512/http://variety.com/2005/film/news/lynch-invades-an-empire-1117922566/ |archive-date=10 January 2014}}</ref> He explained his preference, stating that the medium gives one "more room to dream", and more options in post-production.<ref name=Slate/> Much of the project was shot in [[Łódź]], Poland, with local actors, such as [[Karolina Gruszka]], [[Krzysztof Majchrzak]], [[Leon Niemczyk]], Piotr Andrzejewski and artists of the local circus Cyrk Zalewski. Some filming was also done in [[Los Angeles]], and Lynch returned from Poland in 2006 to complete it. He then edited the final results in [[Final Cut Pro]] in his home office over a six-month period.<ref name="post">{{cite web |last=Blair |first=Ian |date=February 1, 2007 |title=Director's Chair: David Lynch – 'Inland Empire' |url=http://www.postmagazine.com/Publications/Post-Magazine/2007/February-1-2007/DIRECTORS-CHAIR-DAVID-LYNCH-INLAND-EMPIRE.aspx |access-date=19 March 2018 |website=[[Post Magazine]]}}</ref> He edited the film alone without input from his then-wife [[Mary Sweeney]], who often edited his films, which she attributed to the lack of "a real organized script to go by [...] no one knew what was going on except him".<ref name="post"/>

Lynch shot the film without a complete screenplay. Instead, he handed each actor several pages of freshly written dialogue each day.<ref name="grf4"/><ref name=Perez/> In a 2005 interview, he described his feelings about the shooting process:
"I've never worked on a project in this way before. I don't know exactly how this thing will finally unfold&nbsp;... This film is very different because I don't have a script. I write the thing scene by scene and much of it is shot and I don't have much of a clue where it will end. It's a risk, but I have this feeling that because all things are unified, this idea over here in that room will somehow relate to that idea over there in the pink room."<ref name="hwise">{{cite news |last1=Attwood |first1=Chris |last2=Roth |first2=Robert |date=September 2005 |title=A Dog's Trip to the Chocolate Shop – David Lynch |work=Healthy Wealthy N' Wise |url=http://www.healthywealthynwise.com/article.asp?Article=3062 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051201160734/http://www.healthywealthynwise.com/article.asp?Article=3062 |archive-date=2005-12-01}}</ref>

Interviewed at the [[63rd Venice International Film Festival|Venice Film Festival]], Laura Dern admitted that she did not know what ''Inland Empire'' was about or the role she was playing, but hoped that seeing the film's premiere at the festival would help her "learn more".<ref name="grf4"/> Justin Theroux also stated, "I couldn't possibly tell you what the film's about, and at this point, I don't know that [David Lynch] could. It's become sort of a pastime—Laura and I sit around on set trying to figure out what's going on."<ref name="wfaa"/> In an [[NPR]] interview, Dern recounted a conversation she had with Jeremy Alter, one of the film's newer producers; he had asked her if Lynch was joking when he requested a one-legged woman, a monkey, and a lumberjack by 3:15 p.m. Dern replied, "Yeah, you're on a David Lynch movie, dude. Sit back and enjoy the ride." They began filming with the individuals Lynch had requested by 4 p.m.<ref name="npr">{{cite web |website=[[NPR]] |first=Andrea |last=Shea |date=17 December 2006 |url=https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=6637676 |title=David Lynch's Latest Endeavor Breaks New Ground}}</ref>

===Financing and distribution===
Lynch financed much of the production from his own resources, with longtime artistic collaborator and ex-wife Mary Sweeney producing. The film was also partially financed by the French production company [[StudioCanal]], which had provided funding for three previous Lynch films. StudioCanal wanted to enter the film in the [[2006 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web |title=David Lynch continues work on DV project Inland Empire |url=https://movieweb.com/david-lynch-continues-work-on-dv-project-inland-empire/ |date=May 12, 2005 |url-status=live |website=[[MovieWeb]] |access-date=2023-01-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210512120141/https://movieweb.com/david-lynch-continues-work-on-dv-project-inland-empire/ |archive-date=2021-05-12}}</ref> Instead, it premiered at Italy's [[63rd Venice International Film Festival|Venice Film Festival]] on 6 September 2006, where David Lynch also received the [[Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement]] award for his "contributions to the art of cinema". The film premiered in the United States on 8 October 2006 at the [[New York Film Festival]].<ref name="NYFF">{{cite web |date=November 15, 2006 |title=David Lynch Announces Distribution Partnerships and Theatrical Release Dates for Inland Empire |url=http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/david-lynch-announces-distribution-partnerships-and-theatrical-release-dates-for-inland-empire-56396397.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304215520/http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/david-lynch-announces-distribution-partnerships-and-theatrical-release-dates-for-inland-empire-56396397.html |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |access-date=28 July 2015 |website=[[PR Newswire]]}}</ref> The film received a limited release in the US beginning on 15 December 2006; distribution was handled by the specialist company 518 Media.<ref>{{cite web |title=Inland Empire release details |url=http://www.comingsoon.net/films.php?id=17007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181106010541/https://www.comingsoon.net/movie/inland-empire-2006 |archive-date=November 6, 2018 |website=[[ComingSoon.net]]}}</ref>

Lynch hoped to distribute the film independently, saying that with the entire industry changing, he thought he would attempt a new form of distribution as well.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2006-10-10 |title=David Lynch to Self-Distribute Inland Empire |url=https://movieweb.com/david-lynch-to-self-distribute-inland-empire/ |access-date=2023-01-12 |website=[[MovieWeb]] |language=en}}</ref> He acquired the rights to the DVD and worked out a deal with StudioCanal in an arrangement that allowed him to distribute the film himself, through both digital and traditional means.<ref>{{cite web |last=Goldstein |first=Gregg |date=11 October 2006 |title=Filmmaker Lynch to self-distribute 'Inland Empire' |url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/hr/search/article_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1003223922 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070922171752/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/hr/search/article_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1003223922 |archive-date=2007-09-22 |access-date=2023-01-12 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref> A North American DVD release occurred on 14 August 2007. Among other special features, the DVD included a 75-minute featurette, ''More Things That Happened'', which compiled footage elaborating on Sue's marriage to Smithy, her unpleasant life story, the Phantom's influence on women, and the lives of the prostitutes on Hollywood Boulevard. 15 years after the North American DVD release, [[The Criterion Collection]] released a two-disc Blu-ray on 21 March 2023.<ref name="DVDbeaver">{{cite web |last1=Tooze |first1=Gary |title=Inland Empire Blu-ray - Laura Dern |url=http://www.dvdbeaver.com/film2/DVDReviews32/inland_empire.htm |website=DVDbeaver |access-date=24 February 2025}}</ref>

==Release and reception==
===Distribution and box office===
The film was screened at several film festivals around the world, most notably the [[Venice Film Festival]], the [[New York Film Festival]], the [[Thessaloniki Film Festival]], the [[Camerimage|Camerimage Film Festival]], the [[Fajr International Film Festival]], the [[San Francisco Independent Film Festival|San Francisco IndieFest]], the [[International Film Festival Rotterdam]] and the [[Festival Internacional de Cine Contemporáneo de la Ciudad de México|Mexico City International Contemporary Film Festival]].

In October 2006, Lynch bought US distribution rights to the film from StudioCanal, which he would retain in any later deals made. The following month, he announced his intent to self-distribute the film theatrically via his company Absurda and 518 Media, stating: "A conventional distributor is a heartache, and I'm finished with that. With self-distribution, I'm able to shape the outcome of the film so much more." Lynch embarked on a 10-city promotional tour in January 2007 with a cow, explaining "I ate a lot of cheese during the film, and it made me happy. I'm looking forward to meeting theater owners and getting out among the people with the cow." Lynch signed a service deal with [[Rhino Entertainment]], which distributed the film on home video with [[Rykodisc|Ryko Distribution]] on 14 August 2007.<ref name="RYKO">{{cite web |title=Inland Empire |url=http://www.rykodistribution.com/artist_title.php?artist_id=10825&media_id=20361 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070516221854/http://www.rykodistribution.com/artist_title.php?artist_id=10825&media_id=20361 |archive-date=16 May 2007 |website=[[Rykodisc|Ryko Distribution]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Lynch set to self-release 'Empire'|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|first=Gregg|last=Goldstein|date=16 November 2006|access-date=2 December 2023|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/lynch-set-release-empire-143369/}}</ref>

518 Media released ''Inland Empire'' to two theaters in the [[Cinema of the United States|United States]] on 6 December 2006, grossing a total of $27,508 over its opening weekend. It later expanded to its widest release of fifteen nationwide theaters, ultimately grossing $861,355 at the American box office. In other countries outside the United States, ''Inland Empire'' grossed $3,176,222, bringing the film's worldwide total gross to $4,037,577.<ref name=boxofficemojo/> It was released on 20 August 2007 in the [[Cinema of the United Kingdom|United Kingdom]], by [[StudioCanal UK|Optimum Releasing]],<ref name=Play.com>{{cite web |url=http://www.play.com/DVD/DVD/4-/3229343/-/Product.html?searchstring=inland+empire&searchsource=0 |title=Play.com – Buy Inland Empire |website=[[Play.com]] |access-date=13 August 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110521152214/http://www.play.com/DVD/DVD/4-/3229343/-/Product.html?searchstring=inland+empire&searchsource=0 |archive-date=21 May 2011}}</ref> 4 October 2007 in the Benelux, by [[A-Film]],<ref name="A-Film">{{cite web|url=http://www.a-film.be/dvd.php?id=00015231 |website=[[A-Film]] |title=Details of BE & NL DVD release |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929084421/http://www.a-film.be/dvd.php?id=00015231 |archive-date=29 September 2007}}</ref> and 6 August 2008 in [[Cinema of Australia|Australia]], by [[Madman Entertainment]].<ref name="Madman">{{cite web |title=Inland Empire |url=http://www.madman.com.au/actions/catalogue.do?releaseId=8532&method=view |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121231013516/http://www.madman.com.au/actions/catalogue.do?releaseId=8532&method=view |archive-date=2012-12-31 |access-date=13 August 2012 |website=[[Madman Entertainment]]}}</ref>

===Critical response===
On [[review aggregator]] [[Rotten Tomatoes]], 72% of 118 critics gave the film a positive review, with an average rating of 7.6/10. The website's critical consensus reads: "Typical David Lynch fare: fans of the director will find ''Inland Empire'' seductive and deep. All others will consider the heady surrealism impenetrable and pointless."<ref name="Rotten Tomatoes" /> On [[Metacritic]], the film has a weighted average score of 73 out of 100, based on 25 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.metacritic.com/movie/inland-empire|title=Inland Empire – Reviews, Ratings, Credits and More|website=[[Metacritic]]|access-date=5 May 2020}}</ref>

[[Manohla Dargis]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' classified ''Inland Empire'' as "fitfully brilliant" after the New York Film Festival screening.<ref>{{cite news |last=Dargis |first=Manohla |date=2006-10-06 |title=At the New York Film Festival, a Global Glimpse of the State of the Cinema |language=en-US |work=[[The New York Times]] |url-access=subscription |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/10/06/movies/06fest.html |access-date=2023-01-12 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> [[Peter Travers]], the film critic for ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' magazine wrote, "My advice, in the face of such hallucinatory brilliance, is that you hang on."<ref name=rs>{{cite magazine |title=Inland Empire Review |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/reviews/movie/11692273/review/12626084/inland_empire |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061208184344/http://www.rollingstone.com/reviews/movie/11692273/review/12626084/inland_empire |archive-date=8 December 2006 |first=Peter |last=Travers |author-link=Peter Travers |date=21 November 2006 |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |access-date=6 August 2012}}</ref> ''[[The New Yorker]]'' was one of the few publications to offer any negative points about the film, calling it a "trenchant, nuanced film" that "quickly devolves into self-parody".<ref>{{cite news |last=Brody |first=Richard |date=11 December 2006 |title=Inland Empire: The Film File |newspaper=[[The New Yorker]] |url=http://www.newyorker.com/arts/reviews/film/inland_empire_lynch |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080307053736/http://www.newyorker.com/arts/reviews/film/inland_empire_lynch |archive-date=March 7, 2008}}</ref> [[Jonathan Ross (television presenter)|Jonathan Ross]], presenter of the [[BBC]] programme ''[[Film 2007]]'', described it as "a work of genius&nbsp;... I think".<ref name=Film2007>{{Cite episode |title=Inland Empire review |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rIT6KiVtDRM |access-date=2023-01-12 |series=[[Film... (TV programme)#Jonathan Ross (1999–2010)|Film 2007]] |first=Jonathan |last=Ross |author-link=Jonathan Ross (television presenter) |network=[[BBC One]] |date=2007-05-05}}</ref> Damon Wise of ''[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]]'' magazine gave it five stars, calling it "A dazzling and exquisitely original riddle as told by an enigma"<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Wise |first=Damon |date=2007-02-23 |title=Inland Empire |url=https://www.empireonline.com/movies/reviews/inland-empire-review/ |access-date=2023-01-12 |magazine=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]]}}</ref> and Jim Emerson (editor of [[RogerEbert.com]]) gave it 4 stars out of 4: "When people say ''Inland Empire'' is Lynch's ''[[Sunset Boulevard (film)|Sunset Boulevard]]'', Lynch's ''[[Persona (1966 film)|Persona]]'' or Lynch's ''[[8½]]'', they're quite right, but it also explicitly invokes connections to [[Stanley Kubrick]]'s ''[[The Shining (film)|The Shining]]'', [[Jean-Luc Godard]]'s ''[[Pierrot le Fou]]'', [[Luis Buñuel|Buñuel]] and [[Salvador Dalí|Dalí]]{{hsp|'s}} ''[[Un Chien Andalou]]'', [[Maya Deren]]'s LA-experimental ''[[Meshes of the Afternoon]]'' (a Lynch favorite) and others".<ref>{{cite news |last=Emerson |first=Jim |date=25 January 2007 |title=Go Inland, young woman! |work=[[RogerEbert.com]] |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/inland-empire-2007 |access-date=2023-01-12}}</ref> However, Carina Chocano of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' wrote that "the film, which begins promisingly, disappears down so many rabbit holes (one of them involving actual rabbits) that eventually it just disappears for good".<ref name="LATimes">{{cite news |last=Chocano |first=Carina |date=15 December 2006 |title=Inland Empire |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |url=http://www.calendarlive.com/movies/reviews/cl-et-inland15dec15,0,3659742.story |access-date=6 August 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061218135317/http://www.calendarlive.com/movies/reviews/cl-et-inland15dec15,0,3659742.story |archive-date=2006-12-18}}</ref>

''Inland Empire'' tied the second-best film of 2007 by ''[[Cahiers du Cinéma]]''<ref name=caltech/> and was listed among ''[[Sight & Sound]]''{{'}}s films of the decade,<ref name=BFI/> as well as ''[[The Guardian]]''{{'}}s "10 most underrated movies of the decade".<ref name=guardian/> In 2025, it was one of the films voted for the "Readers' Choice" edition of ''[[The New York Times]]''{{'}} list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century," finishing at number 164.<ref>{{cite web |title=Readers Choose Their Top Movies of the 21st Century |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/movies/readers-movies-21st-century.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |date=2 July 2025 |access-date=2 July 2025}}</ref> In ''[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]]''<nowiki/>'s 2025 list of "101 Best Movie Performances of the 21st Century", Dern was placed 19th.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-08-25 |title=The 101 Best Movie Performances of the 21st Century |url=https://www.theringer.com/2025/08/25/movies/101-best-movie-acting-performances-since-2000-21st-century |access-date=2025-08-29 |website=[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Legacy===
''Inland Empire'' has been named as an example of the [[Liminal space (aesthetic)|liminal space aesthetic]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=McQueen’s subverted domestic bliss |url=https://hero-magazine.com//shows/mcqueens-subverted-domestic-bliss |access-date=2026-04-01 |website=Hero |language=en}}</ref> with [[Owen Gleiberman]] of [[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] citing the film as a progenitor to the 2026 psychological horror film ''[[Backrooms (film)|Backrooms]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gleiberman |first=Owen |date=2026-05-27 |title=‘Backrooms’ Review: Experimental Horror Comes Out of the Margins in Kane Parsons’ YouTube-Gone-A24 Head Trip |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/reviews/backrooms-review-chiwetel-ejiofor-kane-parsons-1236758845/ |access-date=2026-05-29 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

''Inland Empire'' also served as an influence to the [[analog horror]] [[web series]] known as ''[[Petscop]]''.<ref name="NTR">{{cite web|last=Peters|first=Lucia|title=The Weird Part Of YouTube: The Making Of "''No Through Road''" And The Power Of Unanswered Questions|url=https://theghostinmymachine.com/2020/11/16/the-weird-part-of-youtube-the-making-of-no-through-road-and-the-power-of-unanswered-questions-found-footage-stevenage-broomhill-farm-time-loop|website=The Ghost in My Machine|access-date=November 16, 2020|date=November 16, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116175053/https://theghostinmymachine.com/2020/11/16/the-weird-part-of-youtube-the-making-of-no-through-road-and-the-power-of-unanswered-questions-found-footage-stevenage-broomhill-farm-time-loop/|archive-date=November 16, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://egmnow.com/theres-something-hiding-in-petscop/ |title=There's Something Hiding in Petscop |last=Moyer |first=Philip |date=March 18, 2020 |magazine=[[Electronic Gaming Monthly]] |publisher=EGM Media LLC |access-date=January 26, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-01-23 |title=Behind the Music of "Petscop," The Cursed Video Game That Never Was |url=https://daily.bandcamp.com/features/petscop-soundtrack-interview |access-date=2024-07-28 |website=[[Bandcamp Daily]]}}</ref> In addition, the film inspired numerous horror works including a short film-turned-web series ''[[No Through Road (web series)|No Through Road]]''.<ref name="NTR" />

The name "Inland Empire" is used in the 2019 detective video game ''[[Disco Elysium]]'' to describe a skill used by the protagonist.

===Restoration===
''Inland Empire'' was restored and remastered by [[Janus Films]] in 2022, and was screened throughout the year beginning on April 8.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pak |first1=J. P. |last2=Zufelt |first2=Sebastian |date=2022-04-12 |title=Review: David Lynch embraces the digital age in 'Inland Empire' |url=https://nyunews.com/arts/film/2022/04/12/inland-empire-review/ |access-date=2023-01-12 |newspaper=[[Washington Square News]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Screening Schedule |url=https://inlandempire.official.film/screening-schedule |website=Inland Empire official |access-date=12 January 2023 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220406215659/https://inlandempire.official.film/screening-schedule |archive-date=April 6, 2022}}</ref> The restoration of the film and soundtrack was overseen by David Lynch.<ref name=Perez>{{cite web|url=https://theplaylist.net/inland-empire-restoration-trailer-david-lynch-april-20220324/|title='Inland Empire' Restoration Trailer: David Lynch's Surreal DV Nightmare Comes Back To Theaters In April|last=Perez|first=Rodrigo|website=ThePlaylist.net|date=March 24, 2022|access-date=April 1, 2022|language=en}}</ref> For the restoration the original upscaled HD footage from the editing process was first downscaled back to [[Standard-definition television|standard definition]] to discard "false detail", then converted to [[4K resolution|4K]] using an AI upscaling algorithm.<ref name="janus">{{Cite web |title=Inland Empire Remastering Note |url=https://s3.amazonaws.com/criterion-production/janus_promo_packages/687-/InlandEmpire_RemasterNote_web_original.pdf |access-date=2022-04-08 |website=[[Janus Films]]}}</ref> This version of the film was released on Blu-Ray by [[The Criterion Collection]].<ref name="DVDbeaver"/>

===Accolades===
Lynch attempted to promote Dern's performance and increase her chances of scoring nomination for the [[79th Academy Awards|2007]] [[Academy Award for Best Actress]] by campaigning with a live cow,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2006/scene/awards/lynch-cow-campaign-for-oscar-1117954009/|website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |title=Lynch, cow campaign for Oscar; Helmer touts 'Inland Empire' thesp Dern, cheese |first=Alex |last=Romanelli |date=15 November 2006 |access-date=6 August 2012}}</ref> though she was ultimately not recognized by the members of the [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences|Academy]].<ref>{{cite episode |title=David Lynch interview - Inland Empire Review |series=[[Film 2007]] |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rIT6KiVtDRM |access-date=12 January 2023 |date=March 7, 2007 |time=3m22s |via=YouTube}}</ref>

WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: List of highest-grossing Indian films
======================================================================

{{Short description|None}}
{{About|the highest-grossing films made in India|the highest-grossing films in the box office territory of India|List of highest-grossing films in India}}
{{pp-semi-indef|small=yes}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=May 2026}}
{{Use Indian English|date=May 2026}}

This ranking lists the '''highest-grossing Indian films''' produced by [[Cinema of India|Indian cinema]], based on conservative global [[box office]] estimates as reported by organisations classified as green by Wikipedia.{{efn|See [[WP:RSP]], [[WP:ICTFSOURCES]]}} The figures are not adjusted for inflation. However, there is no official tracking of figures and sources publishing data are frequently pressured to increase their estimates.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gupta |first=Priya |date=23 November 2013 |title=Box Office column discontinued |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/bollywood/news-interviews/Box-Office-column-discontinued/articleshow/26211585.cms |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131126160700/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2013-11-23/news-interviews/44388852_1_weekend-numbers-box-office-numbers-small-films |archive-date=26 November 2013 |access-date=30 December 2013 |work=[[The Times of India]]}}</ref>

== Overview ==
Indian films have been screened in [[List of highest-grossing Indian films in overseas markets|markets around the world]] since the early 20th century.<ref name="burra">Burra, Rani Day & Rao, Maithili (2006), "Cinema", ''Encyclopedia of India (vol. 1)'', Thomson Gale, {{ISBN|978-0-684-31350-4}}.</ref> Since 2003, there are markets in over 90 countries where films from [[India]] are screened.<ref>Khanna, Amit (2003), "The Future of Hindi Film Business", ''Encyclopaedia of Hindi Cinema: historical record, the business and its future, narrative forms, analysis of the medium, milestones, biographies'', Encyclopædia Britannica (India) Private Limited, {{ISBN|978-81-7991-066-5}}. p 158</ref> During the first decade of the 21st century, there was a steady rise in the ticket price, a tripling in the number of theatres and an increase in the number of prints of a film being released, which led to a large increase in the box office collections.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Prabhakar |first=Binoy |date=26 August 2012 |title=Business of Rs 100-cr films: Who gets what and why |url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2012-08-26/news/33386102_1_box-office-movie-rotten-tomatoes |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140111054228/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2012-08-26/news/33386102_1_box-office-movie-rotten-tomatoes |archive-date=11 January 2014 |access-date=30 December 2013 |work=The Economic Times}}</ref>

As of 2014, [[Hindi cinema]] represents 43% of the net box office revenue in India, while [[Telugu cinema|Telugu]] and [[Tamil cinema]] represent 36%, and other industries constitute 21%.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Digital March Media & Entertainment in South India |url=http://www2.deloitte.com/content/dam/Deloitte/in/Documents/technology-media-telecommunications/in-tmt-economic-contribution-of-motion-picture-and-television-industry-noexp.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160114100635/http://www2.deloitte.com/content/dam/Deloitte/in/Documents/technology-media-telecommunications/in-tmt-economic-contribution-of-motion-picture-and-television-industry-noexp.pdf |archive-date=14 January 2016 |access-date=21 April 2014 |publisher=Deloitte}}</ref> As of 2020, the combined revenue of all other language film industries has surpassed that of the Hindi film industry.<ref>{{Cite news |date=11 July 2020 |title=India Box Office collections: Regional cinema led by Telugu, Tamil movies overtakes Bollywood |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/entertainment/bollywoods-big-but-regional-cinema-is-also-raking-in-the-moolah/2020134/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210509124218/https://www.financialexpress.com/entertainment/bollywoods-big-but-regional-cinema-is-also-raking-in-the-moolah/2020134/ |archive-date=9 May 2021 |access-date=9 May 2021 |work=The Financial Express}}</ref> By 2021, Telugu cinema became the largest film industry of India in terms of box-office.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 January 2022 |title=Tollywood {{!}} ఆ విషయంలో బాలీవుడ్‌ను వెనక్కి నెట్టేసిన టాలీవుడ్.. |url=https://www.ntnews.com/cinema/in-this-year-tollywood-surpassed-bollywood-with-collections-at-box-office-391576 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230718085356/https://www.ntnews.com/cinema/in-this-year-tollywood-surpassed-bollywood-with-collections-at-box-office-391576 |archive-date=18 July 2023 |access-date=20 January 2022 |website=Namasthe Telangana |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=S |first=Srivatsan |date=7 January 2022 |title=The 'pan-Indian' strategy of Telugu cinema |url=https://www.thehindu.com/entertainment/movies/the-pan-indian-strategy-of-telugu-cinema/article38163523.ece |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220110140529/https://www.thehindu.com/entertainment/movies/the-pan-indian-strategy-of-telugu-cinema/article38163523.ece |archive-date=10 January 2022 |access-date=20 January 2022 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last1=Mukherjee |first1=Nairita |last2=Joshi |first2=Tushar |date=22 December 2021 |title=Is South cinema the new Bollywood? |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/movies/regional-cinema/story/is-south-cinema-the-new-bollywood-1890835-2021-12-22 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211227133826/https://www.indiatoday.in/movies/regional-cinema/story/is-south-cinema-the-new-bollywood-1890835-2021-12-22 |archive-date=27 December 2021 |access-date=20 January 2022 |magazine=India Today}}</ref> In 2023, the Hindi film industry accounted for 44% of box office revenue, followed by the Telugu industry at 19% and the Tamil industry at 16%. The [[Kannada cinema|Kannada]] (5%), [[Malayalam cinema|Malayalam]] (3%), [[Cinema of West Bengal|Bengali]], [[Marathi cinema|Marathi]], [[Cinema of Odisha|Odia]], [[Punjabi cinema|Punjabi]], [[Gujarati cinema|Gujarati]] and [[Bhojpuri cinema|Bhojpuri]] industries contributed to the remainder, while the foreign film industry made up 9% of the total revenue.<ref>{{Cite web |title=India – box office distribution by language 2023 |url=https://www.statista.com/statistics/948615/india-regional-box-office-contribution-by-language/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210528201448/https://www.statista.com/statistics/948615/india-regional-box-office-contribution-by-language/ |archive-date=28 May 2021 |access-date=9 May 2021 |website=Statista |language=en}}</ref> In 2024, the Hindi and the Telugu film industries accounted for 40% and 20% of the domestic gross box office revenue respectively, followed by Tamil with 15% share and Malayalam with 10% share.<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 January 2025 |title=The Ormax Box Office 2024 Report |url=https://www.ormaxmedia.com/insights/stories/the-ormax-box-office-2024-report.html |access-date=8 July 2025 |website=Ormax Media Pvt. Ltd. |language=en}}</ref>

== Highest-grossing films by language ==
[[Cinema of West Bengal]] was the center of Indian cinema in the 1930s,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sarkar |first=Bhaskar |year=2008 |title=The Melodramas of Globalization |journal=Cultural Dynamics |volume=20 |pages=31–51 [34] |doi=10.1177/0921374007088054 |issn=0921-3740 |s2cid=143977618}}</ref> and accounted for a quarter of India's film output in the 1950s.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 2014 |title=Pather Panchali: Its history, the genius behind it, and Satyajit Rays style of working |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/society-and-the-arts/films/story/19800331-pather-panchali-its-history-the-genius-behind-it-and-satyajit-rays-style-of-working-806531-2014-02-01 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170614231838/http://indiatoday.intoday.in/story/pather-panchali-its-history-the-genius-behind-it-and-satyajit-rays-style-of-working/1/409539.html |archive-date=14 June 2017 |access-date=30 June 2017}}</ref> [[Cinema of South India|Cinema in South India]] accounted for nearly half of India's cinema halls in the 1940s.<ref name="burra" />

=== Hindi ===
<!-- Note: When contributing to this page, please ensure that all references used for ranking are from green sources as specified in [[WP:ICTFSOURCES]] or [[WP:RSPSS]]. [[Hindi cinema]] is a part of Indian cinema based in [[Mumbai]], [[Maharashtra]].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Gulzar |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8y8vN9A14nkC |title=Encyclopaedia of Hindi Cinema |last2=Nihalani, Govind |last3=Chatterji, Saibal |publisher=Encyclopædia Britannica (India) Pvt Ltd. |year=2003 |isbn=81-7991-066-0 |pages=10–18 |access-date=15 October 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190405040645/https://books.google.com/books?id=8y8vN9A14nkC |archive-date=5 April 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref> The films are made primarily in the [[Hindi]]-language.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Pippa de Bruyn |url=https://archive.org/details/frommersindia0000debr/page/579 |title=Frommer's India |last2=Niloufer Venkatraman |last3=Keith Bain |publisher=Frommer's |year=2006 |isbn=0-471-79434-1 |page=[https://archive.org/details/frommersindia0000debr/page/579 579]}}</ref> It is often known as Bollywood and is one of the largest film producers in India as well as a major centre of film production worldwide.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Wasko, Janet |title=How Hollywood works |publisher=SAGE |year=2003 |isbn=0-7619-6814-8 |page=185}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=K. === Meitei ===
[[Meitei cinema]], also known as ''Maniwood'', is a part of Indian cinema, dedicated to the production of films in [[Meitei language]], officially known as [[Manipuri language]], and is based in [[Imphal]], the capital city of [[Manipur]] state of [[Northeast India]]. [[Boong]] became the first film in the industry, to cross the box office of 1 crore INR.<ref name=":Boong_1_Crore">{{Cite news |title=Farhan Akhtar-Backed <i>Boong</i> Becomes First Manipuri Film To Cross Rs 1 Crore At Box Office |url=https://www.ndtv.com/entertainment/lakshmipriya-devis-boong-emerges-as-first-manipuri-film-to-earn-over-rs-1-crore-at-box-office-11218286 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260316055405/https://www.ndtv.com/entertainment/lakshmipriya-devis-boong-emerges-as-first-manipuri-film-to-earn-over-rs-1-crore-at-box-office-11218286 |archive-date=2026-03-16 |access-date=2026-06-23 |work=NDTV |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-03-15 |title=Lakshmipriya Devis Boong emerges as first Manipuri film to earn over Rs 1 crore at box office |url=https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/entertainment/lakshmipriya-devis-boong-emerges-as-first-manipuri-film-to-earn-over-rs-1-crore-at-box-office/ |access-date=2026-06-23 |website=The Tribune |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tribune |first=The Assam |date=2026-03-16 |title=BAFTA-winning ‘Boong’ becomes first Manipuri film to cross Rs 1 Cr on re-release |url=https://assamtribune.com/north-east/bafta-winning-boong-becomes-first-manipuri-film-to-cross-rs-1-cr-on-re-release-1609491 |access-date=2026-06-23 |website=assamtribune.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=BAFTA-Winner ‘Boong’ Becomes First Manipuri Film to Cross ₹1 Crore at Box Office |url=https://guwahatiplus.com/northeast/bafta-winner-boong-becomes-first-manipuri-film-to-cross-rs1-crore-at-box-office |access-date=2026-06-23 |website=guwahatiplus.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Highest-grossing franchises ==
<!-- Note: When contributing to this page, please ensure that all references used for ranking are from green sources as specified in [[WP:ICTFSOURCES]] or [[WP:RSPSS]]. It is crucial to verify that the references do not originate from unreliable sources, in accordance with [[WP:FRUIT]].-->The ''[[Khiladi (franchise)|Khiladi]]'' franchise was the first film franchise to gross over [[100 Crore Club|{{INR}}100{{nbsp}}crore]]. The ''[[Baahubali (franchise)|Baahubali]]'' is the first franchise to collect over [[1000 Crore Club|{{INR}}1,000{{nbsp}}crore]] at the box office, the ''[[Dhurandhar Duology]]'' is the only franchise where all the films have grossed at least {{INR}}1,000{{nbsp}}crore worldwide.

'''''Megalopolis'''''{{efn|Also referred to as '''''Francis Ford Coppola's Megalopolis: A Fable'''''<ref name="Chang">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2024/05/27/megalopolis-movie-review-francis-ford-coppola |title=The Madly Captivating Urban Sprawl of Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' |last=Chang |first=Justin |author-link=Justin Chang |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |date=May 16, 2024 |access-date=July 8, 2024 |url-access=limited |archive-date=July 8, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240708235944/https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2024/05/27/megalopolis-movie-review-francis-ford-coppola |url-status=live}}</ref>}} is a 2024 American [[Epic film|epic]] [[Science fiction film|science fiction]] [[Drama (film and television)|drama film]] written, directed, and produced by [[Francis Ford Coppola]]. The film features an [[ensemble cast]] including [[Adam Driver]], [[Giancarlo Esposito]], [[Nathalie Emmanuel]], [[Aubrey Plaza]], [[Shia LaBeouf]], [[Jon Voight]], [[Laurence Fishburne]], [[Talia Shire]], [[Jason Schwartzman]], [[Kathryn Hunter]], [[Grace VanderWaal]] in her feature film debut, [[Chloe Fineman]], [[James Remar]], [[D. B. Sweeney]], and [[Dustin Hoffman]]. Set in an [[Alternate history|alternate]] 21st-century [[New York City]] (restyled "New Rome"), the story follows visionary architect Cesar Catilina (Driver) as he clashes with the corrupt Mayor Franklyn Cicero (Esposito), who opposes Catilina's plans to revitalize New Rome by building the futuristic utopia "Megalopolis". The film draws on Roman history, particularly the [[Catilinarian conspiracy]] of 63 BC and the decay of the [[Roman Republic]] into the [[Roman Empire]].

In 1977, Coppola had the idea to make a film drawing parallels between the fall of the Roman Republic and the future of the United States by retelling the Catilinarian conspiracy in modern New York. Although he began plotting the film in 1983, the project spent decades in [[development hell]]. Coppola attempted to produce the film in 1989 and again in 2001, but each time, the studios refused to finance the film, due to Coppola's string of late-career box-office disappointments and the [[September 11 attacks]], respectively. Disillusioned by the studio system, Coppola did not produce ''Megalopolis'' until he built a large fortune in the winemaking business. He spent $120{{nbsp}}million of his own money to make the film. Principal photography took place in [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] from November 2022 to March 2023.

The film reunited Coppola with past collaborators, including actors Esposito, Fishburne, Remar, Shire, and Sweeney, cinematographer [[Mihai Mălaimare Jr.]], composer [[Osvaldo Golijov]], and Coppola's son, second-unit director [[Roman Coppola]]. Like several other Coppola films, ''Megalopolis'' had a troubled production. Coppola adopted an experimental style, encouraging his actors to improvise and write certain scenes during the shoot, and adding his own last-minute changes to the script. Members of the art department and visual effects team, among others, left or were fired from the film.

''Megalopolis'' was selected to compete for the [[Palme d'Or]] at the [[77th Cannes Film Festival]], but polarized critics and Hollywood studios. Coppola could not find a studio that would both reimburse his production costs and pay for a large marketing campaign. He opted to pay for an advertising campaign, with [[Lionsgate Films|Lionsgate]] theatrically releasing the film in the United States. It endured a troubled run-up to release: a trailer was removed for using fabricated [[pull quote]]s, and Coppola sued trade publication ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' for libel after it published allegations of sexual misconduct by him on set. The film premiered at Cannes on May 16, 2024, and was released theatrically on September 27, 2024. It was a [[Box-office bomb|commercial failure]], grossing $14.4{{nbsp}}million against a budget of $120 to $136 million.<ref>Multiple sources:
* {{cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/story/2024-09-29/francis-ford-coppolas-megalopolis-bombs-as-wild-robot-wins |title=Francis Ford Coppola's $120-million 'Megalopolis' Bombs at the Box Office |last=Faughnder |first=Ryan |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=September 30, 2024 |access-date=March 1, 2025 |archive-date=January 27, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250127102616/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/story/2024-09-29/francis-ford-coppolas-megalopolis-bombs-as-wild-robot-wins |url-status=live }}
* {{cite web |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/megalopolis-is-a-box-office-mega-flop-olis.html |title=It's Official: 'Megalopolis' is a Box-Office Mega Flop(olis) |last=Lee |first=Chris |website=[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]] |date=September 30, 2024 |access-date=March 1, 2025 |url-access=registration |archive-date=March 5, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250305222848/https://www.vulture.com/article/megalopolis-is-a-box-office-mega-flop-olis.html |url-status=live }}
* {{cite web |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1676579/megalopolis-reasons-box-office-flop/ |title=5 Reasons Why 'Megalopolis' Flopped at the Box Office |last=Scott |first=Ryan |website=[[/Film|SlashFilm]] |date=September 30, 2024 |access-date=March 1, 2025 |archive-date=December 26, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241226021156/https://www.slashfilm.com/1676579/megalopolis-reasons-box-office-flop/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Critical reviews were mixed, with some  praising the film's ambition, originality, and style while others found it chaotic and uneven. Critics were also greatly polarized on the acting and story.

== Plot ==
In an alternate United States, New Rome is dominated by an elite group of patrician families. Although the Roman elite profess to live by a strict moral code, patricians decadently enjoy forbidden pleasures while ordinary Romans live in poverty.

Patrician architect Cesar Catilina is one of New Rome's leading figures. Cesar wins the [[Nobel Prize]] for inventing the revolutionary building material Megalon. In addition, he can secretly stop time. Despite Cesar's worldly success, he has fallen into alcoholism. Years earlier, his wife disappeared, and District Attorney Franklyn Cicero prosecuted him for murdering her. Although Cesar was acquitted, he remains crushed by guilt, believing his wife took her own life because he was too focused on his work. Cesar pines for his wife, prompting his jealous mistress, TV presenter Wow Platinum, to leave him.

At a televised event, Cesar and now-Mayor Cicero offer different visions for the city's future. Cesar proposes using Megalon to build "Megalopolis", a utopian urbanist community, while Cicero argues that a casino will provide immediate tax revenue. Cesar meets Cicero's well-read but purposeless daughter Julia. Earlier, she watched Cesar stop time while a building was being demolished but was still able to move. Initially, they dislike each other, but Cesar impresses Julia with his vision for Megalopolis, explaining that New Rome needs a grand artistic vision to free itself from its political inertia and unlock its full potential. Later, when Cesar cannot stop time as he once could, Julia encourages him to do so for her. They discover they can stop time when together, and the two become lovers.

Wow marries Cesar's uncle Hamilton Crassus III, the world's richest man. Although Crassus likes his nephew, his mind and health are in decline, and he is easily manipulated by individuals like his other nephew, Clodio Pulcher, who wants to inherit the Crassus bank. Crassus and Wow throw a decadent wedding reception. The headliner is teenage pop star Vesta Sweetwater, who appeals to New Rome's puritanical sensibilities by promising to remain chaste until marriage. To neutralize Cesar, Pulcher leaks a paparazzi video of Cesar having sex with Vesta, prompting Cicero to condemn Cesar. Although Cicero arrests Cesar for statutory rape, Julia exonerates Cesar by discovering that Vesta faked her age and is actually in her twenties.

[[Soviet]] satellite Carthage crashes to Earth, destroying much of New Rome. Cesar begins building Megalopolis in the ruins, financing the project with his family fortune. In a press conference, he makes the case for bold artistic projects that show people that a better world is possible. However, the cost of building Megalopolis contrasts with poverty on the streets. Pulcher becomes a populist politician, encouraging ordinary Romans to oppose Megalopolis as an expensive folly. The allure of power draws Pulcher from populism to fascist demagoguery.

A pregnant Julia tries to broker peace between Cesar and Cicero by taking her father to see the Megalopolis construction site, but Cicero is unimpressed with Cesar's utopianism, and he begs Cesar to leave Julia. In exchange, he offers Cesar valuable blackmail material: a confession that Cicero knew Cesar's wife committed suicide and maliciously prosecuted Cesar anyway. Cesar declines. Pulcher's right-hand man hires an assassin to kill Cesar, but Cesar's doctors use Megalon to rebuild his skull.

Wow tries to force Cesar to leave Julia and marry her by freezing Cesar's account at the Crassus bank. She enlists Pulcher to manipulate Crassus into handing over control of the bank. When Crassus learns of Pulcher's duplicity, he has a stroke and collapses. Pulcher and Wow taunt the bedridden Crassus, but Crassus kills Wow and injures Pulcher with a hidden bow and arrow.

Rioting Pulcher supporters attempt to storm Megalopolis and City Hall. Cesar confronts the rioters, pleading with them to believe in his vision of a better future, while Cicero watches. Cesar's speech inspires the crowd, who go on to hang Pulcher upside down.

With renewed financial support from Crassus, Cesar finally completes Megalopolis. Cicero, holding Julia and Cesar's baby daughter, Sunny Hope, promises to help Cesar build a better future. On New Year's Eve, Julia stops time, but only Sunny remains unaffected.

== Production ==
=== Development ===
[[File:Francis Ford Coppola, Director (05) (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|alt=Filmmaker Francis Ford Coppola in 1973.|Writer, director, and producer [[Francis Ford Coppola]] in 1973]]

Growing up in New York City, [[Francis Ford Coppola]] was fascinated by [[science fiction film]]s, such as [[Fritz Lang]]'s ''[[Metropolis (1927 film)|Metropolis]]'' (1927) and [[William Cameron Menzies]]'s ''[[Things to Come]]'' (1936), and the scientific community's history with dangerous experiments.<ref name="VanityFair-043024">{{cite web |url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/story/megalopolis-francis-ford-coppola-first-look-exclusive |title=Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'': An Exclusive First Look at the Director's Retro-Futurist Epic |last=Breznican |first=Anthony |author-link=Anthony Breznican |website=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]] |date=April 30, 2024 |access-date=April 30, 2024 |url-access=limited |archive-date=April 30, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240430075913/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/story/megalopolis-francis-ford-coppola-first-look-exclusive |url-status=live}}</ref> His reading of the Roman historian [[Sallust]] and [[William Bolitho Ryall]]'s book ''[[Twelve Against the Gods]]'' (1929) inspired him to make a film about [[Lucius Sergius Catiline]], a populist accused by Roman consul [[Marcus Tullius Cicero]] of conspiring to overthrow the [[Roman Republic]] in 63 BC.<ref name="Production Notes"/>{{rp|7}} Coppola conceived the overall idea for ''Megalopolis'' towards the end of filming ''[[Apocalypse Now]]'' (1979) in 1977.<ref name="Romberger"/>{{rp|50}} Sound designer [[Richard Beggs]] described Coppola's vision as an opera screened over four nights, similar to [[Richard Wagner]]'s [[Der Ring des Nibelungen|''Ring'' cycle]] (1876) in [[Bayreuth]], in a "gigantic outdoor purpose-built theatre".<ref name="TheGuardian2024"/> Coppola hoped to have it in "some place as close as possible to the geographical center of the United States",<ref>{{cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/apocalypsenowboo0000cowi/page/180/mode/2up?view=theater |title=The ''Apocalypse Now'' Book |last=Cowie |first=Peter |author-link=Peter Cowie |publisher=[[Da Capo Press]] |date=April 20, 2001 |access-date=March 29, 2024 |isbn=0-306-81046-8 |url-access=registration}}</ref>{{rp|181}} like the [[Red Rocks Amphitheatre]] in the state of Colorado.<ref name="TheGuardian2024"/>

Coppola devoted the beginning of 1983 to developing the film; in two months, he assembled four hundred pages of notes and script fragments.<ref name="Schumacher1999">{{cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/francisfordcoppo0000schu/page/332/mode/2up?view=theater |title=Francis Ford Coppola: A Filmmaker's Life |last=Schumacher |first=Michael |publisher=[[Crown Publishing Group]] |date=October 19, 1999 |access-date=March 29, 2024 |isbn=0-517-70445-5 |url-access=registration}}</ref>{{rp|333}} Over the next four decades, he collected notes and newspaper [[Clipping (publications)|clippings]] for scrapbooks detailing intriguing subjects he envisioned incorporating into a future screenplay, like political cartoons and different historical subjects, before deciding to make a Roman epic film set in an imagined modern America.<ref name="VanityFair-043024"/><ref name="Empire-Aug29"/> In mid-1983, he described the plot as taking place in one day in New York City with Catiline-era Rome as a backdrop, similar to how [[James Joyce]]'s ''[[Ulysses (novel)|Ulysses]]'' (1922) used [[Homer]] in the context of modern [[Dublin]] and how he updated the setting of [[Joseph Conrad]]'s ''[[Heart of Darkness]]'' (1899) from the late 1800s amid [[Colonisation of Africa|European colonial rule in Africa]] to the 1970s [[Vietnam War]] for ''Apocalypse Now''.<ref name="VanityFair-043024"/><ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/pdf/43452924.pdf |title=Idols of the King |last1=Thomson |first1=David |last2=Gray |first2=Lucy |journal=[[Film Comment]] |date=September–October 1983 |access-date=March 29, 2024 |volume=19 |number=5 |pages=61–75 |jstor=43452924}}</ref>{{rp|74}}<ref>{{cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/hollywoodauteurf0000chow/page/214/mode/2up?view=theater |title=Hollywood Auteur: Francis Coppola |last=Chown |first=Jeffrey |publisher=Praeger |date=May 20, 1988 |access-date=March 29, 2024 |isbn=0-275-92910-8 |url-access=registration}}</ref>{{rp|215}}

In January 1989, Coppola announced his plans to move to Italy to work on two productions in the next five years, including ''Le Ribellion di Catilina'', a film "so big and complicated it would seem impossible", which biographer Michael Schumacher said "sounded much like what he had in store for ''Megalopolis''".<ref name="Schumacher1999"/>{{rp|409–410}} It was to be shot in [[Cinecittà]], a film studio in Rome, where production designer [[Dean Tavoularis]] and his design team built offices and an art studio for [[drafter]]s to [[storyboard]] the film.<ref name="Clarke2003">{{cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/coppola0000clar/page/262/mode/2up?view=theater |title=Virgin Film: Coppola |last=Clarke |first=James |author-link=James Clarke (author) |publisher=Virgin Pub |date=January 1, 2003 |access-date=March 29, 2024 |isbn=0-7535-0866-4 |url-access=registration}}</ref>{{rp|266}}<ref>{{cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/coppola0000unse/page/234/mode/2up?view=theater |title=Coppola: A Biography |last=Cowie |first=Peter |author-link=Peter Cowie |publisher=[[Da Capo Press]] |date=August 22, 1994 |access-date=March 29, 2024 |isbn=978-0-306-80598-1 |url-access=registration}}</ref>{{rp|234}} ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' described it as "swing[ing] from the past to the present", merging "the images of Rome{{nbsp}}... with the New York of today". Of it, Coppola said, "I want to be free. I don't want producers around me telling me what to do". Coppola ultimately did not move to Italy, and instead made ''[[The Godfather Part III]]'' (1990).<ref name="Schumacher1999"/>{{rp|410}} Following the 1990–91 [[film awards season]] for that film, Coppola's production company, [[American Zoetrope]], announced several projects in development, including plans to film ''Megalopolis'' in 1991, despite lacking a finished script.<ref name="Schumacher1999"/>{{rp|436}} However, the film was postponed to "no earlier than 1996" after Coppola found himself prioritizing other projects, including ''[[Bram Stoker's Dracula (1992 film)|Bram Stoker's Dracula]]'' (1992), ''[[Jack (1996 film)|Jack]]'' (1996), and ''[[The Rainmaker (1997 film)|The Rainmaker]]'' (1997), to get out of debt accumulated from the box-office failures of ''[[One from the Heart]]'' (1982) and ''[[Tucker: The Man and His Dream]]'' (1988).<ref name="Schumacher1999"/>{{rp|444}}<ref>{{cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/godfatherbook0000cowi/page/110/mode/2up?view=theater |title=The ''Godfather'' Book |last=Cowie |first=Peter |author-link=Peter Cowie |publisher=[[Gardners Books]] |date=January 1, 1997 |access-date=March 29, 2024 |isbn=0-571-19011-1 |url-access=registration}}</ref>{{rp|110}}<ref name="AICN">{{cite web |url=http://legacy.aintitcool.com/node/32584 |title=Harry sits down in Austin with Francis Ford Coppola and talks ''Youth Without Youth'', Seventies film, Wine, ''Tetro'', and the Coppolas |last=Knowles |first=Harry |author-link=Harry Knowles |website=[[Ain't It Cool News]] |date=May 8, 2007 |access-date=November 14, 2022 |archive-date=November 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221114021855/http://legacy.aintitcool.com/node/32584 |url-status=live}}</ref>

{{quote box
| quote = "I've been working on [''Megalopolis''] for about twelve years. But in fits and starts. Whenever I have a couple of weeks off, I tackle it. About a year ago, I gathered all the scattered pieces of what I'd written and read them. I was devastated: it was just a collection of disjointed fragments, I had nothing but criticisms to offer. I was like the guy who leaves his [[advertising agency]] to write a novel and, in the end, can't produce a single line. I think I'm a good screenwriter, a good director, but perhaps not good enough for a project of this caliber and ambition. Then, reflecting, I thought that [[Leo Tolstoy|[Leo] Tolstoy]] had to start over ten times to write ''[[War and Peace]]''. So I'll start again. To write this story, I still have to learn, I need to better grasp the subject I want to address. I have a lot of books to read, I'm going to take notes, all this reading will take me at least a year."
| source = —Coppola in 1998<ref>{{Cite magazine |author1=Kaganski, Serge |author2=Fevret, Christian |date=April 15, 1998 |url=https://www.lesinrocks.com/cinema/entretien-f-f-coppola-lidealiste-0498-100944-15-04-1998/ |title=Entretien F.F Coppola – « L’Idéaliste » – 04/98 |magazine=[[Les Inrockuptibles]] |language=fr |access-date=September 17, 2026}}</ref>
| align = right
| width = 50%
}}

In a 1992 diary entry, Coppola figured he should only make films he had "a burning desire to make", preferably in the [[Ingmar Bergman#Style of working|independent-esque manner of Ingmar Bergman]], though worried that "forget[ting] the money" would not be compatible with "a bigger film" like ''Megalopolis''.<ref>{{cite book Rainmaker''.<ref name="Empire-Aug29"/> In 2001, he held [[Read-through|table reads]] in a production office in [[Park Slope]], Brooklyn, with actors including [[Nicolas Cage]] (his nephew), [[Russell |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240401154653/https://variety.com/2001/voices/columns/coppola-prepping-megalopolis-1117802987/ |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Jim Steranko]], who previously created production illustrations for ''Bram Stoker's Dracula'', was commissioned by Coppola to produce concept art for ''Megalopolis''. As described in [[James Romberger]]'s [[master's thesis]], Steranko's work featured detailed pencil and charcoal architectural drawings of grand buildings and expansive urban plazas, blending elements of ancient Roman design, [[Art Deco]] influences, and speculative sci-fi aesthetics.<ref name="Romberger">{{cite thesis |url=https://academicworks.cuny.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=3312&context=gc_etds |title=The Conflict of Progressive and Conservative Tendencies in the Film Work of Steranko |last=Romberger |first=James H. |author-link=James Romberger |publisher=[[CUNY Academic Works]] |degree=M.A. |date=September 2017 |access-date=March 29, 2024 |archive-date=February 21, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230221235804/https://academicworks.cuny.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=3312&context=gc_etds |url-status=live}}</ref>{{rp|54}} Proposed [[filming location]]s included the cities of Montreal and New York, with an anticipated budget of $50–80{{nbsp}}million (equivalent to ${{Format price|{{Inflation|US-GDP|50000000|2001}}}} to ${{Format price|{{Inflation|US-GDP|80000000|2001}}}} in {{Inflation/year|US}}).<ref name="Clarke2003"/>{{rp|263}}<ref name="VarietyJuly2001"/><ref name="VarietyOct2001"/>

That year, Coppola and cinematographer [[Ron Fricke]] recorded [[second unit]] footage of New York, thinking it would be simpler to do so before [[principal photography]], with the [[24p|24-frames]] per second [[Panavision HD-900F|Sony F900]] [[digital camera]] that [[George Lucas]] used for ''[[Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace]]'' (1999).<ref name="VanityFair-043024"/><ref name="VarietyOct2001"/> Fricke had previously shot [[Godfrey Reggio]]'s ''[[Koyaanisqatsi]]'' (1982), which Coppola served as executive producer.<ref name="Empire-Aug29"/><ref name="Clarke2003"/>{{rp|263}} After the [[September 11 attacks]], during which Coppola and his team were [[location scouting]] in New York, the roughly thirty hours of footage was stashed, including more material they shot two weeks after, due to its resemblance to the script, which involved a Soviet satellite crashing into Earth and destroying a section of [[Lower Manhattan]].<ref name="Romberger"/>{{rp|54}}<ref name="Clarke2003"/>{{rp|263}}<ref name="DeadlineMay2019"/><ref name="Film Comment">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.filmcomment.com/article/brief-encounters-francis-ford-coppolla-interview/ |title=Brief Encounters: Francis Ford Coppola |last=Jacobson |first=Harlan |author-link=Harlan Jacobson |magazine=[[Film Comment]] |date=January–February 2008 |access-date=July 24, 2024 |archive-date=April 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240404141542/https://www.filmcomment.com/article/brief-encounters-francis-ford-coppolla-interview/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Having based the New York of his film on the state of financial and infrastructural disrepair the city faced in the 1980s, he felt ''Megalopolis'' had become more relevant after the event and declared his plans to rewrite it. "I feel as though history has come to my doorstep," he said.<ref name="VarietyOct2001">{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2001/film/news/megalopolis-plans-shifted-1117854393/ |title=''Megalopolis'' plans shifted |last=Lyons |first=Charles |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=October 16, 2001 |access-date=April 1, 2024 |archive-date=April 9, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240409085152/https://variety.com/2001/film/news/megalopolis-plans-shifted-1117854393/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2001/oct/18/news|title=Terror attacks put Coppola's Megalopolis on hold|date=October 18, 2001|first=Betsy|last=Reed|website=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=June 16, 2025}}</ref> In 2002, he shot sixty to seventy hours of second unit footage in Manhattan on [[high-definition video]] that Lucas described as "wide shots of cities with incredible detail at [[Golden hour (photography)|magic hour]] and all kinds of available-light material".<ref name="Clarke2003"/>{{rp|263}}<ref>{{cite web |url=https://experts.uli.org/Content/PressRoom/Fall_03/NewsClips/Clips_03_19.htm |title=Coppola: The City and His Dreams, Famed Director Readies Vision of Future ''Megalopolis'' |last=Kerch |first=Steve |publisher=[[Urban Land Institute]] |date=November 5, 2003 |access-date=April 1, 2024 |archive-date=December 7, 2003 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031207071034/https://experts.uli.org/Content/PressRoom/Fall_03/NewsClips/Clips_03_19.htm |url-status=dead |quote=The director has already shot about 70 hours of film in Manhattan that will serve as background for the movie.}}</ref><ref name="Delorme2010">{{cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/francisfordcoppo0000delo/page/82/mode/2up?view=theater |title=Francis Ford Coppola |last=Delorme |first=Stéphane |publisher=[[Cahiers du Cinéma]] |date=October 1, 2010 |access-date=March 29, 2024 |isbn=978-2866425937 |url-access=registration}}</ref>{{rp|82}} He also disclosed his intent to self-finance the film, still in place as his next project, having become disheartened making films to pay off his debt to Hollywood.<ref name="TheGuardian2002"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2002/film/news/zoetrope-myriad-plan-3-pics-1117861297/ |title=Zoetrope, Myriad plan 3 pics |last1=Vaucher |first1=Andrea R. |last2=Harris |first2=Dana |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=February 24, 2002 |access-date=April 1, 2024 |archive-date=April 9, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240409085152/https://variety.com/2002/film/news/zoetrope-myriad-plan-3-pics-1117861297/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In 2003, [[Ryan Gosling]] shot test footage as Clodio Pulcher.<ref>[https://youtube/jaS6lWFweeQ?is=zQvGGCt4mEwTdjt7 Ryan Gosling Megalopolis 2003 Workshop/Megadoc Appearance video clip]</ref>

Production on the film eventually halted. The success of Coppola's [[Francis Ford Coppola#Francis Ford Coppola Presents|winery and resorts]] meant he could produce it with his own money, which his friend [[Wendy Doniger]] said "paralyzed him". "He had no excuse this time if the film was no good", she remarked, "What froze him was having the power to do exactly what he wanted so that his soul was on the line".<ref name="Time">{{cite magazine |url=https://content.time.com/time/arts/article/0,8599,1681652-2,00.html |title=Coppola, Take 2 |last=Keegan |first=Rebecca |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |date=November 7, 2007 |access-date=April 1, 2024 |archive-date=April 1, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240401161534/https://content.time.com/time/arts/article/0,8599,1681652-2,00.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2005, she bestowed him books that she deemed thematically relevant, including [[Mircea Eliade]]'s ''[[Youth Without Youth (novella)|Youth Without Youth]]'' (1976), a novella about a 70-year-old man struggling to complete an ambitious project. Coppola shelved ''Megalopolis'' to self-finance a [[Youth Without Youth (film)|small-scale adaptation of the book]], intended to be "the opposite of ''Megalopolis''".<ref name="Delorme2010"/>{{rp|85}}<ref name="Time"/> In 2007, Coppola acknowledged that the September 11 attacks were a factor in his hesitancy to return to the film: "A movie about the aspiration of utopia with New York as a main character and then all of a sudden you couldn't write about New York without just dealing with what happened and the implications of what happened. The world was attacked and I didn't know how to try to do with that {{sic}}. I tried".<ref name="AICN"/> In 2009, in regards to the likelihood of revisiting the film, he said: "Someday, I'll read what I had on ''Megalopolis'' and maybe I'll think different of it, but it's also a movie that costs a lot of money to make and there's not a patron out there. You see what the studios are making right now".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://movieline.com/2009/06/francis-ford-coppola-to-movieline-godfather-never-should-have-had-more-than-one-movie.php |title=Francis Ford Coppola to Movieline: 'Godfather Never Should Have Had More Than One Movie' |last=Buchanan |first=Kyle |website=[[Movieline]] |date=June 3, 2009 |access-date=March 29, 2024 |archive-date=June 11, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090611150105/http://movieline.com/2009/06/francis-ford-coppola-to-movieline-godfather-never-should-have-had-more-than-one-movie.php |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Coppola began the final script of the film in 2012, about 12 years before the film's release.<ref name="Production Notes" />{{rp||page=4}} He said that before her death in 2015, Australian novelist [[Colleen McCullough]] (who had written several books set in ancient Rome) wrote a [[novelization]] of the ''Megalopolis'' story.<ref name=":5">{{cite web |last=Barsanti |first=Sam |date=September 3, 2023 |title=Francis Ford Coppola teases a ''Megalopolis'' novelization from Colleen McCullough—who died in 2015 |url=https://www.avclub.com/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-novelization-1850801159 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240507025016/https://www.avclub.com/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-novelization-1850801159 |archive-date=May 7, 2024 |access-date=May 6, 2024 |website=[[The A.V. Club]]}}</ref> However, he did not say whether that novelization resembled the ultimate version of the film, as it was based on his "many scripts and ideas over the decades".<ref name=":4" /> McCullough received a credit as a historical advisor on the film, along with professional historian [[Mary Beard (classicist)|Mary Beard]].<ref name="Production Notes" />{{rp||page=37}}

In 2017, celebrity chef [[Anthony Bourdain]] invited Coppola on his [[Anthony Bourdain: Parts Unknown|travel show]] in Sicily. Coppola took note of his weight gain when he saw his episode and signed up for a five-month program at [[Duke University]]'s fitness center, where he lost close to {{convert|80|lbs}}.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://hauteliving.com/2020/10/francis-ford-coppola-reasonsremaking-godfather-part-iii/690592/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola: Protecting His Legacy During The Pandemic |date=October 15, 2020 |first=Laura |last=Schreffler |website=[[Haute Living]]|access-date=August 25, 2024|archive-date=September 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240907181640/https://hauteliving.com/2020/10/francis-ford-coppola-reasonsremaking-godfather-part-iii/690592/|url-status=live}}</ref> Reflecting on his experience, he recalled listening to readings of ''Megalopolis'' during strict exercise regimens and realizing its relevance despite being written decades earlier. The 2001 draft, he explained, was an early version of the story but had evolved significantly over time. He credited Gandolfini with providing valuable suggestions when he had previously auditioned for the role of the mayor.<ref name="RollingStone-0825">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-features/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-the-godfather-1235068854/ |url-access=limited |title=Francis Ford Coppola: 'I Have Nothing Left to Lose' |date=August 25, 2024 |first=David |last=Fear |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |access-date=August 25, 2024 |archive-date=September 24, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240924060858/https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-features/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-the-godfather-1235068854/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

On April 3, 2019, the day before his 80th birthday, Coppola announced his return to the project, having completed the script and approached [[Jude Law]] and [[Shia LaBeouf]] for lead roles.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2019/04/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-directing-this-year-1202588167/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola Ready to Make ''Megalopolis'' and is Eyeing Cast |last=Fleming |first=Mike Jr. |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=April 3, 2019 |access-date=April 1, 2024 |archive-date=April 4, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404011947/https://deadline.com/2019/04/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-directing-this-year-1202588167/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="DeadlineMay2019">{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2019/05/francis-ford-coppola-apocalypse-now-cannes-40-anniversary-megalopolis-scorsese-godfather-part-ii-re-cutting-godfather-iii-cotton-club-interview-1202613659/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola: How Winning Cannes 40 Years Ago Saved ''Apocalypse Now'', Making ''Megalopolis'', Why Scorsese Almost Helmed ''Godfather Part II'' & Re-Cutting Three Past Films |last=Fleming |first=Mike Jr. |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=May 13, 2019 |access-date=November 6, 2022 |archive-date=May 16, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190516131543/https://deadline.com/2019/05/francis-ford-coppola-apocalypse-now-cannes-40-anniversary-megalopolis-scorsese-godfather-part-ii-re-cutting-godfather-iii-cotton-club-interview-1202613659/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In 2021, Coppola sold his [[Sonoma County wine]]ries to merge his winery business with that of another Napa-based family company, Delicato Family Wines, in an equity deal worth around $650{{nbsp}}million. He then borrowed $200{{nbsp}}million against his ownership stake in Delicato to fund ''Megalopolis'' for $120{{nbsp}}million and pay for other projects at [[Inglenook (winery)|Inglenook]] and [[Sentinel Building (San Francisco)|Sentinel Building]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.northbaybusinessjournal.com/article/industrynews/francis-ford-coppola-plans-to-sell-sonoma-county-wineries-to-delicato-famil/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola selling Sonoma County wineries to Napa's Delicato Family Wines |last=Quackenbush |first=Jeff |website=North Bay Business Journal |date=June 24, 2021 |access-date=June 23, 2024 |archive-date=May 17, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240517230743/https://www.northbaybusinessjournal.com/article/industrynews/francis-ford-coppola-plans-to-sell-sonoma-county-wineries-to-delicato-famil/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="WSJ-Sept26">{{cite web|url=https://www.wsj.com/arts-culture/film/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-movie-799e70c4|url-access=subscription|title=Francis Ford Coppola Bet More Than $100 Million On His Legacy. Now What?|date=September 26, 2024|first=John|last=Jurgensen|website=[[The Wall Street Journal]]|access-date=September 27, 2024|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20240926232456/https://www.wsj.com/arts-culture/film/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-movie-799e70c4|archive-date=September 26, 2024}}</ref> By August, discussions with actors to star in the film had begun; [[James Caan]] was set to star after petitioning Coppola to write him a [[cameo role]] as a potential [[swan song]], while [[Cate Blanchett]], [[Oscar Isaac]], [[Jessica Lange]], [[Michelle Pfeiffer]], [[Jon Voight]], [[Forest Whitaker]], and [[Zendaya]] were in various stages of negotiations.<ref name="Production Notes"/>{{rp|3}}<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2021/08/francis-coppola-megalopolis-epic-financing-oscar-isaac-forest-whitaker-cate-blanchett-james-caan-1234824846/ |title=Francis Coppola, A Gambling Maverick Moviemaker Who Won Big, Betting on Star Cast for Epic ''Megalopolis'' |last=Fleming |first=Mike Jr. |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=August 31, 2021 |access-date=August 31, 2021 |archive-date=January 26, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220126071010/https://deadline.com/2021/08/francis-coppola-megalopolis-epic-financing-oscar-isaac-forest-whitaker-cate-blanchett-james-caan-1234824846/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

March 27, 2022 (Coppola was readying to go to the [[94th Academy Awards]] to receive an honor),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cKAF1YsoyCc|title=Aubrey Plaza on Her Casual
