2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240929045644/https://www.youtube.com/watch?si=4R2P60XkAaq0tzWZ&v=cKAF1YsoyCc|url-status=live}}</ref> while staying at the San Domenico, the same hotel in Sicily that Coppola resided in during the filming of ''[[The Godfather]]'' (1972). Before the meeting, Coppola emailed her the entire script and asked her to consider the role of "Wow Platinum", wanting an actress with a similar screen presence to [[Jean Harlow]] and [[Myrna Loy]] in [[screwball comedies]] from the 1930s.<ref name="Production Notes"/>{{rp|3}}<ref name="DeadlineMay2024">{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2024/05/aubrey-plaza-interview-megalopolis-francis-ford-coppola-1235904319/ |title=Cannes Cover Story: Aubrey Plaza Says Francis Coppola 'Doesn't Need My Defense', Reveals the 'Collaboration and Experimentation' of ''Megalopolis'' |last=Blyth |first=Antonia |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=May 13, 2024 |access-date=May 14, 2024 |archive-date=May 14, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240514073811/https://deadline.com/2024/05/aubrey-plaza-interview-megalopolis-francis-ford-coppola-1235904319/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Coppola came up with the character's name after meeting a [[Southern United States|Southern]] woman whose great-grandmother's name "evolved" to "[[Wiktionary:wow|Wow]]" due to her beauty.<ref name="twitter.com">{{Cite tweet |number=1842258213850497188 |user=megalopolismov |title=I met a southern young lady who told me her great grandmother was so beautiful that her name evolved as "WOW." I asked if she had a picture of her. A while later I heard back from her and she attached a photo of a painting and when I looked at it I said, wow! |date=October 4, 2024 |url=https://twitter.com/megalopolismov/status/1842258213850497188 |via=[[Twitter]]}}</ref> For her performance, Plaza was inspired by [[Faye Dunaway]] in ''[[Network (1976 film)|Network]]'' (1976) and [[Nicole Kidman]] in ''[[To Die For]]'' (1995).<ref name="Today-Sept23">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6yBtxaYUFDM|title=Aubrey Plaza talks 2 new films: ''My Old Ass'' and ''Megalopolis''|date=September 23, 2024|via=[[YouTube]]|publisher=[[Today (American TV program)|Today]]|access-date=October 3, 2024|archive-date=October 3, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241003051651/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6yBtxaYUFDM&gl=US&hl=en|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Chloe Fineman]], Madeleine Gardella, Hoffman, Bailey Ives, [[Isabelle Kusman]], and [[D. B. Sweeney]] would be added in October 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2022/10/francis-coppola-sets-final-casting-for-epic-megalopolis-film-shooting-this-fall-in-georgia-1235134774/ |title=Francis Coppola Sets Final Casting for Epic ''Megalopolis''; Film Shooting This Fall in Georgia |last=Fleming |first=Mike Jr. |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=October 4, 2022 |access-date=October 4, 2022 |archive-date=October 4, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221004171622/https://deadline.com/2022/10/francis-coppola-sets-final-casting-for-epic-megalopolis-film-shooting-this-fall-in-georgia-1235134774/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Coppola had reached out to Fineman, a cast member on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]'', in 2020 after seeing her perform at a theater comedy event where she impersonated [[Ivana Trump|Ivana]] and [[Melania Trump]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/video/hannah-einbinder-chloe-fineman-actors-on-actors-full-conversation/ |title=Hannah Einbinder & Chloe Fineman – Actors on Actors (Full Conversation) |last=Hailu |first=Selome |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |time=25:20 |date=June 14, 2024 |access-date=June 15, 2024 |archive-date=July 18, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240718202107/https://variety.com/video/hannah-einbinder-chloe-fineman-actors-on-actors-full-conversation/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.vogue.com/slideshow/women-led-performing-arts-collective |title=A Women-Led Performing Arts Collective Said Goodbye to 2019 with a Wake at the Hollywood Forever Cemetery |last=Waters |first=Jagger |website=[[Vogue (magazine)|Vogue]] |date=January 17, 2020 |access-date=June 15, 2024 |archive-date=June 15, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240615025152/https://www.vogue.com/slideshow/women-led-performing-arts-collective |url-status=live}}</ref> Recognizing Driver from her [[New York University]] days and feeling ''Megalopolis'' was a reminder to every actor's dreams to do theatre, Fineman looked for [[William Shakespeare]]'s "trustafarians characters" as an inspiration and [[Improvisational theatre|improvised]] like she had done in past projects such as [[Damien Chazelle]]'s ''[[Babylon (2022 film)|Babylon]]'' and [[Noah Baumbach]]'s ''[[White Noise (2022 film)|White Noise]]'' (both 2022).<ref name="FinemanCBR">{{cite web |url=https://www.cbr.com/megalopolis-movie-chloe-fineman-interview/ |title='Francis Changed My Life': Megalopolis Star Chloe Fineman on Working With Francis Ford Coppola |last=Frederick |first=Brittany |website=[[Comic Book Resources]] |date=September 27, 2024 |access-date=November 2, 2024 |archive-date=October 1, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241001044113/https://www.cbr.com/megalopolis-movie-chloe-fineman-interview/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In January 2023, Esposito was confirmed to star;<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2023/01/giancarlo-esposito-joins-cast-francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-1235238149/ |title=Giancarlo Esposito Joins Cast of Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' |last=Fleming |first=Mike Jr. |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=January 23, 2023 |access-date=January 24, 2023 |archive-date=January 24, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230124023604/https://deadline.com/2023/01/giancarlo-esposito-joins-cast-francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-1235238149/ |url-status=live}}</ref> he previously acted in Coppola's ''[[The Cotton Club (film)|The Cotton Club]]'' (1984). His character of Mayor Franklyn Cicero was loosely inspired by Marcus Tullius Cicero and New York's first Black mayor [[David Dinkins]].<ref name="IndieWire-Sept12"/> Esposito, Fishburne, Remar, Shire, and Sweeney previously worked with Coppola.<ref name="Production Notes"/>{{rp|2}} Coppola opted to cast actors with differing political ideologies to avoid accusations of the film being a didactic, "[[woke]] Hollywood production".<ref name="RollingStone-0825"/>

The film's literary influences included the books ''[[Bullshit Jobs]]'' (2018), ''[[The Dawn of Everything]]'' (2021), and ''[[Debt: The First 5000 Years]]'' (2011) by [[David Graeber]]; ''[[The Chalice and the Blade]]'' (1987) by [[Riane Eisler]]; ''Directors on Directing'' (1963), edited by Toby Cole and [[Helen Krich Chinoy]], particularly an entry by [[Elia Kazan]] on his approach to ''[[A Streetcar Named Desire (1951 film)|A Streetcar Named Desire]]'' (1951); ''[[Dream of the Red Chamber]]'' by [[Cao Xueqin]]; ''[[Elective Affinities]]'' (1809) by [[Johann Wolfgang von Goethe]]; ''[[The Glass Bead Game]]'' (1943) by [[Hermann Hesse]]; ''[[The Origins of Political Order]]'' (2011) by [[Francis Fukuyama]]; ''[[The Swerve]]'' (2011) by [[Stephen Greenblatt]]; ''[[To the Lighthouse]]'' (1927) by [[Virginia Woolf]]; ''Twelve Against the Gods'' (1929) by [[William Bolitho Ryall]]; and ''[[The War Lovers]]'' (2010) by [[Evan Thomas]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gq.com/story/francis-ford-coppolas-megalopolis-might-actually-come-out-this-year |title=Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' Might Actually Come Out This Year. Here's Everything We Know |last=Rinder |first=Grant |website=[[GQ]] |date=January 22, 2024 |access-date=March 29, 2024 |url-access=limited |archive-date=March 29, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240329163507/https://www.gq.com/story/francis-ford-coppolas-megalopolis-might-actually-come-out-this-year |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":7">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.newyorker.com/books/book-currents/francis-ford-coppola-on-books-that-influenced-megalopolis|title=Francis Ford Coppola on Books That Influenced ''Megalopolis''|date=October 2, 2024|magazine=[[The New Yorker]]|access-date=October 2, 2024|archive-date=October 2, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241002204042/https://www.newyorker.com/books/book-currents/francis-ford-coppola-on-books-that-influenced-megalopolis|url-status=live}}</ref>

Based on Catiline, the character of Cesar was renamed at classicist [[Mary Beard (classicist)|Mary Beard]]'s suggestion that [[Julius Caesar]] had ties with Catiline and was more known among audiences. The character was inspired by [[Robert Moses]], as portrayed in [[Robert Caro]]'s biography ''[[The Power Broker]]'' (1974), and architects [[Norman Bel Geddes]], [[Walter Gropius]], [[Raymond Loewy]], and [[Frank Lloyd Wright]]. Coppola researched the [[Claus von Bülow]] murder case, the [[Mary Cunningham Agee|Mary Cunningham]]-[[William Agee]] [[Bendix Corporation]] scandal, the emergence of [[New York Stock Exchange]] reporter [[Maria Bartiromo]], the history of [[Studio 54]], and [[Felix Rohatyn]]'s solution for the [[New York City fiscal crisis of 1975]].<ref name="VanityFair-043024"/> The fictional building material of Megalon was based in part on the work of architect and designer [[Neri Oxman]], who appears as "Dr. Lyra Shir" and was credited as the architectural and scientific advisor. Having worked with Coppola on studies for ''Megalopolis'', her four-part model installation ''Man-Nahāta'' displays a potential future design of Manhattan.<ref name="Production Notes"/>{{rp|10; 35}} In line with ''The Godfather'' and ''Dracula'', where he credited [[Mario Puzo]] and [[Bram Stoker]] as the original writers, Coppola branded the film with his name as ''Francis Ford Coppola's Megalopolis''.<ref name="VanityFair-043024"/>

The COVID-19 pandemic delayed the start of production. Before filming began, a week of rehearsals took place with theater-style exercises, much like the one Emmanuel described having in her audition.<ref name="THRMay2024"/> Coppola said he could only rehearse with around a third of the cast, including Plaza and Emmanuel, but notably not Driver, and thus cast [[understudies]] in place of absent members.<ref name="RollingStone-0825"/><ref name="IndieWire-Sept16">{{cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/interviews/francis-ford-coppola-on-megalopolis-1235045897/|title=How Francis Ford Coppola Returned to 'Student' Filmmaking to Pave the Way for ''Megalopolis''|date=September 16, 2024|first=Jim|last=Hemphill|website=[[IndieWire]]|access-date=September 16, 2024|archive-date=October 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007030952/https://www.indiewire.com/features/interviews/francis-ford-coppola-on-megalopolis-1235045897/|url-status=live}}</ref> Fineman, however, recalled rehearsing on [[Halloween]] with Plaza, Driver, Hoffman, and Voight, playing improvisational games with Coppola that encouraged character immersion.<ref name="FinemanCBR"/> Plaza described the workshop-style approach as a collaborative process where actors could improvise and offer input on the script. She recalled working closely with Voight and LaBeouf, writing scenes and passing them to the script supervisor, who would then present them to Coppola. If he approved, the material would sometimes be incorporated into the film.<ref name="DeadlineMay2024"/> One such scene that the actors composed was the part where Plaza's "Wow Platinum" orders LaBeouf's "Clodio Pulcher" to "[[oral sex|orally pleasure]] her as he calls her Auntie Wow", building off an idea of Coppola's.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/09/29/movies/aubrey-plaza-megalopolis-my-old-ass-agatha-all-along.html|url-access=limited|title=Have We Gotten Aubrey Plaza Wrong This Whole Time?|date=September 29, 2024|first=Kyle|last=Buchanan|website=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=September 30, 2024|archive-date=October 1, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241001195107/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/09/29/movies/aubrey-plaza-megalopolis-my-old-ass-agatha-all-along.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Coppola described LaBeouf as an actor who intentionally creates tension with directors, often pushing it to an extreme. He found LaBeouf's approach frustrating and irrational, likening it to [[Dennis Hopper]]'s preparations for ''Apocalypse Now''.<ref name="RollingStone-0825"/><ref name="TheTelegraph-Sept13"/>

=== Filming ===
[[File:Trilith Soundstages.jpg|thumb|The film was shot at [[Trilith Studios]].]]

Principal photography began on November 7, 2022, in [[Fayetteville, Georgia]], at [[Trilith Studios]] and concluded on March 11, 2023. Filming also took place in Atlanta.<ref name="Production Notes"/>{{rp|3}} It was to be the first film shot on Trilith Studios' [[Trilith Studios#Prysm Stage|Prysm Stage]], an [[LED]] [[on-set virtual production|virtual production]] volume, but due to budget constraints, the production pivoted to a "less costly, more traditional [[Chroma key|greenscreen]] approach".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-prysm-stages-1234766888/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' Will Debut Never-Before-Seen Film Technology |last=Bergeson |first=Samantha |website=[[IndieWire]] |date=September 28, 2022 |access-date=May 13, 2024 |archive-date=May 13, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240513145614/https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-prysm-stages-1234766888/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://collider.com/megalopolis-francis-ford-coppola-filming-location-prysm-stages-atlanta/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' to Film at Prysm Stages in Atlanta Using Groundbreaking Technology |last=Klawans |first=Justin |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |date=September 28, 2022 |access-date=November 4, 2022 |archive-date=November 4, 2022 Crew Exodus (Exclusive) |last1=Masters |first1=Kim |last2=Feinberg |first2=Scott |last3=Couch |first3=Aaron |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=January 9, 2023 |access-date=January 10, 2023 |archive-date=January 9, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230109233311/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/francis-ford-coppolas-megalopolis-in-peril-1235284875/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The decision to [[Film industry in Georgia (U.S. state)|film in Georgia]] over the film's setting of New York was due to available tax benefits, studio facilities, local crews, and classical buildings to act as sets.<ref name="Production Notes"/>{{rp|3}}<ref name="TheGuardian2024">{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/article/2024/may/14/has-this-guy-ever-made-a-movie-before-francis-ford-coppola-40-year-battle-megalopolis |title='Has this guy ever made a movie before?' Francis Ford Coppola's 40-year battle to film ''Megalopolis'' |last=Rose |first=Steve |website=[[The Guardian]] |date=May 14, 2024 |access-date=May 14, 2024 |archive-date=July 18, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240718202125/https://www.theguardian.com/film/article/2024/may/14/has-this-guy-ever-made-a-movie-before-francis-ford-coppola-40-year-battle-megalopolis |url-status=live}}</ref> Around July 2023, close to when editing began, additional content was shot on the [[Italy–Switzerland border]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ansa.it/sito/notizie/cultura/cinema/2023/07/10/mike-figgis-vi-porto-nella-megalopolis-di-coppola_4d3d146a-558f-4f2a-a1df-f0fc66a2fc18.html |title=Mike Figgis, 'vi porto nella ''Megalopolis'' di Coppola' |trans-title=Mike Figgis, {{'}}I{{'}}ll take you to Coppola's ''Megalopolis''{{'}} |last=DeLucia |first=Francesca |website=[[Agenzia Nazionale Stampa Associata]] |date=July 10, 2023 |access-date=August 15, 2024 |language=IT |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230710191310/https://www.ansa.it/sito/notizie/cultura/cinema/2023/07/10/mike-figgis-vi-porto-nella-megalopolis-di-coppola_4d3d146a-558f-4f2a-a1df-f0fc66a2fc18.html |archive-date=July 10, 2023 |url-status=dead|quote=For 5 months I was with Francis to tell the whole production process, now he is in the editing phase in Atlanta. We have recently finished shooting extra scenes on the border between Italy and Switzerland.}}</ref>

For the production of ''Megalopolis'', Coppola purchased a [[Days Inn]] drive-in motel in [[Peachtree City, Georgia]], for $4.35{{nbsp}}million to house the crew and his extended family. He renovated the property to include rehearsal and [[post-production]] facilities, which increased the tax incentives available to the project and reportedly reduced the overall production expenditure to $107{{nbsp}}million.<ref name="WSJ-Sept26"/> The site was later opened to the public on July 5, 2024, as the All-Movie Hotel, a hybrid hospitality and filmmaking venue serving as the first U.S. location in Coppola's Hideaway hotel collection and fifth overall. The All-Movie Hotel features 27 suites and rooms personally designed by Coppola, along with a range of production facilities intended for projects of varying scales. These include modular post-production spaces such as two edit suites with laser projection and [[Meyer Sound]] 2.1 monitoring, two additional edit bays, [[Automated dialogue replacement|ADR]] recording capabilities, and a screening room equipped for [[Dolby Atmos]] 9.1.6 sound mixing. The property also houses offices, a wardrobe fitting room, a gym, a swimming pool, and an [[Sound stage|insert stage]]. Coppola's own residential suite from the production of ''Megalopolis'' is available for guests to book, and memorabilia from his past films is displayed throughout the hotel.<ref name="AP-Hotel">{{cite web |url=https://apnews.com/article/coppola-megalopolis-allmovie-hotel-georgia-film-e25192debab6c98c489a5555a2d73d60 |title=Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' wrapped at this Georgia hotel. Soon, it'll be open for business |last=Kramon |first=Charlotte |website=[[Associated Press]] |date=July 17, 2024 |access-date=July 17, 2024 |archive-date=July 18, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240718202057/https://apnews.com/article/coppola-megalopolis-allmovie-hotel-georgia-film-e25192debab6c98c489a5555a2d73d60 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/news/breaking-news/francis-ford-coppola-all-movie-hotel-atlanta-1235024353/ |title=You Can Now Stay Where ''Megalopolis'' Was Completed: Introducing Coppola's All-Movie Hotel |last=Bergeson |first=Samantha |website=[[IndieWire]] |date=July 10, 2024 |access-date=July 10, 2024 |archive-date=July 10, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240710210524/https://www.indiewire.com/news/breaking-news/francis-ford-coppola-all-movie-hotel-atlanta-1235024353/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

The cinematographer was [[Mihai Mălaimare Jr.]], who shot Coppola's ''Youth Without Youth'' (2007), ''[[Tetro]]'' (2009), and ''[[Twixt (film)|Twixt]]'' (2011).<ref>{{cite podcast |url=https://themakingof.substack.com/p/a-cinematographers-life-with-mihai |title=A Cinematographer's Life with Mihai Malaimare Jr. |last=Valinsky |first=Michael |website=The Making of |date=August 3, 2022 |access-date=May 12, 2024 |archive-date=December 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231214115837/https://themakingof.substack.com/p/a-cinematographers-life-with-mihai |url-status=live}}</ref> The crew utilized two [[Arri Alexa 65]]s and one [[Alexa LF]] for high-speed frame rate for the first unit and an [[Alexa Mini LF]] for the second unit. [[Panavision]] provided the lenses, including [[Wide-angle lens|wide]] Sphero 65s, Panaspeeds, and specialty lenses such as the 200{{nbsp}}mm and 250{{nbsp}}mm detuned Primo Artiste, rehoused [[Helios (lens brand)|Helios]], and [[Lensbaby]] for specific scenes. The primary aspect ratio was 2:1, a tribute to [[Vittorio Storaro]]'s [[Univisium]], with select scenes changing to a 1.43:1 aspect ratio.<ref name="Production Notes"/>{{rp|16}}<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/cannes-2024-cameras-arri-furiosa/megalopolis-mihai-malaimare-jr-dp/|title=Cannes 2024 Cinematography: Cameras and Lenses Used to Shoot 59 Films|date=May 17, 2024|first=Sarah|last=Shachat|website=[[IndieWire]]|access-date=September 25, 2024|archive-date=September 25, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240925190523/https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/cannes-2024-cameras-arri-furiosa/megalopolis-mihai-malaimare-jr-dp/|url-status=live}}</ref> To capture authenticity from the actors, Coppola instructed Mălaimare to keep the camera rolling after he said "[[Cut (transition)#Verbal command|cut]]".<ref name="IndieWire-Sept16"/> Some male actors wore [[Caesar haircut]]s to evoke ancient Rome.<ref name="Uphill Battle">{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/megalopolis-francis-ford-coppola-challenges-distribution-1235867556/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' Faces Uphill Battle for Mega Deal: 'Just No Way to Position This Movie' |last1=Abramovitch |first1=Seth |last2=Masters |first2=Kim |last3=McClintock |first3=Pamela |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=April 8, 2024 |access-date=April 14, 2024 |archive-date=April 13, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240413161015/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/megalopolis-francis-ford-coppola-challenges-distribution-1235867556/ |url-status=live}}</ref> For Plaza, the last two weeks of the shoot overlapped with her role on the [[Disney+]] television miniseries ''[[Agatha All Along]]'' (2024). As they were shot on the same lot, she was allowed to do both.<ref name="DeadlineMay2024"/> Plaza and Schwartzman were also recording for the [[Netflix]] anime miniseries ''[[Scott Pilgrim Takes Off]]'' (2023) around the same time; Plaza would refer to Schwartzman as his ''Scott Pilgrim'' character on the ''Megalopolis'' set.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Sepinwall |first=Alan |date=November 20, 2023 |title='Scott Pilgrim Takes Off': Inside an Animated Spinoff for the Ages |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-features/scott-pilgrim-takes-off-netflix-animation-michael-cera-kieran-culkin-aubrey-plaza-1234877646/ |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]}}</ref> In August 2023, during the [[2023 SAG-AFTRA strike|SAG-AFTRA strike]], the film received an interim agreement from the union, possibly for [[Pick-up (filmmaking)|reshoots]] or publicity purposes to qualify for festival screenings and distribution deals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2023/08/francis-ford-coppolas-megalopolis-interim-agreement-sag-aftra-1235533045/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' Lands Interim Agreement from SAG-AFTRA |last=Kroll |first=Justin |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=August 31, 2023 |access-date=August 31, 2023 |archive-date=August 31, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230831191147/https://deadline.com/2023/08/francis-ford-coppolas-megalopolis-interim-agreement-sag-aftra-1235533045/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/news/general-news/francis-ford-coppola-confirms-megalopolis-2024-release-1234940461/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola Confirms ''Megalopolis'' Early 2024 Release: 'Wait and See' |last=Bergeson |first=Samantha |website=[[IndieWire]] |date=January 5, 2024 |access-date=January 6, 2024 |archive-date=January 6, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240106205719/https://www.indiewire.com/news/general-news/francis-ford-coppola-confirms-megalopolis-2024-release-1234940461/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The final film includes footage shot in 2001, consisting of establishing shots of New York City and minimal video of the September 11 attacks out of respect for the families of the victims.<ref name="Collider-Sept25"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2024/09/megalopolis-francis-ford-coppola-interview-1236085381/|title=Francis Coppola & Adam Driver On The Slow Death Of Journalism & Studios; How ''Megalopolis'' Reception Might Evolve Like ''Apocalypse Now'' Did|date=September 26, 2024|first=Mike Jr.|last=Fleming|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=September 26, 2024|archive-date=September 26, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240926213555/https://deadline.com/2024/09/megalopolis-francis-ford-coppola-interview-1236085381/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Alleged conflicts on set ===
==== Creative differences ====
Plaza spoke about Coppola's spontaneous approach to filmmaking, explaining that he would often come up with new ideas on the spot. At times, this resulted in sudden location changes and unexpected shifts in the day's shooting plans, leaving actors unaware of what to expect as the day unfolded.<ref name="DeadlineMay2024"/> Some crew members described that approach as "exasperating" and "old-school", as Coppola was hesitant to decide how the film would look and would spend work days completing shots practically instead of relying on digital techniques. A crew member recounted that Coppola frequently arrived on set in the mornings before major sequences without a clear plan. Since he refused to let his collaborators establish one, he often spent hours in his trailer, avoiding communication and reportedly smoking marijuana. When he eventually emerged, he would improvise scenes that disregarded prior discussions and the script, leaving the crew to adapt. On Driver's first day on set, Coppola allegedly took six hours to achieve an effect by projecting an image on the side of Driver's head.<ref name="TheGuardian2024"/> Coppola denied smoking marijuana on set, adding that he had been avoiding the substance ever since his weight loss in 2017.<ref name="WSJ-Sept26"/>

On December 9, 2022, Coppola fired most of the [[visual effects]] team, with the rest of the department, including supervisor Mark Russell, soon following. In January 2023, reports indicated the budget ballooned higher than its initial $120{{nbsp}}million, which ''The Hollywood Reporter'' compared to Coppola's history of challenging productions, most notoriously ''Apocalypse Now''. Due to an alleged "unstable filming environment", a claim Coppola and Driver contested, other crew members exited the film, including production designer Beth Mickle and art director David Scott, along with the [[art department]].<ref name="Budget"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2023/01/francis-ford-coppola-no-truth-to-apocalypse-on-megalopolis-1235216222/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola: No Truth to Apocalypse on ''Megalopolis'' |last=Fleming |first=Mike Jr. |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=January 10, 2023 |access-date=January 10, 2023 |archive-date=January 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230110203401/https://deadline.com/2023/01/francis-ford-coppola-no-truth-to-apocalypse-on-megalopolis-1235216222/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Coppola replaced Russell with his nephew, Jesse James Chisholm, over a dispute over "live special effects", which he completed with his son and second unit director [[Roman Coppola]] as they had with ''Bram Stoker's Dracula''.<ref name="Production Notes"/>{{rp|9}}

Coppola further explained that he hired Mickle for her work in recreating 1950s New York for [[Edward Norton]]'s ''[[Motherless Brooklyn]]'' (2019) but that creative differences formed "to a degree that it was decided that the best thing would be if I hired a concept artist and came up with frames that showed what I wanted, which I did".<ref name="Empire-Aug29"/><ref name="WSJ-Sept26"/> Working with concept artist Dean Sherriff to translate his vision through [[keyframe]] concept art, which he described as similar in style to that of a woven mural or tapestry, he permitted minimal input from the art department, whose practices, having recently completed the [[Marvel Cinematic Universe]] film ''[[Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3]]'' (2023), he deemed conventional, expensive, and hierarchical.<ref name="Production Notes"/>{{rp|8}}<ref name="WSJ-Sept26"/> "The art department was frustrated because they felt I was evolving the look of the picture independently of them", he said, "They wanted giant sets and images. I wanted other elements like costumes and live effects to do some of the work and have it not all be art-department-centric. So, there was disagreement along those lines".<ref name="Empire-Aug29"/> Coppola had originally set $100{{nbsp}}million for the budget and $20{{nbsp}}million as [[Cost contingency|contingency]]. As the budget was at risk of rising to $148{{nbsp}}million (which he said would have "bankrupted me and my family"), he laid off one of five art directors, leading the entire team to resign. Production allegedly wrapped a week ahead of schedule, with the budget close to the planned $120{{nbsp}}million, according to Coppola.<ref name="Production Notes"/>{{rp|8–9}}<ref name="RollingStone-0825"/> In contrast, one person involved with the film told ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' that production costs ultimately reached $136{{nbsp}}million.<ref name="WSJ-Sept26"/>

==== Allegations of misconduct ====
[[File:Tabernacle wide.jpg|thumb|alt=The interior of the Tabernacle in Atlanta, Georgia, in 2005.|Allegations of misconduct against Coppola were made related to days production took place inside the [[Tabernacle (concert hall)|Tabernacle]] (pictured in 2005)]]

Anonymous crew members characterized Coppola's on-set behavior as unprofessional. On February 14, 2023, a [[Studio 54]]–inspired club scene was filmed at the [[Tabernacle (concert hall)|Tabernacle]], a concert hall in Atlanta, with 150–200 [[Extra (acting)|extras]], some of whom were approved for topless or scantily clad appearances.<ref name="Variety-0726">{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2024/film/news/megalopolis-set-video-francis-ford-coppola-kissing-extras-1236082653/ |title=Video of Francis Ford Coppola Kissing ''Megalopolis'' Extras Surfaces as Crew Members Detail Unprofessional Behavior on Set (Exclusive) |last1=Lang |first1=Brent |last2=Siegel |first2=Tatiana |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=July 26, 2024 |access-date=July 27, 2024 |archive-date=July 26, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240726233638/https://variety.com/2024/film/news/megalopolis-set-video-francis-ford-coppola-kissing-extras-1236082653/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Coppola was accused of pulling women onto his lap and kissing female extras during the shoot. Executive producer Darren Demetre defended Coppola by stating that his hugs and kisses on the cheek to cast members and extras were affectionate gestures, emphasizing that no complaints of harassment or inappropriate behavior were brought to his attention during production.<ref name="TheGuardian2024"/> Addressing the allegations, Coppola referred to advice his mother gave him on treating women with respect and said his actions were not disrespectful; mentioned that one of the women he kissed on the cheek was someone he had known since she was young, and described himself as "too shy" to be touchy-feely.<ref name="NYTDargis">{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/06/06/movies/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-godfather.html |title=Francis Ford Coppola: 'You Can't Be an Artist and Be Safe' |last=Dargis |first=Manohla |author-link=Manohla Dargis |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=June 6, 2024 |access-date=June 6, 2024 |url-access=registration |archive-date=June 12, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240612003247/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/06/06/movies/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-godfather.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

In July 2024, videos surfaced showing interactions between Coppola and extras at the Tabernacle. Sources told ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' that Coppola frequently wandered into frame while engaging with background actors and, after multiple takes, made an announcement over a microphone apologizing in advance for kissing extras, claiming it was for his enjoyment. Another source highlighted the absence of a [[human resources department]] on set, while reports indicated that [[intimacy coordinator]]s were not present during filming. Additionally, senior crew members allegedly informed bystanders that they were prohibited from sharing recordings of the encounters due to [[non-disclosure agreement]]s.<ref name="Variety-0726"/> Days after the controversy surfaced, extras present during filming shared conflicting perspectives. Rayna Menz dismissed allegations of inappropriate behavior, insisting that Coppola did nothing to make her or anyone else on set uncomfortable.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2024/07/salacious-variety-megalopolis-video-a-sham-says-rayna-menz-extra-shown-with-francis-coppola-1236027166/ |title=Salacious Variety ''Megalopolis'' Video a Sham, Says Rayna Menz, the Extra Shown with Francis Coppola |last=Fleming |first=Mike Jr. |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=July 30, 2024 |access-date=July 30, 2024 |archive-date=August 24, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240824153022/https://deadline.com/2024/07/salacious-variety-megalopolis-video-a-sham-says-rayna-menz-extra-shown-with-francis-coppola-1236027166/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In contrast, Lauren Pagone expressed shock at being kissed and hugged unexpectedly, criticizing Menz's remarks by emphasizing that experiences varied. Another crew member claimed that Coppola kissed multiple women without warning after calling "cut" on a New Year's Eve party scene that ended with on-screen kisses.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2024/film/news/extra-kissed-francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-video-speaks-1236093806/ |title=Extra Kissed by Francis Ford Coppola in ''Megalopolis'' Set Video Breaks Silence: 'I Was in Shock' |last1=Siegel |first1=Tatiana |last2=Lang |first2=Brent |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=August 2, 2024 |access-date=August 3, 2024 |archive-date=August 3, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240803005449/https://variety.com/2024/film/news/extra-kissed-francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-video-speaks-1236093806/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Coppola defended himself by stating that the women he kissed on the cheek during the scene were individuals he had known personally.<ref name="RollingStone-0825"/> Coppola was later accused of "leering" at and kissing a 13-year-old female extra on set.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/i-saw-francis-ford-coppola-leer-at-13-year-girlthen-kiss-her-on-set-of-megalopolis/|title=I Saw Francis Ford Coppola 'Leer' at 13-Year-Girl—Then Kiss Her|date=October 14, 2024|first=Eboni|last=Boykin-Patterson|website=[[The Daily Beast]]|access-date=January 15, 2025}}</ref>

On September 9, Pagone filed a lawsuit against Coppola, his production company, and two casting agencies, accusing them of civil assault, civil [[Battery (crime)|battery]], and negligent failure to prevent [[sexual harassment]].<ref name="AJC-Sept10">{{cite web |url=https://www.ajc.com/news/business/extra-files-lawsuit-alleging-sexual-harassment-on-set-of-megalopolis/XDZZ2QWNPBCXTGOZJ2PQEESDHI/ |title=Coppola faces sexual harassment suit for alleged ''Megalopolis'' incident |date=September 10, 2024 |first=Savannah |last=Sicurella |website=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |access-date=September 10, 2024 |url-access=subscription |archive-date=October 7, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007025643/https://www.ajc.com/news/business/extra-files-lawsuit-alleging-sexual-harassment-on-set-of-megalopolis/XDZZ2QWNPBCXTGOZJ2PQEESDHI/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Deadline-Sept11">{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2024/09/francis-ford-coppola-sues-variety-megalopolis-set-behavior-1236085693/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola Sues Variety Over ''Megalopolis'' On-Set Behavior Article After Extra Takes Director To Court In Georgia |date=September 11, 2024 |first=Dominic |last=Patten |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |access-date=September 12, 2024 |archive-date=October 7, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007025818/https://deadline.com/2024/09/francis-ford-coppola-sues-variety-megalopolis-set-behavior-1236085693/ |url-status=live}}</ref> She claimed that during the club scene filmed on February 14, Coppola kissed her on the cheek and touched her back and waist without consent. Additionally, she alleged that he made inappropriate remarks about her appearance and urged her to sit on his lap and refer to him as "uncle".<ref name="AJC-Sept10"/><ref name="TheWrap-Sept17">{{cite web|url=https://www.thewrap.com/megalopolis-libel-suit-variety-francis-ford-coppola-what-happens/|title=''Megalopolis'' Libel Suit: Variety May Make Francis Ford Coppola an Offer He Can't Refuse, Legal Experts Say|date=September 17, 2024|first=Josh|last=Dickey|website=[[TheWrap]]|access-date=September 17, 2024|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240917162947/https://www.thewrap.com/megalopolis-libel-suit-variety-francis-ford-coppola-what-happens/|archive-date=September 17, 2024|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Coppola initially placed a [[cease-and-desist]] letter against ''Variety'' requesting a retraction of their July 26 article that featured videos of the encounters and described his behavior as unprofessional. After ''Variety'' published further articles regarding his alleged misconduct, he filed a [[libel lawsuit]] against them and journalists Brent Lang and Tatiana Siegel on September 10, seeking $15{{nbsp}}million and further punitive and exemplary damages.<ref name="Deadline-Sept11"/><ref name="TheWrap-Sept17"/> In the lawsuit, Coppola challenged the videos' credibility and denied claims that the production did not have a human resources department and that he often inadvertently inserted himself into frame, describing any such instances of the crew being in frame as "anticipated and unavoidable".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-lawsuits-1235999955/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' Drama Now Turns to the Courtroom |date=September 12, 2024 |first=Winston |last=Cho |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |access-date=September 12, 2024 |archive-date=September 12, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240912203905/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-lawsuits-1235999955/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Post-production ===
{{See also|Megalopolis (soundtrack)}}

The son of a classical musician who wrote pieces for ''The Godfather'' and ''Apocalypse Now'', Coppola wanted a non-Hollywood composer. In March 2003, he hand-wrote a letter to Argentinian composer [[Osvaldo Golijov]], and afterward invited him to his home to discuss ''Megalopolis'', asking him to compose a [[symphony]] that would have dictated the film's rhythm.<ref name="Production Notes"/>{{rp|20}}<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/music/features/osvaldo-golijov-composing-the-soundtrack-for-a-coppola-movie-345398.html |title=Osvaldo Golijov: Composing the soundtrack for a Coppola movie |last=Church |first=Michael |website=[[The Independent]] |date=February 14, 2006 |access-date=April 1, 2024 |archive-date=April 1, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240401154233/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/music/features/osvaldo-golijov-composing-the-soundtrack-for-a-coppola-movie-345398.html |url-status=live}}</ref> They would go on to collaborate on ''Youth Without Youth'', ''Tetro'', and ''Twixt'' before returning to complete ''Megalopolis''. Golijov wanted the score to "blur the line between music and sound design." Given the ambiguity surrounding how the city and music of Rome sounded, he relied on Hollywood portrayals and composed a Roman [[Suite (music)|suite]] inspired by [[Miklós Rózsa]]'s [[Ben-Hur (1959 film)#Musical score|score]] for ''[[Ben-Hur (1959 film)|Ben-Hur]]'' (1959). Coppola also asked Golijov to write a [[Love song|love theme]] in the vein of [[Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky]]'s composition ''[[Romeo and Juliet (Tchaikovsky)|Romeo and Juliet]]'' (1870).<ref name="Production Notes"/>{{rp|20–21}} In February 2024, Coppola recorded the score with the Budapest Art Orchestra in Budapest, Hungary.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://hungarytoday.hu/director-francis-ford-coppola-makes-a-splash-during-his-stay-in-budapest/ |title=Director Francis Ford Coppola Makes a Splash during Stay in Budapest |website=Hungary Today |date=February 18, 2024 |access-date=May 18, 2024 |archive-date=May 18, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240518155557/https://hungarytoday.hu/director-francis-ford-coppola-makes-a-splash-during-his-stay-in-budapest/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The suite was eventually played in concert by the [[Chicago Symphony Orchestra]] conducted by [[Riccardo Muti]] on November 7-9, 2024.<ref>[https://news.wttw.com/2024/11/11/maestro-muti-and-cso-soar-brilliant-world-premiere-and-4-exhilarating-classics-review Maestro Muti and the CSO Soar With a Brilliant World Premiere and 4 Exhilarating Classics: Review|Chicago News|WTTW]</ref><ref>[https://cso.org/experience/article/20579/osvaldo-golijov-eager-to-hear-the-incredible Osvaldo Golijov eager to hear ‘the incredible CSO’ in his Megalopolis Suite – Chicago Symphony Orchestra]</ref>

Post-production, from editing to visual effects, was completed at the All-Movie Hotel, where some reshoots were held.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2024/artisans/news/francis-ford-coppola-all-movie-hotel-georgia-1236062350/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola Opens Hotel for Filmmakers and Public in Georgia With On-Site Post-Production Facilities (Exclusive) |date=July 10, 2024 |first=Jazz |last=Tangcay |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=August 21, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2024/09/09/is-a-stay-at-francis-ford-coppolas-hotel-an-offer-you-cant-refuse |url-access=limited |title=Is a Stay at Francis Ford Coppola's Hotel an Offer You Can't Refuse? |date=September 2, 2024 |first=Charles |last=Bethea |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |access-date=September 2, 2024 |archive-date=September 24, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240924060953/https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2024/09/09/is-a-stay-at-francis-ford-coppolas-hotel-an-offer-you-cant-refuse |url-status=live}}</ref> Cam McLauchlin and [[Glen Scantlebury]] edited the film, Coppola having contacted McLauchlin after seeing his work on ''[[Nightmare Alley (2021 film)|Nightmare Alley]]'' (2021).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/ontario-boom-hollywood-collaboration-dgc-tiff-1235981761/ |title=Ontario's Behind-the-Camera Talent Boom Sparks Hollywood Collaborations With Global Impact |date=September 7, 2024 |first=Etan |last=Vlessing |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|access-date=September 7, 2024|archive-date=September 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240907181754/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/ontario-boom-hollywood-collaboration-dgc-tiff-1235981761/|url-status=live}}</ref> McLauchlin defined Coppola's style as theatrical, incorporating theater warm-up techniques. During rehearsal, Cesar and Julia improvised a [[tug-of-war]] with an imaginary rope, a spontaneous moment encouraging them to embrace the script's eccentricity. McLauchlin and Scantlebury were tasked to work on scenes independently but transitioned toward collaboration after realizing they had enough time to keep pace with shooting and experiment with alternate versions. As they edited the film, Coppola was inspired to direct more "unusual takes" of the cast to include.<ref name="Collider-Sept25">{{cite web |url=https://collider.com/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-meaning/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola Reveals the Real Message Behind ''Megalopolis'' |last1=Weisman |first1=Jake |last2=Weintraub |first2=Steven |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |date=September 25, 2024 |access-date=September 26, 2024 |archive-date=October 7, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007031137/https://collider.com/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-meaning/ |url-status=live}}</ref> For a catwalk scene, Coppola mitigated disruptive noise by pre-recording the dialogue and playing it over a loudspeaker for wide shots. As an apparent warm-up exercise, he then had Driver recite the full "[[To be, or not to be]]" soliloquy from Shakespeare's ''[[Hamlet]]'' (1623).<ref name="Empire-Aug29">{{cite web |url=https://gb.readly.com/magazines/empire/2024-08-29/66d07850ff4b9bc5768172af|url-access=limited |title=Building the future |via=[[Readly]] |date=August 29, 2024 |first=Ian |last=Freer|author-link=Ian Freer |website=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]]|access-date=September 2, 2024|archive-date=September 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240907181734/https://gb.readly.com/magazines/empire/2024-08-29/66d07850ff4b9bc5768172af|url-status=live}}</ref> After filming wrapped, Coppola handed McLauchlin the first half of the film and Scantlebury the latter half, allowing them to trade sections to complete the edit. After Scantlebury moved on to another project, McLauchlin and Coppola continued editing for eight more months, during which Coppola suggested including the Shakespeare scene.<ref name="Production Notes"/>{{rp|18–20}} In addition to starring, VanderWaal, a musician who won ''[[America's Got Talent]]'' at age 12 in 2016, wrote two original songs for the film.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2024/music/news/grace-vanderwaal-new-music-megalopolis-americas-got-talent-1236147242/|title=Grace VanderWaal Grows Up: With New Music and ''Megalopolis'' Role, the ''America{{'}}s Got Talent'' Winner Is Coming Into Her Own — Even if It Makes 'People Really Uncomfortable'|date=September 20, 2024|first=Ellise|last=Shafer|website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=September 20, 2024|archive-date=September 20, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240920150202/https://variety.com/2024/music/news/grace-vanderwaal-new-music-megalopolis-americas-got-talent-1236147242/|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Themes ==
=== Rome's example for America ===
[[File:Cicero Denounces Catiline in the Roman Senate by Cesare Maccari.png|thumb|''Megalopolis'' was inspired by the [[Catilinarian conspiracy]]. In [[Cesare Maccari]]'s 1888 painting of the incident, Catiline (right) is depicted sitting alone, deserted by his followers, while Cicero (standing on the left) publicly humiliates him.<ref name="NationalGeographic">{{Cite web |last=Wakeman |first=Gregory |date=October 7, 2024 |title=The real ancient Roman plot that inspired ''Megalopolis'' |url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/history/article/megalopolis-movie-cicero-catiline-conspiracy |access-date=October 7, 2024 |website=[[National Geographic Society]]}}</ref>|350x350px]]

''Megalopolis'' is both a modern retelling of the [[Catilinarian conspiracy]] and a revisionist look at the source material. Coppola described the film as a commentary on the American political system, reasoning that the Roman analogy was appropriate because the American Founding Fathers borrowed from [[Roman law]] to develop their [[Democracy|democratic government]] without a king.<ref name="VanityFair-043024"/> He specifically noted that America was vulnerable to the same political forces and tensions that destroyed the Roman Republic and created the Empire.<ref name="NationalGeographic"/>

''Megalopolis'' was not the first time Coppola had sought to modernize a historical narrative: he had previously updated the colonial-Africa setting of ''[[Heart of Darkness]]'' (1899) to the [[Vietnam War]] for ''[[Apocalypse Now]]'' (1979).<ref name="Production Notes" />{{rp|4}} Nor was it the first time that an artist had offered a revisionist look at Catiline: [[Henrik Ibsen]]'s play ''[[Catiline (play)|Catiline]]'' reimagined Catiline as a "highly principled [man] pitted against the corruption of the world in which he lived".<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Beard |first=Mary |date=October 2, 2015 |title=Mary Beard: why ancient Rome matters to the modern world |url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2015/oct/02/mary-beard-why-ancient-rome-matters |access-date=March 17, 2025 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

==== Allusions to Roman historical figures ====
The two male leads in ''Megalopolis'' directly reference the opposing sides in the Catilinarian conspiracy. Protagonist Cesar Catilina is a double reference to populist politician [[Lucius Sergius Catilina]] (anglicized to Catiline), who plotted to overthrow the Roman Republic in 63 BC, and his occasional political ally [[Julius Caesar]].<ref name="VanityFair-043024" /><ref name="NationalGeographic" /> Antagonist Franklyn Cicero references Catiline and Caesar's political rival, [[Marcus Tullius Cicero]], the leader of the Roman conservatives and the [[Roman consul|consul]] (head of the Roman government) during the conspiracy.<ref name="4Columns-Oct07">{{Cite web |last=Pinkerton |first=Nick |title=Megalopolis |url=https://4columns.org/pinkerton-nick/megalopolis |access-date=October 7, 2024 |website=4columns.org}}</ref> Although Caesar was not implicated in the conspiracy, he famously sought to prevent Catiline's execution.<ref name="ScreenRant-Oct07">{{Cite web |last=Hood |first=Cooper |date=September 28, 2024 |title=Megalopolis: The Catilinarian Conspiracy's History & Movie Inspiration Explained |url=https://screenrant.com/megalopolis-catilinarian-conspiracy-history-inspiration-explained/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006051002/https://screenrant.com/megalopolis-catilinarian-conspiracy-history-inspiration-explained/ |archive-date=October 6, 2024 |access-date=October 7, 2024 |website=[[Screen Rant]]}}</ref>

Several supporting characters were also based on Roman notables. Cesar Catilina's mentor Hamilton Crassus references [[Marcus Licinius Crassus]], one of the richest men in Rome and a power broker who facilitated Caesar's rise to the Roman dictatorship.<ref name="4Columns-Oct07" /> Catilina's enemy Clodio Pulcher references [[Publius Clodius Pulcher]], a patrician turned populist demagogue who sponsored a counter-reaction to Cicero's punishment of Catiline's supporters;<ref name="ScreenRant-Oct07" /> in addition, the manner of Clodio's death in the film is a possible allusion to the [[death of Benito Mussolini]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Russo |first=Jude |date=October 3, 2024 |title='Megalopolis' Now |url=https://modernagejournal.com/megalopolis-now/245116/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241203103030/https://modernagejournal.com/megalopolis-now/245116/ |archive-date=December 3, 2024 |access-date=February 18, 2025 |website=Modern Age |language=en-US}}</ref> Pop star Vesta Sweetwater and her chastity pledge reference the [[Vestal Virgins]], Roman priestesses who swore an oath to remain chaste for 30 years. The real-life Catiline was accused of seducing a Vestal Virgin, an offense punishable by death.<ref name="DenofGeek">{{Cite web |last=George |first=Joe |date=September 27, 2024 |title=The Weirdest and Wildest Moments in Megalopolis |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/movies/the-weirdest-and-wildest-moments-in-megalopolis/ |access-date=October 7, 2024 |website=Den of Geek}}</ref>

Not every character name was an allusion to ancient Rome. Coppola came up with the "Wow Platinum" name after hearing about a woman who was nicknamed "[[wikt:wow|Wow]]" for her great beauty.<ref name="twitter.com"/>

==== Revisionist narrative and historicity ====
In contrast to most academic historians, ''Megalopolis'' portrays its Catiline stand-in as the protagonist and Cicero as the antagonist (albeit a well-meaning one). In 1999, Coppola [[Pitch (filmmaking)|pitched]] the film by drawing parallels between the Catilinarian conspiracy and the present-day United States. He warned that Catiline-esque plotters could try to overthrow the American government just as Catiline tried to overthrow Rome, saying, "Rome became a fascist Empire. Is that what we're going to become?"<ref name=":0">{{cite interview |last=Coppola |first=Francis Ford |subject-link=Francis Ford Coppola |interviewer=Ann Nocenti |title=Writing and Directing ''The Conversation'': A Talk with Francis Ford Coppola |url=http://www.scenariomag.com/interviews/coppola.html |access-date=May 12, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20001215150700/http://www.scenariomag.com/interviews/coppola.html |archive-date=December 15, 2000 |url-status=usurped |website=Scenario |number=1 |date=1999 |interviewer-link=Ann Nocenti |volume=5}}</ref> However, in his production notes written a quarter-century later, Coppola explained that at the time, he had not yet written a script and his views reflected the traditional narrative.<ref name="Production Notes" />{{rp|4}} According to that narrative, [[Catiline]] was a populist seditionist who plotted to overthrow the [[Roman Republic]] after losing the election for [[Roman consul|consul]] three times.<ref name="NationalGeographic" /> [[Cicero]], the head of the Roman government, discovered the plot and drove Catiline out of the city,<ref name="Production Notes" />{{rp|7}} after which Catiline was killed at the [[Battle of Pistoria]].<ref name="NationalGeographic" /> Cicero memorialized his actions by publishing the [[Catilinarian orations]]. Although the conspiracy failed, populist politician [[Julius Caesar]] later took advantage of [[Crisis of the Roman Republic|political chaos]] to become [[dictator of Rome]], paving the way for the [[Roman Empire]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=Oltermann |first=Philip |date=May 17, 2024 |title=Francis Ford Coppola: US politics is at 'the point where we might lose our republic' |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/article/2024/may/17/francis-ford-coppola-us-politics-republic-rome-megalopolis-cannes |access-date=March 16, 2025 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

Coppola rethought the analogy as ''Megalopolis'' languished in [[development hell]]. As early as 1999, he noted that Roman histories of the Catilinarian conspiracy were largely based on Cicero's own retelling of the incident.<ref name=":0" /> In 2008, he said that while the standard narrative of the conspiracy posited that Catiline "was going to take over the city and burn it", he was more interested in the hypothetical of Catiline trying to build "a new society". He said that he wanted to tell a "political fantasy" about "an enlightened [[Robert Moses]], more like an [[Ayn Rand]]", elaborating that "the Ayn Rand character [that is, Howard Roark in ''[[The Fountainhead]]''] wanted to build a city within New York that was the model of what a city could be."<ref name="Film Comment" /> At some point, Coppola began questioning whether Cicero, a political conservative, had simply concocted an excuse to crush the populist policies backed by Catiline and Julius Caesar.<ref name="VanityFair-043024" /> In ''Megalopolis'', Coppola retells two of the real-life Cicero's accusations towards Catiline – that Catiline slept with a Vestal Virgin (a Roman priestess sworn to chastity)<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cadoux |first=T. J. |date=2005 |title=Catiline and the Vestal Virgins |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/4436764 |url-status=live |journal=Historia: Zeitschrift für Alte Geschichte |volume=54 |issue=2 |pages=166–67 |issn=0018-2311 |jstor=4436764 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007224424/https://www.jstor.org/stable/4436764 |archive-date=October 7, 2024 |access-date=October 7, 2024}}</ref> and that Catiline murdered his first wife<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wood |first=Michael |date=October 14, 2024 |title=Michael Wood · At the Movies: 'Megalopolis' |url=https://www.lrb.co.uk/the-paper/v46/n20/michael-wood/at-the-movies |access-date=March 12, 2025 |work=London Review of Books |language=en |volume=46 |issue=20 |issn=0260-9592}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Oratio in Catilinam Prima VI.13-16 Notes |url=https://classics.osu.edu/Undergraduate-Studies/Latin-Program/Catiline/vi13-16/vi13-16-notes |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007224424/https://classics.osu.edu/Undergraduate-Studies/Latin-Program/Catiline/vi13-16/vi13-16-notes |archive-date=October 7, 2024 |access-date=October 7, 2024 |website=The Ohio State University}}</ref> – and acquits Cesar Catilina of both accusations.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Acharya |first=Amartya |date=November 13, 2024 |title=Megalopolis (2024) Movie Ending Explained & Themes Analyzed: What Does Coppola's Magnum Opus Really Want to Say? |url=https://www.highonfilms.com/megalopolis-2024-movie-ending-explained-themes-analysed/ |access-date=March 16, 2025 |website=High On Films |language=en-US}}</ref>

Coppola remained interested in the crisis of Roman republicanism, of which the Catilinarian conspiracy was a part. When promoting the film, he linked its subject matter to what he saw as rising "neo-right, even fascist" tendencies in the United States and abroad, explaining that "what's happening in America, in our republic, in our democracy, is exactly how Rome lost their republic thousands of years ago."<ref name=":2" /> However, in the film, the seditionists plotting to destroy the republic are led by Clodio Pulcher, not Catilina.<ref name="4Columns-Oct07" />

The film's lionization of Catiline diverges from the academic mainstream, although the precise extent is disputed. According to [[Richard Saller]], while the traditional narrative is "Cicero centric", most historians – [[Robin Seager]] being a notable exception – reject the revisionist argument that "Cicero really manufactured the conspiracy".<ref name="NationalGeographic" /> [[Mary Beard (classicist)|Mary Beard]], who received a film credit for her historical advice on the film,<ref name="Production Notes" />{{rp||page=37}} took an intermediate position. In her 2015 book [[SPQR: A History of Ancient Rome|''SPQR'']], she agreed that Catiline was "a disgruntled, bankrupt aristocrat",<ref name="NYTDargis"/> but cautioned that his populist concern for ordinary people may have been genuine.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mount |first=Ferdinand |date=November 20, 2015 |title=Mary Beard's 'SPQR' and Tom Holland's 'Dynasty' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/11/22/books/review/mary-beards-spqr-and-tom-hollands-dynasty.html |access-date=March 17, 2025 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> With respect to Cicero, she conceded that Cicero "probably believed" that Catiline was actually plotting a coup,<ref name=":3" /> but noted that "there is still disagreement about how far the 'reds under the bed' were a figment of Cicero's conservative imagination or paranoia".<ref name=":3" /> She had previously suggested that Cicero needed a major accomplishment as consul to secure his long-term political future and may have been "spoiling for a fight".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Beard |first=Mary |date=August 23, 2001 |title=Lucky City |url=https://www.lrb.co.uk/the-paper/v23/n16/mary-beard/lucky-city |access-date=March 16, 2025 |work=London Review of Books |language=en |volume=23 |issue=16 |issn=0260-9592}}</ref>

=== Artistic idealism as antidote to polarization ===
In 2008, Coppola stated that the character of Cesar Catilina would be inspired by the life of urban planner [[Robert Moses]], who built much of the infrastructure of modern-day New York City, but was criticized for favoring wealthy political interests and ignoring the needs of New York's [[ethnic minorities]]. Coppola said that he wanted to imagine an "enlightened" version of Moses that preserved Moses's desire to build a better city.<ref name="Film Comment"/>

''Megalopolis'' argues that for a [[democracy]] to avoid falling into [[fascism]], it needs a bold and inspirational vision for the future, which artists can help provide. In 1999, Coppola said that "Rome didn't fall for a long time. But how does an Empire die? It dies when its people no longer believe in it".<ref name=":0"/> In 2022, Coppola said his film would offer an optimistic look at humanity and the intuitive goodness in people even in a divided climate. He criticized fellow [[New York Military Academy]] alumnus [[Donald Trump]] for calling Mexicans criminal rapists, saying that "dictators and populists stay in power by having you hate someone else. ... [P]eople are in the habit of saying all people are bad ... We're doing...better. We could be proud of being human beings".<ref name=":1">{{cite web |last=Fleming |first=Mike Jr. |date=March 25, 2022 |title=From ''The Godfather'' Trilogy to ''American Graffiti'', ''Patton'', ''The Conversation'' & ''Apocalypse Now'', Francis Ford Coppola Shares His Oscar Memories |url=https://deadline.com/2022/03/francis-ford-coppola-oscars-memories-godfather-patton-apocalypse-now-1234986966/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240508005526/https://deadline.com/2022/03/francis-ford-coppola-oscars-memories-godfather-patton-apocalypse-now-1234986966/ |archive-date=May 8, 2024 |access-date=May 6, 2024 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref>

The film concludes with Cesar Catilina delivering an impassioned speech that persuades the public to embrace the vision of Megalopolis. Writing for ''[[The New Yorker]]'', [[Justin Chang]] observed that Coppola's struggle to complete the film without studio interference lent the narrative an unintended layer of self-reflection. He described ''Megalopolis'' as an artistic defense of beauty and ambition, arguing that its existence was a statement of hope.<ref name="Chang"/> Coppola himself acknowledged the value of visionary ideas but rejected the notion that Catilina's project should prescribe a specific vision of the future, asserting instead that utopia is not a fixed destination but an ongoing conversation.<ref name=":1"/>

=== Art versus politics ===
In addition to Moses, Coppola based the character of Cesar Catilina and his invention of Megalon on the novels of Ayn Rand.<ref name="Film Comment"/> Catilina specifically resembles two Rand characters who struggle to implement their ideas in the face of the dominant political establishment, which may be either conservative or left-wing. In ''[[The Fountainhead]]'' (1943), modernist architect Howard Roark struggles to be taken seriously by a conservative artistic establishment that insists on aping the architecture of ancient Rome.<ref name="4Columns-Oct07"/> In ''[[Atlas Shrugged]]'' (1957), visionary inventor Hank Rearden creates a high-performance metal alloy, which is subsequently nationalized by a left-wing government. ''Megalopolis'' depicts Cesar Catilina's modernist utopia under simultaneous attack by the left and the right: Cicero's conservatives reject Catilina's bold vision as fanciful, while Pulcher's radicals deride Catilina's ideas as pointlessly extravagant. Writing in ''[[The New York Times]]'', [[Ross Douthat]] commented that "the central conflict isn't really left versus right .... Instead, [''Megalopolis''] pits Catilina ... against various forces representing inertia and sterility: the uncomprehending establishment and the ungrateful masses, ... all ranged against the man of genius".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Douthat |first=Ross |date=October 4, 2024 |title="Megalopolis" and the Vexations of Decadence |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/10/04/opinion/coppola-megalopolis-decadence.html |access-date=October 7, 2024 |work=The New York Times |archive-date=October 7, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007224359/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/10/04/opinion/coppola-megalopolis-decadence.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

During the press tour, Coppola said that he was interested in telling a story about a man who "would have brought something wonderful," until "what usually happens happened—the traditional forces subdued the new idea."<ref name=":7"/> He used the character of Mayor Cicero to demonstrate how "a conservative and a classicist" opposes an "enlightened artist",<ref name=":7" /> adding that Cicero was "committed to a regressive status quo" that puts greed and partisan politics over the public good. He concluded that although Cicero "truly wants to save the city", he embodied "despair" instead of hope for a better society, and no longer entertains "transformative ideas".<ref name="Production Notes"/>{{rp|6, 9, 11}} Coppola compared Cicero to several mayors of New York City (mainly [[Ed Koch]], but also [[David Dinkins]] at one point).<ref name="Film Comment"/><ref name=":0"/><ref name=":7" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cowie |first=Peter |date=September 1990 |title=The Family |url=https://archive.org/details/blitz93_sept_1990/page/44/ |journal=[[Blitz (British magazine)|Blitz]] |issue=93 |pages=44–50 |via=Internet Archive}}</ref>

Although Coppola's press statements largely focused on Cicero over Pulcher, ''[[Den of Geek]]'' noted that Pulcher "serves as the [[Trumpism|Trump]] stand-in" and that "it's unclear if Coppola's trying to evoke the opulence of the Roman ruling classes or Trump's obsession with spray tans and hair-pieces or both".<ref name="DenofGeek"/> ''[[The Sweet East]]'' (2023) screenwriter Nick Pinkerton expressed concern that Pulcher's rapid recruitment of working-class populists implied that "the plebeians [are] easily manipulated rubes, a curious omission in a movie that's positioned as a humanist hymn to our species' higher potential".<ref name="4Columns-Oct07"/>

== Release ==
=== Distribution ===
Coppola saw ''Megalopolis'' in full for the first time on an [[IMAX]] screen at the headquarters of [[IMAX Corporation]] in [[Playa Vista, Los Angeles]]. The film used camera technology for certain sequences that could cover an entire IMAX screen.<ref name="Uphill Battle"/> On March 28, 2024, a private screening was presented to distributors at the [[Universal CityWalk#Universal CityWalk Hollywood|Universal CityWalk]] IMAX Theater in Hollywood. Coppola and his longtime attorney Barry Hirsch, a producer on the film, said they would not decide where to debut the film until they secured a [[Film distribution|distribution partner]] and a firm rollout plan.<ref name="Screening">{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2024/03/francis-coppola-megalopolis-first-screening-distributors-citywalk-imax-1235871124/ |title=Francis Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' Screened for First Time Today for Distributors at CityWalk IMAX |last=Fleming |first=Mike Jr. |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=March 28, 2024 |access-date=March 30, 2024 |archive-date=March 30, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240330021515/https://deadline.com/2024/03/francis-coppola-megalopolis-first-screening-distributors-citywalk-imax-1235871124/ |url-status=live}}</ref> However, the "muted" response to the screening made securing a distributor difficult. Studios weighed the return on investment, as Coppola expected a print-and-advertising (P&A) campaign of $80–100{{nbsp}}million and for producers to receive half of the film's revenues.<ref name="Uphill Battle"/><ref name="Distribution Deal">{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2024/film/news/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-in-talks-french-distribution-deal-le-pacte-1235979859/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' Nears French Distribution Deal with Indie Banner Le Pacte |last=Keslassy |first=Elsa |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=April 23, 2024 |access-date=April 26, 2024 |archive-date=April 24, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240424170703/https://variety.com/2024/film/news/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-in-talks-french-distribution-deal-le-pacte-1235979859/ |url-status=live}}</ref> A distribution veteran suggested that "If [Coppola] is willing to put up the P&A or backstop the spend, I think there would be a lot more interested parties".<ref name="Uphill Battle"/>

Coppola's plan to forgo a sales agent was, thus, altered, with [[Wild Bunch (company)|Goodfellas]] handling international sales; [[Le Pacte]], for France, became the first to acquire distribution rights to a foreign market in late April.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.screendaily.com/news/goodfellas-boards-international-sales-on-francis-ford-coppolas-cannes-selection-megalopolis-exclusive/5192899.article |title=Goodfellas boards international sales on Francis Ford Coppola's Cannes Selection ''Megalopolis'' (exclusive) |last=Kay |first=Jeremy |website=[[Screen International#Screen Daily|Screen Daily]] |date=April 30, 2024 |access-date=April 30, 2024 |archive-date=May 1, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240501174131/https://www.screendaily.com/news/goodfellas-boards-international-sales-on-francis-ford-coppolas-cannes-selection-megalopolis-exclusive/5192899.article |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2024/05/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-new-deals-1235927358/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola's Cannes Contender ''Megalopolis'' Inks Another Raft of International Distribution Deals |last=Goodfellow |first=Melanie |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=May 22, 2024 |access-date=May 22, 2024 |archive-date=May 22, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240522193327/https://deadline.com/2024/05/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-new-deals-1235927358/ |url-status=live}}</ref> ''Variety'' noted that individual territories were not given rights to paid [[video on demand]] or streaming options, "perhaps by design to lure a big [[streaming service]]" into buying the streaming rights after its theatrical run. On May 15, ''Variety'' reported on sources that said Coppola was seeking an "awards-savvy distributor", such as [[A24]], to release ''Megalopolis'' in the fourth quarter of 2024 so it could have an awards season campaign, but that "some potential indie outfits" who saw the film did not envision "much [[Oscars]] potential beyond technical categories" and "fear[ed] that Coppola [would] be an overly demanding partner".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2024/film/news/megalopolis-francis-ford-coppola-cannes-premiere-controversy-1236004301/ |title=Can Cannes Save ''Megalopolis''? Francis Ford Coppola Prepares to Unveil His $120 Million Epic as Controversy Builds |last1=Lang |first1=Brent |last2=Siegel |first2=Tatiana |last3=Donnelly |first3=Matt |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=May 15, 2024 |access-date=May 15, 2024 |archive-date=May 15, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240515163058/https://variety.com/2024/film/news/megalopolis-francis-ford-coppola-cannes-premiere-controversy-1236004301/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

The deal involved Coppola handling marketing costs, estimated to be $15–20{{nbsp}}million.<ref name="Deadline-OpeningWk"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-lionsgate-1235926557/ |title=How Francis Ford Coppola's Embattled ''Megalopolis'' Finally Landed a Distributor |last1=Couch |first1=Aaron |last2=Masters |first2=Kim |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=June 20, 2024 |access-date=June 20, 2024 |archive-date=June 20, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240620224114/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-lionsgate-1235926557/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Lionsgate previously worked on the home video releases of the [[director's cut]]s of Coppola's films, beginning in 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/news/breaking-news/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-sets-release-date-lionsgate-acquisition-1235001151/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' to Be Released This September by Lionsgate |last=Welk |first=Brian |website=[[IndieWire]] |date=June 17, 2024 |access-date=June 17, 2024 |archive-date=June 17, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240617170433/https://www.indiewire.com/news/breaking-news/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-sets-release-date-lionsgate-acquisition-1235001151/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/lionsgate-zoetrope-ink-distribution-deal-25925/|title=Lionsgate, Zoetrope ink distribution deal|date=July 26, 2010|first=Etan|last=Vlessing|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|access-date=September 22, 2024|archive-date=October 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007025643/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/lionsgate-zoetrope-ink-distribution-deal-25925/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Deadline-OpeningWk"/>

The private industry screening and multiple festival premieres, including Cannes, had a person walk on stage in front of the projection screen and address the protagonist, Cesar, who seemingly breaks the [[fourth wall]] by replying in real time.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gq.com/story/megalopolis-is-even-wilder-than-youve-heard |title=''Megalopolis'' is Even Wilder Than You Might've Heard |last=LeBeau |first=Ariel |website=[[GQ]] |date=May 22, 2024 |access-date=May 22, 2024 |url-access=limited |archive-date=May 22, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240522135824/https://www.gq.com/story/megalopolis-is-even-wilder-than-youve-heard |url-status=live}}</ref> Jean Labadie, founder of the film's French distributor, Le Pacte, said in regards to replicating the moment, "We will work on that with every exhibitor in France to try to do it as many times as we can".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2024/05/megalopolis-will-buyers-break-fourth-wall-france-le-pacte-1235923087/ |title=''Megalopolis'': Will Distributors Replicate One of the Movie's Most Talked About Moments? |access-date=May 19, 2024 |archive-date=May 19, 2024 similar pledge in regards to the fourth wall break;<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2024/06/megalopolis-lionsgate-francis-ford-coppola-1235975886/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' to Be Released by Lionsgate in U.S. |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=June 17, 2024 |access-date=June 22, 2024 |archive-date=June 18, 2024 recruited performers for screenings labeled "The Ultimate Experience" to accomplish the scene.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/news/business/how-will-theaters-handle-megalopolis-live-scene-adam-driver-1235050576/|title=How Will Theaters Handle the ''Megalopolis'' Live Scene with Adam Driver When it Opens Wide?|date=September 26, 2024|first=Brian|last=Welk|website=[[IndieWire]]|access-date=September 26, 2024|archive-date=September 26,
