Coppola had initially worked with [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]]'s support team in 2021 to accomplish the fourth wall break by developing a custom version of [[Amazon Alexa|Alexa]]'s voice-recognition software that would have allowed audiences to ask Driver's character a question about the plot, to which "Alexa would choose the most relevant answer from a pre-approved list". However, the partnership did not occur due to layoffs at Amazon in 2022. Driver suggested having a cinema usher ask a pre-agreed question instead.<ref name="TheTelegraph-Sept13">{{cite web |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/0/director-francis-ford-coppola-interview/|url-access=limited |title=Francis Ford Coppola: 'Hollywood doesn't want me any more' |date=September 13, 2024 |first=Robbie |last=Collin |website=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]|access-date=September 15, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240915001308/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/0/director-francis-ford-coppola-interview/|archive-date=September 15, 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

Although Coppola, by virtue of financing the film himself, presumably had full creative freedom, editor Cam McLauchlin alluded to a [[director's cut]] in the film's production notes. McLauchlin said that after the director's cut was produced, it took another eight months before Coppola signed off on the final cut.<ref name="Production Notes"/>{{rp|19}}

=== Marketing ===
==== Tie-ins and documentary ====
In March 2023, comic writer [[Chris Ryall]] and artist Jacob Phillips were announced to be producing a [[graphic novel]] tie-in to the film.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.comicsbeat.com/syzygy-announces-megalopolis-francis-ford-coppola-graphic-novel-at-wondercon/ |title=Syzygy announces ''Megalopolis'', Francis Ford Coppola graphic novel at WonderCon |last=Powell |first=Nancy |website=Comics Beat |date=March 25, 2023 |access-date=May 6, 2024 |archive-date=July 18, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240718202100/https://www.comicsbeat.com/syzygy-announces-megalopolis-francis-ford-coppola-graphic-novel-at-wondercon/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Phillips started drawing the 148-page book in December 2022 and finished in July 2024.<ref name=":6">{{cite web |url=https://bleedingcool.com/comics/jacob-phillips-finishes-adapting-francis-ford-coppolas-megalopolis/ |title=Jacob Phillips Finishes Adapting Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' |last=Johnston |first=Rich |website=[[Bleeding Cool]] |date=July 9, 2024 |access-date=July 11, 2024 |archive-date=July 10, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240710170435/https://bleedingcool.com/comics/jacob-phillips-finishes-adapting-francis-ford-coppolas-megalopolis/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Phillips said that he was allowed to use Coppola's screenplay and concept art from the film as source material, but that he had not seen any footage from the film before drawing the comic.<ref name=":6" /> Originally announced for a 2024 release by [[Image Comics]] and Syzygy Publishing, the graphic novel was later moved to [[Abrams ComicArts]] and published on October 7, 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2025/apr/25/francis-ford-coppola-unveils-megalopolis-graphic-novel |title=Francis Ford Coppola unveils Megalopolis graphic novel |last=Shoard |first=Catherine |website=[[The Guardian]] |date=April 25, 2025 |access-date=June 14, 2025 }}</ref>

Coppola teased that [[Colleen McCullough]] had written a [[novelization]] of the ''Megalopolis'' story before her death in 2015.<ref name=":5" /> In addition, [[Mike Figgis]] filmed a [[Behind-the-scenes|making-of documentary]], ''[[Megadoc]]'', featuring interviews with cast members, Spike Lee, George Lucas, Martin Scorsese, [[Steven Spielberg]], and Coppola's late wife [[Eleanor Coppola]], who died in April 2024 and to whom ''Megalopolis'' is [[Dedication (art)|dedicated]]. The documentary premiered at the [[82nd Venice International Film Festival]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jr |first=Mike Fleming |date=July 31, 2025 |title=Watch 'Megadoc' Trailer: Mike Figgis' Venice-Bound Doc On Francis Coppola's Making Of 'Megalopolis' |url=https://deadline.com/2025/07/megadoc-trailer-megalopolis-documentary-1236473672/ |access-date=August 5, 2025 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Empire-Aug29"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://thefilmstage.com/francis-ford-coppola-and-adam-driver-respond-to-megalopolis-rumors-mike-figgis-plans-a-behind-the-scenes-documentary/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola and Adam Driver Respond to ''Megalopolis'' Rumors; Mike Figgis Plans a Behind-the-Scenes Documentary |last=Newman |first=Nick |website=The Film Stage |date=January 10, 2023 |access-date=January 11, 2023 |archive-date=January 11, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230111003114/https://thefilmstage.com/francis-ford-coppola-and-adam-driver-respond-to-megalopolis-rumors-mike-figgis-plans-a-behind-the-scenes-documentary/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet |number=1711898739701416425 |title=Mike Figgis has interviewed Spike Lee and George Lucas for his documentary on Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' |user=TheFilmStage |date=October 11, 2023 |access-date=May 15, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2024/05/mike-figgis-mourns-fred-roos-megadoc-coppola-documentary-1235925174/ |title=Breaking Baz @ Cannes: Mike Figgis Mourns Fred Roos, Details Fly-on-the-Wall Coppola Documentary ''Megadoc''; Festival Party Talk Through the Night with Blanchett, Schrader & Oldman |last=Bamigboye |first=Baz |author-link=Baz Bamigboye |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=May 21, 2024 |access-date=May 22, 2024 |archive-date=May 22, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240522000042/https://deadline.com/2024/05/mike-figgis-mourns-fred-roos-megadoc-coppola-documentary-1235925174/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Coppola said that the projects were "independent" of him but were based on his "many scripts and ideas over the decades".<ref name=":4">{{cite web |url=https://collider.com/megalopolis-movie-cast-plot-filming-francis-ford-coppola/ |title=''Megalopolis'': Cast, Plot, Filming Details, and Everything We Know So Far About Francis Ford Coppola's Passion Project |last=Echebiri |first=Chike |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |date=May 7, 2024 |access-date=May 8, 2024 |archive-date=May 21, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240521014934/https://collider.com/megalopolis-movie-cast-plot-filming-francis-ford-coppola/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

==== Promotional materials ====
On August 16, 2024, Lionsgate announced a partnership with the company [[Utopia (distributor)|Utopia]] (co-founded by Coppola's nephew, [[Robert Schwartzman]])<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/news/general-news/utopia-help-lionsgate-distribute-market-megalopolis-1235037604/ |title=The Next Generation of Coppolas Will Help the Next Generation of Film Fans Discover ''Megalopolis'' |date=August 16, 2024 |first=Christian |last=Zilko |website=[[IndieWire]]|access-date=August 20, 2024|archive-date=August 17, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240817025050/https://www.indiewire.com/news/general-news/utopia-help-lionsgate-distribute-market-megalopolis-1235037604/|url-status=live}}</ref> on the stateside theatrical release, with the latter working on "specialty marketing, word-of-mouth, and non-traditional theatrical distribution initiatives" to target filmgoers.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2024/08/megalopolis-utopia-1236042574/ |title=''Megalopolis'' Lionsgate Theatrical Release to Get Boost from Utopia |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=August 16, 2024 |access-date=August 16, 2024 |archive-date=August 16, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816212148/https://deadline.com/2024/08/megalopolis-utopia-1236042574/ |url-status=live}}</ref> On August 20, Lionsgate shared a theatrical poster that featured Driver's character holding a [[t-square]] vertically. [[Roger Friedman]] of ''Showbiz411'' felt the tool's resemblance to a [[lightsaber]] may have been intentional, given Driver's role as [[Kylo Ren]] in the [[Star Wars sequel trilogy|''Star Wars'' sequel trilogy]] (2015–2019).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.showbiz411.com/2024/08/20/new-official-poster-for-coppolas-megalopolis-a-riff-on-or-rip-off-of-star-wars-light-saber |title=New Official Poster for Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' A Riff on or Rip Off of ''Star Wars'' Light Saber? |date=August 20, 2024 |first=Roger |last=Friedman|author-link=Roger Friedman |website=Showbiz411|access-date=August 21, 2024}}</ref>

{{anchor|Trailer}}
On August 21, Lionsgate released a [[Trailer (promotion)|trailer]] that opened with snippets of negative reviews for Coppola's ''The Godfather'', ''Apocalypse Now'', and ''Bram Stoker's Dracula'' followed by 90 seconds of footage from ''Megalopolis'', all accompanied by Fishburne's narration that "True genius is often misunderstood" and "One filmmaker has always been ahead of his time" before naming the film "an event nothing can prepare you for". The unconventional tactic, according to ''[[Rolling Stone]]''{{'}}s Daniel Kreps, attempted to combat the film's mixed reception at Cannes by pointing out "similarly misguided critical assessments of Coppola's previous masterpieces".<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-news/megalopolis-new-trailer-movie-critics-1235084436/|url-access=limited |title=''Megalopolis'': New Trailer Says Critics Were Wrong About ''Godfather'', ''Dracula'', and Now This Polarizing Epic |date=August 21, 2024 |first=Daniel |last=Kreps |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|access-date=August 21, 2024|archive-date=August 24, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240824153141/https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-news/megalopolis-new-trailer-movie-critics-1235084436/|url-status=live}}</ref> Oli Welsh of ''[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]'' was critical of the defensiveness of the trailer, which he thought implied that viewers should ignore critics and see the film for themselves "before it is inevitably reevaluated as a visionary classic",<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.polygon.com/movies/442586/megalopolis-trailer-critics-are-haters |title=This might be the most defensive movie trailer of all time |date=August 21, 2024 |first=Oli |last=Welsh |website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|access-date=August 21, 2024}}</ref> while Mary Kate Carr from ''[[The A.V. Club]]'' described it as "pretty clever" for incorporating the film's "baffling reputation" into the marketing.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.avclub.com/megalopolis-trailer-francis-ford-coppola-full |title=''Megalopolis''{{'}} first full trailer insists it will stand the test of time|date=August 21, 2024|first=Mary|last=Kate Carr|website=[[The A.V. Club]]|access-date=August 21, 2024}}</ref>

However, ''[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]]''{{'}}s [[Bilge Ebiri]] verified that the [[blurb]]s cited in the trailer were fabricated, including those credited to [[Vincent Canby]], [[Roger Ebert]], [[Owen Gleiberman]], [[Pauline Kael]], [[Stanley Kauffmann]], [[Rex Reed]], [[Andrew Sarris]], and [[John Simon (critic)|John Simon]]. While some of their opinions were indeed negative, excluding Kael's positive review for ''The Godfather'' and Ebert's for ''Dracula'', the quotes were fake. In Ebert's case, his quote calling a film a "triumph of style over substance" was misattributed from his review for ''[[Batman (1989 film)|Batman]]'' (1989).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/did-the-megalopolis-trailer-make-up-fake-movie-critic-quotes.html|url-access=limited |title=Did the ''Megalopolis'' Trailer Use Fake Movie Critic Quotes? |date=August 21, 2024 |first=Bilge |last=Ebiri|author-link=Bilge Ebiri |website=[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]]|access-date=August 21, 2024|archive-date=August 21, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240821191936/https://www.vulture.com/article/did-the-megalopolis-trailer-make-up-fake-movie-critic-quotes.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2024/film/news/megalopolis-trailer-quotes-movie-critics-1236114212/ |title=''Megalopolis'' Trailer Fabricates Quotes From Famous Movie Critics |date=August 21, 2024 |first=Katcy |last=Stephan |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=August 21, 2024|archive-date=August 24, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240824153031/https://variety.com/2024/film/news/megalopolis-trailer-quotes-movie-critics-1236114212/|url-status=live}}</ref> Consequently, Lionsgate took down the trailer, which had accumulated 1.3{{nbsp}}million views, the same day they published it and issued an apology.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2024/08/megalopolis-trailer-recalled-lionsgate-fabricated-quote-controversy-1236046745/ |title=Lionsgate Recalling ''Megalopolis'' Trailer Amid Fabricated Quote Controversy: 'We Screwed Up' |date=August 21, 2024 |first=Matt |last=Grobar |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=August 21, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://nytimes.com/2024/08/21/movies/megalopolis-trailer-fake-quotes.html|url-access=limited |title=Studio Pulls ''Megalopolis'' Trailer Featuring Fake Review Quotes |date=August 21, 2024 |first=Annie |last=Aguiar |website=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=August 21, 2024|archive-date=August 21, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240821232257/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/08/21/movies/megalopolis-trailer-fake-quotes.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Two days later, they fired Eddie Egan, the marketing consultant who delivered the quotes, citing "an error in properly vetting and fact-checking the phrases". ''Variety'' suggested that the quotes may have been produced by [[generative AI]] after prompting [[ChatGPT]] for negative criticism of Coppola's work from well-known critics and receiving similar results.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2024/film/news/megalopolis-trailer-fake-quotes-ai-lionsgate-1236116485/ |title=''Megalopolis'' Trailer's Fake Critic Quotes Were AI-Generated, Lionsgate Drops Marketing Consultant Responsible For Snafu |date=August 23, 2024 |first1=Gene |last1=Maddaus |first2=Katcy |last2=Stephan |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=August 23, 2024|archive-date=September 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240907181733/https://variety.com/2024/film/news/megalopolis-trailer-fake-quotes-ai-lionsgate-1236116485/|url-status=live}}</ref> Film critic Peter Debruge, also for ''Variety'', compared the situation to when [[Sony Pictures]] invented the fictitious critic [[David Manning (fictitious writer)|David Manning]] to advertise their films in 2000.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2024/film/columns/megalopolis-trailer-fake-quotes-critics-1236115983/ |title=The Critics Are Raving (Mad): ''Megalopolis'' Scandal Reminds How Blurbs Are Used and Misused in Movie Advertising |date=August 22, 2024 |first=Peter |last=Debruge |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=August 25, 2024 |archive-date=September 24, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240924060954/https://variety.com/2024/film/columns/megalopolis-trailer-fake-quotes-critics-1236115983/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

''The Hollywood Reporter'' found it unusual for a studio to publicly name a terminated employee, particularly in the case of Egan, described by a Hollywood executive as "a low-key guy who never liked the spotlight" now permanently linked online to accusations of manipulating information. The publication also appeared to verify the use of an AI engine in generating the disputed quotes and questioned why Egan was the sole person held accountable, pointing out that the trailer had likely been reviewed by multiple studio executives and marketing team members, none of whom caught the issue yet remained employed.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/megalopolis-lionsgate-fires-marketing-consultant-ai-trailer-1235990295/ |title=''Megalopolis'' Finds a Fall Guy for AI Trailer Snafu and Hollywood Cries Foul |date=September 4, 2024|editor-first1=Benjamin|editor-last1=Svetkey|editor-first2=Julian|editor-last2=Sancton |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|access-date=September 6, 2024|archive-date=September 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240906005501/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/megalopolis-lionsgate-fires-marketing-consultant-ai-trailer-1235990295/|url-status=live}}</ref> On September 5, Lionsgate posted a recut version of the trailer without the quotes, which Carr said was "largely pretty similar to the previous one".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.avclub.com/adam-driver-megalopolis-trailer-no-ai-francis-ford-coppola |title=Here's the ''Megalopolis'' trailer without a bunch of phony critic quotes in it |date=September 5, 2024 |first=Mary |last=Kate Carr |website=[[The A.V. Club]] |access-date=September 6, 2024 |archive-date=September 24, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240924060956/https://www.avclub.com/adam-driver-megalopolis-trailer-no-ai-francis-ford-coppola |url-status=live}}</ref> On September 13, ''[[IGN]]'' shared a second, one-minute trailer.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/videos/megalopolis-official-trailer-utopia |title=''Megalopolis'' – Official Trailer (Utopia) |date=September 13, 2024 |website=[[IGN]] |access-date=September 15, 2024 |archive-date=October 7, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007025822/https://www.ign.com/videos/megalopolis-official-trailer-utopia |url-status=live}}</ref> Kaitlyn Booth of ''[[Bleeding Cool]]'' criticized the video's ambiguity in describing the plot, suggesting that instead of attempting to explain its complexity, the studio seemed to rely on Coppola's prestige to generate interest.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bleedingcool.com/movies/new-look-at-francis-ford-coppolas-megalopolis/ |title=New Look At Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' |date=September 14, 2024 |first=Kaitlyn |last=Booth |website=[[Bleeding Cool]] |access-date=September 15, 2024 |archive-date=October 7, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007025646/https://bleedingcool.com/movies/new-look-at-francis-ford-coppolas-megalopolis/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Created by the duo Awkward Moments, the music for the ad features an 852{{nbsp}}Hz frequency, which they claim "stimulates the [[third eye chakra]]{{nbsp}}... for those seeking to expand their spiritual awareness and tap into higher levels of consciousness".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://theplaylist.net/new-megalopolis-trailer-wants-to-stimulate-your-third-eye-chakra-seriously-20240917/|title=New ''Megalopolis'' Trailer Wants To Stimulate Your Third Eye Chakra... Seriously|date=September 17, 2024|first=Charles|last=Barfield|website=ThePlaylist|access-date=September 18, 2024|archive-date=September 24, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240924060859/https://theplaylist.net/new-megalopolis-trailer-wants-to-stimulate-your-third-eye-chakra-seriously-20240917/|url-status=live}}</ref> In September, Coppola created a [[Letterboxd]] account to share a list of 16 films that inspired ''Megalopolis'' and rated his film five stars on the app.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sfgate.com/culture-events/article/coppola-rates-megalopolis-19774662.php|title=Guess how many stars Francis Ford Coppola gave his new film, ''Megalopolis''|date=September 18, 2024|first=Greg|last=Keraghosian|website=[[SFGate]]|access-date=September 19, 2024|archive-date=September 19, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919001224/https://www.sfgate.com/culture-events/article/coppola-rates-megalopolis-19774662.php|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Reception ==
=== Box office ===
''Megalopolis'' grossed $7.6{{nbsp}}million in the United States and Canada, and $6.8{{nbsp}}million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $14.4{{nbsp}}million.<ref>{{Cite web |title=''Megalopolis'' |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/release/rl2238742529/ |website=[[Box Office Mojo]] |access-date=June 9, 2026 |archive-date=September 30, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240930065724/https://www.boxofficemojo.com/release/rl2238742529/?ref_=bo_we_table_6 |url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Deadline Hollywood]]'' calculated the film lost $75.5 million, when factoring together all expenses and revenues.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2025/04/biggest-box-office-bombs-2024-lowest-grossing-movies-1236381446/|title=Four Fanboy Flicks Bomb Out In Deadline's 2024 Most Valuable Blockbuster Tournament|date=April 30, 2025|first=Anthony|last=D'Alessandro|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=May 1, 2025}}</ref>

In the United States and Canada, ''Megalopolis'' received a [[wide release]] alongside ''[[The Wild Robot]]''. It was projected to gross $4–8{{nbsp}}million from 1,854 theaters, including an estimated 200 IMAX locations, in its opening weekend.<ref name="BoPro-Aug30">{{cite web |url=https://www.boxofficepro.com/long-range-forecast-the-wild-robot-megalopolis-close-out-september/ |title=Long Range Forecast: ''The Wild Robot'', ''Megalopolis'' Close Out September |date=August 30, 2024 |website=[[Boxoffice Pro]]|access-date=August 31, 2024|archive-date=September 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240907181641/https://www.boxofficepro.com/long-range-forecast-the-wild-robot-megalopolis-close-out-september/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-tracking-1235992875/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' Tracking for Anemic $5M-Plus Domestic Opening |date=September 5, 2024 |first=Pamela |last=McClintock |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|access-date=September 6, 2024|archive-date=September 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240907181653/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-tracking-1235992875/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Deadline-BO_Preview"/> ''[[Boxoffice Pro]]'' identified the film's target audience as [[cinephile]]s and said "working against" it were "middling reviews", "a career lull" (Coppola having directed two films in the last 15 years), and "a marketing push marred by controversy", referring to the [[#Allegations of misconduct|misconduct allegations against Coppola]] and the [[#Trailer|trailer]] removed over its use of fake quotes. They mentioned that the film's "blockbuster cast" and IMAX release was "no guarantee of audience interest", given Driver's box-office disappointment in "high-concept sci-fi" with ''[[65 (film)|65]]'' the year prior and that the last Coppola–helmed movie to open above $5{{nbsp}}million was ''[[Supernova (2000 film)|Supernova]]'' (uncredited) in 2000.<ref name="BoPro-Aug30"/> ''Megalopolis'' shared IMAX screens with ''The Wild Robot'' before relinquishing them a week later to ''[[Joker: Folie à Deux]]''; reserved for ''The Wild Robot'' were all showtimes up to primetime, with ''Megalopolis'' having evening IMAX showtimes in "key metropolitan locations".<ref name="Deadline-BO_Preview"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2024/film/news/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-release-date-lionsgate-divisive-cannes-premiere-1236040069/ |title=Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' Lands at Lionsgate for U.S. Release After Divisive Cannes Premiere |last=Rubin |first=Rebecca |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=June 17, 2024 |access-date=June 18, 2024 |archive-date=June 17, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240617231517/https://variety.com/2024/film/news/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-release-date-lionsgate-divisive-cannes-premiere-1236040069/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Lionsgate, reportedly "not on the hook" for recovering production or marketing expenses after agreeing to distribute the film for a distribution fee and "some percentage points based on box office", was expected to earn $3–5{{nbsp}}million regardless of box office performance.<ref name="Deadline-BO_Preview">{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2024/09/the-wild-robot-megalopolis-box-office-1236098281/|title=''The Wild Robot'' Set To Walk Through Weekend With $20M+ Opening; ''Megalopolis'' Finally Happens – Box Office Preview|date=September 24, 2024|first=Anthony|last=D'Alessandro|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=September 24, 2024|archive-date=October 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007030957/https://deadline.com/2024/09/the-wild-robot-megalopolis-box-office-1236098281/|url-status=live}}</ref>

The film made $1.8{{nbsp}}million on its first day, including an estimated $770,000 from Monday and Thursday previews.<ref name="Deadline-OpeningWk"/> It debuted to $4{{nbsp}}million, finishing sixth at the box office.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/weekend/2024W39/|title=Domestic 2024 Weekend 39|website=[[Box Office Mojo]]|access-date=October 1, 2024|archive-date=October 1, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241001182108/https://www.boxofficemojo.com/weekend/2024W39/|url-status=live}}</ref> As a result, several publications, including the [[Associated Press]] and ''The Wall Street Journal'', labeled the film a box-office disappointment.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/megalopolis-wild-robot-box-office-b086c1f3259c6075915aedd5a1f4d9f9|title=''Megalopolis'' flops, ''The Wild Robot'' soars at box office|date=September 29, 2024|first=Jake|last=Coyle|website=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=October 2, 2024|archive-date=October 1, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241001215230/https://apnews.com/article/megalopolis-wild-robot-box-office-b086c1f3259c6075915aedd5a1f4d9f9|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wsj.com/business/media/francis-ford-coppolas-big-budget-megalopolis-flops-in-debut-weekend-cfa4edf9|url-access=subscription|title=Francis Ford Coppola's Big-Budget ''Megalopolis'' Flops in Debut Weekend|date=September 29, 2024|first=Andrew|last=Tangel|website=[[The Wall Street Journal]]|access-date=October 2, 2024|archive-date=October 2, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241002101843/https://www.wsj.com/business/media/francis-ford-coppolas-big-budget-megalopolis-flops-in-debut-weekend-cfa4edf9|url-status=live}}</ref> IMAX and premium large-format screens accounted for 41% of the gross, with IMAX specifically earning $1.4{{nbsp}}million (35%) of the opening. Audiences were 70% men, with 38% over 35 and 32% 25–34-year-olds, while the demographics were 66% Caucasian, 18% Latino and Hispanic, 7% Asian, and 5% Black. The main reasons given in exit polling for seeing the film were Coppola (61%) and Driver (29%), while 32% bought tickets because they heard it was "entertaining and fun" and 9% because they heard it "was good". AMC Lincoln Square was the film's highest-grossing theater with earnings of $84,000 through Saturday. Anthony D'Alessandro of ''Deadline Hollywood'' compared the opening to other box-office flops, particularly as being more than the overall gross of [[Michael Cimino]]'s ''[[Heaven's Gate (film)|Heaven's Gate]]'' ($3.5{{nbsp}}million in 1980, unadjusted for inflation) but less than [[Kevin Costner]]'s self-financed ''[[Horizon: An American Saga – Chapter 1]]'' ($11{{nbsp}}million opening in 2024). It also made less than the fellow new release ''[[Devara: Part 1]]'' ($5.6{{nbsp}}million), which played in fewer theaters (1,040).<ref name="Deadline-OpeningWk">{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2024/09/box-office-megalopolis-the-wild-robot-1236101618/|title=''Wild Robot'' Powers To Third Best September Animated Pic Debut With $35M; ''Megalopolis'' Collapses With $4M & D+ CinemaScore; ''Saturday Night'' Alive In Limited Release – Sunday Box Office Update|date=September 29, 2024|first1=Anthony|last1=D'Alessandro|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=September 29, 2024|archive-date=September 29, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240929001241/https://deadline.com/2024/09/box-office-megalopolis-the-wild-robot-1236101618/|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Marc Tracy]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' likened it to [[Joseph L. Mankiewicz]]'s notoriously expensive ''[[Cleopatra (1963 film)|Cleopatra]]'' (1963) and other "ambitious, big-budget spectacle that got out of hand during production and crashed upon contact with the viewing public".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/10/05/movies/megalopolis-francis-ford-coppola-flops.html|url-access=limited|title=With ''Megalopolis'', the Flop Era Returns to Cinemas|date=October 5, 2024|first=Marc|last=Tracy|author-link=Marc Tracy|website=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=October 6, 2024|archive-date=October 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006004851/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/10/05/movies/megalopolis-francis-ford-coppola-flops.html|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[The New Yorker]]''{{'}}s [[Richard Brody]] urged readers to evaluate the film by its story rather than its revenue, "a determinant of what makes a good investment [but] not a determinant of what makes a good film".<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Brody |first=Richard |date=September 26, 2024 |title="Megalopolis" Is Francis Ford Coppola's Artistic Rejuvenation |url=https://www.newyorker.com/culture/the-front-row/megalopolis-is-francis-ford-coppolas-artistic-rejuvenation |access-date=March 21, 2025 |magazine=The New Yorker |language=en-US |issn=0028-792X}}</ref>

=== Critical response ===
{{RT prose|46|<!-- READ THE SOURCE; DO NOT CHANGE THIS TO TOP CRITICS AVERAGE! -->4.8|303|More of a creative manifesto than a cogent narrative feature, Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' is an overstuffed opus that's equal parts stimulating and slapdash.|ref=yes|access-date=September 8, 2025}} [[Metacritic]], which uses a [[Weighted arithmetic mean|weighted average]], assigned the film a score of 55 out of 100, based on 60 critics, indicating "mixed or average" reviews.<ref name="Metacritic">{{cite web |title=''Megalopolis'' |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/megalopolis |website=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[Fandom (website)#Fandom, Inc.|Fandom, Inc.]] |access-date=October 16, 2024 |archive-url= |archive-date= |url-status=}}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "D+" on an A+ to F scale, while those surveyed by [[PostTrak]] were 45% positive (with an average rating of one star out of five).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2024/10/box-office-joker-folie-a-deux-1236107521/|title=No One's Laughing Now: ''Joker Folie à Deux'' Falls Down With $39M–$40M Opening: How The Sequel Went Sideways – Sunday Box Office|date=October 6, 2024|first=Anthony|last=D'Alessandro|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=October 6, 2024|url-status=live|archive-date=October 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006192317/https://deadline.com/2024/10/box-office-joker-folie-a-deux-1236107521/}}</ref>

The early industry screening resulted in divided reactions — while some were mixed, others were primarily of general bewilderment.<ref>Multiple sources:

exist.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/francis-ford-coppola-on-megalopolis-uproar-just-like-apocalypse-now |title=Francis Ford Coppola Responds to ''Megalopolis'' Uproar: Exactly |url-access=registration}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://airmail.news/issues/2024-5-18/the-view-from-here |title=The View from Here |last=Wasson |first=Sam |author-link=Sam Wasson |website=[[Air The film received a similarly polarized critical response at the Cannes Film Festival.<ref>Multiple sources:

Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' splits critics |last=Sun |first=Michael |website=[[The Guardian]] |date=May 16, 2024 |access-date=May 17, 2024 |archive-date=July 18, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240718202600/https://www.theguardian.com/film/article/2024/may/17/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-critic-reviews-roundup-cannes-film-festival |url-status=live}}

* {{cite web |url=https://screenrant.com/megalopolis-movie-reviews-divided-reasons/ |title=10 Reasons ''Megalopolis''{{'}} Reviews Are So Strongly Divided |last=Protheroe |first=Ben |website=[[Screen Rant]] |date=May 20, 2024 |access-date=May 20, 2024 |archive-date=July 18, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240718202640/https://screenrant.com/megalopolis-movie-reviews-divided-reasons/ |url-status=live}}</ref> ''Variety''{{'}}s Matt Donnelly and Ellise Shafer summarized, "Though reactions have been mixed, the film was undoubtedly jam-packed with scenes that ranged from visionary to just plain puzzling".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2024/film/news/megalopolis-craziest-moments-francis-ford-coppola-1236006842/ |title=''Megalopolis'': The 5 Most WTF Moments from Francis Ford Coppola's Sci-Fi Epic |last1=Shafer |first1=Ellise |last2=Donnelly |first2=Matt |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=May 16, 2024 |access-date=May 17, 2024 |archive-date=May 16, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240516233821/https://variety.com/2024/film/news/megalopolis-craziest-moments-francis-ford-coppola-1236006842/ |url-status=live}}</ref> David Ehrlich of ''[[IndieWire]]'' praised Coppola's hopeful envisioning of the future and "transcendent" narrative progression, calling it a "clunky, garish, and transcendently sincere manifesto about the role of an artist at the end of an empire".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/criticism/movies/megalopolis-review-francis-ford-coppola-1235005694/|title=''Megalopolis'' Review: Francis Ford Coppola's Wild and Delirious Fever Dream Inspires New Hope for the Future of Movies|date=May 16, 2024|first=David|last=Ehrlich|website=[[IndieWire]]|access-date=September 24, 2024|archive-date=September 21, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240921011541/https://www.indiewire.com/criticism/movies/megalopolis-review-francis-ford-coppola-1235005694/|url-status=live}}</ref> Joshua Rothkopf of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' described it as "an overstuffed, vigorous, seething story about the roots of fascism that only an uncharitable viewer would call a catastrophe" with moments "too divorced from reality", compared its portrayal of a city modeled after New York to [[Tom Wolfe]]'s novel ''[[The Bonfire of the Vanities]]'' (1987), and complimented the cast for "leaning into their moments with an abandon that was probably a job requirement".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/movies/story/2024-05-16/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-review-cannes-2024|url-access=limited|title=Cannes: Coppola's Roman candle ''Megalopolis'' is juicy and weird|date=May 16, 2024|first=Joshua|last=Rothkopf|website=[[Los Angeles]]|access-date=September 24, 2024|archive-date=September 23, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240923062211/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/movies/story/2024-05-16/francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-review-cannes-2024|url-status=live}}</ref> ''The New York Times''{{'}}s [[Manohla Dargis]] also noted the "heightened" performances; she disagreed with Coppola's "old-fashioned ideas" about [[gender roles]] and [[technological determinism]] but commended his artistic ambition, defining ''Megalopolis'' as "a fascinating film aswirl with wild visions, lofty ideals, cinematic allusions, literary references, historical footnotes, and self-reflexive asides, all of which Coppola has funneled into a fairly straightforward story about a man with a plan".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/05/16/movies/megalopolis-reaction-cannes.html|title=''Megalopolis'' Premieres at Cannes: First Reaction|date=May 16, 2024|first=Manohla|last=Dargis|author-link=Manohla Dargis|website=[[The New York Times]]|url-access=limited|access-date=September 24, 2024|archive-date=September 22, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240922013400/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/05/16/movies/megalopolis-reaction-cannes.html|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Vulture''{{'}}s [[Bilge Ebiri]] opined that while some scenes were "rushed, undernourished, and underpopulated" and the digital cinematography was "sometimes flat and overly bright, which in turn reduces depth and detail and makes things feel one-dimensional", the film "might be the craziest thing I've ever seen. And I'd be lying if I said I didn't enjoy every single batshit second of it".<ref name="Vulture-0517"/>

In a negative review, ''[[Screen Daily]]''{{'}}s Tim Grierson said the film was narratively excessive and incoherent, with "cartoonish performances" and "stray ideas and themes that are introduced, then abandoned".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.screendaily.com/reviews/megalopolis-cannes-review/5193570.article|title=''Megalopolis'': Cannes Review|date=May 16, 2024|first=Tim|last=Grierson|website=[[Screen Daily]]|access-date=September 24, 2024|archive-date=September 24, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240924061500/https://www.screendaily.com/reviews/megalopolis-cannes-review/5193570.article|url-status=live}}</ref> Peter DeBruge, for ''Variety'', likewise categorized the acting as cartoonish and reminiscent of ''[[Southland Tales]]'' (2006) but with "'serious' actors, which lends everything a stilted, almost theatrical quality".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2024/film/reviews/megalopolis-review-francis-ford-coppola-1236005482/|title=''Megalopolis'' Review: Francis Ford Coppola's Bold, Ungainly Epic Crams in Half a Dozen Stars and Decades' Worth of Ideas|date=May 16, 2024|first=Peter|last=DeBruge|website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=September 24, 2024|archive-date=September 23, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240923071001/https://variety.com/2024/film/reviews/megalopolis-review-francis-ford-coppola-1236005482/|url-status=live}}</ref> Writing for ''[[NME]]'', Lou Thomas described ''Megalopolis'' as a film that "has to be seen to be believed", adding, "The dialogue and acting are heightened, skewed, and bizarre, lurching from fascinating philosophical arguments to nonsense rhymes and non-jokes". He further noted the unevenness in the film's evolving styles and visuals and praised the costumes and score.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/reviews/film-reviews/megalopolis-review-francis-ford-coppola-3757777|title=''Megalopolis'' review: as mad and memorable as everyone is saying|date=May 16, 2024|first=Lou|last=Thomas|website=[[NME]]|access-date=September 24, 2024|archive-date=September 21, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240921093819/https://www.nme.com/reviews/film-reviews/megalopolis-review-francis-ford-coppola-3757777|url-status=live}}</ref> Nicholas Barber of the [[BBC]] panned the movie, criticizing its "incoherent plot", "stilted dialogue", narrow use of "big-name actors" like Hoffman and Schwartzman, the contrast between "Driver taking it all so seriously, while Plaza goes gloriously over the top{{nbsp}}... [and] LaBeouf prances around chewing the scenery to shreds", and the "horribly cheap and amateurish" visual effects. He concluded, "It's like listening to someone tell you about the crazy dream they had last night – and they don't stop talking for well over two hours".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20240517-megalopolis-film-review-francis-ford-coppolas-passion-project-is-a-pretentious-portentous-curio|title=Megalopolis film review: Francis Ford Coppola's passion project is a 'pretentious, portentous curio'|date=May 16, 2024|first=Nicholas|last=Barber|website=[[BBC]]|access-date=September 24, 2024|archive-date=September 24, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240924061500/https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20240517-megalopolis-film-review-francis-ford-coppolas-passion-project-is-a-pretentious-portentous-curio|url-status=live}}</ref> Maureen Lee Lenker of ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' gave the film an "F", the lowest grade, condemning Coppola's direction for obtaining "horribly wooden performances" from the ensemble, further criticizing the "troubling gender roles and gross sexual dynamics at play" before saying the film's "greatest sin" is "how profoundly boring and bloated it all is.{{nbsp}}... I at least expected something a little batshit. Something so bad it's good, an experience you could give yourself over to. But instead, it only prompted me to check my watch".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/megalopolis-review-francis-ford-coppola-film-bloated-dull-8710050|title=Francis Ford Coppola's ''Megalopolis'' is bloated and unforgivably dull|date=May 16, 2024|first=Maureen|last=Lee Lenker|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|access-date=September 24, 2024|archive-date=September 23, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240923142442/https://ew.com/megalopolis-review-francis-ford-coppola-film-bloated-dull-8710050|url-status=live}}</ref>

''[[Sight and Sound]]'' put the film at 17 on their list of the best 50 movies of 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bfi.org.uk/sight-and-sound/polls/50-best-films-2024|title=The 50 best films of 2024|date=December 6, 2024|website=[[Sight and Sound]]|access-date=January 19, 2024|archive-date=December 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241207002204/https://www.bfi.org.uk/sight-and-sound/polls/50-best-films-2024|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Manohla Dargis]] of ''The New York Times'' put it at 8 on her list of the best 10 movies of 2024, while [[Richard Brody]] ranked it third on his 2024 best-of list.<ref>{{Cite news |date=November 30, 2024 |title=Best Movies of 2024 |first1=Manohla |last1=Dargis |author-link1=Manohla Dargis |first2=Alissa |last2=Wilkinson |website=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/11/30/movies/best-movies-2024.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |last=Brody |first=Richard |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |title=The Best Movies of 2024 |url=https://www.newyorker.com/culture/2024-in-review/the-best-movies-of-2024 |date=December 5, 2024 |access-date=April 10, 2025}}</ref> Filmmakers [[Davy Chou]], [[Vera Drew]], [[Ciro Guerra]], |work=[[Filmmaker (magazine)|Filmmaker]]}}</ref>

== Home media and roadshow screenings ==
''Megalopolis'' was released on [[Ultra HD Blu-ray]], [[Blu-ray]] and DVD by Lionsgate in Europe following its theatrical run, but did not receive a North American physical home media release.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Plale |first=Mathew |date=March 10, 2025 |title=Why isn't Megalopolis on Blu-ray or streaming? |url=https://www.joblo.com/why-isnt-megalopolis-on-blu-ray-or-streaming/ |access-date=July 24, 2025 |website=JoBlo |language=en-US}}</ref> The film became available for purchase and rental on premium video-on-demand services, including North America, on November 12, 2024, but was pulled from digital platforms in selected markets in early 2025, reportedly because Coppola prefers that the film only be screened in theaters.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Obias |first=Rudie |date=November 13, 2024 |title=Where to Stream 'Megalopolis' Online |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/watch-stream-megalopolis-online-1236060356/ |access-date=July 24, 2025 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Svetkey |first=Benjamin |date=May 7, 2025 |title=Where, Oh Where, Did 'Megalopolis' Go? |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/why-cant-stream-francis-ford-coppola-megalopolis-1236207923/ |access-date=July 24, 2025 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US|last2=Sancton|first2=Julian}}</ref> The film was made available for streaming on [[Mubi (streaming service)|Mubi]] and [[Netflix]] in some European countries in September 2025.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WVZd5b--U6w MEGALOPOLIS|Official Trailer|Hand-picked by MUBI on official YouTube channel]</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.justwatch.com/de/Film/megalopolis |title=Francis Ford Coppola's Megalopolis - Eine Fabel - Stream: Online |language=de |access-date=October 12, 2025 |via=www.justwatch.com}}</ref>

Coppola held six [[Roadshow theatrical release|roadshow screenings]] of ''Megalopolis'' in the U.S. from July 20–August 1, 2025. ''The Atlantic'' criticized Coppola's decision to limit the film to theatrical screenings and eschew a home video release, writing, "But rather than allow audiences to organically find ''Megalopolis'', Coppola has made it hard to screen legally. Rather than wait for reevaluations of it to emerge over time, Coppola initiated the conversation from his end. His efforts to reintroduce ''Megalopolis'' to the public demonstrate the challenge of transforming a flop into a cult classic."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Li |first=Shirley |date=August 18, 2025 |title=A Famed Director Tried to Build a Fan Base for His Movie. It Was Awkward. |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/culture/archive/2025/08/megalopolis-francis-ford-coppola-cult-classics/683896/ |access-date=November 21, 2025 |website=The Atlantic |language=en}}</ref>

'''''Precious: Based on the Novel "Push" by Sapphire''''',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.weareallprecious.com/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090516185056/http://www.weareallprecious.com/|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 16, 2009|title=Precious: Based on the Novel "Push" by Sapphire|website=[[Lionsgate Entertainment]]|access-date=May 16, 2009}}</ref> or simply '''''Precious''''', is a 2009 American [[drama film]] directed and co produced by [[Lee Daniels]]. Its script was written by [[Geoffrey S. Fletcher]], adapted from the 1996 novel ''[[Push (novel)|Push]]'' by [[Sapphire (author)|Sapphire]]. The film stars [[Gabourey Sidibe]] and [[Mo'Nique]], alongside [[Paula Patton]], [[Mariah Carey]], [[Sherri Shepherd]], and [[Lenny Kravitz]]. It marked the acting debut of Sidibe, who portrays a young woman struggling against poverty and abuse. Filming took place in [[New York City]] from October to December 2007.

''Precious'', then without a distributor, premiered to acclaim at both the [[2009 Sundance Film Festival]] and the [[2009 Cannes Film Festival]], under its original title of ''Push: Based on the Novel by Sapphire''.<ref name="varietydec08">{{cite news|url=https://www.variety.com/index.asp?layout=festivals&jump=story&id=2470&articleid=VR1117996739&cs=1 |first=Todd |last=McCarthy |title=Sundance unveils competition lineup |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=December 3, 2008 |access-date=November 16, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091123101804/http://www.variety.com/index.asp?layout=festivals&jump=story&id=2470&articleid=VR1117996739&cs=1 <!--Added by H3llBot--> |archive-date=November 23, 2009}}</ref> At Sundance, it won the Audience Award and the Grand Jury Prize for best drama, as well as a Special Jury Prize for supporting actress Mo'Nique. After ''Precious''' screening at Sundance in January 2009, [[Tyler Perry]] announced that he and [[Oprah Winfrey]] would be providing promotional assistance to the film, which was released through [[Lionsgate Entertainment]]. ''Precious'' won the People's Choice Award at the [[Toronto International Film Festival]] in September. The film's title was changed from ''Push'' to ''Precious:'' Based on the Novel ''Push'' by Sapphire, to avoid confusion with the 2009 action film ''[[Push (2009 film)|Push]]''.<ref name="variety022009">{{cite news |url=https://variety.com/2009/film/news/when-push-comes-to-shove-1118000415/ |first=Tatiana |last=Siegel |title=When 'Push' comes to shove |work=Variety |date=February 20, 2009 |access-date=November 16, 2009 |archive-date=April 22, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130422012245/http://variety.com/2009/film/news/when-push-comes-to-shove-1118000415/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Lionsgate gave the film a limited release in the United States on November 6, 2009, before expanding on November 20. ''Precious'' received positive reviews from critics; the performances of Sidibe and Mo'Nique, the story, and its message were highly praised. The film was also a box office success, earning over $63 million on a $10 million budget. It received six nominations at the [[82nd Academy Awards]], including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]], [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]], and [[Academy Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]] for Sidibe. Mo'Nique won the award for [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress|Best Supporting Actress]], while Geoffrey Fletcher won for [[Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay|Best Adapted Screenplay]], becoming the first African-American to win a screenplay award at the Oscars.

==Plot==
In 1987, 16-year-old Claireece Precious Jones lives in [[New York City]]'s [[Harlem]] neighborhood with her unemployed mother, Mary, who subjects her to constant [[Physical abuse|physical]], [[Sexual abuse|sexual]], and [[verbal abuse]]. Precious has also been [[rape]]d by her now-absent father, Carl, resulting in two pregnancies. The family resides in a [[Section 8 (housing)|Section 8]] [[tenement]] and survives on [[welfare spending|welfare checks]]. Precious often finds a way out of her traumatic daily life by escaping into daydreams in which she is loved and appreciated.

Precious's first child, a daughter named "Mongo", short for [[Mongoloid idiot|Mongoloid]], has [[Down syndrome]] and is being cared for by Precious's grandmother, though Mary forces the family to pretend that Mongo lives with her and Precious during social worker visits so she can receive extra welfare money from the government. When Precious's second pregnancy is discovered, her junior high principal, Mrs. Lichtenstein, arranges for her to attend an [[alternative school|alternative school program]] called [[Each one teach one|Each One Teach One]], where she hopes Precious can change her life's direction.

Despite her mother's insistence that Precious apply for welfare, Precious goes to the alternative school and enrolls. She meets her new teacher, Ms. Blu Rain, as well as several other girls who all come from troubled backgrounds and are looking to get their GED to advance their educations. Precious's life begins to turn around when she slowly starts to learn to read and write with the help of Ms. Rain and finds herself inspired by her. While she learns, she starts to meet with social worker Ms. Weiss, who learns about the sexual assault in the household when Precious accidentally reveals who fathered her children. One day, while telling a story in class, Precious's water breaks, and she is rushed to the hospital. She gives birth to a healthy son named Abdul and is acquainted with a kind nursing assistant named John McFadden. While in the hospital, Precious writes letters to Ms. Rain through her notebook that is taken to and from her by Joann, one of the girls in her class.

Once discharged from the hospital, Precious returns home to find Mary waiting for her. Mary asks to hold Abdul, but deliberately drops him before furiously attacking Precious, as Precious's revelation about the abuse has resulted in the termination of welfare payments. Precious fights off Mary, retrieves Abdul, and after falling down the stairs and narrowly avoiding Mary dropping her television on them from the top of the stairwell, flees and eventually breaks into her school classroom for shelter. When Ms. Rain discovers Precious and Abdul sleeping the next morning, she frantically calls local shelters in search of a safe place for Precious and Abdul to live, but they end up staying with Ms. Rain and her live-in girlfriend for the holiday. The next morning, Ms. Rain takes Precious and Abdul to find assistance, and Precious is able to continue her schooling while raising Abdul in a [[halfway house]].

Mary returns to inform Precious of her father's death from [[AIDS]]. Precious later learns that she is [[HIV-positive]], though Abdul is not. Feeling dejected, Precious distracts Ms. Weiss and steals her case file from her office. As she shares the details of her file with her fellow students, she begins to hope for the future. Later, Precious meets with her mother, who brings Mongo to Ms. Weiss's office. Ms. Weiss confronts Mary about her and Carl's abuse of Precious, going back to when Precious was a toddler. Mary tearfully confesses that she always hated Precious for "stealing her man" by "letting him" abuse her and for eventually "making him leave", and that she allowed the abuse to continue because she wanted "someone to love her". Precious tells Mary that she finally sees her for who she really is and severs ties with her, leaving with both Mongo and Abdul and telling her mother she will never see her or her children again. Mary begs Ms. Weiss to retrieve her daughter and grandchildren, but a shaken and disgusted Ms. Weiss silently rejects her and walks away, leaving Mary distraught.

Planning to complete a [[General Educational Development|GED]] test to receive a high-school diploma equivalency, followed by college, Precious walks into the city with her children, ready to start a new life with a brighter future.

==Cast==
* [[Gabourey Sidibe]] as Claireece "Precious" Jones. The film's casting director, Billy Hopkins, found her at an open-call audition held at New York City's [[Lehman College]]. Sidibe was chosen over 300 others who auditioned in nationwide casting calls<ref name="varietyoct07">{{cite news |author=Fleming |first=Michael |date=October 29, 2007 |title=Lee Daniels to direct 'Push' |url=https://variety.com/2007/film/markets-festivals/lee-daniels-to-direct-push-2-1117974944/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100816011832/http://www.variety.com/article/VR1117974944.html?categoryid=13&cs=1 |archive-date=August 16, 2010 |access-date=November 15, 2009 |work=Variety}}</ref> and had no prior acting experience.<ref name="mcmtv" />
* [[Mo'Nique]] as Mary Lee Johnston, Precious's unemployed, profane, and abusive mother.<ref name="mcmtv">{{cite web |url=http://www.mtv.com/news/1619596/mariah-carey-and-gabourey-sidibe-became-besties-on-precious-set/ |first=Eric |last=Ditzian |date=August 26, 2009 |title=Mariah Carey And Gabourey Sidibe Became 'Besties' On 'Precious's Set |website=MTV News |access-date=November 16, 2009 |archive-date=September 3, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903220509/http://www.mtv.com/news/1619596/mariah-carey-and-gabourey-sidibe-became-besties-on-precious-set/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Mo'Nique and Daniels had previously worked together in ''[[Shadowboxer]]'' (in which Mo'Nique's character was named Precious). 
* [[Paula Patton]] as Blu Rain, Precious's alternative-school teacher.<ref name="patton">{{cite web |url=http://radiofree.com/profiles/paula_patton/interview05.shtml |first=Michael |last=J. Lee |title=Paula Patton on 'Push' |website=Radio Free Entertainment |date=August 12, 2008 |access-date=November 15, 2009 |archive-date=April 29, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090429103855/http://radiofree.com/profiles/paula_patton/interview05.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref> Patton said that her character teaches Precious to "learn and read and write from the very beginnings, and pushes her to believe in herself, and pushes her to realize that anything is possible." She is a [[lesbian]].<ref name="patton" />
* [[Mariah Carey]] as Ms. Anna Weiss, a [[social worker]] who supports Precious during her struggles. In September 2008,<ref name="nydailycarey" /><ref name="rscarey">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/mariah-careys-hardest-precious-challenge-going-with-no-makeup-20090918 |first=Karen |last=Bliss |title=Mariah Carey's Hardest "Precious" Challenge: Going With No Makeup |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |date=September 18, 2009 |access-date=November 15, 2009 |archive-date=February 7, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120207082526/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/mariah-careys-hardest-precious-challenge-going-with-no-makeup-20090918 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Carey described her character as "not really a likable person, but she does bring this to the surface."<ref name="rscarey" /><ref name="nyprepcarey">{{cite web |url=https://www.vulture.com/2009/11/mariah_carey_speaks_out_on_her.html |date=November 6, 2009 |title=Mariah Carey Speaks Out on Her Precious Mustache |author=Madeleine Kuhns |website=[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]] |access-date=November 15, 2009 |archive-date=October 23, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023030628/http://www.vulture.com/2009/11/mariah_carey_speaks_out_on_her.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Carey and Daniels had previously worked together on ''[[Tennessee (film)|Tennessee]]''.<ref name="varietyoct07" /> Daniels said that he cast Carey because he was "so impressed" by her performance in ''Tennessee''.<ref name="nydailycarey" /> According to director Daniels, [[Helen Mirren]], who starred in his previous film ''[[Shadowboxer]]'', was originally set to play the part of Ms. Weiss, but obtained a role in a "bigger project."<ref>{{cite video|title=Precious|publisher=Lions Gate Home Entertainment|people=Daniels, Lee|medium=DVD|date=March 9, 2010}} ([[audio commentary]])</ref>
* [[Sherri Shepherd]] as Lisa "Cornrows", the receptionist at Each One Teach One.
* [[Lenny Kravitz]] as John McFadden, a nurse who shows kindness to Precious.<ref name="varietyoct07" /><ref name="nydailycarey">{{cite news |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/entertainment/gossip/mariah-carey-new-push-acting-article-1.322058 |first=Molloy |last=Rush |title=Mariah Carey makes new 'Push' into acting |work=[[New York Daily News]] |date=September 22, 2008 |access-date=November 15, 2009 |archive-date=October 22, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121022111758/http://www.nydailynews.com/entertainment/gossip/mariah-carey-new-push-acting-article-1.322058 |url-status=live }}</ref> This film is Kravitz's feature film acting debut.<ref name="varietyoct07" /> Later in 2011, he released the song "[[Push (Lenny Kravitz song)|Push]]", inspired by the novel and movie.

* [[Xosha Roquemore]] as Jo Ann Rogers, Precious's classmate who aspires to be a record producer
* Aunt Dot as Betty "Toosie" Johnston, Mary's mother and Precious's grandmother, who fails to intervene Mary's abuse. Aunt Dot is the real-life aunt of director [[Lee Daniels]].<ref name="danielsinterview" />
* Angelic Zambrana as Consuelo Montenegro, a girl who attends the same alternative school as Precious and gets into a fight with her after calling her fat, but later befriends her.
* Quishay Powell as Mongo, Precious's daughter, who has [[Down syndrome]].
* [[Grace Hightower]] as Ms. Turner, the Social Worker who visits Precious's family.
* [[Kimberly Russell]] as Katherine, Ms. Rain's partner.
* [[Bill Sage]] as Mr. Wicher, Precious's math teacher.
* [[Sapphire (author)|Ramona "Sapphire" Lofton]] (the author of the novel) makes a cameo appearance as a woman at a daycare center near the film's end.
* [[Jamie Foxx]] as Frank Mason (deleted cameo).
* Rodney 'Bear' Jackson as Carl Kenwood Jones, the incestuous father and rapist of Precious, who sexually abuses and impregnates her.

==Production==
===Development===
Daniels had said that he was attracted to the novel based on how "raw and honest" it felt.<ref name="AVClubinterview">{{cite web|last1=Rabin|first1=Nathan|title=Lee Daniels and Gabby Sidibe|url=https://www.avclub.com/lee-daniels-and-gabby-sidibe-1798218222|website=The A.V. Club|date=November 5, 2009|access-date=May 30, 2021|archive-date=June 2, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210602214701/https://www.avclub.com/lee-daniels-and-gabby-sidibe-1798218222|url-status=live}}</ref> In an interview with AMC, he noted that reading the book brought back a memory from his childhood of a young abused girl who knocked on his family's door, claiming that her mom was going to kill her. Daniels recalls that the incident was the first time he saw his mother frightened, specifically noting the helplessness of the situation, and stating "she knew that she'd have to send this little girl home, and that was what disturbed her&nbsp;— that she couldn't save her. She tried to make it easier for her. That's all she could do." In creating the movie, Daniels hoped that the experience would be cathartic and that "maybe I could heal. And maybe I could heal other people, too."<ref name="AMCstraighttodvd">{{cite web|title=Q&A&nbsp;– Lee Daniels Expected Precious to Go Straight to DVD|url=http://www.amc.com/talk/2010/02/qa-lee-daniel|website=AMC|access-date=August 19, 2016|archive-date=October 7, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151007161223/http://www.amc.com/talk/2010/02/qa-lee-daniel|url-status=dead}}</ref> Another stated goal Daniels had was to challenge the general public's perception of [[incest]].<ref name="PWeekly">{{cite web|last1=Peters|first1=Monica|title=Lee Daniels' 'Precious' Moment|date=November 11, 2009|url=http://philadelphiaweekly.com/2009/nov/11/Lee-Daniels-Uncut/#.V7bVnZgrLIU|website=Philadelphia Weekly|access-date=August 19, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160917215324/http://philadelphiaweekly.com/2009/nov/11/Lee-Daniels-Uncut/#.V7bVnZgrLIU|archive-date=September 17, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The film was co-produced by Daniels's company, Lee Daniels Entertainment, and the Sarah Siegel-Magness and Gary Magness-owned Smokewood Entertainment Group.<ref name="productioncompanies" /> The two production companies had previously collaborated with Daniels on ''[[Tennessee (film)|Tennessee]]'' (2008).<ref name="productioncompanies">{{cite news |last=Davis |first=Joyzelle |date=January 22, 2008 |title=Billionaires behind the camera |url=http://www.rockymountainnews.com/news/2008/jan/22/billionaires-behind-the-camera/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091121150341/http://www.rockymountainnews.com/news/2008/jan/22/billionaires-behind-the-camera/ |archive-date=November 21, 2009 |access-date=August 10, 2014 |newspaper=[[Rocky Mountain News]]}}</ref> ''Precious'' had, in total, thirteen producers: Daniels, [[Oprah Winfrey]], Tom Heller, [[Tyler Perry]], [[Lisa Cortés]], Gary Magness, [[Valerie Hoffman]], Asger Hussain, Mark G. Mathis, Andrew Sforzini, Bergen Swason, Simone Sheffield and Sarah Siegel-Magness. Initially, Daniels did not expect the movie to generate much buzz, expecting the movie to go [[straight to video]], stating "That it made it to the big screen says there was an angel looking after me."<ref name="AMCstraighttodvd"/>

===Filming===
[[Principal photography]] began on October 24, 2007 and concluded on November 24, 2007.<ref>{{cite web |title=Precious: Based on the novel 'Push' by Sapphire |url=https://catalog.afi.com/Film/55798-PRECIOUS-BASEDONTHENOVELPUSHBYSAPPHIRE |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210602214021/https://catalog.afi.com/Film/55798-PRECIOUS-BASEDONTHENOVELPUSHBYSAPPHIRE |archive-date=June 2, 2021 |access-date=May 30, 2021 |website=[[AFI Catalog of Feature Films]]}}</ref> It took place on location in various parts of [[New York City]]. Despite the dark subject matter, Sidibe has stated that the mood on the set was lighthearted, that "Every day was a party" and that the cast would frequently sing and tell jokes to "lighten the atmosphere."<ref name="AVClubinterview"/> The production budget was $10&nbsp;million.<ref name="boxofficemojo" />

===Post-production===
After ''Precious'' was screened at the 2009 Sundance Film Festival in January, it was picked up for distribution by [[Lions Gate Entertainment]] and received promotional assistance from Oprah Winfrey's [[Harpo Productions]] and Tyler Perry's 34th Street Films.<ref name="variety090202">{{cite news |author=McClintock |first=Pamela |date=February 2, 2009 |title=Lionsgate, Winfrey, Perry push 'Push' |url=https://variety.com/2009/film/markets-festivals/lionsgate-winfrey-perry-push-push-1117999429/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090408200108/http://www.variety.com/article/VR1117999429.html?categoryId=13&cs=1 |archive-date=April 8, 2009 |access-date=November 17, 2009 |work=Variety}}</ref> ''Precious'' was the first theatrical film to be affiliated with Perry's company.<ref name="Can Oprah Lead Precious All the Way to Oscar?">{{cite magazine |url=http://content.time.com/time/arts/article/0,8599,1925070,00.html |title=Can Oprah Lead Precious All the Way to Oscar? |date=September 21, 2009 |access-date=November 17, 2009 |first=S. |last=James Snyder |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |archive-date=July 13, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140713114736/http://content.time.com/time/arts/article/0,8599,1925070,00.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In February 2009, Lionsgate and [[The Weinstein Company]] filed lawsuits contesting ownership of the rights to release ''Precious''.<ref name="distributedeal">{{cite news |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2009-feb-06-fi-push6-story.html |first=John |last=Horn |title='Push' comes to shove in movie rights fight |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=February 5, 2009 |access-date=November 17, 2009 |archive-date=May 17, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090517010845/http://articles.latimes.com/2009/feb/06/business/fi-push6 |url-status=live }}</ref> Both companies claim that they had purchased distribution rights to ''Precious'': The Weinstein Company claimed that they had "secured" their rights while Lionsgate stated that they owned the rights to the film's distribution in North America.<ref name="distributedeal" /> ''Precious''{{'}}s sales agent Cinetic Media denied Weinstein's claims, stating that they failed to finalize the deal.<ref name="distributedeal" />

==Music==
{{Main|Precious: Original Motion Picture Soundtrack}}
The soundtrack accompanying the film featured a compilation of original songs and covers with artists such as [[Labelle|LaBelle]] (a pop group composed of [[Nona Hendryx]], [[Sarah Dash]], and [[Patti LaBelle]]), [[Donna Allen (singer)|Donna Allen]], [[Jean Carn]], Sunny Gale, [[MFSB]], [[Grace Hightower]], [[Queen Latifah]] and [[Mahalia Jackson]].<ref name="tracklistings">{{cite web |url=http://www.interscope.com/artist/news/default.aspx?nid=23505&aid=1147 |date=November 3, 2009 |title= Precious Soundtrack is available now! |website=Interscope |access-date=November 20, 2009 |archive-date=January 5, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100105123214/http://interscope.com/artist/news/default.aspx?nid=23505&aid=1147 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Mary J. Blige's co-wrote and performed the original song "I Can See in Color" which was separately released as a single.<ref name="upialbum">{{cite news |url=http://www.upi.com/Entertainment_News/Movies/2009/11/09/Blige-performs-on-Precious-soundtrack/UPI-14131257785271/ |title=Blige performs on 'Precious' soundtrack |work=[[United Press International]] |date=November 9, 2009 |access-date=November 18, 2009 |archive-date=January 26, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110126082545/http://www.upi.com/Entertainment_News/Movies/2009/11/09/Blige-performs-on-Precious-soundtrack/UPI-14131257785271/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Blige's [[Matriarch Records]] and [[Geffen Records]] along with Lionsgate released the soundtrack online as a digital download on November 3, 2009,<ref name="allmusiclistings">{{cite web |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/precious-mw0001364990 |title=Precious – Original Motion Picture Soundtrack |website=[[AllMusic]] |first=James |last=Christopher Monger |access-date=August 10, 2014 |archive-date=January 26, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160126160956/http://www.allmusic.com/album/precious-mw0001364990 |url-status=live }}</ref> and in stores on November 24.<ref name="islistings">{{cite web |url=http://www.interscope.com/artist/news/default.aspx?nid=23468&aid=1147&cmnt=1 |work=[[Interscope records|InterScope.com]] |title=Matriarch/Geffen Records release soundtrack to Precious |access-date=November 18, 2009 |archive-date=March 23, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323161026/http://www.interscope.com/artist/news/default.aspx?nid=23468&aid=1147&cmnt=1 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The album received positive praise; mainly the song "I Can See In Color".<ref name="upialbum" />

==Release==

===Marketing===
[[File:Lee Daniels at the 2009 Tribeca Film Festival.jpg|thumb|right|alt=A dark skinned man with a black afro. The man is smiling and is wearing a dark green button shirt wide open on top of a buttoned up turquoise shirt. |The film's director, [[Lee Daniels]], stated that he was initially "embarrassed" to screen ''Precious'' at the [[Cannes Film Festival]] because he felt that it would show African Americans in a negative light, due to its content.<ref name="danielsinterview"/>]]
''Precious'' was screened during the [[2009 Sundance Film Festival]] from January 15, 2009, until January 25 in [[Park City, Utah]].<ref name="dates">{{cite web|url=http://www.sundance.org/festival/press_industry/press_industry.asp |title=Press & Industry – Sundance Film Festival (festival dates) |website=[[Sundance.org]] |first=Brooks |last=Addicott |access-date=February 7, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080216012831/http://www.sundance.org/festival/press_industry/press_industry.asp |archive-date=February 16, 2008 }}</ref> At Sundance, ''Precious'' was originally listed under the title ''Push: Based on the Novel by Sapphire''; the title was later modified to avoid confusion with another 2009 film entitled ''[[Push (2009 film)|Push]]''.<ref name="varietydec08" /> ''Precious'' appeared in the [[Un Certain Regard]], an award section recognising unique and innovative films, at the [[2009 Cannes Film Festival|62nd Cannes Film Festival]] in May 2009.<ref name="festival-cannes.com">{{cite web |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/10885446/year/2009.html |title=Festival de Cannes: Precious |access-date=November 17, 2009 |website=[[Cannes Film Festival|Festival.Cannes.com]] |archive-date=August 23, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110823001027/http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/10885446/year/2009.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> At Cannes, the film received a fifteen-minute standing ovation from the audience after the film was screened.<ref name="danielsinterview">{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/10/25/magazine/25precious-t.html?_r=1 |title=The Audacity of 'Precious' |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=October 25, 2009 |first=Lynn |last=Hirschberg |access-date=August 10, 2014 |archive-date=September 28, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180928035319/https://www.nytimes.com/2009/10/25/magazine/25precious-t.html?_r=1 |url-status=live }}</ref> 

Daniels commented that, at first he was "embarrassed" to show ''Precious'' at Cannes because he did not want "to exploit black people" and wasn't sure if he "wanted white French people to see our world".<ref name="danielsinterview" /> After the success at ''Precious'''s screenings at Sundance, reporters took note that the film could mirror the success of other films that had been screened and praised at the festival.<ref name="Can Oprah Lead Precious All the Way to Oscar?" /><ref name="Oprah flick 'Precious' wins top award at Toronto"/> S. James Snyder, of ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'', compared ''Precious's'' success at Sundance to that of 2008's ''[[The Wrestler (2008 film)|The Wrestler]]'' and ''[[Slumdog Millionaire]]''; both films later were nominated for multiple [[Academy Awards]], and ''Slumdog'' itself won Best Picture at the 81st Annual Academy Awards.<ref name="Can Oprah Lead Precious All the Way to Oscar?" />

Winfrey used her status as both a celebrity and a media personality to give the film what was described by Ben Child of ''[[The Guardian]]'', as a "high-profile promotional push."<ref name="Can Oprah Lead Precious All the Way to Oscar?" /><ref name="Oprah Winfrey helps Precious find love in Toronto">{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2009/sep/21/oprah-winfrey-precious-toronto |title=Oprah Winfrey helps Precious find love in Toronto |date=September 21, 2009 |access-date=November 17, 2009 |work=[[The Guardian]] |first=Ben |last=Child |location=London |archive-date=January 16, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140116085126/http://www.theguardian.com/film/2009/sep/21/oprah-winfrey-precious-toronto |url-status=live }}</ref> At a press conference Winfrey announced her intention to lead a promotional campaign on behalf of ''Precious'' along with her other various platforms, hoping to be able to "bring in different audiences" by promoting the film [[The Oprah Winfrey Show|on her show]], [[O, The Oprah Magazine|in her magazine]] and on [[Oprah Winfrey#Radio|her satellite-radio channel]].<ref name="Can Oprah Lead Precious All the Way to Oscar?" /> Katie Walmsley of [[CNN]] remarked, based on the film's positive reception at the Toronto Film Festival, that the film "at the very least, the [Toronto] award will guarantee "Precious" substantial distribution, as well as exposure for two-time director Daniels."<ref name="Oprah flick 'Precious' wins top award at Toronto">{{cite news |url=http://edition.cnn.com/2009/SHOWBIZ/Movies/09/21/toronto.film.festival.wrap/ |title=Oprah flick 'Precious' wins top award at Toronto |date=September 21, 2009 |work=[[CNN]] |first=Katie |last=Walmsley |access-date=November 16, 2009 |archive-date=May 26, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120526231657/http://edition.cnn.com/2009/SHOWBIZ/Movies/09/21/toronto.film.festival.wrap/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The trailer for ''Precious'' was shown during previews of the film's producer Perry's film ''[[I Can Do Bad All By Myself (film)|I Can Do Bad All By Myself]]'' in September 2009.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://news.moviefone.com/2009/02/20/push-shoved-precious-is-the-new-title-for-sundance-smash/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140812040945/http://news.moviefone.com/2009/02/20/push-shoved-precious-is-the-new-title-for-sundance-smash/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 12, 2014 |title='Push' Shoved; 'Precious' is the New Title for Sundance Smash |first=William |last=Gross |date=February 20, 2009 |website=[[Moviefone]] |access-date=November 17, 2009 }}</ref>

===Box office===
''Precious'' was given a limited-theatrical release on November 6, 2009, and was originally scheduled to appear on screens only in North America. During its opening weekend, the film earned $1,872,458, which placed twelfth on that weekend's box office list, despite being in only 18 theaters.<ref name="boxofficemojo">{{cite web |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=preciouspush.htm |title=Precious: Based On The Novel 'Push' By Sapphire |website=[[Box Office Mojo]] |access-date=November 16, 2009 |archive-date=November 20, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091120022618/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=preciouspush.htm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/weekend/chart/?view=&yr=2009&wknd=45&p=.htm |title=November 6–8, 2009 |website=Box Office Mojo |access-date=November 16, 2009 |archive-date=November 18, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091118002631/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/weekend/chart/?view=&yr=2009&wknd=45&p=.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> The film saw a 214 percent increase in its second week of release, earning $5,874,628 at 174 theaters, which catapulted it up to third place in that weekend's box office, with a per-theater average of $33,762.<ref name="boxofficemojochart">{{cite web |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/weekend/chart/ |title=November 13–15, 2009 |work=[[Box Office Mojo]] |access-date=November 20, 2009 |archive-date=June 14, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100614183248/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/weekend/chart/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On November 20, 2009, the film received a wider release, showing at 629 theaters (thus tripling the number of theaters showing the film).<ref name="boxofficemojo" /> In its third week, ''Precious'', as studios had previously estimated, placed sixth at the box office, with the revenues estimated $11,008,000{{emdash}}an 87.4% increase from the previous week.<ref name="boxofficemojo" />

After riding that three-week wave of success, ''Precious'' began to see a decrease in box office earnings. Brandon Grey of [[Box Office Mojo]] described ''Precious'' as having had a "robust expansion" in its second week of release, and he confirmed that the film holds the record for having the second-highest grossing weekend for a movie playing at fewer than 200 sites, behind only ''[[Paranormal Activity]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=2624&p=.htm |title=Weekend Report: '2012' Plagues the Box Office |website=Box Office Mojo |date=November 16, 2009 |first=Branon |last=Grey |access-date=November 21, 2009 |archive-date=November 19, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091119022611/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=2624&p=.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Precious'' grossed a total of $40,320,285 in over six weeks of release.<ref name="boxofficemojo" /> The film opened at ninth place in the United Kingdom, with revenues totaling £259,000 in its opening weekend from a limited release of 47 cinemas, generating a £5,552 screen average.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/filmblog/2010/feb/02/precious-uk-box-office |title=Precious gives Avatar a run for its screen average at UK box office |work=The Guardian |access-date=February 2, 2010 |date=February 2, 2010 |first=Charles |last=Gant |archive-date=June 12, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150612005843/http://www.theguardian.com/film/filmblog/2010/feb/02/precious-uk-box-office |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Home media===
The film was released on [[DVD-Video]] and [[Blu-ray Disc]] formats on March 9, 2010, reaching number one on the top DVD sales chart in the United States with 1.5 million DVDs sold in its first week of release.<ref name="dvdsales"/> It also reached the top position on the rental charts for [[iTunes]] and [[Amazon.com]].<ref name="dvdsales">{{cite web |url=http://www.mariahcarey.com/news/news.php?uid=2838 |website=MariahCarey.com (official website) |title="Precious" sales report |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100603190142/http://www.mariahcarey.com/news/news.php?uid=2838|archive-date=June 3, 2010 |access-date=March 24, 2010}}</ref>

==Reception==

===Critical response===
{{multiple image
