Geoffrey McNab at ''[[The Independent]]'' called the film "both a surefire crowdpleaser and a magnificent piece of film-making" in his 5 star review from the [[Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite news|last=McNab|first=Geoffrey|title=The Artist, Cannes Film Festival|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/reviews/the-artist-cannes-film-festival-2285354.html|work=The Independent|location=UK|access-date=27 October 2011|date=18 May 2011|archive-date=1 December 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111201213444/http://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/reviews/the-artist-cannes-film-festival-2285354.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Rick Groen of ''[[The Globe and Mail]]'' assessed ''The Artist'' highly, noting the film "uses old technology to dazzling effect to illustrate the insistent conquest of a new technology."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/arts/movies/the-artist-mostly-mute-it-speaks-volumes-about-silent-film/article2264777/|title=The Artist: Mostly mute, it speaks volumes about silent film|work=[[The Globe and Mail]]|publisher=The Globe and Mail Limited|first=Rick|last=Groen|date=9 December 2011|access-date=13 January 2012|location=Toronto|archive-date=10 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120110141110/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/arts/movies/the-artist-mostly-mute-it-speaks-volumes-about-silent-film/article2264777/|url-status=live}}</ref> Sukanya Verma for [[Rediff.com]] feels ''The Artist'' is an extremely well-researched film and is an instant classic.<ref name="Review : The Artist ">{{cite web|url=http://www.rediff.com/movies/review/review-the-artist-is-an-instant-classic/20120224.htm|title=Review: The Artist is an instant classic|author=Sukanya Verma|work=Rediff.com|access-date=24 February 2012}}</ref> David Thomson of ''[[The New Republic]]'' called ''The Artist'' an "accomplished and witty entertainment" and went on to write, "Whether Hazanavicius can do more things as elegant and touching, without the gimmick of silence, remains to be seen (and heard). Meanwhile, he is to be congratulated on the grounds of pleasure alone. He may be due for much more in the way of rewards."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.tnr.com/article/film/99237/artist-cannes-hazanavicius-dujardin|title=Why 'The Artist' Just Might Win the Oscars|author=David Thomson|publisher=The New Republic|date=5 January 2012|archive-date=10 January 2012|access-date=26 February 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120110222702/http://www.tnr.com/article/film/99237/artist-cannes-hazanavicius-dujardin|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'' [[film criticism|film critic]] [[Roger Ebert]] gave the film four out of four stars, praising the performances, and calling the film "one of the most entertaining films in many a moon, a film that charms because of its story, its performances and because of the sly way it plays with being silent and black and white."<ref>{{cite news|last=Ebert|first=Roger|author-link=Roger Ebert|url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/the-artist-2011|title=The Artist review|website=[[RogerEbert.com]]|publisher=Ebert Digital LLC|date=25 July 2013|archive-date=12 April 2020|access-date=20 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200412040356/https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/the-artist-2011|url-status=live}}</ref>

Writing for ''[[Slant Magazine]]'', Jaime N. Christley gave the film one-and-a-half out of four stars, explaining Michel Hazanavicius ignores "everything that's fascinating and memorable about the era, focusing instead on a patchwork of general knowledge, so eroded of inconvenient facts that it doesn't even qualify as a ''roman à clef''."<ref>{{cite web|title=Film Review – The Artist|url=https://www.slantmagazine.com/film/review/the-artist/5846|work=[[Slant Magazine]]|access-date=27 February 2012|author=Jaime N. Christley|date=16 October 2011|archive-date=26 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120126034311/http://www.slantmagazine.com/film/review/the-artist/5846|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[America (magazine)|America]]'' argued that while Jean Dujardin carried the film, Bejo's performance was disappointing.<ref name="america">{{cite news|title=The French Connection|first=Victor|last=Stepien|url=http://www.americamagazine.org/content/culture.cfm?cultureID=258|newspaper=[[America (Jesuit magazine)|America]]|date=12 March 2012|access-date=6 March 2012|archive-date=15 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121015094749/http://americamagazine.org/content/culture.cfm?cultureid=258|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Kim Novak controversy===
On 9 January 2012, actress [[Kim Novak]] stated that "rape" had been metaphorically committed in the film's licensed use of a portion of [[Bernard Herrmann]]'s score from [[Alfred Hitchcock]]'s 1958 film ''[[Vertigo (film)|Vertigo]]'' (in which Novak starred). The final portion of ''The Artist'' is accompanied not by original music, but by a 1992 recording of the Herrmann composition ''Scene d'Amour'', conducted by [[Elmer Bernstein]]. In the article published, by ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'', she stated that "I feel as if my body—or at least my body of work—has been violated by the movie."<ref name="Vertigo">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/entertainment-arts-16482624|title=Artist director responds to Kim Novak Vertigo claim|publisher=BBC News|access-date=10 January 2012|date=10 January 2012|archive-date=10 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120110174114/http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/entertainment-arts-16482624|url-status=live}}</ref> "This film should've been able to stand on its own without depending on Bernard Herrmann's score from Alfred Hitchcock's ''Vertigo'' to provide more drama" and that "It is morally wrong for the artistry of our industry to use and abuse famous pieces of work to gain attention and applause for other than what they were intended", ending her comments with "Shame on them!"<ref name="CNN">{{cite news|title='The Artist' director defends use of Hitchcock score|url=http://marquee.blogs.cnn.com/2012/01/10/the-artist-director-defends-use-of-hitchcock-score/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120110234927/http://marquee.blogs.cnn.com/2012/01/10/the-artist-director-defends-use-of-hitchcock-score/|url-status=dead|archive-date=10 January 2012|work=The Marquee Blog|publisher=CNN|access-date=12 January 2012|date=10 January 2012}}</ref>

In response, director Hazanavicius released a statement:<blockquote>''The Artist'' was made as a love letter to cinema, and grew out of my (and all of my cast and crew's) admiration and respect for movies throughout history. It was inspired by the work of Hitchcock, [[Fritz Lang|Lang]], [[John Ford|Ford]], [[Ernst Lubitsch|Lubitsch]], [[F. W. Murnau|Murnau]] and [[Billy Wilder|Wilder]]. I love Bernard Herrmann and his music has been used in many different films and I'm very pleased to have it in mine. I respect Kim Novak greatly and I'm sorry to hear she disagrees.<ref>{{cite news|title='The Artist' Director Responds to Kim Novak Slam Over 'Vertigo' Music|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/race/artist-kim-novak-michel-hazanavicius-279757|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|access-date=12 January 2012|date=9 January 2012|archive-date=12 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120112031131/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/race/artist-kim-novak-michel-hazanavicius-279757|url-status=live}}</ref></blockquote> Hazanavicius also told [[CNN]] "I used music from another movie, but it's not illegal. We paid for that, we asked for that and we had the permission to do it. For me there is no real controversy.... I feel sorry for her, but there's a lot of movies with music from other movies, directors do that all the time and I'm not sure it's a big deal."<ref name="CNN" />

In May 2011, when the film was first shown at the Cannes Festival, [[Todd McCarthy]] from ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' mentioned the use of Herrmann's music, "Hazanavicius and Bource daringly choose to explicitly employ Bernard Herrmann's love theme from ''Vertigo'', which is dramatically effective in its own right but is so well known that it yanks you out of one film and places you in the mind-set of another. Surely some sort of reworked equivalent would have been a better idea."<ref name=McCarthy>{{cite news|last=McCarthy|first=Todd|title=The Artist: Cannes Review|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/review/artist-cannes-review-188493|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|publisher=[[Prometheus Global Media|Prometheus Global Media, LLC]]|access-date=12 January 2012|date=15 May 2011|archive-date=1 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120101230321/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/review/artist-cannes-review-188493|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Accolades===
{{main|List of accolades received by The Artist (film)|l1=List of accolades received by ''The Artist'' (film)}}
At the [[65th British Academy Film Awards]], the film won seven awards, including Best Film, Best Actor for Dujardin, Best Original Screenplay for Hazanavicius, Cinematography for Schiffman, Costume Design for Bridges and Original Score for [[Ludovic Bource]].<ref name="Orange BAFTA Film Award Winners">{{cite web|url=http://www.digitalspy.co.uk/movies/news/a364820/orange-bafta-film-awards-2012-winners-list-in-full.html|title=Orange BAFTA Film Awards 2012 winners list&nbsp;— in full|date=12 February 2012|publisher=Digital Bits|access-date=16 February 2012|archive-date=16 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120316084410/http://www.digitalspy.co.uk/movies/news/a364820/orange-bafta-film-awards-2012-winners-list-in-full.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="BAFTA 2012 Winners">{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2012/feb/12/baftas-2012-winners-full-list?intcmp=239|title=BAFTA 2012 the winners&nbsp;— the full list|work=The Guardian|location=UK|date=12 February 2012|access-date=16 February 2012|archive-date=20 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180620102114/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2012/feb/12/baftas-2012-winners-full-list?intcmp=239|url-status=live}}</ref> At the [[69th Golden Globe Awards]], the film was nominated for six [[Golden Globes]] to win three of them; [[Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy|Best Motion Picture&nbsp;– Musical or Comedy]], [[Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Motion Picture Musical or Comedy|Best Actor&nbsp;– Motion Picture Musical or Comedy]] for Dujardin and [[Golden Globe Award for Best Musical Score|Best Musical Score]] for Bource.<ref name="Golden Globes 2012 Winners">{{Cite web|date=15 January 2012|title=Golden Globes 2012: The Winners List|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/golden-globes-2012-winners-list-282032/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210519035628/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/golden-globes-2012-winners-list-282032/|archive-date=19 May 2021|access-date=2 September 2023|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref>

At the [[84th Academy Awards]], ''The Artist'' received ten nominations, winning five awards, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]], [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]] for Hazanavicius, [[Academy Award for Best Actor|Best Actor in a Leading Role]] for [[Jean Dujardin]], [[Academy Award for Best Costume Design|Best Costume Design]], and [[Academy Award for Best Original Score|Best Original Score]].<ref name="Oscar winners 2012">{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2012/feb/27/oscars-2012-full-list-winners|title=Oscar 2012 winners&nbsp;– The full list|work=The Guardian|location=UK|date=27 February 2012|access-date=28 February 2012|archive-date=27 February 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120227121239/http://www.guardian.co.uk/film/2012/feb/27/oscars-2012-full-list-winners|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Academy Awards 2012 winners">{{cite web|url=http://www.oscars.org/awards/academyawards/84/nominees.html|title=Nominees and Winners for the 84th Academy Awards|publisher=Academy Awards of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (Oscars)|access-date=21 February 2012|archive-date=25 August 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130825202636/http://www.oscars.org/awards/academyawards/84/nominees.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/entertainment-arts-17178811|title=France hails The Artist's Oscars triumph|date=27 February 2012|publisher=BBC News|access-date=27 February 2012|archive-date=27 February 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120227185525/http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/entertainment-arts-17178811|url-status=live}}</ref>

'''''The Assassin''''' ({{zhl|c=刺客聂隐娘}}) is a 2015 [[wuxia]] film co-written and directed by [[Hou Hsiao-hsien]], starring [[Shu Qi]] and [[Chang Chen]]. A Taiwanese–Chinese–Hong Kong [[international co-production]], the film is loosely based on the ninth-century Chinese short story "[[Nie Yinniang]]" by [[Pei Xing]].

''The Assassin'' premiered on 21 May 2015 at the [[2015 Cannes Film Festival|Cannes Film Festival]], where Hou won [[Best Director Award (Cannes Film Festival)|Best Director]]. It was released in China and Hong Kong on 27 August 2015, and a day later in Taiwan. It was Taiwan's entry for the [[Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film|Best Foreign Language Film]] at the [[88th Academy Awards]], but was not nominated. Critically acclaimed, ''The Assassin'' was named the best film of 2015 by ''[[Sight & Sound]]'' magazine. It was Hou's final film before his retirement in 2023 after it was announced that he was battling with [[dementia]].

== Synopsis ==
''The Assassin'' is loosely based on the ninth-century Chinese short story "[[Nie Yinniang]]" by Pei Xing, a core text in [[Chinese swordsmanship]] and [[wuxia]] fiction.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://variety.com/2015/film/features/hou-hsiao-hsien-the-assassin-taiwan-director-1201620922/|title= 'The Assassin': Hou Hsiao-hsien on the Making of His Martial-Arts Epic |author= Justin Chang|date= 21 October 2015|access-date= 10 November 2015|work= [[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Altenburger |first=Roland |title=The Sword or the Needle: The Female Knight-errant (xia) in Traditional Chinese Narrative |publisher=Peter Lang |series=Worlds of East Asia |volume=15 |date=2009 |chapter=2.1 Social Policing and Gender Reversal: The Assassin Nie Yinniang |page=57 |isbn=978-3-0343-0036-0}}</ref> The film is set in China during the [[Emperor Dezong of Tang#Period of strong chancellors Li Mi and Lu Zhi (early Zhenyuan era)|Zhenyuan era]] (785–805) of the mid-[[Tang dynasty]], a few years after the [[An Lushan rebellion]] (755–763). The [[Circuit (administrative division)|circuit]] of [[Weibo (Tang dynasty)|Weibo]], though nominally a part of the Tang Empire, is ''de facto'' ruled independently by military governor [[Tian Ji'an]].

The film centers on Nie Yinniang, an assassin who is directed to slay corrupt government officials by her master, Jiaxin, a nun who raised her from the age of ten. When Yinniang displays mercy by failing to kill during her duties, Jiaxin punishes her with a ruthless assignment designed to test Yinniang's resolve: she is sent to the distant circuit of Weibo in northern China to kill its military governor, her cousin Tian Ji'an, to whom she was betrothed as a child.

As Lady Nie Tian (Yinniang's mother) recounts to her when she arrives, the betrothal was a consequence of Jiacheng's own marriage. Jiacheng was married off to an official of Weibo to quell unrest in Weibo, whereupon she adopted her husband's son, Tian Ji'an as her own. At her request, Tian Ji'an was betrothed to Yinniang at the age of fifteen. However, the betrothal was canceled in favor of a politically pressing marriage, and Yinniang was sent off to live with Princess Jiacheng's sister the nun Jiaxin. Yinniang wrestles with her mission to kill Tian Ji'an, especially in front of his children.

When Yinniang's uncle [[Tian Hongzheng|Tian Xing]] expresses views Tian Ji'an finds offensive in a meeting of state, Tian Ji'an demotes Tian Xing and sends him away to [[Linqing]] under the protection of Nie Feng, Yinniang's father. They are soon ambushed, but Yinniang arrives in time to rescue them. She accompanies the wounded survivors to a village where they meet a young mirror-polisher.

Yinniang protects Tian Ji'an on the journey where she was expected to kill him, and eventually tells Jiaxin that killing him while his sons were young would have plunged Weibo into chaos. Jiaxin dismisses Yinniang for her emotional failures after praising her unmatched martial skills. Yinniang then spares the life of the old nun before joining the traveling mirror-polisher as his guardian.

== Production ==
{{quote box|width=40%|quote="I haven't shot a movie in six or seven years. It's really a whole new world for me because the market is now so big, because of China. So the scale is much bigger, and that makes every detail different, so now even I have to adjust my scale."|source=—Hou Hsiao-hsien<ref name=Hou>{{cite web|url= http://www.filmbiz.asia/news/golden-horse-talent-hou-hsiao-hsien|title= Golden Horse Talent: Hou Hsiao-hsien|author= Staff Reporter|date= 20 November 2013|access-date= 15 January 2014|work= [[Film Business Asia]]|url-status= dead|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140116095901/http://www.filmbiz.asia/news/golden-horse-talent-hou-hsiao-hsien|archive-date= 16 January 2014|df= dmy-all}}</ref>}}
The film received several subsidies from the Taiwanese government: in 2005 of [[New Taiwan dollar|NT$]]15 million ([[United States dollar|US$]]501,000), in 2008 of NT$80 million (US$2.67 million) and in 2010 of NT$20 million (US$668,000).<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.filmbiz.asia/news/hous-assassin-stops-production-again|title= Hou's Assassin stops production (again)|author= Stephen Cremin|date= 31 July 2013|access-date= 15 January 2014|work= [[Film Business Asia]]|url-status= dead|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140116095808/http://www.filmbiz.asia/news/hous-assassin-stops-production-again|archive-date= 16 January 2014|df= dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.filmbiz.asia/news/taiwan-cinema-north-or-south|title= Taiwan cinema: north or south?|author= Stephen Cremin|date= 20 March 2013|access-date= 15 January 2014|work= [[Film Business Asia]]|url-status= dead|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160303205433/http://www.filmbiz.asia/news/taiwan-cinema-north-or-south|archive-date= 3 March 2016|df= dmy-all}}</ref> However, over the production, Hou encountered various budget problems; thus more than half of the film's final budget came from China, a first for Hou.<ref name=wraps/> As of September 2012, its budget was [[Renminbi|CN¥]]90 million (US$14.9 million).<ref name=wraps>{{cite web|url= http://www.filmbiz.asia/news/hou-hsiao-hsiens-assassin-wraps|title= Hou Hsiao-hsien's Assassin wraps|author= Stephen Cremin|date= 14 January 2014|access-date= 15 January 2014|work= [[Film Business Asia]]|url-status= dead|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140116095813/http://www.filmbiz.asia/news/hou-hsiao-hsiens-assassin-wraps|archive-date= 16 January 2014|df= dmy-all}}</ref>

The film was filmed in several places in China, mainly in [[Hubei]], [[Inner Mongolia]] and [[northeast China]].<ref name=press>{{cite book|title=The Assassin Press Kit|publisher=Cannes Film Festival}}</ref> Hou recalled that he was "blown away" when he saw "those silver birch forests and lakes: it was like being transported into a Chinese classical painting."<ref name=press/>

== Release ==
The first press conference of ''The Assassin'' since its Cannes premiere was held in [[Shanghai]] on 16 June 2015, where Hou and the film's cast discussed their Cannes experience and their upcoming promotional activities for the film.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://video.mtime.com/54694/?mid=49650|title=上海发布会 (Shanghai Press Conference)|type=video|publisher=Mtime.com Inc.}}</ref>

The film premiered in [[Beijing]] on 23 August 2015, ahead of its nationwide release on 27 August 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://video.mtime.com/56007/?mid=49650|title=新闻发布会|publisher=Mtime.com Inc.}}</ref> For its American release, the film's distribution rights were acquired by independent distribution company [[Well Go USA Entertainment]] on 11 May 2015, and the film was released on 16 October 2015.<ref name=Aqcuired>{{cite news|last1=Hipes|first1=Patrick|title=Hou Hsiao-hsien's 'The Assassin' Acquired By Well Go USA Ahead Of Cannes Premiere|url=https://deadline.com/2015/05/the-assassin-movie-hou-hsiao-hsien-acquired-well-go-usa-1201424519/|access-date=22 December 2015|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|publisher=Penske Business Media, LLC|date=11 May 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=The Assassin 刺客聶隱娘|url=http://www.wellgousa.com/theatrical/the-assassin|website=Well Go USA Entertainment|publisher=Well Go USA, Inc.|access-date=22 December 2015|archive-date=6 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906010409/http://www.wellgousa.com/theatrical/the-assassin|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Home media ===
''The Assassin'' was released on [[Blu-ray]] and DVD in Hong Kong on 20 December 2015. The North American release was 26 January 2016 and included four behind-the-scenes featurettes regarding the film.<ref>{{cite news|author1=Webmaster|title=The Assassin (2015) Blu-ray Detailed|url=http://www.blu-ray.com/news/?id=18094|access-date=22 December 2015|work=Blu-ray.com|publisher=Blu-ray.com|date=8 December 2015}}</ref>

== Reception ==
=== Box office ===
The film earned {{CNY|61.385 million}} at the Chinese box office.<ref name=cbooo>{{cite web|url= http://www.cbooo.cn/m/7954|script-title= zh:刺客聂隐娘（2015）|access-date= 20 October 2015|work= cbooo.cn|language= zh|archive-date= 17 July 2015|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20150717065421/http://www.cbooo.cn/m/7954|url-status= dead}}</ref> Worldwide box office is around U.S. $12 million.<ref name=BoxOfficeMojo>{{cite web |url= https://www.boxofficemojo.com/movies/?page=intl&id=theassassin.htm|title= The Assassin（2015）}}</ref>

=== Critical response ===
[[File:Shu Qi Cannes 2015 3.jpg|thumb|[[Shu Qi]] promoting the film at the 2015 Cannes Film Festival]]
''The Assassin'' opened to critical acclaim. On review aggregator website [[Rotten Tomatoes]], the film holds an 80% rating, based on 102 reviews, with an average rating of 7.5/10. The site's consensus states: "''The Assassin''{{'}}s thrilling visuals mark a fresh highlight for director Hsiao-hsien Hou, even if its glacial pace may keep some viewers at arm's length."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/the_assassin_2015/ |title=The Assassin (2015) |work=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Flixster]] |access-date=22 December 2015}}</ref> [[Metacritic]] reports an 81 out of 100 rating, based on 29 critics.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/the-assassin |title=The Assassin reviews |work=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |access-date=22 December 2015}}</ref> ''[[Sight & Sound]]'' magazine ranked ''The Assassin'' as the best film of 2015 based on a poll of 168 critics from around the world.<ref name="S&S">{{cite web|title=The 20 best films of 2015|url=https://www2.bfi.org.uk//best-films-2015|access-date=1 January 2016|website=[[Sight & Sound]]|publisher=[[British Film Institute]]|archive-date=1 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160101173019/http://www.bfi.org.uk/best-films-2015|url-status=live}}</ref> The Online Film Critics Society called the film the best foreign language film of 2015.<ref>{{cite news|title='Mad Max' Earns Top Honors from the Online Film Critics Society|url=http://www.ofcs.org/mad-max-earns-top-honors-from-the-online-film-critics-society/|access-date=14 December 2015|work=Online Film Critics Society|date=13 December 2015}}</ref>
It also ranked 50th in a 2016 [[BBC]] poll of the 21st century's greatest films.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bbc.com/culture/story/20160819-the-21st-centurys-100-greatest-films |title=The 21st Century's 100 greatest films |publisher=BBC |date=August 23, 2016 |access-date=September 20, 2016}}</ref>

''[[New York Times]]'' co-chief film critic [[Manohla Dargis]] called the film "staggeringly lovely" at Cannes, describing it as having "held the Wednesday-night audience in rapturous silence until the closing credits, when thunderous applause and booming bravos swept through the auditorium like a wave".<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.nytimes.com/2015/05/21/movies/at-the-cannes-film-festival-some-gems-midway-through.html|title= At the Cannes Film Festival, Some Gems Midway Through |author= Manohla Dargis|date= 20 May 2015|access-date= 24 May 2015|work= [[nytimes.com]]}}</ref> ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]''{{'}}s chief film critic [[Justin Chang]] highly praised the film, saying: "The sheer depth of its formal artistry places ''The Assassin'' in a rather more rarefied realm.... Hou implicitly grasps the expressive power of stillness and reserve, the ways in which silence can build tension and heighten interest. Above all, he never loses sight of the fact that the bodies he moves so fluidly and intuitively through space are human, and remain so even in death. ... Hou Hsiao-hsien proves himself to be not just the creator of this assassin but an unmistakably kindred spirit."<ref>{{cite web |url= https://variety.com/2015/film/news/the-assassin-review-cannes-hou-hsiao-hsien-1201501865/|title= Cannes Film Review: 'The Assassin'|author= Justin Chang|date= May 2015|access-date= 24 May 2015|work= [[variety.com]]}}</ref> On ''[[Film Business Asia]]'', Derek Elley gave it nine out of ten, saying that "Hou Hsiao-hsien's first [[wuxia]] masterfully blends the genre's essence and his own style".<ref name=Elley>{{cite web|url= http://www.filmbiz.asia/reviews/the-assassin|title= The Assassin|author= Derek Elley|date= 22 May 2015|access-date= 24 May 2015|work= [[Film Business Asia]]|url-status= dead|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160510193309/http://www.filmbiz.asia/reviews/the-assassin|archive-date= 10 May 2016|df= dmy-all}}</ref> Deborah Young of ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' said: "Hou Hsiao-hsien brings a pure, idiosyncratic vision to the martial arts genre".<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/review/assassin-cannes-review-797267|title= 'The Assassin': Cannes Review|author= Deborah Young|date= 20 May 2015|access-date= 24 May 2015|work= [[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref> [[Ignatiy Vishnevetsky]] of ''[[The A.V. Club]]'' described the "enigmatic and often mesmerizing" ''The Assassin'' as "one of the most flat-out beautiful movies of the last decade, and also one of the most puzzling". He stated: "Mood is key here...[the film is] all muted and subsumed by a poetic atmosphere that's radical even by Hou's standards... It's a movie most will be intoxicated by, but few will be able to confidently say that they understand—which may be the point, part and parcel with its conception of a world of gestures and values so absolute as to be nearly unknowable."<ref>{{Cite web|title = The Assassin is as beautiful and transfixing as it is enigmatic|url = https://www.avclub.com/review/assassin-beautiful-and-transfixing-it-enigmatic-226652|website = www.avclub.com| date=15 October 2015 |access-date = 2015-11-17}}</ref>

John Esther of ''[[UR Chicago]]'' gave the film a more mixed review, saying that "the real strength (and strain) of ''The Assassin'' is the mise-en-scène by Hou and director of photographer Mark Lee Ping Bing (''In the Mood for Love''; ''Renoir'')" but was critical of the glossy depiction of the environment, saying: "The costumes, the people, the woods, the art, and the interiors are relentlessly pretty. Other than human nature, ''The Assassin'' suggests there was nothing ugly to witness during this period in time".<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.urchicago.com/reviews/2015/10/16/the-assassin.html|title= The Assassin|author= John Esther|access-date= 30 October 2015|work= [[UR Chicago]]|archive-date= 19 April 2017|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170419002625/http://www.urchicago.com/reviews/2015/10/16/the-assassin.html|url-status= dead}}</ref>

Sarah Cronin of the British magazine ''Electric Sheep'' wrote: "The intricacies of the story are bewildering, with the 'who' and the 'why' only obliquely revealed as the film lingers on. But rather than lending ''The Assassin'' an air of intrigue, these mysteries seem pointlessly and frustratingly obtuse, with the most potent symbolism left to be teased out of a broken piece of jade, while not enough is done to bring the characters to life, to make them whole. Hou Hsiao-hsien deliberately avoids giving its audience any of the pleasures of wuxia, but its take on the genre offers little, and feels like a pale shadow of fellow auteur Wong Kar Wai's ''[[Ashes of Time]]''.  It looks gorgeous, but there's a shallowness to its beauty. ''The Assassin'', unfortunately, is more still life than cinema".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.electricsheepmagazine.co.uk/reviews/2016/01/21/the-assassin-2/|title=The Assassin|work=Electric Sheep|last=Cronin|first=Sarah|date=21 January 2016}}</ref>

In his review for the ''[[Los Angeles Review of Books]]'', Victor Fan concluded: "''The Assassin'' is indeed like a [[Chinese ceramics|Ming vase]], beautiful — ''and'' — empty. Those who love this film can see only the vase, and those who dislike this film can see only the emptiness inside it".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-12-29 |title=The Something of Nothing: Hou Hsiao-Hsien's "The Assassin" |url=https://lareviewofbooks.org/article/the-something-of-nothing-hou-hsiao-hsiens-the-assassin |access-date=2024-05-31 |website=Los Angeles Review of Books}}</ref>

'''''The Commitments''''' is a 1991 [[musical film|musical]] [[comedy-drama]] film based on the [[The Commitments (novel)|1987 novel]] by [[Roddy Doyle]]. It was directed by [[Alan Parker]] from a screenplay written by Doyle, [[Dick Clement]] and [[Ian La Frenais]]. Set in the [[Northside (Dublin)|Northside of Dublin]], the film tells the story of Jimmy Rabbitte ([[Robert Arkins]]), a young music fanatic who assembles a group of working-class youths to form a [[soul music|soul]] band named "The Commitments". The film is the first in a series known as ''[[The Barrytown Trilogy]]'', followed by ''[[The Snapper (film)|The Snapper]]'' (1993) and ''[[The Van (1996 film)|The Van]]'' (1996).

Producers [[Lynda Myles (British producer)|Lynda Myles]] and Roger Randall-Cutler acquired the film rights to the novel in 1988, and commissioned Doyle, a first-time screenwriter, to write an adaptation. Doyle spent one year working on the script before Myles brought in veteran screenwriters Clement and La Frenais to help complete it. Upon reading the novel, Parker signed on as the film's director in 1989. An [[Co-production (media)|international co-production]] between [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]], the [[United States]] and the [[United Kingdom]], ''The Commitments'' was the first film produced by [[Beacon Pictures]], which provided an estimated [[production budget|budget]] of $12–15 million. The film's young lead actors were mostly inexperienced, and were cast because of their musical backgrounds and resemblance to the characters in the novel. [[Principal photography]] took place in [[Dublin]], from late August to October, 1990.

''The Commitments'' underperformed at the North American box office, grossing $14.9 million during its theatrical run. Reviewers praised the music, performances and humour, while criticism was occasionally aimed at the pacing and Parker's direction. The film resulted in two soundtrack albums released by [[MCA Records]]; the first reached number eight on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] [[record chart|album chart]] and achieved [[British Phonographic Industry#Certifications|triple-platinum status]], while the second album achieved gold sales status. At the [[45th British Academy Film Awards|1992 British Academy Film Awards]], the film won four of six [[British Academy Film Awards|BAFTA Awards]] for [[BAFTA Award for Best Film|Best Film]], [[BAFTA Award for Best Direction|Best Direction]], [[BAFTA Award for Best Adapted Screenplay|Best Adapted Screenplay]] and [[BAFTA Award for Best Editing|Best Editing]]. It also received an [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] nomination for [[Academy Award for Best Film Editing|Best Film Editing]]. The film has since gained [[cult film|cult status]].

==Plot==
In the [[Northside (Dublin)|Northside]] of [[Dublin]], Ireland, Jimmy Rabbitte is a young music fanatic who aspires to manage an Irish [[Soul music|soul]] and [[rock and roll]] band in the tradition of 1950s and 60s African-American recording artists. He places an advert in the local newspaper and holds auditions in his parents' home. After being deluged by several unsuitable performers, Jimmy decides to put together a band consisting of friends and people he encounters—lead singer Deco Cuffe, guitarist Outspan Foster, keyboardist Steven Clifford, alto saxophonist Dean Fay, bassist Derek Scully, drummer Billy Mooney, and female backing singers Bernie McGloughlin, Natalie Murphy and Imelda Quirke. Jimmy then meets trumpeter Joey "The Lips" Fagan, a veteran musician who offers his services, and has unlikely stories about meeting and working with famous musicians. Joey names the band "The Commitments".

After purchasing a drum set and acquiring a piano from Steven's grandmother, Jimmy secures the remainder of the band's musical equipment from Duffy, a [[black market]] dealer. The band rehearses on the first floor above a [[snooker]] hall, and after much practice, they convince a local church community centre to give them a gig, under the pretence of it being an anti-[[heroin]] campaign. Jimmy then hires Mickah Wallace, a belligerent and hot-tempered bouncer, to act as the band's security. The band draws a good crowd, but after Deco inadvertently hits Derek with his microphone stand, the amplifiers explode, resulting in a power outage.

Tensions run high among the band members, as Joey seduces Natalie, then Bernie, then Imelda, all while Deco grows increasingly obnoxious and unruly, believing himself to be the star of the band. The band performs at another venue where, at the end of one song, Billy accidentally knocks over his [[hi-hat]] cymbals, leading to a heated argument between him and Deco. Billy leaves the band in fear of going to jail if he beats up Deco{{snd}}much to Jimmy's frustration{{snd}}and Mickah replaces him as the band's drummer. During the band's next performance at a [[roller disco]], their first paying gig, Jimmy is confronted by Duffy, who demands payment for the equipment he provided the band. Mickah intervenes and violently attacks Duffy, who is escorted out. Jimmy then goes on stage and introduces the band, which elicits boisterous cheers from the audience.

After the band secures another gig, Joey promises Jimmy that he can get his friend [[Wilson Pickett]] to sing alongside them. On this promise, Jimmy convinces several journalists to attend the band's next performance. At the venue, the band draws a large crowd, but its members begin arguing with each other offstage, and become doubtful when it appears that Pickett will not show. They go back on stage, where Deco denounces Jimmy for misleading the audience about Pickett's appearance; the band's performance of one of Pickett's songs, "[[In the Midnight Hour]]", silences the crowd's protests. After the performance, the fighting continues; during a heated argument, Mickah beats up Deco outside the club, and Jimmy storms off in frustration, claiming that the band is finished. Joey follows Jimmy, who berates him for misleading the band about Pickett. Joey apologizes to Jimmy, and assures him that despite the band breaking up, Jimmy is still a success for helping the others realize their self worth and potential to rise above their previous lot in life. Just as Joey leaves, Pickett's limousine pulls up next to Jimmy, and his driver asks for directions to the club, revealing that Joey was telling the truth about Pickett; he just showed up too late.

In a closing monologue, Jimmy explains that the band's members have since gone their separate ways; Bernie joined a country band, Deco got his record deal and became a bigger egomaniac, Mickah sings for a punk band, Outspan & Derek still play as street [[buskers]], Dean formed a successful jazz band, Joey's mother got a postcard that he was touring with Joe Tex (who had died a decade prior), Steven became a doctor but misses playing music, Billy is recovering from getting kicked in the head by a horse, Imelda married Greg (who won't let her sing anymore), Natalie became a successful solo singer, and implies that she and Jimmy are in a relationship.

==Production==

===Development===
{{multiple image|caption_align=center|header_align=center
 | align = right
 | width1 = 130
 | image1 = doyleroddy33.jpg
 | alt1 =
 | width2 = 140
 | image2 = Alan Parker (Director), London, 2012.jpg
 | alt2 =
 | footer = [[Roddy Doyle]] (left), who co-wrote the film adaptation of his novel, and [[Alan Parker]], who directed the film.
}}

Following the 1988 publication of [[Roddy Doyle]]'s novel ''[[The Commitments (novel)|The Commitments]]'' (1987) in the [[United Kingdom]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Looking back at THE COMMITMENTS: 25 Years Later with author/co-screenwriter Roddy Doyle|date=29 January 2016 |url=https://www.tenement.org/blog/looking-back-at-the-commitments-25-years-later-with-authorco-screenwriter-roddy-doyle/|publisher=[[Lower East Side Tenement Museum]]|access-date=4 January 2017}}</ref> producers [[Lynda Myles (British producer)|Lynda Myles]] and Roger Randall-Cutler acquired the [[film rights]], and asked Doyle to write an [[film adaptation|adaptation]].<ref name="IrishSoul" /><ref name="ProdNotes">{{cite web|last=Parker|first=Alan|author-link=Alan Parker|title=The Commitments – The Making of the Film|url=http://alanparker.com/film/the-commitments/making|publisher=Alan Parker.com|access-date=28 August 2015}}</ref> Doyle, an inexperienced screenwriter, spent one year drafting the script,<ref name="IrishSoul" /> accompanied by Myles and Randall-Cutler.<ref name="DisGlobe">{{cite web|title=This Distracted Globe — Film reviews and commentary tonight, before I forget tomorrow|url=http://thisdistractedglobe.com/page/74/|publisher=This Distracted Globe|access-date=4 January 2017|archive-date=5 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170105175539/http://thisdistractedglobe.com/page/74/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Although a script was completed, Myles felt it needed improvement, and passed the book on to [[Dick Clement]] and [[Ian La Frenais]],<ref name="DisGlobe" /> hoping that they would suggest a more experienced writer.<ref name="IrishSoul" /> Upon reading the novel, Clement and La Frenais agreed to help write the script themselves.<ref name="DisGlobe" />

In 1989, Myles took the project to [[Beacon Pictures]], an independent film company established that year by [[Armyan Bernstein]], a former television journalist turned screenwriter and producer.<ref name="IrishSoul" /> Clement and La Frenais traveled to Los Angeles to discuss the project with [[Alan Parker]], and gave him a copy of the novel.<ref name="IrishSoul" /> Upon reading the novel, Parker was intrigued by its dialogue and humour, stating, "The book was all dialogue with very little description, but by the use of this wonderful language, and almost nothing but language, in a few lines [Doyle] was able to make his characters as vivid and strong as a dozen pages of purple [[Joycean|Joycian]] prose."<ref name="ProdNotes" /> He signed on to direct the project after concluding work on his previous film ''[[Come See the Paradise]]'' (1990).<ref name="IrishSoul" /><ref name="ProdNotes" /> After Beacon agreed to finance the film, [[20th Century Fox]] acquired the North American and UK distribution rights,<ref name="IrishSoul" /> and Parker was given [[artistic control|creative control]].<ref name="IrishSoul" /><ref name="ProdNotes" /><ref name="Producer">{{cite web|title= Producer Remembers His Prior 'Commitments' : Lecture: Roger Randall-Cutler tells a UC Irvine audience that he's 'rather disappointed' with film's performance in the U.S.|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=10 January 1992|url= https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1992-01-10-ca-1750-story.html|access-date=18 November 2010|first=Rick|last=Vanderknyff}}</ref> The film was an [[international co-production]] between companies in the United Kingdom and the United States.<ref name="IrishFilm" /> Randall-Cutler's The First Film Company and Parker's Dirty Hands Productions, both based in England, were enlisted as production companies.<ref>{{harvnb|Monaco|1992|p=33}}</ref> Parker and the producers later attended the [[1990 Cannes Film Festival]] to secure worldwide [[Film finance#Pre-sales|pre-sales]].<ref name="ProdNotes" />

===Casting===
[[Casting (performing arts)|Casting directors]] John and Ros Hubbard travelled to Dublin, Ireland in April 1990 and spent two months visiting local clubs in their search for musicians to appear in the film.<ref name="ProdNotes" /> In June of that year, Parker travelled to Dublin and placed an advertisement in the magazine ''[[Hot Press]]'', requesting young artists to audition for roles in the film.<ref name="IrishSoul" /><ref>{{harvnb|White|2001|p=33}}</ref> Parker wanted actors who could play a musical instrument and resembled the characters from the novel. He said, "I would stop kids [[busking]] on the streets and call them in to audition&nbsp;... we had to choose kids who were quite talented, because they had to play musicians who were awful at first, but gradually improved."<ref name="IrishSoul" />

Auditions were first held at The Waterfront, a nightclub located near the [[River Liffey]]. [[Jim Corr]] and his sisters [[Andrea Corr]], [[Sharon Corr]] and [[Caroline Corr]] were among those who auditioned.<ref name="ProdNotes" /> Andrea was cast in the non-musical role of Sharon Rabbitte, Jimmy's younger sister, while Sharon and Caroline were cast as members of an Irish band known as "Country & Western"; Jim appears in a brief role as a member of the band "Avant-Garde-A-Clue".<ref name="Deadly"/> Parker then held a casting call at the [[Mansion House, Dublin|Mansion House]] on [[Dawson Street]], Dublin, where 1,500 people auditioned for various roles.<ref name="IrishSoul" />{{rp|2}}<ref name="ProdNotes" /> During the auditions, Parker met [[Andrew Strong]], son of the film's vocal coach Rob Strong, who performed "[[Mustang Sally (song)|Mustang Sally]]". After meeting with Parker to discuss the project, Strong secured the role of Deco Cuffe, the lead singer of The Commitments.<ref name="IrishSoul" /><ref name="ProdNotes" /> [[Robert Arkins]] was initially considered for the role of Deco before he was ultimately cast as Jimmy Rabbitte.<ref name="Commentary">{{cite video|people=Parker, Alan|title=Audio commentary for ''The Commitments''.|medium=[[DVD]]|publisher=[[20th Century Fox Home Entertainment]] }}</ref> Although his character does not have a singing part in the film, Arkins performs the song "[[Treat Her Right (Roy Head song)|Treat Her Right]]" during the [[opening credits]].<ref name="IrishSoul" />{{rp|2}}<ref name="ProdNotes" />

For the role of Joey "the Lips" Fagan, the eldest member of the band, Parker and La Frenais wanted veteran musician [[Van Morrison]]. Although his meeting with Parker did not go well, Morrison offered his songs for use in the film.<ref name="Gonthier, Jr. 2015 201">{{harvnb|Gonthier|O'Brien|2015|p=201}}</ref> [[Rory Gallagher]] was also considered before veteran film and stage actor Johnny Murphy secured the role.<ref name="Murphy">{{cite news|title=Commitments actor Johnny Murphy has died|work=[[The Irish News]]|date=23 February 2016|url=http://www.irishnews.com/news/republicofirelandnews/2016/02/23/news/commitments-actor-johnny-murphy-has-died-428171/|access-date=4 July 2016|first=John|last=Monaghan}}</ref> Although Murphy could not play an instrument,<ref name="WhateverHappened">{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/culturenews/10341635/Whatever-happened-to-The-Commitments.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/culturenews/10341635/Whatever-happened-to-The-Commitments.html |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Whatever happened to The Commitments?|first=Paul|last=Kendall|work=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]|date=29 September 2013|access-date=4 July 2016}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Parker felt that he best captured the essence of both the character and the film.<ref name="Gonthier, Jr. 2015 201" /> Murphy was the only cast member who did not do his own playing in the film.<ref name="Deadly">{{cite web|url=http://www.dailyedge.ie/7-deadly-things-you-may-not-know-about-the-commitments-32207-Oct2010/|title=7 'deadly' things you may not know about The Commitments|first=Susan|last=Daly|date=7 October 2010|work=[[The Daily Edge]]|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> [[Bronagh Gallagher]], another established actor, was cast as Bernie McGloughlin, one of the band's three backup singers known as "The Commitmentettes". The actress, born in Derry, Northern Ireland, had to learn a Dublin accent for the role.<ref>{{cite interview|title=The Arts Show|medium=Programme|chapter=In Conversation with Bronagh Gallagher|date=7 March 2013|location=United Kingdom|publisher=[[BBC]]}}</ref> [[Angeline Ball]] secured the role of Imelda Quirke after a private audition with the Hubbards.<ref>{{cite web|title=Recommitted: 'The Commitments' star on why she shuns the limelight|work=[[Irish Independent]]|date=20 February 2011|url=http://www.independent.ie/style/fashion/recommitted-the-commitments-star-on-why-she-shuns-the-limelight-26706895.html|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref>

[[Maria Doyle Kennedy]] was a member of the Irish quartet band The Black Velvet Band before she was cast as Commitmentette singer Natalie Murphy.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jQ8EAAAAMBAJ&q=maria+doyle+kennedy+black+velvet+band&pg=RA1-PA84|title=Lively Irish Music Business Has Thriving Export Industry|pages=84|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|volume=104|first=Ken|last=Stewart|date=13 June 1992|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> Michael Aherne, who plays The Commitments' pianist Steven Clifford, was an employee of the [[Dublin Corporation]] and took a three-month leave of absence to make the film.<ref name="ProdNotes" /> Future Oscar-winner [[Glen Hansard]], the lead singer of [[The Frames]], was cast as Outspan Foster, the band's guitarist.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/music/features/glen-hansard-interview-the-singer-songwriter-on-finding-fame-in-the-commitments-and-once-a6677831.html|title=Glen Hansard interview: The singer-songwriter on finding fame in The Commitments and Once|first=Nick|last=Duerden|date=3 October 2015|work=[[The Independent]]|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref>

Dave Finnegan was cast as Mickah Wallace, a belligerent and hot-tempered bouncer who becomes a drummer for the band. Parker's first meeting with Finnegan began civilly before their exchanges grew more and more heated. They soon became verbally abusive, threatening each other with disturbing acts of violence. Parker cast Finnegan immediately, explaining that he simply wanted to test the limits of Finnegan's aggression, as he wanted the truculence of the character to be convincing.<ref name="Gonthier, Jr. 2015 201" /> [[Colm Meaney]] first learned of the film adaptation while working with Parker on ''Come See the Paradise''. After Parker held auditions for the younger cast members, Meaney secured the role of Jimmy's father Jimmy Rabbitte Sr.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colm Meaney · Random Roles|work=[[The A.V. Club]]|first=Will|last=Harris|date=4 November 2011|url=http://www.avclub.com/article/colm-meaney-64556|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> The audition scene in the film, in which various musicians audition at Jimmy Rabbitte's home, required more than 100 band members.<ref name="ProdNotes" /> Peter Rowen, brother of Irish artist [[Guggi]], appears as a young skateboarding boy who asks to audition for the band. At the time of the film's production, Rowen had appeared on the cover art of [[U2]]'s albums ''[[Boy (album)|Boy]]'' (1980) and ''[[War (U2 album)|War]]'' (1983), and was a national skating champion.<ref name="Deadly" />

===Filming===
Parker spent five weeks rehearsing with the cast members<ref name="ProdNotes"/><ref name="Gonthier, Jr. 2015 201"/> before [[principal photography]] commenced on 27 August 1990, with an estimated budget of $12–15 million.<ref name="IrishSoul"/><ref name="ScreeningIreland"/><ref name="Surprise"/> While Doyle's novel is set in the fictional [[The Barrytown Trilogy|Barrytown]] (based on [[Kilbarrack]], where Doyle was a schoolteacher), Parker suggested that the film take place in Dublin. A total of 44 locations in the city were used for filming.<ref name="ProdNotes"/><ref name="Gonthier, Jr. 2015 201"/> [[Cinematographer]] [[Gale Tattersall]] sought to create "a gritty, ugly look" that would become more composed and polished as the band became more successful. He felt that this visual style would support the film's story arc.<ref>{{harvnb|Lesko|2011|p=136}}</ref>

The film's opening scene, depicting Jimmy Rabbitte trying to offload cassettes and shirts in a street market, was filmed on [[Sheriff Street]], in front of the St. Lawrence O'Toole Catholic Church.<ref name="locations">{{cite web|title=Film locations for The Commitments (1991)|url=http://www.movie-locations.com/movies/c/Commitments.html|access-date=5 September 2015|archive-date=13 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150913064037/http://www.movie-locations.com/movies/c/Commitments.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> A house located on [[Darndale]] in the [[Northside (Dublin)|Northside of Dublin]] was used to depict the Rabbitte family home.<ref name="locations"/> The home where Joey "the Lips" Fagan resides with his mother was a house located at 118 Pembroke Road in [[Ballsbridge]].<ref name="locations"/> The production also filmed scenes at Ricardo's Pool Hall, a dilapidated building located at 84–87 Lower [[Camden Street, Dublin|Camden Street]]. The second floor of the pool hall was used to depict the band's rehearsals.<ref name="locations"/> The Archbishop Byrne Hall (also known as St. Kevin's Hall), located in the [[Portobello, Dublin|Portobello]] district of Dublin, was used to depict a local church community centre, where The Commitments first perform on stage. The [[Saint Francis Xavier Church, Dublin]], located on Upper [[Gardiner Street]], was used to film a scene in which Jimmy finds Commitments pianist Steven Clifford playing "[[A Whiter Shade of Pale]]" on an organ.<ref name="locations"/> The production team also filmed a scene at a [[Phibsborough]] bus depot; the location was used to depict Jimmy convincing Deco to become a part of the band. A walkway, where Jimmy discusses his plan to form a band with Outspan and Derek was filmed at the [[Kilbarrack railway station|Kilbarrack D.A.R.T. Station]].<ref name="locations"/> Principal photography concluded in mid-October 1990 after 53 days of filming.<ref name="ProdNotes"/><ref name="Gonthier, Jr. 2015 201"/>

===Music===
''The Commitments'' does not have an original [[film score]], but features existing music tracks. [[Music supervisor]] [[G. Marq Roswell]] spent several months during the film's pre-production listening to and categorising hundreds of [[Rhythm and blues|R&B]] songs before travelling to Dublin to help Parker finalise songs that would be used in the film.<ref name="35Sound">{{cite web|url=http://www.35sound.com/content/gmarq_about.html|title=35 Sound|publisher=35Sound.com|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> Parker and Roswell had created a "short list" of 1,000 possible song choices.<ref name="Muse">{{cite web|url=http://www.musesmuse.com/00000398.html|title=The Story Leads the Dance: An Interview with music supervisor G. Marq Roswell|first=Jerry|last=Flatum|work=The Muse's Muse|date=17 January 2003|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> From May to June 1990, Parker had listened to more than 300 songs from the 1960s before narrowing his choices down to 75 songs. The finished film features 68 different musical cues and 52 songs. 24 songs were chosen by the director to be performed by the cast.<ref name="ProdNotes" /> Roswell also organised and oversaw the recording sessions.<ref name="35Sound" /> The songs were recorded live on set, as Parker wanted to capture the reality of the band's rehearsals and performances.<ref name="ProdNotes" /> The filmmakers used [[Out Of Phase Stereo|out-of-phase speakers]], which enabled them to play pre-recorded tracks at maximum volume, creating a live performance atmosphere. Each song was then recorded onto a [[Multitrack recording|24-track recorder]].<ref name="ProdNotes" />

==Soundtracks==
{{Main|The Commitments (soundtrack)}}
A motion picture soundtrack album with music produced by [[Kevin Killen]] and [[Paul Bushnell]] was released on 13 August 1991, by [[MCA Records]].<ref name="CDUniverse1">{{cite web |url=http://www.cduniverse.com/productinfo.asp?pid=1103429&style=music|title=Commitments Soundtrack CD Album|publisher=CD Universe|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> The soundtrack features fourteen songs, most of which appeared in various scenes in the film. [[Niamh Kavanagh]] performed as both a lead and backing vocalist in songs such as "[[The Marvelettes|Destination Anywhere]]" and "[[Do Right Woman, Do Right Man]]".<ref name="CDUniverse1" /> According to ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'', the first soundtrack has sold 12 million copies worldwide.<ref name="WhateverHappened" />

After the commercial success of the first soundtrack album, a follow-up entitled ''The Commitments, Vol. 2: Music From The Original Motion Picture Soundtrack'' was released on 17 March 1992. The album included four more songs from the film, as well as seven additional songs performed by the cast.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cduniverse.com/productinfo.asp?pid=1103500&style=music&fulldesc=T|title=Commitments, Vol. 2 Soundtrack CD Album|publisher=CD Universe|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref>

In 2007, Geffen Records released a 2-CD Deluxe Edition of the soundtrack, which collects ''The Commitments (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)'' and ''The Commitments, Vol. 2: Music From The Original Motion Picture Soundtrack,'' as well as five tracks from cast member Andrew Strong's 1993 solo album ''Strong.''

==Release==
===Strategy===
20th Century Fox felt that ''The Commitments'' would attract young adult audiences, but [[test screening]]s indicated that the film would appeal more to older viewers, due to its musical content.<ref name="AFINotes" /> Parker, a former advertising executive, collaborated with the studio on the film's marketing, running an extensive campaign to attract the intended target audience.<ref name="AFINotes" /> Theatrical posters for the film were distributed to exhibitors in February 1991. Beginning in April 1991, Fox arranged several screenings in Toronto, New York City, San Francisco, Los Angeles and Chicago, with audience members being music industry executives, journalists, disc jockeys and club owners.<ref name="AFINotes" /> In August 1991, the studio hosted a [[Film promotion|press junket]] in Dublin, Ireland for several media outlets.<ref name="AFINotes" /><ref>{{cite news|title=Commitments|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|page=16|volume=318|date=14 August 1991}}</ref> ''The Commitments'' premiered at the [[Pacific Design Center]] in [[West Hollywood, California]] on 6 August 1991,<ref name="AFINotes" /> the [[Cinerama Dome]] Theatre in Hollywood on 7 August 1991,<ref name="AFINotes" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Director Alan Parker attends the premiere of 'The Commitments' at the Cinerama Dome Theater on August 7, 1991 in Hollywood, California. (Photo by Ron Galella, Ltd.)|url=http://www.wireimage.com/celebrity-pictures/Director-Alan-Parker-attends-the-premiere-of-The-Commitments-at-the/156107534|publisher=WireImage|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> the Cineplex Odeon Century Plaza Cinemas in Century City, Los Angeles on 13 August 1991,<ref>{{cite web|title=Director Alan Parker attends the premiere of The Commitments at the&nbsp;... |url=http://www.wireimage.com/celebrity-pictures/Director-Alan-Parker-attends-the-premiere-of-The-Commitments-at-the/156107947|publisher=WireImage|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> and the [[Savoy Cinema]] in Dublin, Ireland on 19 September 1991.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/archives/category/arts-and-culture/2016/0916/817062-dublin-soul-city-for-commitments-premiere/|title=Dublin Soul City For Commitments Premiere|publisher=[[RTÉ]]|access-date=17 December 2016}}</ref>

Fox gave ''The Commitments'' a [[Limited release#Platform release|platform release]] which involved opening the film in select cities before expanding distribution in the following weeks. The film had a [[limited release]] in New York City, Los Angeles, and Ireland on 14 August 1991, and expanded to Toronto, San Francisco and Chicago on 16 August 1991.<ref name="AFINotes" /> The film was released [[wide release|nationwide]] in North America on 13 September 1991, and Ireland on 4 October 1991.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.joe.ie/movies-tv/joes-film-flashback-the-commitments-1991/532185|title=JOE's Film Flashback: The Commitments (1991)|work=[[Joe (website)|Joe]]|first=Tony|last=Cuddihy|access-date=29 January 2017}}</ref><ref name="BOMWeekend">{{cite web|url=http://www.boxofficemojo.com/movies/?page=weekend&id=commitments.htm|title=The Commitments (1991) – Weekend Box Office Results|publisher=[[Box Office Mojo]]|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> The English-based studio Sovereign Pictures handled distribution outside North America except the United Kingdom and Ireland where Fox also handled distribution.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1990-08-26-ca-84-story.html|title=Films going into production|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=26 August 1990|first=David|last=Pecchia|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref>

===Box office===
''The Commitments'' grossed $271,333 on its first week of limited release in North America—an average of $33,916 per theatre.<ref name="WeekendBOM">{{cite web|url=http://www.boxofficemojo.com/movies/?page=weekend&id=commitments.htm|title=The Commitments (1991) – Weekend Box Office Results|publisher=[[Box Office Mojo]]|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> The film grossed an additional $268,653 in its second weekend, with an overall domestic gross of $775,824.<ref name="WeekendBOM" /> More theatres were added in its third week; the film grossed an additional $1,366,223 from 104 theatres, which was a +409% increase from its second weekend.<ref name="WeekendBOM" /> The following week, the film was released to a total of 555 theatres in the United States and Canada. It grossed $2,511,091, securing the number three position at the domestic box office.<ref name="WeekendBOM" /> The film saw a significant drop in attendance during the following week, the film grossed $1,752,234, a 30.2% overall decrease from the previous weekend.<ref name="WeekendBOM" /> After eight weeks of release, ''The Commitments'' ended its theatrical run with an overall gross of $14,919,570.<ref name="BOMWeekend" /> In North America, it was the 80th highest-grossing film of 1991<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?yr=1991&p=.htm|title=1991 Yearly Box Office Results|publisher=Box Office Mojo|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> and the 42nd highest-grossing [[Motion Picture Association of America film rating system|R-rated]] film of that year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/mpaarating.htm?rating=R&yr=1991&p=.htm|title=1991 Yearly Box Office for R Rated Movies|publisher=Box Office Mojo|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref>

The film was the highest-grossing film in Ireland of all time with a gross of [[Irish pound|IR£]]2.23 million ($3.5 million).<ref>{{cite magazine|magazine=[[Daily Variety]]|date=7 March 1994|title=Oscar Boosts Films O'seas|page=38|last=Harris|first=Mike}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|magazine=[[Screen International]]|date=25 April 1997|page=27|title=Ireland flocks to the flicks}}</ref> It grossed £8,285,701 in the UK.<ref name="org"/>

===Home media===
In North America, ''The Commitments'' was released on [[VHS]] on 9 April 1992 by [[CBS/Fox Video#FoxVideo, Inc.|FoxVideo, Inc.]]<ref name=AFINotes /> To promote the release, FoxVideo distributed 90,000 videocassette copies of a "making-of" featurette to home video retailers. The featurette was made available to consumers as a free rental. FoxVideo spent an estimated $300,000 on the marketing, and an additional $200,000 promoting the featurette using print and broadcast advertising.<ref name=AFINotes />

A [[DVD region code#1|Region 1]] [[DVD]] was released on 19 August 2003, by [[20th Century Fox Home Entertainment]].<ref name="DVD Beaver">{{cite web |url=http://www.dvdbeaver.com/film/DVDCompare2/commitments.htm|title="The Commitments" 20th Century/Fox (Full Frame) – Region 1 – NTSC vs. 20th Century/Fox (Collector's Edition) – Region 1 – NTSC|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> The DVD presents the film in [[Standard-definition television|standard definition]]. Special features include a [[making-of]] featurette, a music video for the song "[[Treat Her Right (Roy Head song)|Treat Her Right]]", a [[Trailer (promotion)|theatrical trailer]], and CD sampler that plays four songs from the motion picture soundtrack.<ref name="DVD Beaver" /> A two-disc special edition DVD was later released on 16 March 2004.<ref name="DVD Beaver" /> The first disc presents the film in [[widescreen]], and features an [[audio commentary]] by Parker. Other special features include the theatrical trailer, the "Treat Her Right" music video with optional introductions by Parker and Robert Arkins, three featurettes, six [[Television advertisement|TV spots]] for the film, four radio spots, and a still gallery.<ref name="DVD Beaver" /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/9781/commitments-collectors-edition-the/|title=The Commitments (Collector's Edition) : DVD Talk Review of the DVD Video|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref>

''The Commitments'' was released on [[Blu-ray]] on 30 August 2016 by [[RLJ Companies|RLJ Entertainment]], coinciding with the film's 25th anniversary.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.blu-ray.com/movies/The-Commitments-Blu-ray/110699/|title=The Commitments Blu-ray: 25th Anniversary Edition|publisher=BluRay.com|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> The Blu-ray presents the film in [[1080p]] [[High-definition video|high definition]], and contains all the additional materials found on the Special Edition DVD, as well as new interviews with Parker and the cast, and a collective booklet featuring production notes written by Parker.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blu-ray.com/news/?id=19266|title=The Commitments: 25th Anniversary Blu-ray Release Detailed|work=BluRay.com|date=18 June 2016|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref>

==Reception==

===Critical response===
''The Commitments'' received mostly positive reviews.<ref name="AFINotes" /> Review aggregator [[Rotten Tomatoes]] sampled 53 reviews, and gave the film an approval rating of 91%, with an average score of 7.4/10. The critical consensus reads, "''The Commitments'' is a vibrantly funny and blissfully heartfelt ode to the power of music".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/1037024-commitments/|title=The Commitments (1991)|publisher=[[Fandango Media]]|work=[[Rotten Tomatoes]]|access-date=20 July 2026}}</ref> It is also ranked sixth on the website's best reviewed films of 1991.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/top/bestofrt/?year=1991|title=Top 100 Movies of 1991|publisher=[[Fandango Media]]|work=[[Rotten Tomatoes]]|access-date=5 July 2016}}</ref> On [[Metacritic]], the film has a score of 73 out of 100 based on reviews from 23 critics, indicating "generally favorable reviews".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/the-commitments|title=The Commitments Reviews|website=[[Metacritic]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|access-date=25 August 2020}}</ref> Roddy Doyle, author of the 1987 novel, praised the film, stating that Parker and the filmmakers did a "terrific job".<ref name="White 2001 34">{{harvnb|White|2001|p=34}}</ref>

''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' magazine called the film "well-executed and original", and praised the performances as well as the editing by [[Gerry Hambling]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/1990/film/reviews/the-commitments-1200428723/|title=The Commitments|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=January 1991 |access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> [[Jonathan Rosenbaum]] of the ''[[Chicago Reader]]'' wrote, "If [Parker] can't resist the occasional fancy or cutesy flourishes&nbsp;... that tend to compromise his work, he still allows his material to exist on its own level and makes it fun to watch."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chicagoreader.com/chicago/the-commitments/Film?oid=1055053|title=The Commitments|work=[[Chicago Reader]]|first=Jonathan|last=Rosenbaum|date=26 October 1985 |author-link=Jonathan Rosenbaum|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> [[Hal Hinson]] of ''[[The Washington Post]]'' described the film as "a deadly funny movie; nearly every scene is broken off with a punch line. But Parker's sense of comedy is organic; he never lets the jokes elbow the characters, or the music, out of the spotlight."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/style/longterm/movies/videos/thecommitmentsrhinson_a0a704.htm|title='The Commitments' (R)|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|first=Hal|last=Hinson|author-link=Hal Hinson|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> [[Kenneth Turan]] of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' also praised Parker's direction, writing, "&nbsp;... Parker has loosened up quite a bit here, not forcing the action as much as he did in the similar ''[[Fame (1980 film)|Fame]]'' and bringing a surprisingly loony touch to characters like Jimmy's [[Elvis Presley|Elvis]]-obsessed father."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1991-08-30-ca-1357-story.html|title=MOVIE REVIEW : An Irish Soul Lullaby : Parker's 'Commitments' an R&B Rave-Up|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|first=Kenneth|last=Turan|author-link=Kenneth Turan|date=30 August 1991|access-date=6 July 2016}}</ref> ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' magazine reviewer [[Richard Corliss]] wrote, "The film offers no message, no solutions, only a great time at the movies."<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Cinema: Dublin Soul|last=Corliss|first=Richard|author-link=Richard Corliss|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|date=26 August 1991|volume=138}}</ref>

[[Roger Ebert]] of the ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'' wrote that the film was "filled with life and energy, and the music is honest."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/the-commitments-1991|title='The Commitments Movie Review and Film Summary|publisher=RogerEbert.com|first=Roger|last=Ebert|author-link=Roger Ebert|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> On the syndicated television program ''Siskel & Ebert At the Movies'', Ebert gave the film a "Thumbs Up" rating, while his colleague [[Gene Siskel]] gave the film a "Thumbs Down".<ref>{{cite video|people=Gene Siskel and Roger Ebert|title=[[At the Movies (1986 TV program)|Siskel and Ebert and the Movies]]|date=17 August 1991}}</ref> Siskel, writing for the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'', felt that the film was "a joyful but empty mixture of Irish kids and black American soul music".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/1991/08/16/the-commitments-just-another-name-for-fame/|title='The Commitments' Just Another Name For 'Fame'|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|first=Gene|last=Siskel|date=16 August 1991 |author-link=Gene Siskel|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> In his review for ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'', [[Owen Gleiberman]] criticised the overall premise as being "downright insulting", explaining, "In Parker's hands, soul music becomes little more than a self-serving metaphor – an easy symbol for 'commitment' and integrity."<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.ew.com/article/1991/08/16/commitments|title=The Commitments|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|first=Owen|last=Gleiberman|author-link=Owen Gleiberman|date=16 August 1991|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> [[Peter Travers]] of ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' criticised the storytelling, writing in his review, "&nbsp;... the predictable way in which the band's nine men and three women argue about music, sex and fame robs the story of urgency."<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/reviews/the-commitments-19910828|title=The Commitments|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|first=Peter|last=Travers|author-link=Peter Travers|date=28 August 1991|access-date=7 July 2016}}</ref> [[Janet Maslin]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' stated, "''The Commitments'' becomes repetitive after a while, since so much of it is about the group's stage show, and since the effort to create an off-stage story never really works."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/movie/review?res=9D0CE7D91039F937A2575BC0A967958260?|title=Review/Film; How American Soul Music Conquered Dublin|work=[[The New York Times]]|first=Janet|last=Maslin|author-link=Janet Maslin|date=14 August 1991|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> [[David Denby]] of ''[[New York (magazine)|New York Magazine]]'' felt that the film has "a raspy surface authenticity and a great deal of affection for its characters and milieu but not much dramatic interest."<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=B-kCAAAAMBAJ&q=Van+Morrison+The+Commitments+Alan+Parker&pg=PA50|title=Dubliners|magazine=[[New York (magazine)|New York Magazine]]|first=David|last=Denby|author-link=David Denby|date=19 August 1991|pages=50|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref>

===Accolades===
''The Commitments'' received various awards and nominations in categories ranging from recognition of the film itself to its writing, direction, editing and sound to the supporting performance of Andrew Strong. In September 1990, the film debuted at the 4th [[Tokyo International Film Festival]], where it competed for the "Tokyo Grand Prix Award"<ref name="Tokyo1">{{cite web |url=http://2008.tiff-jp.net/en/tiff/lineup.php?id=4|title=Tokyo International Film Festival Line up|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> and was nominated for the Best Director Award, with Parker winning in the latter category.<ref name="Tokyo2">{{cite web |url=http://2008.tiff-jp.net/en/tiff/outline4.html|title=Tokyo International – Outline|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> In January 1992, the film received a [[Golden Globe Award]] nomination for [[Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy|Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy]] though it failed to win the award at the [[49th Golden Globe Awards]], losing to the animated feature ''[[Beauty and the Beast (1991 film)|Beauty and the Beast]]''.<ref name="Globes">{{cite web|url=http://www.goldenglobes.com/winners-nominees/1992|title=Winners & Nominees 1992 (Golden Globes)|publisher=[[Hollywood Foreign Press Association]]|access-date=4 July 2016|archive-date=20 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220080813/http://www.goldenglobes.com/winners-nominees/1992|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 19 February 1992,<ref>{{cite news|last=Weinraub|first=Bernard|title='Bugsy' a Big Winner In Oscar Nominations Rife With Surprise|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1992/02/20/movies/bugsy-a-big-winner-in-oscar-nominations-rife-with-surprise.html?pagewanted=all&src=pm|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=20 February 1992|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> ''The Commitments'' received one [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] nomination for [[Academy Award for Best Film Editing|Best Film Editing]], but lost to ''[[JFK (film)|JFK]]'' at the [[64th Academy Awards]] ceremony on 30 March 1992.<ref name="Oscars1992">{{cite web|url=http://www.oscars.org/oscars/ceremonies/1992|title=The 64th Academy Awards (1992) Nominees and Winners |date=9 October 2014 |publisher=Oscars.org|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref> At the [[45th British Academy Film Awards]], the film received six nominations, and won four for [[BAFTA Award for Best Film|Best Film]], [[BAFTA Award for Best Direction|Best Direction]], [[BAFTA Award for Best Adapted Screenplay|Best Adapted Screenplay]] and [[BAFTA Award for Best Editing|Best Editing]].<ref name="BAFTA">{{cite web|url=http://awards.bafta.org/award/1992/film|title=Film in 1992 |publisher=[[British Academy of Film and Television Arts]]|access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref>
