and contemporary.<ref name=FaroutMagazineRaffertie/>

==Design and effects==
{{external media|image1=[http://mubi.io/substancelookbook Official lookbook] released by MUBI, containing images which inspired the screenplay (92 pages)}}

Fargeat used [[practical effects]] including extensive [[Prosthetic makeup|prosthetics and makeup]], accounting for 70–80% of effects in the film.<ref name="Variety">{{Cite web |last=Tangcay |first=Jazz |date=23 September 2024 |title=How 'The Substance' Pulled Off That Bloody, Gloriously Disgusting Ending With Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley |url=https://variety.com/2024/artisans/news/the-substance-ending-explained-demi-moore-margaret-qualley-1236152183/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240923213740/https://variety.com/2024/artisans/news/the-substance-ending-explained-demi-moore-margaret-qualley-1236152183/ |archive-date=23 September 2024 |access-date=12 October 2024 |website=Variety}}</ref> She resisted the push toward cheaper digital effects<ref name=CNC/> and has stated that the use of practical effects was crucial to convey the themes of violence.<ref name="EWPushed">{{Cite web |last=Nolfi|first=Joey|date=18 September 2024| title=Demi Moore, Margaret Qualley pushed to their 'brutal' physical limit in 'The Substance' |url=https://ew.com/demi-moore-the-substance-brutal-shoot-prosthetics-blood-preview-8713538 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240918173611/https://ew.com/demi-moore-the-substance-brutal-shoot-prosthetics-blood-preview-8713538 |archive-date=18 September 2024 |access-date=12 October 2024 |website=EW.com}}</ref>

The effects were created by [[Pierre-Olivier Persin]] and his company, Pop FX, based in [[Montreuil, Seine-Saint-Denis|Montreuil]], Paris.<ref name="MarieClaire">{{Cite web |last=Bell |first=Sadie |date=2024-09-22 |title=How 'The Substance' Uses Practical Effects and Splashy Makeup to Craft a Body Horror Film That Tears Down Beauty Standards |url=https://www.marieclaire.com/culture/movies/the-substance-makeup-effects-artist-interivew/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240922122043/https://www.marieclaire.com/culture/movies/the-substance-makeup-effects-artist-interivew/ |archive-date=22 September 2024 |access-date=2024-11-27 |website=Marie Claire Magazine}}</ref> Leading a team of 15,<ref name="Chaos">{{Cite web |last=Delorme |first=Gérard |date=9 Nov 2024 |title=Rencontre avec Pierre-Olivier Persin, créateur de prothèses et d'effets spéciaux de maquillage pour "The Substance" |url=https://www.chaosreign.fr/monstro-elisasue-reigns-rencontre-avec-pierre-olivier-persin-createur-de-protheses-et-deffets-speciaux-de-maquillage-pour-the-substance/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241222095057/https://www.chaosreign.fr/monstro-elisasue-reigns-rencontre-avec-pierre-olivier-persin-createur-de-protheses-et-deffets-speciaux-de-maquillage-pour-the-substance/ |archive-date=22 December 2024 |access-date=26 Nov 2024 |website=Chaos Reign}}</ref> Persin oversaw the work both at Pop FX's studio and at a second rented workshop.<ref name=MarieClaire/> Persin dedicated 11 months to the project, spanning [[pre-production]] and shooting.<ref name=AwardsWatch/> He was hired at the recommendation of executive producer Nicolas Royer<ref name=Chaos/><ref name=CNC/> (who appears in the film as "guy in the elevator" and previously worked with Persin). Initially, Fargeat had chosen another company to create the designs but was disappointed with their work.<ref name=AwardsWatch/> Persin later described their designs as good from an artistic perspective, but overly masculine<ref name="PersinYoutubeInterview">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?t=1244&v=vj99p8uExuY&feature=youtu.be |title=interview – pierre olivier persin – the substance {{!}} let's talk about... fresh blood 2024 |date=11 September 2024 |last=fantasy filmfest |access-date=12 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241112212107/https://www.youtube.com/watch?t=1244&v=vj99p8uExuY&feature=youtu.be |archive-date=12 November 2024 |via=YouTube}}</ref>—"a rubber monster for the guys."<ref name=MarieClaire/> Meanwhile, Fargeat had always envisioned the film ending with a monster that she referred to as a "[[Pablo Picasso#Style and technique|Picasso]] of male expectations".<ref name="Vulture">{{Cite web |last=Jacobs |first=Matthew |date=7 October 2024 |title=How The Substance Created the Ultimate Body of Horrors |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/the-substance-demi-moore-margaret-qualley-ending.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007132147/https://www.vulture.com/article/the-substance-demi-moore-margaret-qualley-ending.html |archive-date=7 October 2024 |access-date=12 October 2024 |website=Vulture}}</ref>

Persin read the script, made a bid, and, while working on another project, sculpted a small [[plasticine]] [[maquette]]{{sfn|The Horror Flicks and Guitar Picks Podcast|2024|loc=23:30}} (mockup) of his design for the creature at the climax, "Monstro Elisasue",{{refn|group=note|The monster is instead referred to as MonstroElisaSue (without spaces) in the 2020 draft<ref name=2020ScriptDraft/> and shooting script<ref name=2024Script/> and as MONSTROELISASUE in the film credits.}} over a few nights.<ref name=AwardsWatch/> In the script, Monstro Elisasue was loosely outlined, only described as having Elisabeth's face located on its back.<ref name=Chaos/> Persin wanted to give Monstro some "humility" and "gracefulness"<ref name=MarieClaire/> and for her to resemble Sue.<ref name="IndieWire">{{Cite web |last=Desowitz |first=Bill |date=1 October 2024 |title=Inside Elisabeth's Transformation Into 'Gollum' and 'Monstro' in 'The Substance' |url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/craft/the-substance-prosthetic-designer-gollum-monstro-interview-1235051839/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241001160648/https://www.indiewire.com/features/craft/the-substance-prosthetic-designer-gollum-monstro-interview-1235051839/ |archive-date=1 October 2024 |access-date=12 October 2024 |website=IndieWire}}</ref> Fargeat was impressed with his choices, such as the tilted head, backward-facing arm, and the inclusion of breasts, and offered him the position.<ref name=AwardsWatch/> Fargeat and Persin later spent a month refining Monstro's design.<ref name=AwardsWatch/><ref name=TDBMonster/> Persin would later remark in an interview: "Coralie wanted her as if the body was put in a shaker."<ref name=IndieWire/>

Persin and Fargeat conducted a technical read-through over several days, outlining the requirements of each sequence. Persin visualized Fargeat's ideas for each transformation with [[Photoshop]], [[Digital sculpting|digital sculpture]], and regular [[sculpture]].<ref name=MarieClaire/> He created designs based on digital scans of the actors, which Fargeat could select, combine, or modify prior to the creation of actual prosthetics for screen tests.<ref name=MarieClaire/>

Elisabeth's transformation process was organized into a series of five stages, following the birth of Sue: a withered finger ("The Finger"),<ref name=MarieClaire/> a more aged look called "Requiem" (inspired by ''[[Requiem for a Dream]]''), a hunched-backed design referred to as "[[Gollum]]", "Monstro Elisasue", and "The Blob".<ref name="TDBMonster">{{Cite news |last=Cadenas |first=Kerensa |date=23 September 2024 |title=How Demi Moore Became a Grotesque, Hideous Monster |url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/obsessed/the-substance-how-demi-moore-became-a-grotesque-hideous-monster |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240923115216/https://www.thedailybeast.com/obsessed/the-substance-how-demi-moore-became-a-grotesque-hideous-monster |archive-date=23 September 2024 |access-date=12 October 2024 |website=[[The Daily Beast]]}}</ref><ref name=IndieWire/> Fargeat deliberately sought to avoid making the effects look realistic, aiming instead to create a deformed representation of the aging process, shaped by the characters' fear and anger.<ref name="FilmmakerMagazine">{{Cite magazine |last=Loayza |first=Beatrice |date=18 September 2024 |title=The Monster You Become: Coralie Fargeat on The Substance |url=https://filmmakermagazine.com/127299-interview-coralie-fargeat-substance/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919125448/https://filmmakermagazine.com/127299-interview-coralie-fargeat-substance/ |archive-date=19 September 2024 |access-date=12 October 2024 |magazine=[[Filmmaker (magazine)|Filmmaker]]}}</ref>

Fargeat's vision for how quickly Elisabeth's transformations should occur sparked debate with Persin and the lead makeup artist, Stéphanie Guillon. For the pre-substance scenes, Guillon felt that "[Moore's Elisabeth] had to be beautiful in the beginning{{nbsp}}... before she has all the prosthetics", while Fargeat wanted her to appear flawed from the start. Similarly, Persin felt that pacing the changes more gradually would enhance their impact, explaining, "It'll be wild and insane eventually."<ref name=MarieClaire/>

Fargeat described the dialogue-free scene where Moore removes her makeup in front of a mirror as "the most challenging" of the film.<ref name="MakeupChallenging">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?t=230&v=5l9EZDdKB-E |title=Demi Moore et sa relation à son corps – Interview The Substance avec Demi Moore et Coralie Fargeat |date=2024-11-10 |author=AlloCiné – Interviews |access-date=2024-11-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241207080816/https://www.youtube.com/watch?t=230&v=5l9EZDdKB-E |archive-date=7 December 2024 |via=YouTube}}</ref> Fargeat was stressed on the day of the shoot because she knew she was creating the "emotional heart of the movie" where performance, rhythm and lighting had to be perfect.<ref name="MakeupChallenging" /> Fargeat felt if Moore and the crew could pull it off, it would be incredibly powerful.<ref name="MakeupChallenging" /> After the 11th take, Guillon intervened to stop filming for the day. "I took the remover pad and I squashed everything, and I said, 'I removed everything, that's over. You have already 11. You cannot have more because tomorrow she will have a red face.' Normally you don't do that! But it was too much because it was very hard on her skin."<ref name="MarieClaire" />

Prosthetics application ranged between 45 minutes<ref name="TDBMonster" /> and 7 hours<ref name="PersinYoutubeInterview" />{{refn|group=note|Sources differ on the exact number; for instance, Moore stated that she spent 6.5 to 9 hours in the chair, possibly including takedown time.{{sfn|Late Night with Seth Meyers|2024|loc=3:59}}}} depending on character complexity, sometimes only leaving an hour or two for filming in a given day.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?t=1669&v=ftOcGyJtNXU&feature=youtu.be|title=THE SUBSTANCE – Press Conference – English – Cannes 2024|date=20 May 2024|last=Festival de Cannes|access-date=12 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241130111334/https://www.youtube.com/watch?t=1669&v=ftOcGyJtNXU&feature=youtu.be|archive-date=30 November 2024|via=YouTube}}</ref><ref name="HollywoodReporterInterview" /><ref name="CinemaBlend">{{Cite web |author1=Eric Eisenberg|date=1 October 2024|title=The Substance's Director Discusses Her 'Super Important' Conversations With Demi Moore And Margaret Qualley About The Film's Extreme Prosthetics And Nudity|url=https://www.cinemablend.com/interviews/the-substance-director-discusses-important-conversations-demi-moore-margaret-qualley-extreme-prosthetics-nudity|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241001015147/https://www.cinemablend.com/interviews/the-substance-director-discusses-important-conversations-demi-moore-margaret-qualley-extreme-prosthetics-nudity|archive-date=1 October 2024|access-date=12 October 2024|website=CinemaBlend}}</ref> For her [[Nudity in film|nude scenes]], Margaret Qualley was fitted with custom-made [[breast prostheses]] to portray an idealized image of beauty, reminiscent of [[Jessica Rabbit]]. Qualley humorously explained the process: "Unfortunately, there is no magic boob potion, so we had to glue those on{{nbsp}}... [they endowed] me with the rack of a lifetime—just not my lifetime."<ref name="QualleyCelebrity" />

===Birth of Sue===
Early in production, without life casts or scans from the actresses,<ref name=AwardsWatch/> Persin created and filmed a 30&nbsp;cm{{sfn|Le Club Cinéma|2024|loc=5:42}} maquette of the back opening to send to Fargeat for her approval.<ref name=AwardsWatch/> This enabled him to begin work on the scene.<ref name=AwardsWatch/>

Persin initially believed the prosthetic designs in the bathroom would be visually enhanced by moody lighting, akin to ''[[The Howling (film)|The Howling]]''{{sfn|The Horror Flicks and Guitar Picks Podcast|2024|loc=34:16}} or [[Dario Argento]]'s films.<ref name=Chaos/> However, he would learn this was not the case, as he explained: "At first, I asked Coralie, I said, in the bathroom, because lots of things happen in the bathroom, are we going to have a nice something a bit dark and with shadows and to hide a little bit of the [[silicone]] and all that. And she was like, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. Cut to the [bright] white tiles."{{sfn|Scenecraft|2024|loc=32:03}}

For the birthing scene, Persin used a combination of prosthetics on [[body double]]s<ref name=IndieWire/> and [[puppetry]],<ref name=HollywoodReporterInterview/> which relied on two faceless,<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?t=65&v=UZ43tAoBytE&feature=youtu.be |title=Dans l'atelier de Pierre-Olivier Persin, maquilleur FX au cinéma |date=2024-11-09 |author=CNews |author-link=CNews |access-date=2024-11-30 |via=YouTube}}</ref> [[Hyperrealism (visual arts)|hyper-realistic]] silicone dummies that took between one and one-and-a-half months to construct.{{sfn|Le Club Cinéma|2024|loc=11:36}} The entire sequence was shot with practical effects, with the exception of the close up of the eye splitting.<ref name=BritishCinematographer/> Shots of the back splitting were achieved with the dummies on a raised set, operated by 5–6 puppeteers below while Fargeat directed from under the set or nearby.<ref name=AwardsWatch/> For the stitching of the back, Persin alternated between a dummy and a prosthetic applied directly to the actresses' skin.<ref name="HollywoodReporterTransformation">{{Cite web |last=Verhoeven |first=Beatrice |date=2024-11-17 |title=If You Thought Demi Moore's Transformation Was Crazy in 'The Substance', Wait Til You Hear How They Did It |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/demi-moore-the-substance-crazy-scenes-1236062561/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241117180150/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/demi-moore-the-substance-crazy-scenes-1236062561/ |archive-date=17 November 2024 |access-date=2024-11-30 |website=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref> Careful attention was paid to the realism of the skin: the pores and [[cellulite]] were meticulously crafted, while layers of various colors: reds, yellows, greens, blues, and [[ochre]]s — were applied in a [[pointillism|pointillist]] manner, as no single paint color can replicate a natural skin tone, according to Persin.<ref name="MarieClaireFr">{{Cite web |date=2024-11-09 |title="The Substance" : Rencontre avec Pierre-Olivier Persin, maquilleur effets spéciaux aux commandes d'incroyables transformations |url=https://www.marieclaire.fr/the-substance-rencontre-avec-pierre-olivier-persin-maquilleur-effets-speciaux-aux-commandes-d-incroyables-transformations,1483863.asp |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241110051234/https://www.marieclaire.fr/the-substance-rencontre-avec-pierre-olivier-persin-maquilleur-effets-speciaux-aux-commandes-d-incroyables-transformations,1483863.asp |archive-date=10 November 2024 |access-date=2024-11-30 |website=Marie Claire |language=fr}}</ref> One challenge was avoiding giving the skin a "too rubbery or too elastic" appearance, so the team designed a prosthetic with soft material, but stiffer wound edges to make the needle weaving through the skin appear more realistic.<ref name=HollywoodReporterTransformation/> The spine scar and other prosthetics were applied to Moore, two stunt doubles and two body doubles."<ref name=HollywoodReporterTransformation/>

===The Finger===
[[File:The Finger (prosthetics for The Substance).png|thumb|right|Prosthetics design for "The Finger"]]

Persin's first project began with the finger prosthetic. However, the first test looked extremely fake, reminiscent of "[[Mickey Mouse]]".<ref name=HollywoodReporterTransformation/> Correcting it took a month<ref name=HollywoodReporterTransformation/> and temporarily halted the development of other prosthetics until the finger met Persin's desired standard of a balanced appearance, ensuring it would not look bulkier than the natural ones.<ref name=TDBMonster/> Achieving this required creating extremely thin prosthetics, and in total, all the prosthetics were redesigned twice.<ref name=TDBMonster/> A prosthetic arm was used for the scene where Moore tries to wash her finger in the sink.<ref name=IndieWireCinematicMetamorphosis/>{{sfn|IndieWire|2025|loc=5:15}}

===Requiem===
Persin praised Moore's professionalism during the five- to six-hour prosthetic application for the "Requiem" stage, likening it to "going to the dentist for six hours."<ref name=MarieClaire/> The crew were especially impressed when Moore decided to postpone filming one of her scenes until the next day after noticing that her prosthetics had deteriorated over several hours of earlier shots, as she felt it would be extremely disrespectful to their hard work.<ref name=MarieClaire/>

Due to Moore being born with [[amblyopia]] in one eye,<ref>{{Cite news |title=World's Most Beautiful: Of Course It's Demi! Read Her Candid Interview and See the Stunning Photos |url=https://people.com/worlds-most-beautiful-demi-moore-cover-story-photos-exclusive-11717760 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260421163818/https://people.com/worlds-most-beautiful-demi-moore-cover-story-photos-exclusive-11717760 |archive-date=2026-04-21 |access-date=2026-06-06 |work=People.com}}</ref> she requested the makeup team avoid working too closely around the eye.<ref name=Chaos/> Persin assumed the makeup effects would be further altered digitally but later discovered this was not the case.<ref name=Chaos/> Most of the Requiem sequence relied on applied prosthetics adhered directly to the skin, while a few shots, such as Elisabeth's leg in the shower, were fake body parts.<ref name=AwardsWatch/> For the scene with Elisabeth's stuck kneecap, a modified chair was used to conceal Moore's real legs while revealing prosthetic, mechanical ones crafted from silicone.<ref name="InSessionFilm">{{Cite web |last=Larki |first=Shadan |date=2024-12-14 |title=Chasing The Gold Interview: 'The Substance' Special Makeup Effects Designer Pierre Olivier Persin |url=https://insessionfilm.com/chasing-the-gold-interview-the-substance-special-makeup-effects-designer-pierre-olivier-persin/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241223122107/https://insessionfilm.com/chasing-the-gold-interview-the-substance-special-makeup-effects-designer-pierre-olivier-persin/ |archive-date=23 December 2024 |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=InSession Film |language=en-US}}</ref> To achieve the look of translucent skin, the team used thin, prosthetic appliances that allowed the veins and bones to show through.<ref name=AwardsWatch/>

===Gollum===
Moore's transformation into "Gollum" was more extensive, with layers of silicone prosthetics glued directly onto her body. Red and blue wool was embedded in the silicone to mimic the appearance of veins beneath the skin.<ref name=AwardsWatch/>{{sfn|Scenecraft|2024|loc=31:30}} Persin used silicone because it looked more natural and did not easily wrinkle during the filming of action scenes.{{sfn|Scenecraft|2024|loc=31:17}} When Elisabeth runs down the hallway, Moore was switched out for a thinner body double to match the idea of Gollum having a "spider-like" physicality.<ref name=AwardsWatch/>{{sfn|Scenecraft|2024|loc=30:23}}

A sophisticated fake head, capable of realistic bleeding, was created for the mirror-smashing scene.<ref name=HollywoodReporterTransformation/> Qualley smashed the fake head against the mirror and Moore mimed the action later with her real head; the visual effects team seamlessly blended the two shots to depict the head-on-mirror impact and Moore's reaction.<ref name=HollywoodReporterTransformation/>

===Monstro Elisasue===
[[File:Photo on set for the Substance.webp|thumb|right|Facial prosthetics and latex suit for "Monstro Elisasue"]]

{{Quote box
| quote = The head is a little bit like a female [[Elephant Man]] [...] that was what Coralie wanted, the sensibility of ''[[The Elephant Man (1980 film)|The Elephant Man]]'', the [[David Lynch]] movie. We spent lots of time designing Monstro with all the breasts and trying to balance everything. Is she fat enough? How many boobs? Maybe we should add a jaw here. Maybe we can [add a spine], because there's lots of spines in the story from the very beginning.<ref name=TDBMonster/>
| source = —Pierre-Olivier Persin
| align = right
| width = 30%
}}

Despite disagreements over previous transformations, for "Monstro", Persin and Fargeat were in sync.<ref name=HollywoodReporterTransformation/> Since there were time constraints (as the design for Monstro had not been finalized until after shooting began{{sfn|Blackburn|2024|loc=1:07:21}}), Persin subcontracted the Monstro build to [[Dave Elsey|Dave and Lou Elsey]] of UK-based Igor Studios.<ref name=AwardsWatch/>{{sfn|Scenecraft|2024|loc=33:31}}<ref name=IgorStudiosPage>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-29 |title=The Substance |website=Igor Studios – SFX Makeup & Prosthetics |publisher=Igor Studios |url=https://igorstudios.net/recent-project/the-substance/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241129121744/https://igorstudios.net/recent-project/the-substance/ |access-date=2024-12-07 |archive-date=29 November 2024}}</ref> The final design was created using five prosthetic heads (including a special head with a cavity that splits open to birth a breast attached to an [[umbilical cord]]), two full bodysuits, two partial bodysuits, and a mold of Moore's head.<ref name=Vulture/> The suit was entirely practical, with the exception of Moore's screaming face, which was achieved using digital effects,<ref name="GQEffects">{{Cite web |last=Motamayor |first=Rafael |date=25 September 2024 |title=How 'The Substance's' Effects Team Pulled Off Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley's Monster Makeovers |url=https://www.gq.com/story/the-substance-effects |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240925195259/https://www.gq.com/story/the-substance-effects |archive-date=25 September 2024 |access-date=12 October 2024 |website=GQ}}</ref> using a [[photogrammetry]] scan of Moore's face<ref name=Chaos/> by Clear Angle Studios.<ref name="ClearAngleStudios">{{Cite web |last=Rogez |first=Benoît |date=2024-12-11 |title=From Dune: Part Two to The Substance: meet 3D scanning specialists Clear Angle Studios! |url=https://3dvf.com/en/redaction/from-mission-impossible-to-dune-2-and-the-substance-meet-3d-scanning-specialists-clear-angle-studios/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211121326/https://3dvf.com/en/redaction/from-mission-impossible-to-dune-2-and-the-substance-meet-3d-scanning-specialists-clear-angle-studios/ |archive-date=11 December 2024 |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=3DVF |language=en-US}}</ref>

Persin drew inspiration from [[Niki de Saint Phalle]], a French sculptor known for her vibrant and curvaceous figures (especially her depictions of female dancers);<ref name=MarieClaire/> artist [[Fernando Botero]], whose sculptures often feature women with exaggerated proportions;<ref name=Vulture/> and [[David Cronenberg]]'s 1986 film ''[[The Fly (1986 film)|The Fly]]''.<ref name=IndieWire/>

During [[pre-production]], Persin expressed concern about the plan to have Qualley wear the full suit, noting that only Qualley's eye would be visible.<ref name=TDBMonster/> Fargeat ultimately had Qualley do close-up shots for Monstro, recognizing the importance of her performance. Persin later acknowledged that this decision was essential to making Monstro's scenes visibly impactful in the final film.<ref name=MarieClaire/>

Qualley would later describe wearing the prosthetics as "torture", adding, "I had this awesome team of prosthetic artists that put it on me and took it off of me and got me through the day, making me laugh a couple of times while I was just on the brink of panic."<ref name="USATodayStars">{{Cite web |last=Truitt |first=Brian |title='The Substance' stars discuss that 'beautiful' bloody finale (spoilers!) |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/movies/2024/09/21/demi-moore-the-substance-movie-spoilers/75240970007/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240921130110/https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/movies/2024/09/21/demi-moore-the-substance-movie-spoilers/75240970007/ |archive-date=21 September 2024 |access-date=12 October 2024 |website=USA TODAY}}</ref> "My problem was I had to cry while I had the monster costume on. At a certain point, you're just swimming—there's like a layer of tears and snot inside your prosthetics, and they're just trying to reglue it down."{{sfn|Collider|2024|loc=19:51}} The prosthetics application for Qualley required six hours<ref name=Vulture/> and was filmed over the course of eight days.<ref name="LATimesThereWillBeBlood">{{Cite web |last=McCord |first=Jennifer |date=3 September 2024 |title=There will be blood: Demi Moore, Margaret Qualley and director Coralie Fargeat on the fall's most shocking movie |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/movies/story/2024-09-03/demi-moore-margaret-qualley-director-coralie-fargeat-the-substance-interview-fall-preview |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240903122350/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/movies/story/2024-09-03/demi-moore-margaret-qualley-director-coralie-fargeat-the-substance-interview-fall-preview |archive-date=3 September 2024 |access-date=12 October 2024 |website=Los Angeles Times}}</ref> According to Qualley, the prosthetics caused her face to break out with [[acne]], taking over a year to heal{{sfn|Horowitz|2025}}<ref name="VarietyFace">{{Cite web |last=Dunn |first=Jack |date=2025-01-15 |title=Margaret Qualley Says It Took 'a Year' to Recover From the Damage Caused by Prosthetics Used in 'The Substance': 'My Face Was So F–ed Up' |url=https://variety.com/2025/film/news/margaret-qualley-year-to-recover-damage-face-prosthetics-the-substance-1236274611/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250115083444/https://variety.com/2025/film/news/margaret-qualley-year-to-recover-damage-face-prosthetics-the-substance-1236274611/ |archive-date=15 January 2025 |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> and affecting the filming of her subsequent role in ''[[Kinds of Kindness]]''.{{sfn|Horowitz|2025|loc=11:58}} Shots of Sue walking down the palm-lined street were deliberately filmed at low angles to conceal the blemishes.{{sfn|Horowitz|2025|loc=12:29}} To prevent overheating, the suit incorporated a [[cooling vest]] similar to that which [[Auto racing|racecar drivers]] use.<ref name=Variety/>

Fargeat personally donned the Monstro suit for the shots showing blood spraying from Monstro's point of view. She held the camera herself, without the headpiece, while wearing the suit, as her arm was inside the blood rig.<ref name=TDBMonster/> Persin also put on the suit to operate a breast puppet, which required at least 10–15 takes and left his arm numb from holding it above his head for extended periods.<ref name=AwardsWatch/> The constant spraying of blood caused the latex to turn pink as it became saturated quickly. The suit required repainting, resewing, and drying after each day. For sanitary and hygiene purposes, the crew sprayed [[vodka]] inside the suit every night to kill bacteria and remove moisture.<ref name=IndieWire/>

Near the end of the film, the [[stunt performer]] had to be moved on a dolly, due to limited mobility of the suit. When the blood rig was first tested, the performer slipped and went rolling backward down the long blood-soaked hallway featured near the end of the film.<ref name=GQEffects/>

===The Blob===
Ending the film with "The Blob" featuring Moore's face, Fargeat aimed for a clear visual that would allow for full facial expressions. Persin and his team constructed and manually maneuvered a puppet blob for the scene, which was overlaid on Moore's face with [[visual effects]].<ref name=TDBMonster/> It was referred to as "Gremlin"<ref name=MarieClaire/> in the shooting schedule, a nod to Stripe melting at the end of the 1984 film ''[[Gremlins]]''.{{sfn|The Horror Flicks and Guitar Picks Podcast|2024|loc=26:26}}

Working Title's parent company, [[Universal Pictures]], which originally signed on as the distributor through a deal with Working Title Films,<ref name="Deadline"/> stepped away from the project but remained credited as a copyright holder in the film's credits. Multiple sources told ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' that the studio was "worried about the prospect of releasing the film."<ref name=HollywoodReporterInterview/>{{sfn|Toronto International Film Festival|2024|loc=5:03}} According to Fargeat, the film encountered significant challenges during post-production, including a contentious test screening attended by two unnamed male executives and one unnamed female representative from Universal. One male executive vehemently opposed the film and insisted on a recut, a demand deemed unfeasible due to Fargeat's contractual [[final cut privilege]]. This led to Universal breaking off their distribution deal with Fargeat. Although the female representative later expressed her support for the film privately to Fargeat, she felt unable to voice her opinion during the screening.<ref name="LePointCoulisses">{{Cite web |date=2024-05-23 |title=En coulisses, le film " The Substance ", c'était " Apocalypse Now " ! |url=https://www.lepoint.fr/pop-culture/clashs-avec-demi-moore-tensions-sur-le-plateau-les-coulisses-mouvementees-du-film-the-substance-23-05-2024-2560928_2920.php#11 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240527183930/https://www.lepoint.fr/pop-culture/clashs-avec-demi-moore-tensions-sur-le-plateau-les-coulisses-mouvementees-du-film-the-substance-23-05-2024-2560928_2920.php#11 |archive-date=27 May 2024 |access-date=5 November 2024 |website=Le Point |language=fr}}</ref>

[[Advertising]] and [[film distribution]] costs for ''The Substance'' were under $20M worldwide and in the single digits in the United States.<ref name="Deadline70M">{{Cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |date=November 17, 2024 |title='The Substance' Set To Soar Past $70M+: How Mubi Fueled Demi Moore's Comeback At The Global Box Office |url=https://deadline.com/2024/11/the-substance-box-office-demi-moore-1236178368/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241128124257/https://deadline.com/2024/11/the-substance-box-office-demi-moore-1236178368/ |archive-date=28 November 2024 |access-date=November 25, 2024 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]]}}</ref> The marketing used [[avant-garde]] imagery such as a chicken bone and shiny hot pink exercise leotard and was overseen by Fargeat. The only vestige of Moore was a [[one sheet]] showing her stitched up back. Despite this unconventional approach, the film spread on social media. Demi Moore's posts reached her 15M followers and contributed to a total online reach of 45M across platforms, as estimated by RelishMix (including 7.6M views on [[TikTok]], 10.8M on [[Instagram]], and millions of views for other [[fan made]] content).<ref name=Deadline70M/>

The film returned to theaters in the United States on January 17, 2025, as part of its [[awards season]] campaign, a few days before the announcement of the nominees for the [[97th Academy Awards]] on January 23.<ref name="January2025ReRelease">{{Cite web |last=Bergeson |first=Samantha |date=2025-01-13 |title='The Substance' Lands Theatrical Re-Release Amid Oscar Season |url=https://www.indiewire.com/news/breaking-news/the-substance-theatrical-re-release-mubi-1235083804/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250118221351/https://www.indiewire.com/news/breaking-news/the-substance-theatrical-re-release-mubi-1235083804/ |archive-date=18 January 2025 |access-date=2025-01-14 |website=[[IndieWire]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Home media===

==Reception==

===Box office===
''The Substance'' grossed $17.6 million in the United States and Canada, and $59.7 million in other territories, for a worldwide total reported between $77.3<ref name="BOM">{{Cite Box Office Mojo|title=The Substance|id=17526714|website=[[Box Office Mojo]]|access-date=February 17, 2025|archive-date=March 12, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250312005237/https://www.boxofficemojo.com/title/tt17526714/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="NUM">{{Cite The Numbers|title=The Substance|id=Substance-The-(2024)|website=[[The Numbers (website)|The Numbers]]|access-date=March 3, 2025|archive-date=October 12, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251012101742/https://www.the-numbers.com/movie/Substance-The-(2024)#tab=summary|url-status=live}}</ref> and $82 million.<ref name="NYTBreakThrough">{{Cite news |last=Sperling |first=Nicole |date=2025-02-27 |title=How 'The Substance' Helped Mubi Break Through |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/02/27/business/media/the-substance-mubi-streaming.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250227102352/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/02/27/business/media/the-substance-mubi-streaming.html |archive-date=February 27, 2025 |access-date=2025-03-04 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>{{refn|group=note|''Variety'' states $79.1 million.<ref name=VarietyBudgetBoxOffice>{{cite web |last=Keslassy |first=Elsa |date=2025-01-29 |title=The Brains Behind 'The Substance:' How Coralie Fargeat Stayed True to Her Gutsy Vision: 'Everyone Wanted Me to Make It Less Violent, Less Excessive' |url=https://variety.com/2025/film/global/the-substance-coralie-fargeat-oscars-1236289808/ |access-date=2025-02-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250130020227/https://variety.com/2025/film/global/the-substance-coralie-fargeat-oscars-1236289808/ |archive-date=30 January 2025 |url-status=live |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |language=en-US}}</ref>}}

===Critical response===
{{Rotten Tomatoes prose|89|8.1|378|consensus=Audaciously gross, wickedly clever, and possibly Demi Moore's finest hour, ''The Substance'' is a gasp-inducing feat from writer-director Coralie Fargeat.|ref=yes|access-date=13 October 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250328100707/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/the_substance|archive-date=28 March 2025|url-status=live}} [[Metacritic]], which uses a [[Weighted arithmetic mean|weighted average]], assigned the film a score of 78 out of 100, based on 57 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref name="Metacritic">{{cite web |title=''The Substance'' |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/the-substance |website=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[Fandom (website)#Fandom, Inc.|Fandom, Inc.]] |access-date=3 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250328105523/https://www.metacritic.com/movie/the-substance/ |archive-date=28 March 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> On [[AlloCiné]], the film received an average rating of 3.6 out of 5, based on 39 reviews, from French critics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Critiques Presse pour le film The Substance |url=https://www.allocine.fr/film/fichefilm-300680/critiques/presse/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250220144749/https://www.allocine.fr/film/fichefilm-300680/critiques/presse/ |archive-date=20 February 2025 |access-date=6 November 2024 |publisher=[[AlloCiné]] |language=en-FR}}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "B" on an A+ to F scale, while those surveyed by [[PostTrak]] gave it an 80% overall positive score (including an average of 4 out of 5 stars), with 75% saying they would definitely recommend it.<ref name="opening"/>

[[Peter Bradshaw]]'s four-star (out of five) review in ''[[The Guardian]]'' called it "a cheerfully silly and outrageously indulgent piece of [[Gonzo journalism|gonzo]] body-horror comedy."<ref>{{cite news |last=Bradshaw |first=Peter |author-link=Peter Bradshaw |date=19 May 2024 |title='The Substance' review – Demi Moore is game for a laugh in grisly body horror caper |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/article/2024/may/19/the-substance-review-demi-moore-coralie-fargeat |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241213225544/https://www.theguardian.com/film/article/2024/may/19/the-substance-review-demi-moore-coralie-fargeat |archive-date=13 December 2024 |access-date=19 May 2024 |newspaper=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> [[David Ehrlich]] of ''[[IndieWire]]'' graded the film an A, calling it "an epic, audacious body horror masterpiece{{nbsp}}... an instant classic. The most sickly entertaining theatrical experience of the year."<ref>{{cite web |last=Ehrlich |first=David |author-link=David Ehrlich |date=19 May 2024 |title='The Substance' Review: Margaret Qualley 2024 |access-date=19 May 2024 |website=[[IndieWire]]}}</ref> Nicholas Barber of the [[BBC]] awarded the film four stars out of five, while singling out Moore's performance, writing: "Ripping into her best big-screen role in decades, Demi Moore is fearless in parodying her public image."<ref name="BBCReviewBarber">{{cite web |last=Barber |first=Nicholas |date=19 May 2024 |title='The Substance' |access-date=19 May 2024 |publisher=[[BBC]]}}</ref> Phil de Semlyen's five star (out of five) review in ''[[Time Out (magazine)|Time Out]]'' said it is "Moore who glues it all together, going full [[Isabelle Adjani]]-in-''[[Possession (1981 film)|Possession]]'' in a vanity-free performance full of bruised ego, dawning horror and vulnerability."<ref>{{cite web |last=de Semlyen |first=Phil [[File:SD25E25FF2TeamFP.jpg|thumb|Feminist art critic [[Jan Lisa Huttner]] (in pink suit) and other members of International SWANs (Support Women Artists Now) at the Manhattan SWAN Day 2025 event on March 29th honoring Demi Moore.]]

Filmmakers [[Ana Lily Amirpour]], [[Edward Berger]], [[Davy Chou]], [[Kelly Fremon Craig]], [[Robert Eggers]], [[Adam Elliot]], [[Hannah Fidell]], [[Michael Gracey]], [[Kitty Green]], [[Laurel Parmet]], [[Rich Peppiatt]] and [[Juel Taylor]] cited it as among their favorite films of 2024.<ref>{{cite web |last=O'Flat |first=Chris |date=30 December 2024 |title=65 Directors Pick Their Favorite Films of 2024 |url=https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/directors-pick-best-films-2024/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241230230833/https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/directors-pick-best-films-2024/ |archive-date=30 December 2024 |access-date=30 December 2024 |website=[[IndieWire]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Kneecap Director Rich Peppiatt Top Ten Feature Films of 2024 |url=https://directorsnotes.com/2024/12/30/rich-peppiatt-top-ten-2024/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250122213610/https://directorsnotes.com/2024/12/30/rich-peppiatt-top-ten-2024/ |archive-date=22 January 2025 |website=Director's Notes |date=December 30, 2024}}</ref>

In March 2025, feminist art critic [[Jan Lisa Huttner]] honored Demi Moore at SWAN Day 2025 events in [[New York City]] and [[Chicago]] for her performances in ''The Substance'' and ''[[Ghost (1990 film)|Ghost]]'', the film which previously earned her a [[Golden Globe Award|Golden Globe]] nomination in 1991.<ref>{{cite web |title=Actress Demi Moore to be Honored Worldwide on SWAN Day 2025 |url=https://www.canadiantimesjournal.com/article/790616545-actress-demi-moore-to-be-honored-worldwide-on-swan-day-2025 |website=Canadian Times Journal |access-date=17 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Huttner |first1=Jan Lisa |title=SWAN Day 2025: We Celebrated Demi Moore’s Exemplary Career in Manhattan |url=https://www.ff2media.com/blog/2025/04/05/swan-day-2025-we-celebrated-demi-moores-exemplary-career-in-manhattan/ |website=FF2 Media |access-date=17 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Huttner |first1=Jan Lisa |title=SWAN Day 2025: We Celebrated Demi Moore’s Exemplary Career in Metro Chicago |url=https://www.ff2media.com/blog/2025/04/05/swan-day-2025-we-celebrated-demi-moores-exemplary-career-in-metro-chicago/ |website=FF2 Media |access-date=17 October 2026}}</ref> Writing for FF2 Media, Julia Lasker said:<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lasker |first1=Julia |title=5 Noms for Coralie Fargeat’s “The Substance” Make Oscar History |url=https://www.ff2media.com/blog/2025/02/24/coralie-fargeats-the-substance/ |website=FF2 Media |access-date=18 October 2026}}</ref> <blockquote>Through Elisabeth’s transformation and its gruesome aftermath, [Fargeat] creates a powerful metaphor for the violence that the entertainment industry inflicts on women’s bodies and psyches, because they must fit impossible beauty standards in order to succeed. ''The Substance'''s unflinching examination of this history makes its recognition by AMPAS (the Academy of Motion Picture Arts & Sciences) both momentous and ironic — ''The Substance'' is being celebrated by the very institution it critiques.</blockquote>

In June 2025, ''[[IndieWire]]'' ranked the film at number 91 on its list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 2020s (So Far)."<ref name="Best">{{cite web |date=June 16, 2025 |title=The 100 Best Movies of the 2020s (So Far) |url=https://www.indiewire.com/lists/best-movies-2020s/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250616195818/https://www.indiewire.com/lists/best-movies-2020s/ |archive-date=16 June 2025 |access-date=2025-06-23 |website=[[IndieWire]]}}</ref> In July 2025, it was one of the films voted for the "Readers' Choice" edition of ''[[The New York Times]]''{{'}} list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century," finishing at number 126.<ref>{{cite web |date=July 2, 2025 |title=Readers Choose Their Top Movies of the 21st Century |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/movies/readers-movies-21st-century.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250702200131/https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/movies/readers-movies-21st-century.html |archive-date=2 July 2025 |access-date=2 July 2025 |website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>

===Accolades===
{{Main|List of accolades received by The Substance{{!}}List of accolades received by ''The Substance''}}

[[File:Coralie Fargeat at 2024 Cannes Film Festival.jpg|thumb|150px|Fargeat holding the [[Cannes Film Festival Award for Best Screenplay|Best Screenplay award]] she received at the [[2024 Cannes Film Festival|77th Cannes Film Festival]]]]

''The Substance'' has won a number of awards. At the [[97th Academy Awards]], ''The Substance'' was nominated for five awards and won [[Academy Award for Best Makeup and Hairstyling|Best Makeup and Hairstyling]]. It was nominated for [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]], [[Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay|Best Original Screenplay]] and [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]] for Fargeat, and [[Academy Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]] for Moore. Fargeat became the first woman to be nominated for writing and directing a horror film, and the ninth woman to be nominated for directing overall in Academy Awards history.{{refn|group=note|Multiple ==Themes and influences==

Wendy Ide of ''The Guardian'' noted ''The Substance'' for its [[Feminism|feminist]] perspective of older women, contrasting it with other female-led horror films like ''[[Carrie (1976 film)|Carrie]]'' and ''[[Rosemary's Baby (film)|Rosemary's Baby]]'' which centre on themes of menstruation and childbirth. She wrote that ''The Substance'', in contrast, "not only offers a female perspective on women's bodies, but also argues that things only start to get properly messy once fertility is a dim memory."<ref name="GuardianReviewIde">{{cite news |last=Ide |first=Wendy |date=22 September 2024 |title='The Substance review' – Demi Moore is fearless in visceral feminist body horror |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2024/sep/22/the-substance-review-demi-moore-is-fearless-in-visceral-female-body-horror-coralie-fargeat |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125180805/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2024/sep/22/the-substance-review-demi-moore-is-fearless-in-visceral-female-body-horror-coralie-fargeat |archive-date=25 January 2025 |access-date=22 September 2024 |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> ''[[The New York Times]]'' critic Alissa Wilkinson described the film as an exploration of the [[male gaze]], noting the satirically exaggerated camera angles and shots, depicting the female characters in a way "that feels reminiscent mostly of [[Pornographic film|porn]]".<ref name="NYTReviewWilkinson">{{cite news |last=Wilkinson |first=Alissa |date=19 September 2024 |title='The Substance' Review: An Indecent Disclosure |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/09/19/movies/the-substance-review.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126110254/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/09/19/movies/the-substance-review.html |archive-date=26 January 2025 |newspaper=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> In exaggerating these portrayals of female beauty standards to the point of absurdity, the film becomes humorous: "the worse things become for Elisabeth, the harder it is not to giggle with glee."<ref name="NYTReviewWilkinson"/> She also notes that the film can be seen as exploring [[mind–body dualism]].<ref name="NYTReviewWilkinson"/>

Alison Willmore of ''[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]]'' said that the film's strongest theme is about the dangers of addiction, comparing it to ''Requiem for a Dream''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Willmore |first=Alison |date=20 September 2024 |title=Are We Getting 'The Substance' All Wrong? |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/are-we-getting-demi-moores-the-substance-all-wrong.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124035048/https://www.vulture.com/article/are-we-getting-demi-moores-the-substance-all-wrong.html |archive-date=24 January 2025 |access-date=27 October 2024 |website=[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]]}}</ref> Elisa Battistini for ''Scraps from the Loft'' (originally published on Quinlan.it) called the film "a strange blend of ''[[Death Becomes Her]]'' and ''[[Society (film)|Society]]'' with hints of ''[[Tetsuo: The Iron Man|Tetsuo]]''".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Battistini |first=Elisa |date=2024-06-29 |title=Coralie Fargeat's "The Substance": Irony and Grotesque in Youth Obsession {{!}} Review |url=https://scrapsfromtheloft.com/movies/coralie-fargeat-the-substance-irony-and-grotesque-in-youth-obsession/ |access-date=2025-01-26 |website=Scraps from the loft |language=en-GB}}</ref> Several critics have noted the film's similarities to [[Oscar Wilde]]'s 1890 novel ''[[The Picture of Dorian Gray]]''.{{refn|group=note|Multiple sources:<ref name="SlateReview">{{cite web |last=Stevens |first=Dana |date=18 September 2024 |title='The Substance' Lacks Any |url=https://slate.com/culture/2024/09/the-substance-demi-moore-movie-margaret-qualley.html |access-date=12 October 2024 |website=[[Slate (website)|Slate]] |issn=1091-2339}}</ref><ref name="TheTimesReviewShone">{{cite news |last=Shone |first=Tom |date=21 September 2024 |title='The Substance' — Demi Moore and the dangers of eternal youth |url=https://www.thetimes.com/culture/film/article/the-substance-review-demi-moore-hollywood-vanities-wvmz8zmhd |access-date=30 September 2024 |newspaper=[[The Times]]}}</ref><ref name="CNNReviewHeching">{{cite web |last=Heching |first=Dan |date=21 September 2024 |title='The Substance': What to know about Demi Moore's powerhouse new film |url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/09/21/entertainment/demi-moore-the-substance/index.html |access-date=30 September 2024 |publisher=[[CNN]]}}</ref><ref name="BBCReviewBarber"/><ref name="GuardianReviewIde"/><ref name="GuardianReviewHorton">{{cite news |last=Horton |first=Adrian |date=28 September 2024 |title=Is 'The Substance' brilliant feminist critique or a soulless mess? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2024/sep/28/substance-movie-demi-moore |access-date=30 September 2024 |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref name="WCBE">{{cite web |date=22 September 2024 |title=The Substance |url=https://www.wcbe.org/arts-life/2024-09-22/the-substance |access-date=30 September 2024 |publisher=[[WCBE]]}}</ref>}}

The film's influences include works by [[David Cronenberg]] (''[[The Fly (1986 film)|The Fly]]''),<ref>{{Cite web |last=Howells |first=Nick |date=2024-09-19 |title=The Substance review: Demi Moore is brilliant in the best film of 2024 |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/culture/film/the-substance-review-demi-moore-margaret-qualley-b1182394.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919164919/https://www.standard.co.uk/culture/film/the-substance-review-demi-moore-margaret-qualley-b1182394.html |archive-date=19 September 2024 |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=The Standard |language=en}}</ref> [[John Carpenter]] (''[[The Thing (1982 film)|The Thing]]''), [[Coen brothers|Joel and Ethan Coen]] (''[[Barton Fink]]''), [[David Lynch]] (''[[Mulholland Drive (film)|Mulholland Drive]]''), [[Darren Aronofsky]] (''[[Requiem for a Dream]]''), and [[Stanley Kubrick]] (''[[2001: A Space Odyssey]]'').<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Falt |first=Chris |date=2025-01-14 |title=Six Films That Directly Influenced 'The Substance' |url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/podcast/the-substance-films-influenced-coralie-fargeat-1235084591/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250114211850/https://www.indiewire.com/features/podcast/the-substance-films-influenced-coralie-fargeat-1235084591/ |archive-date=14 January 2025 |access-date=2025-02-01 |website=[[IndieWire]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''''The Sweet Hereafter''''' is a 1997 Canadian [[drama film]] written and directed by [[Atom Egoyan]], adapted from the [[The Sweet Hereafter (novel)|1991 novel]] by [[Russell Banks]]. It tells the story of a school bus accident in a small town that kills 14 children; survivors and grieving parents file a [[class action|class-action]] lawsuit, which proves divisive in the community and becomes tied with personal and family issues. The [[ensemble cast]] includes [[Ian Holm]], [[Sarah Polley]], [[Maury Chaykin]], [[Bruce Greenwood]], [[Tom McCamus]], [[Gabrielle Rose (actress)|Gabrielle Rose]], [[Arsinée Khanjian]] and [[Alberta Watson]].

While the book was set in a small town in upstate New York, the film was set in a Canadian town, and was filmed in [[British Columbia]] and [[Ontario]]. The [[film score]] had [[medieval music]] influences and references to the story of the [[Pied Piper of Hamelin]].

Although ''The Sweet Hereafter'' was not a box office success, it was critically acclaimed and won three awards, including the [[Grand Prix (Cannes Film Festival)|Grand Prix]], at the [[1997 Cannes Film Festival]], along with seven [[18th Genie Awards|Genie Awards]], including [[Canadian Screen Award for Best Motion Picture|Best Motion Picture]]. It also received two [[70th Academy Awards|Academy Award]] nominations, for [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]] and [[Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay|Best Adapted Screenplay]]. [[Toronto International Film Festival]] critics ranked ''The Sweet Hereafter'' as one of the [[Top 10 Canadian Films of All Time|top 10 Canadian films]].

==Plot==
In the small town of Sam Dent, British Columbia, a school bus hits a patch of ice, runs through a barrier, and crashes into a lake, killing 14 children. The grieving parents are approached by an out-of-town lawyer, Mitchell Stephens, who is haunted by his dysfunctional relationship with his drug-addicted daughter. Stephens persuades the reluctant parents and bus driver Dolores Driscoll to file a [[class action|class-action]] lawsuit against the town and bus company for damages, arguing that the accident is a result of negligence in constructing the barrier or the bus.

The case depends on coaching the few surviving witnesses to say the right things in court, particularly Nicole Burnell, a 15-year-old paralyzed from the waist down as a result of the accident. Before the accident, Nicole was an aspiring musician and was being sexually abused by her father, Sam.

One bereft parent, Billy Ansel, distrusts Stephens and pressures Sam to drop the case; Nicole overhears their argument. In the pretrial [[deposition (law)|deposition]], Nicole unexpectedly states that Dolores was speeding, going {{convert|72|mph}}, far beyond the actual speed shown in an earlier scene, but nonetheless halting the lawsuit. Stephens and Sam know she is lying but can do nothing. Two years later, Stephens sees Dolores working as a bus driver in a city.

==Production==
===Adaptation===
[[File:Atomegoya.jpg|upright|thumb|Director [[Atom Egoyan]] adapted [[Russell Banks]]' novel ''[[The Sweet Hereafter (novel)|The Sweet Hereafter]]'' and incorporated ''[[The Pied Piper of Hamelin]]''.]]
The Canadian director [[Atom Egoyan]] adapted the screenplay after his wife, the actress [[Arsinée Khanjian]], suggested he read [[Russell Banks]]' ''[[The Sweet Hereafter (novel)|The Sweet Hereafter]]''.<ref name="Macnab">{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/film-interview-the-inscrutable-in-pursuit-of-the-unspeakable-1239896.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220620/https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/film-interview-the-inscrutable-in-pursuit-of-the-unspeakable-1239896.html |archive-date=20 June 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=Film interview: The inscrutable in pursuit of the unspeakable |last=Macnab |first=Geoffrey |date=18 September 1997 |access-date=3 August 2016|work=[[The Independent]]}}</ref> The novel is inspired by an incident in [[Alton, Texas]], in 1989, in which a bus crash killed 21 students, leading to multiple lawsuits.{{sfn|Robbennolt|Hans|2016|p=8}} Egoyan found it challenging to acquire the rights, as they had been [[Option (filmmaking)|optioned]] to another studio that was not actually producing it. Shortly before the option expired, novelist [[Margaret Atwood]] suggested to Egoyan that he meet with Banks personally after the director's success with the film ''[[Exotica (film)|Exotica]]'' (1994),<ref name="Kaufman2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/1997/11/an-interview-with-atom-egoyan-director-of-the-sweet-hereafter-part-ii-83315/ |title=An Interview with Atom Egoyan, Director of 'The Sweet Hereafter,' Part II |last=Kaufman |first=Anthony |date=24 November 1997 |access-date=2 August 2016|work=[[IndieWire]]}}</ref> and Banks was willing to grant him the rights. Egoyan later stated he was drawn to filming the novel because he felt film is for "confronting the most extreme things."{{sfn|Wilson|2009|p=89}} As an [[Armenian Canadian]], he also saw the story as a metaphor for the [[Armenian genocide]], in which those guilty had not accepted responsibility.{{sfn|Hutchison|2004|p=146}}

In adapting the novel, Egoyan changed the setting from [[Upstate New York]] to British Columbia, to help secure Canadian funding.{{sfn|Cardullo|2004|p=41}} He also added references to the story of ''[[The Pied Piper of Hamelin]]'' by [[Robert Browning]], to emphasize how Egoyan saw ''The Sweet Hereafter'' as a "grim [[fairy tale]]."<ref name="Pulver">{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2005/may/14/adaptationoftheweek.books |title=Grim fairytale |last=Pulver |first=Andrew |date=14 May 2005 |access-date=2 August 2016|work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> Nicole is seen reading ''The Pied Piper'' to children who later die in the accident.{{sfn|Cardullo|2004|p=45}} In that story, the Pied Piper leads all the children away, never to return, after their parents refuse to honour their debt to him. Egoyan wrote a new stanza in the ''Pied Piper'' style for the scene in which Nicole testifies Dolores was speeding, in which she describes her father's lips as "frozen as the winter moon."{{sfn|Wilson|2009|p=101}} Egoyan also made Mitchell Stephens the main character and increased the importance of Stephens' daughter, and moved the revelation of [[incest]] between the Burnells to later in the film.<ref name="Pulver"/>

===Filming===
The film was shot in British Columbia ([[Merritt, British Columbia|Merritt]] and [[Spences Bridge]]) and Ontario ([[Toronto]] and [[Stouffville, Ontario|Stouffville]]),{{sfn|Rist|2001|p=218}} on a budget of $5 million.<ref name="Kaufman1"/> Funding came from the company [[Alliance Communications]].<ref name="Macnab"/> Egoyan assembled many Canadian actors he had worked with in prior films, including [[Bruce Greenwood]], [[Gabrielle Rose (actress)|Gabrielle Rose]] and [[Sarah Polley]].{{sfn|Cardullo|2004|p=50}} Egoyan explained the benefit of working with a familiar cast, saying "When you're working on a limited production schedule, it's a comfort to know that you know the personalities involved, you know what they need as opposed to having to discover that and be surprised by that."<ref name="Kaufman2"/>

[[Ian Holm]] was cast as Mitchell Stephens after the actor originally set to play the character, [[Donald Sutherland]], quit the project.{{sfn|Mell|2005|p=234}} In casting the part, Egoyan was inspired by Holm's "strangely compassionate, yet furtive and menacing" performance in ''[[The Homecoming (film)|The Homecoming]]'' (1973).<ref name="Macnab"/> Holm explained why he accepted the role, saying, "It's not often you get offered a leading role at age 65... This is my first in a movie," and afterwards said the film is "very touching" and "a masterpiece".<ref>{{Cite web|last=Kirkland|first=Bruce|date=15 October 1997|title=Ian Holm sweet on Hereafter|url=http://jam.canoe.com/Movies/Artists/H/Holm_Ian/1997/10/15/759160.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160822145244/http://jam.canoe.com/Movies/Artists/H/Holm_Ian/1997/10/15/759160.html|archive-date=22 August 2016|access-date=3 August 2016|work=[[Canoe.ca]]}}</ref> Holm called his part challenging, as it was his first lead, but he found Egoyan and the Canadian actors to be great to work with.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/masterpiece/archive/programs/kinglear/holm.html |title='Every inch a king': A Talk with Sir Ian Holm |year=1998 |access-date=3 August 2016 |work=[[Masterpiece (TV series)|Masterpiece Theatre]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820023604/http://www.pbs.org/wgbh/masterpiece/archive/programs/kinglear/holm.html |archive-date=20 August 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Music===
{{main|The Sweet Hereafter (soundtrack)}}
{{multiple image
 | align     = right
 | direction = horizontal
 | footer    = [[Mychael Danna]], left, arranged popular Canadian songs which actress [[Sarah Polley]] performed, and the two worked together to create original songs.
 | footer_align = left
 | width     =
 | image1    = Mychael Danna.jpg
 | width1    = 163
 | alt1      =
 | image2    = Sarah Polley - 66th Venice International Film Festival, 2009 (2).jpg
 | width2    = 150
 | alt2      =
}}
The ''Pied Piper'' references influenced the composer [[Mychael Danna]]'s music, which uses a [[Ney|Persian ney flute]] along with old instruments such as [[Recorder (musical instrument)|recorders]], [[crumhorn]]s and [[lute]]s,{{sfn|Mera|2007|p=37}} creating "a pseudo-[[Medieval music|medieval]] score"{{sfn|Mera|2007|p=36}} which was performed by the [[Toronto Consort]], conducted by [[David Fallis]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Whitesell|first=Lloyd|title=Musical Eclecticism and Ambiguity in The Sweet Hereafter|journal=American Music|publisher=University of Illinois Press|volume=29|issue=2|date=Summer 2011|doi=10.5406/americanmusic.29.2.0229|s2cid=192566992 |page=245}}</ref> The score thus combined Danna's interests in old and exotic music.{{sfn|Mera|2007|p=38}} Egoyan stated medieval-style music was used to make the film feel timeless, evoking [[Brothers Grimm]] fairy tales and avoiding the feel of a [[TV movie]].{{sfn|Wood|2006|p=59}}

Polley's character, Nicole, is an aspiring singer before the accident, and is seen on stage performing [[Jane Siberry]]'s "[[One More Colour]]." Danna and Polley cooperated to create Nicole's music, with Polley writing lyrics to Danna's original songs and Danna arranging the adaptations of "[[Courage (for Hugh MacLennan)|Courage]]" and "One More Colour". The songs were chosen because of their domestic popularity, reinforcing the local nature of Nicole's music.{{sfn|Mera|2007|p=41}} [[The Tragically Hip]]'s original version of "Courage" also appears in the film.{{sfn|Mera|2007|p=42}}

==Release==
The film debuted at the [[1997 Cannes Film Festival|Cannes Film Festival]] in May 1997, and went on to play at the [[1997 Toronto International Film Festival|Toronto International Film Festival]], [[Telluride Film Festival]], [[New York Film Festival]] and [[Valladolid International Film Festival]].{{sfn|Burwell|Tschofen|2007|p=368}} In Canada, the film was distributed by [[Alliance Films|Alliance Communications]] on October 10, 1997.<ref name="Wise">{{cite magazine |last=Wise |first=Wyndham |author-link=Wyndham Wise |date=Spring 1998 |title=Editorial |magazine=[[Take One (Canadian magazine)|Take One]] |volume=6 |issue=9 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the-numbers.com/movie/Sweet-Hereafter-The#more |title=The Sweet Hereafter (1997) |access-date=3 August 2016|work=[[The Numbers (website)|The Numbers]]}}</ref>   Following its screening at Cannes, [[Fine Line Features]] secured rights for the film for distribution in the United States, releasing it there on November 21, 1997.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the-numbers.com/movie/Sweet-Hereafter-The#more |title=The Sweet Hereafter (1997) |access-date=3 August 2016|work=[[The Numbers (website)|The Numbers]]}}</ref>

In [[DVD region code#1|Region 1]], ''The Sweet Hereafter'' was released on [[DVD]] in May 1998.<ref>{{Cite web|date=12 December 2018|title=Sweet Hereafter, The|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/1999/12/20/sweet-hereafterthe|website=[[IGN]]}}</ref> In Canada, the film had a [[Blu-ray]] release in June 2012, with special features, including interviews.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Monk|first=Katherine|date=18 June 2012|title=New on DVD, Blu-ray: Exotica among highlights of week's releases|url=https://montrealgazette.com/health/exotica+among+highlights+week+releases/6801857/story.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820020118/https://montrealgazette.com/health/exotica+among+highlights+week+releases/6801857/story.html|archive-date=20 August 2016|access-date=|work=[[The Gazette (Montreal)|The Gazette]]}}</ref>

In 2023, [[Telefilm Canada]] announced that the film was one of 23 titles that will be digitally restored under its new Canadian Cinema Reignited program to preserve classic Canadian films.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Mullen |first=Pat |date=May 9, 2023 |title=Oscar Winning Doc Leads List of Restored Canadian Classics |url=https://povmagazine.com/oscar-winning-doc-leads-list-of-restored-canadian-classics/ |magazine=Point of View}}</ref>

==Reception==
===Box office===
By the spring of 1998, ''The Sweet Hereafter'' had grossed $1 million domestically.<ref name="Wise"/> According to ''[[The Numbers (website)|The Numbers]]'', ''The Sweet Hereafter'' grossed $4,306,697 in North America and $3,644,550 in other territories, for a worldwide total of $7,951,247.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the-numbers.com/movie/Sweet-Hereafter-The#more |title=The Sweet Hereafter (1997) |access-date=3 August 2016|work=[[The Numbers (website)|The Numbers]]}}</ref> Although Canadian historian [[George Melnyk]] said the film achieved "mainstream popularity",{{sfn|Melnyk|2004|p=160}} another Canadian historian, [[Reginald C. Stuart]], said that the film "aimed for, but did not reach, a mass audience."{{sfn|Stuart|2007|p=59}} Dan Webster of ''[[The Spokesman-Review]]'' concluded that "despite generally good reviews", the film "never attracted much box-office attention."<ref>{{cite news |last=Webster |first=Dan |date=29 May 1998 |title='Sweet Hereafter' studies town coping with deaths of children |newspaper=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |page=3}}</ref>

The [[Writers Guild of Canada]] commented that ''The Sweet Hereafter'' and contemporary Canadian films "never succeeded in scoring a home run at the international box office."{{sfn|Pryke|Soderlund|2003|p=439}} Melnyk suggested Egoyan's previous film ''[[Exotica (film)|Exotica]]'' performed better at the box office than ''The Sweet Hereafter'' because of ''Exotica''{{'s}} "sexual content&nbsp;... rather than the early film's artistic merit."{{sfn|Melnyk|2004|p=160}}

===Critical reception===
[[File:Ian Holm.jpg|thumb|[[Ian Holm]] received critical praise for his performance in the film and won the [[18th Genie Awards|Genie Award]] for [[Canadian Screen Award for Best Actor|Best Actor]].|219x219px]]
{{Rotten Tomatoes prose|98||61|Director Atom Egoyan examines tragedy and its aftermath with intelligence and empathy.|ref=yes|access-date={{RT data|access date}}}} On [[Metacritic]], the film has a weighted average score of 91 out of 100, based on 23 critics, indicating "universal acclaim".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/the-sweet-hereafter |title=The Sweet Hereafter Reviews |work=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|access-date=March 5, 2018}}</ref> In 2002, readers of ''[[Playback (magazine)|Playback]]'' voted it the greatest Canadian film ever made.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.playbackonline.ca/articles/magazine/20020902/best.html |title=Egoyan tops Canada's all-time best movies list |last=Dillon |first=Mark |date=2 September 2002 |access-date=2 August 2016|work=[[Playback (magazine)|Playback]]}}</ref> In 2004, the [[Toronto International Film Festival]] ranked it third in the [[Top 10 Canadian Films of All Time]], tied with ''[[Goin' Down the Road]]'',<ref name="Gravestock">{{Cite web|url=http://tiff.net/canadas-all-time-top-ten |title=Essay |last=Gravestock |first=Steve |authorlink=Steve Gravestock |access-date=28 August 2016 |work=[[Toronto International Film Festival]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160704203521/http://tiff.net/canadas-all-time-top-ten |archive-date= 4 July 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and in 2015, it was the sole film in the third spot.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/north/atanarjuat-voted-no-1-canadian-film-of-all-time-1.3047162 |title=Atanarjuat voted No. 1 Canadian film of all time |date=24 April 2015 |access-date=29 August 2016|publisher=[[CBC News]]}}</ref>

[[Roger Ebert]] gave the film four stars, calling it "one of the best films of the year, an unflinching lament for the human condition."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ebert |first=Roger |date=23 December 1997 |title=The Sweet Hereafter |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/the-sweet-hereafter-1997 |access-date=2 August 2016 |publisher=Chicago Sun-Times |via=RogerEbert.com}}</ref> [[Janet Maslin]], writing for ''[[The New York Times]]'', said "this fusion of Mr. Banks's and Mr. Egoyan's sensibilities stands as a particularly inspired mix", with [[Sarah Polley]] and [[Bruce Greenwood]] "particularly good here".<ref>{{Cite web|last=Maslin|first=Janet|date=3 October 1997|title=FILM FESTIVAL REVIEW; A Town Bereft, Limping Into the Future|url=https://archive.nytimes.com/www.nytimes.com/library/film/sweet-film-review.html|access-date=2 August 2016|work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>  Brendan Kelly of ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' praised ''The Sweet Hereafter'' as "Egoyan's most ambitious work to date", and as "a rich, complex meditation on the impact of a terrible tragedy on a small town", adding Polley and [[Tom McCamus]] are "excellent".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://variety.com/1997/film/reviews/the-sweet-hereafter-1117341459/ |title=Review: 'The Sweet Hereafter' |last=Kelly |first=Brendan |date=16 May 1997 |access-date=2 August 2016|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref>

''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' gave the film an A, saying it "puts you in a rapturous emotional daze", and calling it a "hymn to the agony of loss" and "a new kind of mystical fairy tale, one that seeks to uncover the forces holding the world together, even as they tear it apart."<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Gleiberman|first=Owen|author-link=Owen Gleiberman|date=28 November 1997|title=The Sweet Hereafter|url=https://ew.com/article/1997/11/28/sweet-hereafter-3/|access-date=2 August 2016|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]}}</ref> Paul Tatara of ''[[CNN]]'' called ''The Sweet Hereafter'' "devastating" and wrote Ian Holm gives "the performance of his hugely impressive career."<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cnn.com/SHOWBIZ/9712/15/review.sweet.hereafter/ |title=Review: Vengeance in a town full of grief in 'The Sweet Hereafter' |last=Tatara |first=Paul |date=15 December 1997 |access-date=2 August 2016|work=[[CNN]]}}</ref> David Denby of ''[[New York (magazine)|New York]]'' magazine said that the film had "Ian Holm's greatest role in the movies" and the cast are "all excellent".<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Denby|first=David|date=24 November 1997|title=From Here to Eternity|magazine=[[New York (magazine)|New York]]|page=|pages=68, 70}}</ref> The film made over 250 critics' Top 10 lists for the best films of 1997.{{sfn|Burwell|Tschofen|2007|p=368}}

In 2001, an industry poll conducted by ''[[Playback (magazine)|Playback]]'' named it the best Canadian film of the preceding 15 years.<ref>[[Michael Posner (journalist)|Michael Posner]], "Egoyan tops film poll". ''[[The Globe and Mail]]'', November 25, 2001.</ref>

In 2004, Slovenian critic [[Slavoj Žižek]] called ''The Sweet Hereafter'' "arguably {{em|the}} film about the impact of trauma on a community."{{sfn|Bullard|2013|p=26}} That year, ''The New York Times'' also included the film on its list of "the Best 1,000 Movies Ever Made".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/ref/movies/1000best.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160722141147/https://www.nytimes.com/ref/movies/1000best.html |title=The Best 1,000 Movies Ever Made |last=The Film Critics |year=2004 |access-date=13 August 2016 |archive-date=22 July 2016 |work=[[The New York Times]] |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref> In 2011, British director [[Clio Barnard]] praised the "real depth" and "healthy ambiguity" of the story and described Holm and Polley as "brilliant", giving "powerful, subtle performances".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/film/classic-movies/8390433/Clio-Barnard-on-The-Sweet-Hereafter.html |title=Clio Barnard on The Sweet Hereafter |last=Lee |first=Marc |date=18 May 2011 |access-date=2 August 2016|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]}}</ref> One year later, ''[[The A.V. Club]]'' named ''The Sweet Hereafter'' the 22nd best film of the 1990s, praising it as a "masterpiece of adaptation".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.avclub.com/article/the-50-best-films-of-the-90s-2-of-3-86361 |title=The 50 best films of the '90s |last1=Adams |first1=Sam |last2=D'Angelo |first2=Mike | last3=Murray |first3=Noel | last4=Phipps |first4=Keith | last5=Rabin |first5=Nathan | last6=Robinson |first6=Tasha | last7=Tobias |first7=Scott | last8=Willmore |first8=Alison |date=9 October 2012 |access-date=2 August 2016|work=[[The A.V. Club]]}}</ref>

===Accolades===
''The Sweet Hereafter'' won three awards at the [[1997 Cannes Film Festival]]: the [[FIPRESCI Prize]], the [[Grand Prix (Cannes Film Festival)|Grand Prize of the Jury]], and the [[Prize of the Ecumenical Jury]].<ref name="festival-cannes.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/4810/year/1997.html |title=Festival de Cannes: The Sweet Hereafter |access-date=23 September 2009 |publisher=festival-cannes.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110822142730/http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/4810/year/1997.html |archive-date=22 August 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> This was the highest honour won at Cannes for a Canadian film and made Egoyan the first Canadian to win the Grand Prix, followed by [[Xavier Dolan]] with ''[[It's Only the End of the World]]'' in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Howell |first=Peter |date=22 May 2016 |title=Canada's Xavier Dolan wins Grand Prix at Cannes for It's Only the End of the World |url=https://www.thestar.com/entertainment/movies/2016/05/22/canadas-xavier-dolan-wins-grand-prix-at-cannes-for-its-only-the-end-of-the-world.html |access-date=22 June 2016 |website=Toronto Star}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://etcanada.com/news/15605/atom-egoyan-on-1997-cannes-victory-i-still-think-it-was-a-fluke/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160918074951/http://etcanada.com/news/15605/atom-egoyan-on-1997-cannes-victory-i-still-think-it-was-a-fluke/|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 September 2016|title=Atom Egoyan On 1997 Cannes Victory: 'I Still Think It Was A Fluke' |work=[[ET Canada]] |last=Humphreys |first=David|date=26 May 2014|access-date=26 June 2016}}</ref>

''The Sweet Hereafter'' also won Best Motion Picture, Best Director, Best Cinematography, Best Actor for Holm, and three other prizes, at the [[18th Genie Awards]]. It was nominated for Best Director and Best Adapted Screenplay at the [[70th Academy Awards]], but lost to ''[[Titanic (1997 film)|Titanic]]'' and ''[[L.A. Confidential (film)|L.A. Confidential]]'', respectively.<ref name="Oscars1998">{{Cite web|url=http://www.oscars.org/oscars/ceremonies/1998 |title=The 70th Academy Awards (1998) Nominees and Winners |access-date=19 November 2011|work=Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences|publisher=AMPAS}}</ref>
